Next up is the Big 12 Championships, hosted by Oklahoma State on Saturday 31 October. BYU are aiming for a fourth straight conference title. Originally reported in LetsRun , LetsRun , BYU Athletics - Official Athletics Website - BYU Cougars , FloTrack
- [Dan Camac runs 87 loops as Australia close on 1,069 at Backyard Ultra team worlds](https://filmmyrun.com/news/dan-camac-runs-87-loops-as-australia-close-on-1-069-at-backyard-ultra): News Dan Camac runs 87 loops as Australia close on 1,069 at Backyard Ultra team worlds Dan Camac runs 87 loops as Australia close on 1,069 at Backyard Ultra team worlds 22 October 2026 Photo: abc.net.au Dan Camac was the last Australian runner left at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship. He completed 87 loops of the 6.7km course at Kembla Grange, in the Illawarra region of New South Wales. That is about 583km of running since Saturday night. His finish closed the Australian race on a team total of 1,069 loops. More than four days in, only Belgium still had athletes on course, with two runners left. The championship began on Saturday 17 October with 990 runners from 67 countries. Each nation races a team of up to 15 on its own course, all starting together across the time zones. Kembla Grange set off at 11pm local time. Runners start a loop of 6.706km every hour and are out once they fail to finish inside the hour. Every completed loop adds a point to the national total, and each country's race runs until one athlete remains. Australia led for much of the race and went in front on lap 56. The United States then closed the gap overnight and moved ahead. Barry Keem , 46, from Wollongong, had targeted 100 loops on his home course but stopped after 70 hours. He went to bed with eight or nine teammates still running and woke to find only two left. Race director Red Barnett put the attrition down to fatigue, nutrition problems and physical ailments. Jonathan Ash, an engineer from Shellharbour, was the first Australian out. He went over the hour on his 41st loop on Monday afternoon, slowed by knee bursitis and muscle tightness that began around lap 16. He called it one of the most painful experiences of his life. Ash ran 100 loops, or 670km, in 2024, one of only two Australians to reach that mark. Melbourne's Brandon Lee Gretch, 32, stopped after lap 73. It was a personal best, reached despite a shooting pain in his back from around the 67th loop. Canada raced on the B.C. Backyard Ultra course at Sicamous, British Columbia. On the third morning the team was sixth, with seven of its 15 runners still going. Sandra Auger had gone furthest of those out, with 51 yards, or 342km, and finished her last lap carrying a shoe. Austin Sedgwick made 48 yards and Viktoria Brown 45. After 52 hours Japan, the United States, Belgium and Australia led the standings, with 135 runners and 20 countries still in. Belgium won the team title in 2024 with 1,147 yards. Originally reported in abc.net.au ,
- [Ian Winship, 90, runs 1:04:37 at Cumbernauld 10K for M90 world best](https://filmmyrun.com/news/ian-winship-90-runs-1-04-37-at-cumbernauld-10k-for-m90-world-best): News Ian Winship, 90, runs 1:04:37 at Cumbernauld 10K for M90 world best Ian Winship, 90, runs 1:04:37 at Cumbernauld 10K for M90 world best 26 September 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Scotland's Ian Winship has set a new standard for 90-year-olds over 10K on the road. The former paratrooper clocked 1:04:37 at the Cumbernauld 10K in North Lanarkshire on 13 September. Scottish Athletics regards the time as a world best for the M90 category. No quicker road 10K by a man aged 90 or over has been reported. The run also took down the British M90 best. That mark stood at 1:07:02 and had belonged to Gordon Porteous since 2004. For comparison, the official M90 world record for 10,000m on the track is 1:02:48.93. Australia's David Carr set it in Perth in 2022. It was a family outing. Winship's daughter, Fiona Fleming, was also in the field, as was his grandson Kyle Fleming, 26. Kyle finished third overall. The three generations have raced together before. Kyle told Canadian Running that his grandfather was the reason he took up the sport, calling him a "living legend". Winship admitted to Scottish Athletics that the result had surprised him. He described himself as "a wee guy fae Cumbernauld" and joked that the town might now be famous on his account. His working life began in the Army. After leaving the forces he became a steeplejack, climbing tall structures to maintain and repair them. He still covers about 20,000 steps a day. Winship said getting out keeps him engaged and that staying indoors was not an option. "I must meet people," he said. His next target, he told Scottish Athletics, is to "live to 100". The start was sunny, but rain arrived in the evening and continued through the night, with hail at times. Its chief executive, Bert Bean, is an ultrarunner himself. This year second place earned $8,500 and third $5,000, with prize money down to seventh. Details of payouts for the rest of the field in 2027 are still to come. Abramowitz called the prize "certainly unprecedented". Originally reported in iRunFar , ,
- [Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz cuts more than two hours off the GR20 record in Corsica](https://filmmyrun.com/news/aurelien-dunand-pallaz-cuts-more-than-two-hours-off-the-gr20-record-in): News Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz cuts more than two hours off the GR20 record in Corsica Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz cuts more than two hours off the GR20 record in Corsica 26 September 2026 Photo: franceinfo Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz has lowered the record for Corsica's GR20 by more than two hours. - [Norwegian mountain runner Ida Amelie Robsahm dies weeks after Kalie McCrystal lost on Matterhorn](https://filmmyrun.com/news/norwegian-mountain-runner-ida-amelie-robsahm-dies-weeks-after-kalie-mc): News Norwegian mountain runner Ida Amelie Robsahm dies weeks after Kalie McCrystal lost on Matterhorn Norwegian mountain runner Ida Amelie Robsahm dies weeks after Kalie McCrystal lost on Matterhorn 26 September 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Norwegian mountain runner Ida Amelie Robsahm has died after a fall on Romsdalseggen in western Norway on Saturday 19 September. Robsahm had been out with a group near the top of the ridge, which rises to 1,329 metres, when she fell several dozen metres. - [Joe McConaughy sets supported John Muir Trail record of 2 days 16 hours](https://filmmyrun.com/news/joe-mcconaughy-takes-3-hours-26-minutes-off-the-supported-john-muir-tr): News Joe McConaughy sets supported John Muir Trail record of 2 days 16 hours Joe McConaughy sets supported John Muir Trail record of 2 days 16 hours 26 September 2026 Photo: Caroline Himbert / iRunFar Joe McConaughy has set a new men's supported fastest known time on California's John Muir Trail. He ran it northbound in 2 days and 16 hours. Canadian Running notes the time is still pending verification. It was his third go at the record, after failed attempts in 2022 and 2024. The route covers about 223 miles, or 352km, through the Sierra Nevada. It runs from Whitney Portal to Happy Isles in Yosemite National Park and climbs more than 14,000 metres. For roughly the first 100 miles he stayed level with D'Haene's schedule, going over Whitney and about six more passes. By around 135 miles on Tuesday morning he had edged some two miles clear. At nightfall on Tuesday he had covered about 185 miles and led the record pace by more than nine miles. The last 40 miles went smoothly overnight. He reached Happy Isles early on Wednesday, before 6am local time. His tracker had him about 13 miles up on D'Haene at the finish. In 2025 he placed third over 100km at Black Canyon, and at Western States 100 that same year he came home 14th. Originally reported in iRunFar , Canadian Running Magazine
- [Run Rabbit Run 100 winners to receive US$100,000 each in 2027 and 2028](https://filmmyrun.com/news/run-rabbit-run-100-winners-to-receive-us-100-000-each-in-2027-and-2028): News Run Rabbit Run 100 winners to receive US$100,000 each in 2027 and 2028 Run Rabbit Run 100 winners to receive US$100,000 each in 2027 and 2028 26 September 2026 Photo: Canadian Running The men's and women's winners of the Run Rabbit Run 100 in Steamboat Springs, Colorado, will each receive US$100,000 in 2027 and 2028. On the Singletrack podcast, host Finn Melanson asked whether the money might lure top athletes away from other races and push rival events to raise their own purses. Local runner Devon Olson was second at mile 89, 26 minutes behind Sullivan, when he fell and separated his shoulder. He walked to an aid station for treatment. He said afterwards he was fine but "disappointed". More than 800 runners took part in the 14th edition across the 100-mile hare and tortoise divisions and the 50-mile race.
- [Almgren wins world half marathon title in Copenhagen with European record of 58:06](https://filmmyrun.com/news/almgren-wins-world-half-marathon-title-in-copenhagen-with-european-rec): News Almgren wins world half marathon title in Copenhagen with European record of 58:06 Almgren wins world half marathon title in Copenhagen with European record of 58:06 26 September 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Andreas Almgren of Sweden is the world half marathon champion. He won in Copenhagen in 58:06, a European record. That takes 35 seconds off his own previous best of 58:41, set in Valencia last year. Almgren raced cautiously early on and made clear he had no wish to lead. He was ninth at 5km, sitting behind the front runners. As the pace lifted he worked his way forward. With roughly 3km left through the streets of the Danish capital, only three men remained in contention. They were Kenya's Nicholas Kipkorir, Uganda's Joshua Cheptegei and Almgren. Kipkorir led and glanced back several times. Cheptegei was the first to crack. The other two stayed close all the way to the line, and a sprint settled it. He admitted to simply sitting in, noting he had done plenty of front running when he won the European title in Birmingham. The result makes him the first non-African to win the world half marathon title since Stefano Baldini in 1996. It is his third major championship medal, after world bronze and European gold over 10,000m. Kipkorir said he was proud of silver and had helped push the winner. Rival Charles Wheeler called Almgren "a monster" and the best in the sport at present. There will be little celebration for now. Almgren flies to Flagstaff in the United States on Monday for an altitude camp. It is preparation for his marathon debut in New York on 1 November. - [Kosgei and Talbi win record-sized 45th Great North Run as McColgan pulls out injured](https://filmmyrun.com/news/kosgei-and-talbi-win-record-45th-great-north-run-as-mccolgan-limps-out): News Kosgei and Talbi win record-sized 45th Great North Run as McColgan pulls out injured Kosgei and Talbi win record-sized 45th Great North Run as McColgan pulls out injured 27 September 2026 Photo: BBC Sport Brigid Kosgei and Zouhair Talbi won the 45th Great North Run on 13 September, a UK half marathon that drew a record field of about 63,000. - [Courtney-Bryant and Kavanagh kick late to win UK 5km road titles in Cardiff](https://filmmyrun.com/news/courtney-bryant-and-kavanagh-kick-late-to-win-uk-5km-road-titles-in-ca): News Courtney-Bryant and Kavanagh kick late to win UK 5km road titles in Cardiff Courtney-Bryant and Kavanagh kick late to win UK 5km road titles in Cardiff 29 September 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Melissa Courtney-Bryant and Jack Kavanagh are the new UK Athletics 5km Road champions. - [Canada to launch nine-race national skyrunning series in 2027](https://filmmyrun.com/news/canada-to-launch-nine-race-national-skyrunning-series-in-2027): News Canada to launch nine-race national skyrunning series in 2027 Canada to launch nine-race national skyrunning series in 2027 30 September 2026 Photo: Alex Guiry / Canadian Running Canada is to get its own national skyrunning series next year. The Canadian Skyrunning National Series will link nine races across three mountain weekends in the west of the country, all scored on a single points table. Racing runs from June to August 2027. Canadian Running reported the news on 29 September. Six of the nine races carry Skyrunner National Series status, which ties the new Canadian circuit to the international Skyrunner World Series. The headline race covers 33.5km with 2,900m of climbing on a course certified by the International Skyrunning Federation. Alongside it are the Mini-Taur, 10.5km with 950m of ascent, and the Minotaur VK at Castle Mountain Resort, which gains 970m in 4km. The event is no newcomer. Its main race has featured on the Skyrunner World Series for three editions. This year the weekend decided Canada's national skyrunning titles. It also hosted the inaugural youth championships for North and Central America. July brings the Wildside SkyRace weekend at Apex Mountain Resort, high above Penticton in British Columbia. There are three races. The Wildside Vertical climbs 650m in 2.5km. Wildside Sky 16 fits 1,400m of ascent into 16km. The 28km Wildside SkyRace, with 2,500m of climbing, is the weekend's Skyrunner National Series race. The finale is the Stoked Ultra weekend in Revelstoke, British Columbia, in August. It opens with the Stoked VK, 6.6km with 1,200m of ascent. The second day offers a choice. The Stoked Scramble covers 25km with 1,600m of climbing. The Stoked Ultra runs to 50.5km with 3,500m of gain. All three Revelstoke races hold Skyrunner National Series status. Points are awarded by finishing position to the top 50 in each race. SkyRace and SkyUltra results score more than vertical kilometres. To feature in the overall standings, runners must complete at least four events. Prize money goes to the first three women and first three men in the final standings, with $2,500 for the winner, $1,250 for second and $750 for third. Originally reported in Canadian Running
- [Megan Keith takes 96 seconds off River Ness 10K record in Inverness](https://filmmyrun.com/news/megan-keith-takes-96-seconds-off-river-ness-10k-record-in-inverness): News Megan Keith takes 96 seconds off River Ness 10K record in Inverness Megan Keith takes 96 seconds off River Ness 10K record in Inverness 30 September 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Megan Keith broke the women's course record at the Baxters River Ness 10K in Inverness on Sunday 27 September, winning in 31:24. - [Gemma Steel and Lee Gratton win first English Masters Cross Country titles](https://filmmyrun.com/news/gemma-steel-and-lee-gratton-win-first-english-masters-cross-country-ti): News Gemma Steel and Lee Gratton win first English Masters Cross Country titles Gemma Steel and Lee Gratton win first English Masters Cross Country titles 30 September 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Gemma Steel and Lee Gratton are the first English Masters Cross Country champions. - [Olympic hurdles silver medallist Cyréna Samba-Mayela provisionally suspended over whereabouts failures](https://filmmyrun.com/news/olympic-hurdles-silver-medallist-cyrena-samba-mayela-provisionally-sus): News Olympic hurdles silver medallist Cyréna Samba-Mayela provisionally suspended over whereabouts failures Olympic hurdles silver medallist Cyréna Samba-Mayela provisionally suspended over whereabouts failures 28 September 2026 Photo: Kevin Morris / Canadian Running Cyréna Samba-Mayela, the French hurdler who took 100m hurdles silver at the Paris Olympics in 2024, has been provisionally suspended for whereabouts failures. The Athletics Integrity Unit confirmed the decision on Friday 25 September. The suspension has been in force since 18 September. The 25-year-old has not raced since July. She then pulled out of August's European Championships in Birmingham with a calf injury. The case concerns three whereabouts failures within a 12-month period. Elite athletes must tell anti-doping officials where they will be each day, including at training camps and while travelling, so that unannounced tests can take place. Missed tests, filing failures or a mix of the two can add up to an anti-doping rule violation. The maximum ban is two years. French media, including L'Équipe, reported in August that she was facing a suspension. The AIU made no official announcement until this week. A provisional suspension does not mean she has failed a test. Her agent, Maka Haïdara, said she had never returned a positive result. He said the proceedings concerned only administrative whereabouts obligations and not the use of any substance. He added that she had answered within the deadlines, was cooperating fully and would not comment further. Samba-Mayela can contest the charge before an AIU committee, including disputing at least one of the recorded absences. If the committee rejects her explanation, she could be banned until September 2028 and miss the Los Angeles Games. The other route is to accept the sanction and hope for a one-year reduction that would leave her free to compete at the next Olympics. Her 2024 season was the best of her career. She won the European title in Rome in a French record of 12.31. A few months later she finished second in Paris behind world record holder Masai Russell of the United States. It was the only athletics medal France won at its home Games. A calf injury then kept her out of almost all of 2025. There were signs of a revival this year. She raced eight meets and went under 13 seconds in four of them, including 12.50 in June. On medical advice she did not defend her European title in Birmingham. At the time she said on Instagram that she would concentrate on rehabilitation and return in 2027. Originally reported in Canadian Running ,
- [Boston Marathon cut-off tightens to 5:17 for the 2027 race](https://filmmyrun.com/news/boston-marathon-cut-off-tightens-to-5-17-for-the-2027-race): News Boston Marathon cut-off tightens to 5:17 for the 2027 race Boston Marathon cut-off tightens to 5:17 for the 2027 race 30 September 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Getting into the Boston Marathon has become harder again. The Boston Athletic Association said on Tuesday 29 September that applicants had to beat their age-group qualifying standard by 5:17 to earn a place on the start line in Hopkinton. That margin is 43 seconds wider than the 4:34 needed for the 2026 race. The 131st edition will be held on Monday 19 April 2027. In all, 33,649 people applied, and they came from 129 countries and every one of the US states. It said 25,630 qualified runners had been accepted so far or were being processed, pending checks on their qualifying performances. That is a record, up from 24,362 accepted for 2026. Runner's World reported that 8,019 applicants who had run a qualifying time missed out. In the fastest category, men aged 18 to 34, the cut-off works out at 2:49:43. It is the first time that mark has fallen below 2:50. Women in the same age group needed 3:19:43. Until 2024 a sub-three-hour run was enough for the younger men, apart from 2021, when Covid rules limited the field. The equivalent figure was 2:54:31 in 2024, 2:53:09 in 2025 and 2:50:26 in 2026. Some of those left out still have a chance. In July the BAA introduced a random draw for 1,000 runners who met their standard but not the cut-off. The organisers said a key aim was to get more qualified athletes into the race. Runner's World put the odds of selection at about 12.5 per cent, and winners are due to be told in the coming days. The field remains capped at 30,000 official entrants. Time qualifiers make up about 80 per cent, with the rest made up of invited professionals, Para athletes and charity runners. New for 2027 is a "downhill index", under which times from courses with large net elevation drops either carry a penalty or cannot be used at all. BAA chief executive Jack Fleming said the number of marathoners worldwide "only continues to grow". The qualifying window for the 2028 race opened on 19 September 2026. Originally reported in Canadian Running , BostonGlobe.com ,
- [Catherine Debrunner beats Sabastian Sawe at rock, paper, scissors to settle London Marathon elite days](https://filmmyrun.com/news/catherine-debrunner-beats-sabastian-sawe-at-rock-paper-scissors-to-set): News Catherine Debrunner beats Sabastian Sawe at rock, paper, scissors to settle London Marathon elite days Catherine Debrunner beats Sabastian Sawe at rock, paper, scissors to settle London Marathon elite days 1 October 2026 Photo: BBC Sport Rock, paper, scissors has decided the order of elite racing at next year's two-day London Marathon. Switzerland's Catherine Debrunner , the women's wheelchair marathon world record holder, beat Kenya's Sabastian Sawe two games to nil in a best-of-three contest. The pair had agreed beforehand that the winner would take Sunday, the race's traditional day. The elite women's and women's wheelchair races will therefore be held on Sunday 25 April 2027. The elite men and the men's wheelchair race move to Saturday 24 April. Both are reigning London champions. Sawe ran 1:59:30 in London this year, the first time anyone has broken two hours in a record-eligible marathon. Debrunner has won London four times and set her world record of 1:34:16 in Berlin in 2023. She holds all nine women's T53 world records, from the 100m to the marathon. Canadian Running pointed out that Sawe had not lost a competition of any kind since a runner-up place over 10K at the adizero Road to Records meeting in Germany in 2024. An adjudicator from Guinness World Records watched the game, and it was ratified as the first elite marathon start ever decided this way. Male Championship and Good for Age runners will race on the Saturday, and their female counterparts on the Sunday. For the first time in London, Championship women will start directly after the elite women instead of following the elite men. The elite women's wheelchair race will start just ahead of them. Each day's mass race will mix men, women and non-binary runners. The entry window for Championship and Good for Age places was due to open on Thursday 1 October. Organisers confirmed in June that the 2027 race would be spread over two days. A record 1.33 million people entered the ballot for 2027, up from 1.1 million for this year's race. The Double will put 100,000 runners on the Greenwich-to-Westminster course and is expected to raise more than £150m for charity. Ballot places will be assigned to one of the two days, and runners cannot choose which. Organisers say the format is for 2027 only. Hugh Brasher, chief executive of London Marathon Events, described the contest as "an entertaining way" to allocate the days. He called the 2027 race "a momentous one-off event". Both Sawe and Debrunner are expected to return to defend their titles. Originally reported in BBC Sport ,
- [Double London Marathon in 2027 to double as British trial for Beijing and LA 2028](https://filmmyrun.com/news/double-london-marathon-in-2027-to-double-as-british-trial-for-beijing): News Double London Marathon in 2027 to double as British trial for Beijing and LA 2028 Double London Marathon in 2027 to double as British trial for Beijing and LA 2028 1 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Next year's two-day London Marathon will decide the British marathon titles. UK Athletics will also use it as its official trial for two global events: the 2027 worlds in Beijing and the Olympics in Los Angeles a year later. Organisers confirmed the arrangement on 1 October. Eilish McColgan and Mahamed Mahamed won the national titles in 2026. For the first time, and for one year only, the race will run over two days. The elite men go on Saturday 24 April and the elite women on Sunday 25 April. For Beijing, the first two British men and first two British women will be eligible for selection. That depends on each having run the World Athletics qualifying times before or on race day. Those times are 2:06:00 for men and 2:23:20 for women. The Olympic route is shorter. The first British man and first British woman home will be pre-selected for LA 2028, provided they meet Olympic qualifying times due to be confirmed by the end of the year. Their Team GB places will only be confirmed after further performances across race distances during the 2028 season. UK Athletics will publish the full detail in its selection policy. Tom Craggs, the governing body's endurance performance lead, said British marathon running was going "from strength to strength". Hugh Brasher, who runs London Marathon Events, noted that the country's best would be racing for places at "not one, but two" global championships. Debrunner won, so the elite women and women's wheelchair races take the Sunday. The game was recognised as a Guinness World Records title in front of an official adjudicator. The mass races will run on both days over the course from Greenwich to Westminster. More than £150m is expected to be raised for charity. Championship and Good for Age entries open on 1 October. McColgan made her marathon debut in London in 2025, finishing eighth in 2:24:25 as the first British runner. Originally reported in ,
- [Strangeway and Wyness take Loch Ness Marathon titles as record 11,100 run in Inverness](https://filmmyrun.com/news/strangeway-and-wyness-take-loch-ness-marathon-titles-as-record-11-100): News Strangeway and Wyness take Loch Ness Marathon titles as record 11,100 run in Inverness Strangeway and Wyness take Loch Ness Marathon titles as record 11,100 run in Inverness 1 October 2026 Photo: RunABC Scotland William Strangeway and Hazel Wyness won the Baxters Loch Ness Marathon on Sunday 27 September. Strangeway, 40, of Lincoln Wellington AC, is listed in the results at 2:20:16, though local reports had him a second quicker. Wyness, 48, of Metro Aberdeen, took the women's race in 2:52:04. It was the first Loch Ness title for both. The marathon was full at 6,000 entries and sold out earlier than in any previous year. The race starts at 10:00 and runs point to point beside the south-eastern shore of Loch Ness, finishing at Bught Park in Inverness. Organisers said 58% of runners had come from outside Scotland. Logan Rees of Fife won the men's race for the second time in 28:52. The River Ness 5K and the Wee Nessie children's race completed the day at Bught Park. Originally reported in RunABC Scotland ,
- [Karen Nash, 65, wins women's 180km at the 13 Valleys Ultra](https://filmmyrun.com/news/karen-nash-65-wins-women-s-180km-at-the-13-valleys-ultra): News Karen Nash, 65, wins women's 180km at the 13 Valleys Ultra Karen Nash, 65, wins women's 180km at the 13 Valleys Ultra 1 October 2026 Photo: Runner's World Karen Nash , 65, from Preston, has won the women's 180km race at the Altra 13 Valleys Ultra in the Lake District. She finished in 35 hours, 58 minutes and 26 seconds. The event started in Keswick on Friday 25 September. Runner's World reports that the result made her the oldest British woman to win an ultramarathon. Nash was first woman rather than first overall. The men's race went to Mark Darbyshire from Birmingham in 22:09:03, more than two hours inside last year's course record. The 180km route crosses the Lake District fells and carries around 7,000m of climbing. It was a busy summer by any measure. The 13 Valleys was her fourth race of 100 miles or more in four months. - [Tamás Bódis breaks the Spartathlon course record with 19:40:51](https://filmmyrun.com/news/tamas-bodis-breaks-the-spartathlon-course-record-with-19-40-51): News Tamás Bódis breaks the Spartathlon course record with 19:40:51 Tamás Bódis breaks the Spartathlon course record with 19:40:51 2 October 2026 Photo: Notospress.gr Tamás Bódis has won the 44th Spartathlon in a course record of 19:40:51. They set off in rain, and showers returned at intervals through the day. - [Reid Burrows takes second in the Wériga 93K at Chihuahua by UTMB](https://filmmyrun.com/news/reid-burrows-takes-second-in-the-weriga-93k-at-chihuahua-by-utmb): News Reid Burrows takes second in the Wériga 93K at Chihuahua by UTMB Reid Burrows takes second in the Wériga 93K at Chihuahua by UTMB 6 October 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Canada's Reid Burrows finished second in the Wériga 93K at Chihuahua by UTMB in northern Mexico. It also gives him direct entry to the CCC, the 100K race at the 2027 UTMB World Series Finals. Securing one of those automatic places had been his main aim. He added that the run through the Copper Canyon mattered just as much, and that the chance to "run with the Tarahumara" had drawn him south. The Wériga course measured 94 km with 4,700 metres of climbing. It started in Cerocahui and ran through the Copper Canyon to the finish. Sixty-seven runners completed it. Burrows came to trail running as a professional after a background in triathlon. His earlier results include eighth at the 2023 Leadville Trail 100 and victory at the Sulphur Springs 50K. The women's race went to Rarámuri runner Jenifer Yáñez Cruz of Guachochi in 14:12:34. It was her second straight win over the distance, and it again earns her a place at UTMB in Chamonix. Markéta Brabcová of the Czech Republic was second in 16:21:58, more than two hours back. Portugal's Jamila Dionisio was third in 16:27:38. This was the second edition of Chihuahua by UTMB, which ran from 1 to 3 October across six races in the Copper Canyon and the Sierra Tarahumara. It drew 1,100 runners from 27 countries, close to 90 per cent of them Mexican. More than 100 Rarámuri athletes took part, with entries and mandatory kit paid for by the event through its Norawa programme. The name means "friend" in the Rarámuri language. - [Steve Rankin wins North East Harrier League opener at Thornley](https://filmmyrun.com/news/steve-rankin-wins-north-east-harrier-league-opener-at-thornley): News Steve Rankin wins North East Harrier League opener at Thornley Steve Rankin wins North East Harrier League opener at Thornley 3 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly The North East cross country season is under way. Steve Rankin, an M40, was first across the line at the opening Start Fitness North East Harrier League fixture in Thornley, County Durham, on 26 September. He reached the finish in 34:17 and also recorded the quickest net time of the day, 31:46. Rankin set off from the M pack and still got the better of three runners who had started in the S pack. S Capewell was second home in 35:07 and M Anderson, another M40, third in 36:26. Behind Rankin on net time came L McConnell in 34:16 and D Green, also an M40, in 34:17. The women's race split the same way. Alex Sneddon, a W35 who ran in the 2023 Masters International, started from the S pack and was first woman home in 27:01. Amy Fuller followed in 27:22. Kate Storey crossed the line third in 28:59, but she had started in the M pack and her net time of 26:38 was the fastest of the field. A Pigford was third quickest on 27:06. - [Jakob Ingebrigtsen wins 1500m and 5km at first Runfest Norway in Sandnes](https://filmmyrun.com/news/jakob-ingebrigtsen-wins-1500m-and-5km-at-first-runfest-norway-in-sandn): News Jakob Ingebrigtsen wins 1500m and 5km at first Runfest Norway in Sandnes Jakob Ingebrigtsen wins 1500m and 5km at first Runfest Norway in Sandnes 4 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Jakob Ingebrigtsen won both elite races he entered at the first Runfest Norway, held on the streets of his hometown of Sandnes on 2 and 3 October. The Olympic, world and European champion co-hosts the new festival with his brothers Henrik and Filip. He raced after a bout of Covid that followed the world road running championships in Copenhagen, where he took silver over 5km. Friday's men's 1500m had eight starters and was run into a headwind. The Slovenian pacemaker Žan Rudolf led, and only Ingebrigtsen and Andreas Fjeld Halvorsen went with him from the gun. When Rudolf stepped aside after about 1000m, Ingebrigtsen pulled clear at once. He won in 3:40.7, though one timing had him at 3:40.6. Halvorsen, who once took the world under-20 title over 3000m, finished runner-up in 3:43.3. Sigurd Tveit was third in 3:47.8 and Filip Ingebrigtsen seventh. The women's elite 1500m went to Malin Hoelsveen in 4:27.9. Hoelsveen moved to the 800m this year after giving up skiing and sealed the race with the strongest finish. On Saturday Ingebrigtsen sat behind the leaders in the 5km before taking over with about 300m left. He won in 13:26. Halvorsen was again second, two seconds back, and Ethiopia's Abdreselam Worku third in 13:29. Rudolf and Germany's David Scheller followed. Ingebrigtsen admitted he had felt tired and slept badly after racing. Filip finished sixth and said he would now weigh his motivation and whether his body could still cope with racing at the top level. Ethiopia's Biniyam Melak won the 10km in 27:29. The festival drew 2540 registered runners over four distances. The 10km and half marathon were the busiest, with 838 and 822 entries respectively, while 711 signed up for the 5km and 266 for the shortest race. A winner's prize of up to €1,600 helped attract elite fields that included the Ethiopian steeplechase world record holder Lamecha Girma and a group of Kenyans. Both evenings' elite races were broadcast live. Ingebrigtsen called the event "a celebration of running joy" and stressed that anyone could take part alongside the best. - [Jepkosgei breaks Cardiff Half Marathon course record as Kiprotich completes Kenyan double](https://filmmyrun.com/news/jepkosgei-breaks-cardiff-half-marathon-course-record-as-kiprotich-comp): News Jepkosgei breaks Cardiff Half Marathon course record as Kiprotich completes Kenyan double Jepkosgei breaks Cardiff Half Marathon course record as Kiprotich completes Kenyan double 5 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Joyciline Jepkosgei set a women's course record at the Cardiff Half Marathon on Sunday 4 October, winning in 1:05:40. More than 29,000 runners tackled the 13.1-mile course in fine weather, and the Welsh Half Marathon Championships were decided within the race. Ethiopia's Wede Kefale, whose best is also quicker than the old record, matched her for most of the way. Jepkosgei made her move with three miles left, around Roath Park Lake, and held on through the run back into the centre. Kefale finished second in 1:05:54 and Tigist Tesema third in 1:07:23. Lloyd Sheppard-Brown won the men's Welsh title in 1:03:41 on his debut at the distance. - [Record 35,000 runners take part in Great Scottish Run as Crowe and Ballantyne win half marathon](https://filmmyrun.com/news/record-35-000-runners-take-part-in-great-scottish-run-as-crowe-and-bal): News Record 35,000 runners take part in Great Scottish Run as Crowe and Ballantyne win half marathon Record 35,000 runners take part in Great Scottish Run as Crowe and Ballantyne win half marathon 5 October 2026 Photo: RunABC Scotland The AJ Bell Great Scottish Run had its largest weekend yet in Glasgow, with 35,000 runners taking part across two days. Organisers said it was the biggest staging in the event's history. More than 2,000 of the entrants were children, who opened the weekend on Saturday at the Junior and Mini races. Those events have a new home on Glasgow Green and were back after last year's were called off over fears about Storm Amy. Sunday brought the 10K and the half marathon. Both started on St Vincent Street and crossed the River Clyde. The half marathon then went south through Pollok Country Park before finishing through the McLennan Arch onto Glasgow Green. Central Athletics Club's Jamie Crowe won the men's race in 1:03:27. Jamie Burns was second in 1:05:24 and Dougie Selman third in 1:06:52. The fastest woman was Katrina Ballantyne, who runs for Leeds City AC. She crossed the line in 1:13:33. Brogan Wallace finished second in 1:15:16 and Amy Frankland third in 1:16:00. Ballantyne said she had entered only about six weeks earlier, after friends signed up. She works as a dietitian and runs to and from work, so much of her training is done carrying a backpack. She said the crowd "really carry you round". Lewis Hannigan won the men's 10K in 29:32. Nancy Scott was the first woman home in 33:27. Kyle Brotherton won the men's wheelchair 10K in 31:17. Eilish McColgan , a four-time Olympian and the British record holder for the half marathon, rang the bell to start the half. Craig Ferguson, the Tartan Trekker, started the 10K and then ran the half marathon himself. Earlier this year he walked from Los Angeles to Boston to raise money for SAMH. The Paralympic skier Scott Meenagh ran the 10K. So did Glasgow Warriors head coach Franco Smith, who was raising money for Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity. Much of the field was running for charity, and plenty came in costume. One 10K runner wore full plate armour. Shrek ran with Donkey on his shoulder. Two others wore traffic cones on their heads in tribute to the city's Duke of Wellington statue. Entries are open for next year, when the event will be held on 2 and 3 October 2027. Originally reported in RunABC Scotland ,
- [Alex Durant and Molly Smith win English titles at record-sized Manchester Half](https://filmmyrun.com/news/alex-durant-and-molly-smith-win-english-titles-at-record-sized-manches): News Alex Durant and Molly Smith win English titles at record-sized Manchester Half Alex Durant and Molly Smith win English titles at record-sized Manchester Half 5 October 2026 Photo: RunABC North Alex Durant won the ASICS Manchester Half on Sunday 4 October in 1:02:51, taking the men's English Half Marathon Championship title in the process. Her time was given as 1:11:40 in one report and 1:11:42 by the organisers. Nathan Maguire set a course record in the men's wheelchair race, finishing in 47:01. Roz Delap won the women's wheelchair race in 1:12:13. The wheelchair wave set off at 8:50am, with the elite fields following and the mass waves leaving at nine-minute intervals. It was the biggest field in the race's history, although the figures quoted differ. The organisers put it at over 23,000. Other reports gave around 32,000, against 28,000 the year before. Entries sold out six months in advance. A quarter of the runners were tackling their first half marathon, among them England amputee football captain Sean Jackson, whose side head to Mexico for the World Cup in November. The start drops downhill out of Trafford. From there the course takes in Stretford and Sale before reaching Chorlton-cum-Hardy, and a good part of it is spent on Chester Road. It comes back to finish on Talbot Road, so the opening hill has to be climbed again in the closing stretch. There were records further down the field. David Price set a Guinness World Record for the fastest half marathon by someone with Multiple Sclerosis, running 1:30:30. Joshua Thompson, a 29-year-old paramedic, ran in uniform to attempt the record for the fastest half marathon dressed as a healthcare professional. He thought he had finished in about 1:33, well inside the 1:58 mark he needed. He said the trousers were "incredibly sweaty". He raised more than £1,000 for the North West Ambulance Charity. The organisers said £1.6 million had been raised for charity by the end of the day, with the total still climbing. Other estimates put the final figure at around £1.8 million. The Christie, Cancer Research UK, Moya Cole Hospice and Alzheimer's Society were among the beneficiaries. The race, first held in 2016, returns on Sunday 3 October 2027. - [Mark Kiptoo wins San Sebastián half in 1:03:57 for M50 world record](https://filmmyrun.com/news/mark-kiptoo-wins-san-sebastian-half-in-1-03-57-for-m50-world-record): News Mark Kiptoo wins San Sebastián half in 1:03:57 for M50 world record Mark Kiptoo wins San Sebastián half in 1:03:57 for M50 world record 6 October 2026 Photo: Kevin Morris / Canadian Running Mark Kiptoo of Kenya has set a world best for men aged 50 and over in the half marathon. He won the San Sebastián Rural Kutxa Half Marathon in Spain on Sunday 4 October in 1:03:57. The previous M50 mark was 1:06:23, set by Titus Mamabolo of South Africa in 1991. Kiptoo took 2 minutes 26 seconds off it. He was also the fastest runner in the field, regardless of age. Joseba Díaz paced the early kilometres at around 3:05 per kilometre and held that until just past 7km. Kiptoo then went clear of Iraitz Arrospide, a former world 50km champion, and ran alone to the finish in Donostia. Arrospide was second in 1:04:51 and Youness Assehli third in 1:07:19. The women's race went to the home favourite Maitane Melero in 1:15:44. Melero is 43 and a five-time Spanish champion. Maria Lázaro, the 2025 Spanish marathon champion, set the early pace before fading from about 8km. Janice Studler of Switzerland passed her close to the line for second in 1:18:19. Lázaro was third in 1:18:27. Light rain and wet tarmac stayed with the runners for much of the race. This was its fifth edition, and a record 5,200 people entered. The result was not a great surprise. In March, still aged 49, Kiptoo won the Azkoitia-Azpeitia Half Marathon in 1:03:17. He already holds the M45 marathon record of 2:09:12. His half-marathon best is 1:00:29, run at 34, and his marathon best is 2:06:00, set in Eindhoven in 2015. Before moving to the roads he ran 12:53.46 for 5000m and 27:14.67 for 10,000m on the track, and he twice won 5000m gold at the Military World Games. - [Khairi Bejiga retains tRUNsylvania 10km title as Asefu Abreha springs upset in Brasov](https://filmmyrun.com/news/khairi-bejiga-retains-trunsylvania-10km-title-as-asefu-abreha-springs): News Khairi Bejiga retains tRUNsylvania 10km title as Asefu Abreha springs upset in Brasov Khairi Bejiga retains tRUNsylvania 10km title as Asefu Abreha springs upset in Brasov 6 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Khairi Bejiga became the first athlete to win the tRUNsylvania 10km in consecutive years on Sunday 4 October. The 20-year-old Ethiopian ran 27:01 in Brasov, Romania, one second clear of his training partner Nibret Kinde. Asefu Abreha, also 20, won the women's race in 30:16 as Ethiopians took all six podium places. The race, a World Athletics Elite Label event, has now been held six times. Bejiga took a group of 12 through halfway in 13:32, then covered the sixth and seventh kilometres in 2:42 and 2:40. Five men were left shortly after 8km, reached in 21:44. Uganda's Kenneth Kiprop, one of the favourites, fell a short way further on and finished 11th. A 2:41 ninth kilometre dropped Kenya's Amos Bett and then Ayele Tadesse. Kinde, the reigning Ethiopian 10,000m champion, stayed with Bejiga until the final 200m before losing out on the $5,000 first prize. His 27:02 was a substantial personal best. Bejiga was not entirely satisfied. Speaking through an interpreter, he said the early pace was too slow because "nobody wanted to go faster". He had been chasing both the course record and his own best, which stand at the same time of 26:51. He now turns to the Valencia Half Marathon on 25 October. His only previous half marathon took 1:02:04. Tadesse was third in 27:10, a 30-second improvement. Bett finished fourth in 27:13, two seconds outside his best. Fifth place brought a Djibouti national record. France's Meziane Benhammou came 18th in 28:39, a European under-18 best by 14 seconds. The women had raced earlier in the morning. It was 8°C at the start, and splits of 9:06 at 3km and 15:11 at 5km put the course record of 30:07 out of reach early on. Seven women passed halfway together. Abreha, Aynadis Mebratu and Yenenesh Shimket , 19, pulled away during the next kilometre. Mebratu pressed on from 7km, but Shimket only lost contact in the last kilometre. Abreha then attacked Mebratu and made a second, decisive move with about 200m left. Mebratu finished in 30:19 and Shimket in 30:21, a world under-20 best for 10km. Abreha had limited international experience coming into the race, though she won 10,000m bronze at the African Championships earlier this year. Her one previous road 10km was 31:32 in difficult conditions in Bengaluru, India, in April. Behind the Ethiopian trio, Samia Hassan Nour set a Djibouti record of 30:37 in fourth. South Africa's Tayla Kavanagh was fifth in a national record of 30:50, having been 18 seconds behind the leaders at halfway.
- [Influencer Abeeeer apologises after riding a bicycle near 38km of the Berlin Marathon](https://filmmyrun.com/news/influencer-abeeeer-apologises-after-riding-a-bicycle-near-38km-of-the): News Influencer Abeeeer apologises after riding a bicycle near 38km of the Berlin Marathon Influencer Abeeeer apologises after riding a bicycle near 38km of the Berlin Marathon 6 October 2026 Photo: Yahoo News UK A Chinese fitness influencer has apologised after she was photographed sitting on the back of a bicycle near 38km of the Berlin Marathon on 27 September. Abeeeer, who has around 530,000 followers across social media, finished in 4:53:46 and then posted that she had run a personal best. Her splits did not sit easily with that claim. She covered 35km to 40km in 30:49, her quickest 5km of the day. The previous section, from 30km to 35km, had taken her 36:51. The faster stretch matched the part of the course where she was pictured on the bike. The photograph spread widely online and was picked up by an Instagram account, the Official Marathon Time Integrity Unit, which checks race times posted by influencers. Abeeeer first said she had felt ill, vomited and fallen at around 38km. She said she got on a friend's bicycle to find a race official and pull out. On hearing that only about 4km remained and a personal best was still possible, she said, she went back to where she had got on the bike and carried on. She maintained that she had not missed any of the course. On 3 October she changed her account. She admitted that riding the bicycle broke the race rules and said she offered no excuses. She also admitted hiding the ride from her followers, calling that "extremely dishonest". Feeling unwell, she said, was no reason to break the rules. Her marathon posts have since been taken down from her RedNote account. Brooks China, which knew her training plans for Berlin and had supplied her race kit, ended the partnership on 4 October and ruled out any future collaboration with her. The company said it had checked her finishing result and the pictures and videos she sent, but had not looked closely at her whole race, including the segment data. It apologised to runners and customers. No sanction from the race organisers had been announced as of that Sunday. Berlin drew an entry of over 56,000 this year, with runners coming from 162 countries. Most of them covered all 42.2km on foot. A finishing time is only worth anything if the runner has run every step of the course to earn it. Originally reported in Yahoo News UK , LADbible ,
- [Joseph Vis and Nicola Reece win the 16th Kielder Marathon in Northumberland](https://filmmyrun.com/news/joseph-vis-and-nicola-reece-win-the-16th-kielder-marathon-in-northumbe): News Joseph Vis and Nicola Reece win the 16th Kielder Marathon in Northumberland Joseph Vis and Nicola Reece win the 16th Kielder Marathon in Northumberland 7 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Joseph Vis and Nicola Reece won the Kielder Marathon in Northumberland on Sunday 4 October. Vis, of Kent, crossed the line first in 2:52:53. Reece, of Wilmslow and racing in the W40 category, won the women's race in 3:08:38. The organisers' own figures put the pair a few seconds quicker, at 2:52:52 and 3:08:35. This was the 16th edition of the race. It is organised by Events of the North and loops around Kielder Water, described as northern Europe's largest man-made lake. The 26.2-mile route mixes lakeside paths with forest tracks through Kielder Forest, England's largest woodland. The course is hard enough that winning times are only measured against earlier years at Kielder. Both half-marathon winners ran for Heaton. Jacob Garthwaite took the 13.1-mile race in 74:24. Charlotte Redhead , also a W40, was the first woman home in 88:37. The organisers recorded slightly different times for them, 1:14:23 and 1:28:34. The weather on the day was mixed. There was sunshine for much of it, with occasional showers and some strong gusts. Race figurehead Steve Cram still judged conditions to be "really good" for the marathon and half-marathon fields. Junior races were also held around the reservoir. Thousands of people took part over the weekend. One of them was North East Mayor Kim McGuinness. Ten runners have now completed every Kielder Marathon since the first one, among them David Ailano, Susan Wilson and Martin Randall. Originally reported in Athletics Weekly , northumberland.gov.uk Back to News
- [Josh Kerr, Sabastian Sawe and Tigst Assefa among 20 nominees for World Athlete of the Year](https://filmmyrun.com/news/josh-kerr-sabastian-sawe-and-tigst-assefa-among-20-nominees-for-world): News Josh Kerr, Sabastian Sawe and Tigst Assefa among 20 nominees for World Athlete of the Year Josh Kerr, Sabastian Sawe and Tigst Assefa among 20 nominees for World Athlete of the Year 7 October 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Josh Kerr is among the 20 nominees for the 2026 World Athlete of the Year awards, announced on 6 October. The Scot is one of ten men on the list. He broke the mile world record at the London Diamond League on 18 July, running 3:42.66. That took 0.47 seconds off Hicham El Guerrouj 's 3:43.13, which had stood since 1999. Kerr passed 1500m in 3:27.62, a British record and the fastest 1500m of the year. He also won the Ultimate Championship 1500m, the world indoor 3000m and the Commonwealth Games mile in Glasgow. Sabastian Sawe of Kenya is on the men's list too. He won the London Marathon on 26 April in 1:59:30. No man had broken two hours in a record-eligible marathon before. Ethiopia's Tigst Assefa is among the ten women. In April she won London in 2:15:41, a world record for a women-only race. On 27 September she won Berlin in 2:11:04, the third fastest time by a woman, and finished with her right Achilles tendon ruptured. She had surgery in Munich the next day and is expected to be out for about seven months. Agnes Ngetich of Kenya completes the distance running contingent. Her 1:05:15 at the world half marathon championships was a women-only world record and left the rest of the field 50 seconds behind. She was also 42 seconds clear when she became world cross country champion. Several other world record holders are nominated. They include Masai Russell (100m hurdles, 12.09), María Pérez (half marathon race walk, 1:30:06), Alison dos Santos (400m hurdles, 45.80), Ja'Kobe Tharp (110m hurdles, 12.75) and Mondo Duplantis (pole vault, 6.31m). Duplantis won the men's award in 2025. The rest of the women's list is Chase Jackson, Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, Marileidy Paulino, Camryn Rogers, Audrey Werro and Yan Ziyi . The men's list also has Kenneth Bednarek, Kristjan Čeh, Andy Díaz Hernández, Collen Kebinatshipi and Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage. Some notable names are missing. Keely Hodgkinson ran 1:54.87 indoors at Liévin in February, a world record for the short-track 800m. In June she set a British record in Stockholm but was beaten there by Werro. Jacob Kiplimo, the world cross country champion, is also absent. So is Yomif Kejelcha, who ran 1:59:41 behind Sawe in London on his marathon debut. Kejelcha also holds the half marathon world record of 56:51, set in Buenos Aires. An eight-strong panel of statisticians chose the nominees. The governing body supplied two of them, and each of the six continental bodies put forward one more. A four-way vote now ranks the athletes from first to 10th. Fans, athletes, accredited media and the World Athletics family each provide 25 per cent of the result. Voting closes at midnight CEST on Saturday 17 October. Three women and three men will be named as finalists on 10 and 11 November. The winners will be announced on stage in Monaco on 29 November, alongside the Rising Star, Coach of the Year and President's awards and a new Moment of the Year award.
- [Danielle MacGill wins The District Backyard Ultra in Cumbria with 33 yards](https://filmmyrun.com/news/danielle-macgill-wins-the-district-backyard-ultra-in-cumbria-with-33-y): News Danielle MacGill wins The District Backyard Ultra in Cumbria with 33 yards Danielle MacGill wins The District Backyard Ultra in Cumbria with 33 yards 7 October 2026 Danielle MacGill ran 33 yards to take victory at The District Backyard Ultra. She was the only runner left from a field of 84. Darren, the other runner still going after yard 30, stopped after 32 yards and took the assist. The race got under way on Saturday 3 October at Into the Woods, Cumbria. Each yard measured 6.706km (4.167 miles), with a new loop starting on the hour. Anyone who failed to get round before the next start was out. Heart & Soul Racing, the organiser, put MacGill's total at 221.1km and Darren's at 214.4km. Under the format there is only one winner, and she had to run the 33rd yard on her own to claim it. Darren's 32 yards gave her the chance to do so. The organiser describes the loop as undulating trail with plenty of runnable ground. Blencathra and the Lake District fells lie to the west and the Pennines to the east. The route was planned to give runners a view of the mountains while sparing them the big climbs found in many Lake District races. The event was self-supported. A single aid station offered water and basic supplies. Each runner had a 3m by 3m pitch for a base and was asked to bring shelter, lights, warm clothing and kit for charging devices. In April MacGill took the assist at Heart & Soul Racing's LSD BYU with 29 yards. Her result at The District added four yards to that. The organiser said 33 yards was a personal best for her and the highest backyard total recorded at any of its events. Originally reported in Run Ultra Back to News More Stories
- [Caroline Pomerleau wins Quebec City Marathon in course record on postpartum return](https://filmmyrun.com/news/caroline-pomerleau-wins-quebec-city-marathon-in-course-record-on-postp): News Caroline Pomerleau wins Quebec City Marathon in course record on postpartum return Caroline Pomerleau wins Quebec City Marathon in course record on postpartum return 7 October 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Caroline Pomerleau won the women's race at the Beneva Quebec City Marathon on Sunday 4 October in 2:42:48. That is the fastest women's time on the current course, which has been used since 2022. It was her first marathon since becoming a mother and only the second of her career. She finished at Place Jean-Béliveau with her daughter, Charlène, in her arms. The Quebec City runner won by more than eight minutes. Véronique Leboeuf was second in 2:51:25 and Amélie Simard third in 2:52:56. The previous best on this course was 2:51:58, set by Rosalie Ménard last year. The race also doubled as the Quebec road championship over the marathon distance, so the win made Pomerleau the Quebec women's marathon champion. Pomerleau won the Canadian marathon title at the 2023 Toronto Waterfront Marathon in 2:34:44. The same season brought third place at the Canadian 10K Championships. An IT-band injury followed. She then took time out so that she and Anouka Tremblay, who is both her wife and her coach, could have a baby. She still won the 5K at the 2024 Quebec City Marathon at 20 weeks pregnant, and their daughter was born in February 2025. Afterwards she described finishing with her daughter as "simply incredible". She said she hoped to show other mothers that sporting ambitions need not end with parenthood. She called Sunday "only the beginning" of her comeback, now with a 20-month-old at home. The men's record fell too. Jonathan Tedeschi, from Quebec, won in 2:21:36 to take the Quebec men's title. That beat the event record of 2:23:05, set by Kenya's Joseph Maina in 2001. Guillaume Ruel was second in 2:22:28, also inside the old mark. The 27th edition was sold out, with more than 20,000 runners and walkers across five races over the weekend in ideal weather. The races ranged from a 2km children's run to the marathon. Organisers relied on about 2,000 volunteers. Originally reported in Canadian Running , Je Cours Qc , ,
- [Adam Hickey wins Essex League opener at Hylands Park by 88 seconds](https://filmmyrun.com/news/adam-hickey-wins-essex-league-opener-at-hylands-park-by-88-seconds): News Adam Hickey wins Essex League opener at Hylands Park by 88 seconds Adam Hickey wins Essex League opener at Hylands Park by 88 seconds 13 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Adam Hickey opened the Essex League cross-country season with a clear win at Hylands Park in Chelmsford on Sunday 11 October. Havering took the men's first division team match on 74 points, ahead of Southend on 128 and Colchester Harriers on 160. Hickey has finished as the league's top man many times before. - [Doncaster City 10K full with eight weeks still to go](https://filmmyrun.com/news/doncaster-city-10k-full-with-eight-weeks-still-to-go): News Doncaster City 10K full with eight weeks still to go Doncaster City 10K full with eight weeks still to go 8 October 2026 Photo: RunABC North There are no places left for the Doncaster City 10K. The race was declared full on 3 October with all 3,500 entries taken. That was eight weeks before the field gathers at Doncaster Racecourse on Sunday 29 November. Demand has outstripped supply before. The 2025 edition also reached its 3,500 limit months ahead of race day, and more than 800 people were left on the waiting list. Organisers brought forward the opening of 2026 entries so those who missed out had another chance. Every place has gone again. This year's race is the ninth since the first edition in 2017. It is run on roads. Runners leave the racecourse, head out through the city and come back to finish in front of the grandstand. The 2026 medal has a racing theme. It commemorates the 250th running of the St Leger Stakes, recently staged at the course and billed as the world's oldest Classic. The 2025 race was decided by a narrow margin. Daniel James won in 31:25, just three seconds clear of Adam Theaker. Georgina Weston was the leading woman in 36:30. Organisers say the event has reached its limit. They will look at whether the course could be changed to take more runners in future. They will only do so if the event does not suffer as a result. - [Saskatchewan 800m runner Avery Pearson signs professional deal with On Athletics Club](https://filmmyrun.com/news/saskatchewan-800m-runner-avery-pearson-signs-professional-deal-with-on): News Saskatchewan 800m runner Avery Pearson signs professional deal with On Athletics Club Saskatchewan 800m runner Avery Pearson signs professional deal with On Athletics Club 8 October 2026 Photo: Asa Fletcher / Canadian Running Avery Pearson , a 23-year-old 800m runner from Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan, has signed a professional contract with the On Athletics Club. The deal was announced on Tuesday 6 October. She joins the club's Global Team and is the first Canadian athlete on its squad in Boulder, Colorado. She will race as a professional from 2027. Pearson spent four years with the University of Saskatchewan Huskies. There she was named U Sports Female Rookie of the Year and won several U Sports medals and Canada West titles. She also reached the 800m final at the World U20 Championships for Canada. For her final year of eligibility she moved to the University of Colorado, where she was coached by Sean Carlson. She earned All-American status there and won the 2026 Big 12 indoor title over 600 yards. Her 800m best now stands at 2:00.76. A year ago it was 2:03.17, and she has gone under that old mark consistently through 2026. Breaking two minutes is her next target. On says she also hopes to represent Canada at an Olympic Games. Her start in the sport was modest. Meadow Lake had no track team, and her coaching came from her father or her high school vice-principal. She took up track during the COVID period and did not know then that running could be a career. She has called it a dream job she had no idea how to reach. She is now settling in Boulder, more than 1,600 metres above sea level. The club is coached by Dathan Ritzenhein, a three-time US Olympian. Its athletes include Yared Nuguse of the United States, who won 1500m bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics, and Kenya's Hellen Obiri, a two-time world champion. OAC team manager Andrew Wheating praised Pearson's potential and determination. Pearson said the group's people, its culture and its focus on learning drew her in. For her first professional season she wants to stay "humble" and learn as much as she can from her coaches and teammates. Originally reported in Canadian Running , On ,
- [Hustle at Pinehurst revives Run for the Toad with course records at every distance](https://filmmyrun.com/news/hustle-at-pinehurst-revives-run-for-the-toad-with-course-records-at-ev): News Hustle at Pinehurst revives Run for the Toad with course records at every distance Hustle at Pinehurst revives Run for the Toad with course records at every distance 10 October 2026 Photo: Canadian Running The Run for the Toad has come back under a new name. The first Hustle at Pinehurst was held on Sunday at the Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area near Cambridge, Ontario. Nearly 400 runners raced distances from 12.5K to 50K. As it was the first edition, every winner set a course record. George and Peggy Sarson founded the original race and ran it for 19 years before stepping back in 2019 with retirement in mind. At its height it drew more than 1,000 runners. Straw Dog Racing, which organises Sulphur Springs, has kept the old menu of 12.5K, 25K, 50K and a 50K relay. Co-race directors Stephen Connor and Mauro Campanelli spent two years on the revival, with New Balance as partner. Connor said the team had felt an "overwhelming responsibility" to do justice to the old event. The course is built on loops, and each 12.5K lap packs in more than 250 metres of climb over rolling, cross-country style ground. Karl Olivo, who lives in Cambridge, won the 12.5K by almost three minutes in 46:37. Bryce Neary of Puslinch was second in 49:33. Mitch Free of St. George took third in 50:56 after a sprint finish. Karlie Janes of Guelph was the first woman home in 52:18. Aya Tomioka of Toronto won the non-binary division in 1:18:07. Jacob Zerko of Kitchener had the 25K to himself, finishing in 1:42:26. Michal Kapral of Port Hope came next in 1:55:02, with Juan Aja Aguinaco of Burlington third in 1:56:24. Adrienne Hol of Ancaster won the women's race in 2:09:17. Erika Howarth of Woodstock took the non-binary division in 2:39:25. Robert Brouillette won the 50K in 3:34:36, well clear of Burlington's Kyle McCandless in 4:17:16 and Toronto's Mark Carey in 4:33:30. Lauren Maher of Brantford won the women's race in 5:30:36. Behind her, Hamilton's Nicki Tober held off Patricia Halligan of Niagara Falls by seven seconds, 5:32:08 to 5:32:15. The Weekend Warriors won the 50K relay in 4:02:29. The organisers say they already have ideas for the 2027 edition. Originally reported in Canadian Running ,
- [Alkerton and Sintayehu take weekly Under Armour honours after cross-country wins](https://filmmyrun.com/news/alkerton-and-sintayehu-take-weekly-under-armour-honours-after-cross-co): News Alkerton and Sintayehu take weekly Under Armour honours after cross-country wins Alkerton and Sintayehu take weekly Under Armour honours after cross-country wins 10 October 2026 Photo: digitalmediawindsor / Canadian Running The latest Under Armour Athletes of the Week are Alyshia Alkerton, who runs for Windsor, and Lalem Sintayehu, who races for St. Francis Xavier. The weekly award picks one woman and one man from the U Sports cross-country season. It runs until the U Sports Cross Country Championships in Hamilton on 14 November, and each winner receives a pair of shoes from the Under Armour Velociti range. On Friday 2 October Alkerton took the 5K at the Joe Piane Notre Dame Invitational in 17:04. The Indiana race was an NCAA meet, and she beat the American field. Her Windsor teammate Samara Quanz was second in 17:12. That made it two races in a row with a one-two for the pair, and their efforts helped Windsor to third in the team standings. It was also Alkerton's second straight win of the season. Her strong start follows a year on the sidelines. Alkerton graduated from Queen's in 2024 and moved to Windsor for teacher's college. OUA rules counted that as a transfer, so she could not race officially for the Lancers in 2025. Windsor host the OUA championships this year. Alkerton said the plan was for the squad to race as a group and reel in rivals one by one. Sintayehu, from Addis Ababa in Ethiopia, is in his first year of U Sports eligibility. He opened with an 8K win at the UPEI Invitational on 19 September in 24:56, with St. Francis Xavier third as a team. On Saturday 3 October he won again at the Acadia Invitational, on a much tougher course, in 25:43. Aidan Douglas of the Memorial Sea-Hawks was second in 26:36, and the X-Men finished second. This is Sintayehu's first season of cross-country. The second-year science student only began running competitively late in high school and was mainly a 1,500m runner on the track. He has had to adjust to the team's high mileage. A teacher from home who had studied at St. Francis Xavier persuaded him to enrol. He has said he hopes to win both the AUS and U Sports titles.
