He cited knee bursitis and tight muscles, and called it among the "most painful experiences" of his life. Brandon Lee Gretch, 32, from Melbourne, stopped after 73 laps, a personal best, having finished his last loop with 20 seconds to spare. Canada, racing in Squamish, British Columbia, finished ninth with a national best of 830 yards. Michael Serani of Kelowna led them with 82. Originally reported in ,
- [Audrey Werro and Gianmarco Tamberi named European Athletes of the Year in Lausanne](https://filmmyrun.com/news/audrey-werro-and-gianmarco-tamberi-named-european-athletes-of-the-year): News Audrey Werro and Gianmarco Tamberi named European Athletes of the Year in Lausanne Audrey Werro and Gianmarco Tamberi named European Athletes of the Year in Lausanne 25 October 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Switzerland's Audrey Werro and Italy's Gianmarco Tamberi have been voted the 2026 European Athletes of the Year. The awards were presented at the Golden Tracks ceremony in Lausanne on Saturday 24 October. Britain's Amy Hunt was one of the two beaten women's finalists. She won gold in the 100m, 200m, 4x100m and mixed 4x100m at this summer's European Championships in Birmingham. She became only the third woman to go under 1:54 and ran three of the five fastest times in history. Her best of 1:53.70 left her 0.42 seconds outside Jarmila Kratochvílová's world record. In Birmingham she won her first senior European title, with Keely Hodgkinson second and Femke Broeders-Bol third. - [Pema Choki and Jamphel Choda win the 2026 Snowman Race in Bhutan](https://filmmyrun.com/news/pema-choki-and-jamphel-choda-win-the-2026-snowman-race-in-bhutan): News Pema Choki and Jamphel Choda win the 2026 Snowman Race in Bhutan Pema Choki and Jamphel Choda win the 2026 Snowman Race in Bhutan 29 October 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Pema Choki and Jamphel Choda have won the 2026 Snowman Race, a five-day stage race of 185 km across the Bhutanese Himalaya. - [Hyrox joins triathlon's governing body in bid for Olympic place](https://filmmyrun.com/news/hyrox-joins-world-triathlon-in-bid-for-olympic-place): News Hyrox joins triathlon's governing body in bid for Olympic place Hyrox joins triathlon's governing body in bid for Olympic place 29 October 2026 Photo: Hyrox Ottawa / Canadian Running Hyrox has signed a partnership that makes hybrid racing a recognised discipline of triathlon's global governing body. Hybrid racing will run in three formats. Ultimate mirrors the existing Hyrox race. Fast is shorter and more intense, and Ultra is a longer endurance version. Hyrox becomes the exclusive operator of the elite World, Continental and National Championships in the Ultimate format. Triathlon's world body has more than 177 member federations. Organisers named the fields on 27 October. The road mile runs along Kalakaua Avenue beside Waikiki Beach, the day before the 53rd JAL Honolulu Marathon. Eight Olympians from six nations will line up. Strand heads the men's list. The 24-year-old American won the 2025 USATF 1500m title and set a mile best of 3:46.97 at the Prefontaine Classic in July. He has never raced the Merrie Mile, though he used Oahu as a training base before the 2025 World Athletics Championships. He is one of six men in the field with a sub-3:50 mile. He described the race as a chance to "get my season rolling". Hoare, the Australian who took Commonwealth 1500m gold in 2022, brings a mile best of 3:47.48. Young, the 2025 USATF 10,000m champion, is also entered. So is Vince Ciattei, the US 5000m champion, who has just placed eighth over the mile when the world road championships were staged in Copenhagen. Ciattei has run the Merrie Mile three times and was second in 2023. Ky Robinson, a double Commonwealth medallist in 2026, and Canadian 1500m champion Foster Malleck complete a strong line-up. The women's field is led by Dorcus Ewoi of Kenya, silver medallist over 1500m at the 2025 World Championships. She has a mile best of 4:17.62 and will be visiting Hawaii for the first time. Addy Wiley, the US road mile champion and 2026 world indoor 800m bronze medallist, is her likeliest rival. Abbey Caldwell, Nozomi Tanaka, Susan Ejore-Sanders and Josette Andrews are also entered. The race uses a chase format. The women set off first with a fixed head start, which was 31 seconds last year, and prize money follows the combined finishing order. The winner takes $15,000, the biggest first prize of any road mile this year, from $39,000 in guaranteed money. A $5,000 bonus goes to the best finisher of the opposite sex to the winner. The course is certified and record-eligible. Its records stand at 3:53.3 for men, set by Edward Cheserek in 2019, and 4:21.66 for women, set by Sinclair Johnson in 2025. Originally reported in ,
- [Heather Jackson beats Carla Molinaro by 55 seconds as Rob Molke wins Javelina 100 Mile](https://filmmyrun.com/news/heather-jackson-beats-carla-molinaro-by-55-seconds-as-rob-molke-wins-j): News Heather Jackson beats Carla Molinaro by 55 seconds as Rob Molke wins Javelina 100 Mile Heather Jackson beats Carla Molinaro by 55 seconds as Rob Molke wins Javelina 100 Mile 1 November 2026 Photo: ultramarathondatabase.com Rob Molke and Heather Jackson won the Javelina 100 Mile on 31 October, and Britain's Carla Molinaro came within a minute of the women's title. Jackson finished in 13:48:29 for her second win at the Arizona race. Molinaro, the 50km world champion, crossed the line in 13:49:24. Molke won the men's race in 12:11:30. That was 78 seconds outside the course record of 12:10:12 set by Will Murray in 2025. The race is held in McDowell Mountain Regional Park, near Fountain Hills, about an hour northeast of Phoenix. It runs over five loops, a first of 22.3 miles and then four of 19.45 miles, with 1,919m of climb in total. Heavy rain the night before the 6am start left mud and minor washouts on the trails. The day stayed overcast, with a high of 24C and humidity of at least 72%. Showers returned in the closing hours of the elite race. Cade Michael set the early pace in the men's race but stopped at Coyote Camp, 45.3 miles in. Noah Dusseau took over and still led by just under five minutes at mile 83.7. Molke, who did not finish last year, was third at that point. Dusseau was 58 seconds ahead at Jackass Junction, mile 90.2. Molke passed him soon after and led by 29 seconds at mile 95.3, then finished 1min 27sec clear. Dusseau's 12:12:57 is the third-fastest time recorded on the course. Can-Hua Luo was third in 12:19:39, ahead of Jacob Banta in 12:23:30 and Rajpaul Pannu in 12:26:47. Des Linden, the two-time Olympic marathoner and 2018 Boston Marathon winner, led the women by mile 41.1 and was still in front at mile 60.3. The next 4.3 miles took her 1hr 22min 37sec, and Molinaro went into the lead. Jackson was 8min 15sec behind the British runner at mile 71 and still 3min 21sec down at Rattlesnake Ranch, mile 95.3. She passed Molinaro late, in the dark and the rain, and was 42 seconds up at mile 99.7. Katie Asmuth , last year's 100K winner, was third in 14:06:34. Valérie Arsenault was fourth in 14:09:24 and Devon Yanko fifth in 14:12:55. Javelina is the second of seven Golden Ticket races for the 2027 Western States 100, with places for the top two men and the top two women. Molke, Dusseau, Jackson and Molinaro all finished in those positions. Molke reached Western States in 2025 with a single lottery ticket and finished 16th. Jackson, a former professional triathlete, first won Javelina in 2023 in 14:24:47. Her time this year was 16min 42sec slower than the women's record of 13:31:47, set by Tara Dower last year.
- [Habtom Samuel and Rachael Rudel win Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K in New York](https://filmmyrun.com/news/habtom-samuel-and-rachael-rudel-win-abbott-dash-to-the-finish-line-5k): News Habtom Samuel and Rachael Rudel win Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K in New York Habtom Samuel and Rachael Rudel win Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K in New York 1 November 2026 Photo: LetsRun Eritrea's Habtom Samuel and Rachael Rudel of the United States won the elite races at the Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K in New York on Saturday 31 October. Samuel ran 13:31. Rudel ran 15:35, a personal best. It was the first New York Road Runners race for both of them. Samuel is in his first season as a professional and has yet to lose. The five-time NCAA champion arrived with wins and course records at the Falmouth Road Race and the Houston Half Marathon. He did most of the leading, with a tight group behind him. Around the 10-minute mark he broke away and won by seven seconds. Edwin Kurgat of Kenya, an Olympian in 2024, was second in 13:38. Amon Kemboi, last year's winner, was third in 13:40. Samuel had his eye on the course record, but wind in midtown Manhattan got in the way. He said he had planned to run "13:10". When pushing harder proved tough, he changed his approach and settled for the win. Kemboi, who was born in Kenya, appeared under the United States flag on the livestream and the official timing page. Rudel won the USATF 20K title recently and took the Bolder Boulder 10K in the summer. She pulled clear in the final 400 metres to win by six seconds. Americans filled the podium. Rudel ends a run of three straight wins in the race by Annie Rodenfels. She said she had come in with "no expectations". More than 11,500 runners took part in the 3.1-mile race, which is held on the Saturday of New York City Marathon weekend. The course started on the East Side near the United Nations. It ran along 42nd Street past Grand Central Terminal and up Sixth Avenue past Radio City Music Hall. After the rolling hills of Central Park, it finished on the marathon finish line, the day before nearly 60,000 runners were due to cross it. Originally reported in LetsRun , ,
- [Andreas Almgren wins New York City Marathon in 2:06:01 on his debut](https://filmmyrun.com/news/andreas-almgren-wins-new-york-city-marathon-in-2-06-01-on-his-debut): News Andreas Almgren wins New York City Marathon in 2:06:01 on his debut Andreas Almgren wins New York City Marathon in 2:06:01 on his debut 2 November 2026 Photo: LetsRun Andreas Almgren won the TCS New York City Marathon on Sunday 1 November in 2:06:01. It was the first time the 31-year-old Swede had run 26.2 miles, in a race or in training. He finished 13 seconds ahead of Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa. Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race in 2:24:36. Patrick Dever was the leading British man, 17th in 2:09:53, and Phily Bowden was 17th among the women in 2:30:45. The men ran as a large group for most of the race, with 15 still together at 35km. Benson Kipruto, the defending champion, broke it up with a 4:38 24th mile that left only himself, Almgren and Crippa in contention. Almgren went to the front for the first time just before 40km. Crippa stayed with him for another kilometre, but a second surge along Central Park South decided it. Almgren jogged the final few metres and waved to the crowd. Crippa ran 2:06:14. Lesotho's Kamohelo Mofolo was third in a personal best of 2:06:26, one second ahead of Kipruto. Australia's Haftu Strintzos was fifth in 2:06:34. Zouhair Talbi was the first American, sixth in 2:06:43, and Conner Mantz was 11th in 2:07:27. Almgren is the first European-born man to win in New York in 30 years, since Italy's Giacomo Leone in 1996. He said he had probably "never felt so emotional" after a race. He began his career at 800m and won world under-20 bronze over the distance in 2014. In August he won the European 10,000m title in Birmingham in a championship record of 27:23.44. In September he took the world half marathon title in Copenhagen with a European record of 58:06. He picked New York for his debut because its course races like a championship, with the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles in mind. The women's race was settled in the final 150m, where Chepkirui moved away from her compatriot Hellen Obiri, a two-time winner here. It was Chepkirui's second New York title after her win in 2024, when she ran 2:24:35. Jess McClain finished fast to take second in 2:24:42. She said she had not felt good for the first 18 miles. She passed Obiri in the last strides, and Obiri was third in 2:24:43. No American woman had reached the New York podium since 2018. Behind the leading three, Edna Kiplagat took fourth with 2:25:42, four seconds ahead of Mercy Chelangat in fifth. Weini Kelati was seventh in 2:26:51 on her marathon debut. Dever's time was well outside his personal best of 2:06:18 from the London Marathon this spring. The New York course, with its bridges and climbs, rarely gives up fast times. He was upgraded to third last year after crossing the line fourth on his debut. Uruguay's Julia Paternain, who grew up in the UK and won an English Schools title as a teenager, was 12th in 2:29:09. In the women's wheelchair race, Britain's Eden Rainbow-Cooper finished fifth. Marcel Hug won a close men's wheelchair race in 1:28:14, just ahead of Daniel Romanchuk. David Weir was third and Johnboy Smith ninth. Catherine Debrunner won the women's wheelchair race by more than eight minutes in 1:40:02. Her course record in New York is 1:39:32. Tatyana McFadden was second, four seconds ahead of Susannah Scaroni. This was the 50th anniversary edition of the race, which passes through all five boroughs from Staten Island to Manhattan. The retired footballer James Milner finished in 3:09:04 after reaching halfway in 1:31.
- [Sheila Chepkirui wins second New York City Marathon as Jess McClain takes second](https://filmmyrun.com/news/sheila-chepkirui-wins-second-new-york-city-marathon-as-jess-mcclain-ta): News Sheila Chepkirui wins second New York City Marathon as Jess McClain takes second Sheila Chepkirui wins second New York City Marathon as Jess McClain takes second 2 November 2026 Photo: NBC Sports Sheila Chepkirui won the New York City Marathon for the second time in three years on Sunday 1 November, reaching the Central Park finish in 2:24:36. The American Jess McClain was six seconds behind in 2:24:42. She caught defending champion Hellen Obiri in the last few strides, and Obiri was third in 2:24:43. Britain's David Weir finished third in the men's wheelchair race in 1:35:38. Conditions were sunny and cool for the 50th year of the race's five-borough course. Eight women broke clear at around 20km. Among them were Chepkirui, Obiri, McClain and Weini Kelati, an American running her first marathon. By the approach to Central Park it had become a contest between the two Kenyans. Obiri pushed on with about a mile left. Chepkirui responded and opened the decisive gap over the final 150m. She described the last mile as "really tricky" and said she had to stay patient. Edna Kiplagat, the 2010 champion, was fourth at the age of 46. McClain's second place made her the first American woman in the top three since 2018. No US runner of either sex had reached the podium since Shalane Flanagan was third that year. She said she had not felt good for the first 18 miles but kept going, and called it a "magical day". In April she was fifth at the Boston Marathon in 2:20:49, the quickest time by an American woman on that course. It was her second year in a row as the leading American there. In September she cut her half marathon best to 1:06:53 when the global road championships came to Copenhagen. Chepkirui, 35, won on her New York debut in 2024 in 2:24:35, with Obiri behind her. She came back in 2025 and was third in 2:20:24, while Obiri won in a course record of 2:19:51. In March this year Chepkirui won the Nagoya Women's Marathon for the second year running in 2:21:54. In September she was second at the Great North Run in 1:08:19, behind Brigid Kosgei . Obiri, a two-time New York winner, had won the NYC Half earlier in the season and was second in London in a personal best of 2:15:53. Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men's race on his marathon debut in 2:06:01, 13 seconds clear of Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa. Marcel Hug took his eighth men's wheelchair title in 1:28:14, one second ahead of Daniel Romanchuk, with Weir behind them. Catherine Debrunner won the women's wheelchair race in 1:40:02, more than eight minutes ahead of Tatyana McFadden. Susannah Scaroni was third, three months after giving birth to her son. Sifan Hassan had pulled out through illness three weeks before the race.
- [Ciara Mageean, European 1500m champion from Portaferry, dies aged 34](https://filmmyrun.com/news/ciara-mageean-european-1500m-champion-from-portaferry-dies-aged-34): News Ciara Mageean, European 1500m champion from Portaferry, dies aged 34 Ciara Mageean, European 1500m champion from Portaferry, dies aged 34 2 November 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Ciara Mageean , the middle-distance runner from Portaferry in County Down, Northern Ireland, has died aged 34. Her family said in a statement on social media that she died at 6.30am on Sunday 1 November with her loved ones around her. Her bowel cancer, already at stage four, was found in May 2025. Mageean won the European 1500m title in Rome in 2024 in 4:04.66. Before her, Sonia O'Sullivan was the only Irish athlete to have taken an individual European crown. It also completed her set of European medals. She had taken 1500m bronze in 2016, silver in 2022 and a European indoor bronze in 2019. She also won Commonwealth Games silver in 2022 and was fourth in the 1500m final at the 2023 World Championships in Budapest. She ran the 1500m for Ireland at the Olympic Games in Rio in 2016 and in Tokyo. She was selected for Paris in 2024 but an Achilles injury ruled her out a day before her first heat. She held Irish records at 800m (1:58.51), 1000m (2:31.06), 1500m (3:55.87) and the mile (4:14.58). She made her illness public in July 2025. At first she had put her symptoms down to the stomach trouble many runners live with. Her partner, Thomas Moran, persuaded her to see a doctor. By Christmas 2025 she had been through 12 rounds of chemotherapy. Surgery and radiotherapy were not possible, and doctors gave her two to three years. The illness ended a career she had hoped to close at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. In July she hosted a Run with Ciara Mageean event at the Irish National Championships. She also told her story in a memoir, My Greatest Race, written with the journalist Clíona Foley. Mageean and Moran married at Belfast City Hall in October, about three weeks before her death. She leaves her husband and her parents, Catherine and Christopher. President Catherine Connolly paid tribute to her "strength and perseverance". Micheál Martin, the Taoiseach, offered his sympathy to her husband, Thomas, and to her family and friends. The Olympic Federation of Ireland's chief executive, Peter Sherrard, described her as a national hero taken too early. Athletics Ireland described her as "much-loved and inspirational". Michelle O'Neill, Northern Ireland's first minister, said the loss would be keenly felt in Portaferry, where Mageean was regarded as one of the town's own. Originally reported in Canadian Running ,
- [Tonbridge keep English cross-country relays title as Herne Hill end Belgrave's women's run](https://filmmyrun.com/news/tonbridge-keep-english-cross-country-relays-title-as-herne-hill-end-be): News Tonbridge keep English cross-country relays title as Herne Hill end Belgrave's women's run Tonbridge keep English cross-country relays title as Herne Hill end Belgrave's women's run 2 November 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Tonbridge retained the senior men's title at the English Cross-Country Relays at Berry Hill Park, Mansfield, on 31 October. Herne Hill took the women's race and ended Belgrave Harriers' sequence of three straight wins. The early mist burned off and there was no wind, which made for quick running around the Nottinghamshire park. Tonbridge covered the 4x5km in 59:07, each leg two laps of the course. Western Tempo were second in 59:51 and Cambridge & Coleridge third in 59:59. Jack Higgins ran the opening stage for the winners and was edged by Woodford Green's Ben Potrykus, who posted 14:36. Potrykus, runner-up at the Scottish Cross Country, admitted he had "hammered it" on his first go at the event. Jamie MacDonald, the slowest of the Tonbridge four in 15:12, still brought them to halfway in front. Ted Higgins then produced the quickest lap of the day, 14:32, and handed over to James Kingston. The 25-year-old former English National champion jogged the final leg in 14:44 and gave the credit to his team-mates, saying he had done "nothing". Jacob Cann lifted Western Tempo to second on the third stage and Dom James kept them there. Callum Elson ran 14:42 on the last leg to bring Cambridge & Coleridge up two places to third. The women ran 3x3km, and Herne Hill won in 28:43. Belgrave were second in 29:34 and Aldershot, Farnham & District third in 29:41. Lucy Jones handed over in third. Sophie Tooley moved them up to second despite being unwell during the week. Katie Snowden , third quickest overall, took them home. Snowden had been back only two weeks since the World Road Running Championships and called the course "brilliant underfoot". The fastest women's laps came on the opening stage. Cambridge Harriers' Holly Dixon and Derby's Molly Hudson could not be separated at the line and were both given 9:18. Neither club stayed in contention as the race went on. The meeting also staged a mixed relay for the first time, four legs of about 1.6km with two men and two women per team. Cambridge & Coleridge won it in 19:33, helped by Alex Melloy's 4:27, the fastest men's split. Originally reported in Athletics Weekly
- [Jadyn Keeler runs 15:10 in Hamilton to break 22-year-old Canadian 5K record](https://filmmyrun.com/news/jadyn-keeler-runs-15-10-in-hamilton-to-break-22-year-old-canadian-5k-r): News Jadyn Keeler runs 15:10 in Hamilton to break 22-year-old Canadian 5K record Jadyn Keeler runs 15:10 in Hamilton to break 22-year-old Canadian 5K record 2 November 2026 Photo: Jasmine Fehr / Canadian Running Jadyn Keeler set a Canadian 5K road record of 15:10 at the Mizuno Elite 5K in Hamilton, Ontario, on Saturday. The 23-year-old from Barrie took six seconds off the previous mark. Émilie Mondor ran 15:16 at the Carlsbad 5000 in California in 2004, and nobody had bettered it in 22 years. Keeler won by 13 seconds. Siona Chisholm was second in 15:23 and Simone Plourde third in 15:36. The race formed part of the Road2Hope Marathon weekend and was held on a flat, certified course beside the water at Confederation Park. Keeler's time also lowered the women's course record, which had been 15:19. The record came without much preparation for the distance. Keeler said she had been doing little 5K-specific work and was unsure of her shape over the distance. The outing was intended to "shock my system" before a new block of training and racing. It caps a strong autumn on the roads. Copenhagen hosted the World Athletics Road Running Championships in September, and Keeler wore a Canada vest at senior level for the first time. She finished 16th in the half marathon in 1:08:03. That beat Andrea Seccafien's Canadian record of 1:09:38 by more than a minute and a half. Shortly before, she had won the Canadian championships in Edmonton in 1:12:12 on her debut at the distance. A measurement error made that course roughly 675 metres longer than advertised. Keeler previously ran for the University of North Dakota. In December 2025 she clocked 15:14.76 for 5,000m indoors, a Canadian under-23 best. At the 2025 Junior Pan American Games she won gold over 10,000m and silver over 5,000m. Her race-morning routine is sourdough bread with maple syrup. She always has some form of carbohydrate with syrup before a race. Next up is a road 10K at the Rockin' Rib Run in Miramar, Florida, on 15 November, where she plans to chase a quick time. Originally reported in Canadian Running Back to News

- [Cassandra de Winter beats every man to win Javelina Jundred 100K in record time](https://filmmyrun.com/news/cassandra-de-winter-beats-every-man-to-win-javelina-jundred-100k-in-re): News Cassandra de Winter beats every man to win Javelina Jundred 100K in record time Cassandra de Winter beats every man to win Javelina Jundred 100K in record time 3 November 2026 Photo: @emmanuel.runes / Canadian Running Cassandra de Winter , from Lethbridge in Alberta, won the Javelina Jundred 100K outright in Arizona on Saturday 31 October. She crossed the line in 7:44:45, ahead of every man in the field. Anna Louden had held the women's best on the course since 2023 with 8:13:07. De Winter beat it by more than 28 minutes. Only two faster times have ever been run on the course, men included. The race is held at McDowell Mountain Regional Park, northeast of Phoenix, and the 100K set off at 7am. Runners cover loops of mostly runnable desert trail with about 1,206m of climb. Rain on the Friday had left mud and minor washouts, and Saturday stayed humid. In the 100-mile race on the same course, Britain's Carla Molinaro was second woman in 13:49:24. The American Heather Jackson passed her late on and won by 55 seconds in 13:48:29. Second place still earns Molinaro a Golden Ticket for the 2027 Western States 100. De Winter expected a quick start and chose not to follow it. She kept an eye on her effort and heart rate and let the leaders go, planning to claw back time later. At mile 45 James Cecil was about five minutes up on her. She caught him on the final lap. Juan Rocha of the US was first man and second overall in 7:50:28. Cecil was next in 7:51:59, with Addison Porcelli third man in 8:25:02. Behind De Winter in the women's race, Brittany Charboneau was second in 8:26:09 and Steph McCall third in 8:50:43. De Winter is a mother of three who runs her own business. She only began racing competitively in 2025. Her husband and mother made the trip to Arizona to crew for her. This season has gone well for her in Canada too. In July she won the Sinister 7 Ultra 50K. In September she won the Lost Soul Ultra 50K in Lethbridge outright. Both runs were women's course records, and she said they persuaded her to try one more big race before winter. Julie Hamulecki has held the fastest 100K on the road by a Canadian woman since 2022, at 7:36:39. De Winter's Javelina time was only eight minutes slower. She said she had not realised she was so close. Now that she knows, she would like to "take a crack at it". Originally reported in Canadian Running ,
- [Jennifer MacDonell sets Canadian W70-74 half marathon record at Road2Hope](https://filmmyrun.com/news/jennifer-macdonell-sets-canadian-w70-74-half-marathon-record-at-road2h): News Jennifer MacDonell sets Canadian W70-74 half marathon record at Road2Hope Jennifer MacDonell sets Canadian W70-74 half marathon record at Road2Hope 3 November 2026 Photo: courtesy Jennifer MacDonell / Canadian Running Jennifer MacDonell has added a Canadian W70-74 half marathon record to an extraordinary autumn. The 70-year-old from Ottawa ran 1:39:42 at the Hamilton Marathon Road2Hope on Sunday 1 November. That took 4 minutes 49 seconds off the old mark. Roslyn Smith of British Columbia had set it at 1:44:31 in March 2023, on the Comox Valley RV Half Marathon course. The new time still awaits confirmation as the national record. MacDonell averaged 4:44 per kilometre. She won her age group, which had seven women in it. She was 43rd of 684 women and 172nd of 1,333 finishers overall. She admitted she had started with legs only "60 per cent" recovered. She called it a big gamble, but said the flat course and perfect weather had helped. It was her fourth age-group record in a month. On 9 October she set a Canadian mile record of 6:51 at the Beneva Marathon de Montréal. A day later she ran a Canadian 5K record of 21:40. Two weeks before Hamilton she finished the TCS Toronto Waterfront Marathon in 3:23:59. That was a W70-74 world record, and it beat the previous best of 3:27:00. She crossed the line in Toronto cramping badly and close to empty. Afterwards she described feeling "absolute elation" at having believed in a single goal and trained hard enough to reach it. The Hamilton time was not her fastest on the course. Last year, aged 69, she ran the same half marathon in 1:36:03. This time she was racing in a new age category. MacDonell puts much of her success down to Steve Boyd, who coaches her, and Norman Marcotte, her husband, who logs her results and urges her on. Her earlier age-group marks include performances at 15K and 10 miles. Originally reported in Canadian Running , irunmagazine.com , iRun Magazine
- [Josh Kerr's mile world record shortlisted for World Athletics moment of the year](https://filmmyrun.com/news/josh-kerr-s-mile-world-record-shortlisted-for-world-athletics-moment-o): News Josh Kerr's mile world record shortlisted for World Athletics moment of the year Josh Kerr's mile world record shortlisted for World Athletics moment of the year 4 November 2026 Photo: BBC Sport Josh Kerr 's mile world record is one of three finalists for Moment of the Year at the World Athletics Awards. The governing body named its shortlist on Tuesday 3 November. The winner will be announced at the ceremony in Monaco on 29 November. The Scot, 29, from Edinburgh, ran 3:42.66 at the London Diamond League on 18 July. That took 0.47 seconds off the 3:43.13 set by Morocco's Hicham El Guerrouj in Rome in 1999. No men's mile record had lasted longer. Kerr went through 1500m in 3:27.62 on the way, a British record in its own right. The home crowd at the London Stadium was behind him from start to finish. The second British race on the list is the London Marathon. Kenya's Sabastian Sawe , 31, won there on 26 April in 1:59:30. Nobody had gone under two hours in a record-eligible marathon before. He took 65 seconds off the late Kelvin Kiptum's record of 2:00:35 from 2023. Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha also broke two hours, running 1:59:41 in second place on his marathon debut. Jacob Kiplimo was third and also finished inside the old record. The third finalist is Botswana's men's 4x400m relay team. They won at the World Athletics Relays in Gaborone in May, in front of a home crowd, with a championship record of 2:53.47. World Athletics introduced the award last month. It is meant to recognise the most memorable occasion of the season, which need not be a single performance, and the reaction it drew from fans. Other prizes on the night in Monaco include awards for the best male and female athletes of the season, the most promising young talent and the top coach, along with the President's Award. Originally reported in BBC Sport , A Mile. A Minute. , BBC Sport
- [Alabama sweeps SEC cross-country team titles as Kiplagat and Cheruiyot take individual wins](https://filmmyrun.com/news/alabama-sweeps-sec-cross-country-team-titles-as-kiplagat-and-cheruiyot): News Alabama sweeps SEC cross-country team titles as Kiplagat and Cheruiyot take individual wins Alabama sweeps SEC cross-country team titles as Kiplagat and Cheruiyot take individual wins 4 November 2026 Photo: World-Track and Field The Southeastern Conference cross-country championships on Friday 30 October ended with Alabama winning both team competitions. The races were held at the Gans Creek Cross Country Course in Columbia, Missouri, with the home university, Missouri, acting as host. Caren Kiplagat won the women's 6km race. Florida's Kelvin Cheruiyot won the men's 8km race for the second year running. Kiplagat finished in 18:46. Isca Chelangat of Arkansas was a single second behind in 18:47. Salma Elbadra of South Carolina finished third in 18:58. Alabama, ranked ninth, won the women's team title with 48 points. It was their fifth SEC women's crown and their second in three years. Four Alabama runners finished in the top 11. Cynthia Jemutai was eighth in 19:08.1, Brenda Tuwei 10th in 19:11.6 and Mildred Rono 11th in 19:13.4. Milicent Wafula was the fifth Alabama scorer in 18th place in 19:32.4. Florida were the defending women's champions and ranked fourth. They finished second on 80 points, with Judy Chepkoech fourth and Claire Stegall sixth. South Carolina were third on 110 points. Missouri scored 138 for fourth place and Arkansas took fifth with 161. In the men's race Cheruiyot finished in 22:03. Dismus Lokira of Alabama was six seconds back in 22:09. Rodgers Minatum, a first-year runner at Alabama, was third in 22:11. His teammate Dennis Kipruto was fourth in 22:16. Duncan Gituku in 13th and Bismack Kipchirchir in 15th completed Alabama's five scorers, so the whole scoring team finished inside the top 15. The Alabama men are ranked fourth and won with 37 points. It was their second conference title in a row and their sixth in total. Arkansas were second with 76 points, led by Nick Busienei in fifth and Ernest Cheruiyot in seventh. Florida were third on 82. Missouri took fourth with 145, three points ahead of Tennessee on 148. Both Alabama teams have now won three conference titles since 2022. The SEC teams race next at the NCAA regional championships on 13 November. Originally reported in LetsRun , World-Track and Field
- [McMaster men and Victoria women top U Sports cross-country rankings after regional championships](https://filmmyrun.com/news/mcmaster-men-and-victoria-women-top-u-sports-cross-country-rankings-af): News McMaster men and Victoria women top U Sports cross-country rankings after regional championships McMaster men and Victoria women top U Sports cross-country rankings after regional championships 5 November 2026 Photo: @dlr.shoots / Canadian Running The four U Sports regional cross-country championships were decided over the weekend. In the final national rankings, released on Monday, 13 of the top 20 teams changed places. The McMaster Marauders men and the University of Victoria Vikes women go into the national championships seeded first. McMaster hosts the nationals at Christie Lake Conservation Area in Dundas, Ontario, on 14 November. McMaster won both team titles at the Ontario championships, hosted by the University of Windsor. The men scored 30 points to Guelph's 68, with Western third on 81. Five McMaster men finished in the top 10. Guelph's Jack Lehto won the individual race in 23:56.2 to complete an unbeaten season. Samuel Patrick of McMaster was second in 24:22 and Luke Feltham third in 24:25. Windsor's Samara Quanz won the women's race in 27:41, four seconds ahead of teammate Alyshia Alkerton. McMaster's Ana Morariu was third in 28:18, and her team won on 40 points from Windsor on 54 and Guelph on 61. Queen's Gaels had arrived as defending champions in both divisions. Victoria swept both team titles at the Canada West championships on 31 October. The four-lap 8 km course had muddy corners, a long single-track section and a hill that runners could climb on the trail or by a set of stairs. UBC's Maximilion Fillion won the men's race in 25:52 from Regina's Ian Teichler in 26:00. Vikes Daniel Damian, Tyler Browne and Jaxon Kuchar followed in 26:14, 26:16 and 26:33. Victoria scored 39, Regina 63 and UBC 66. That three-point margin pushed UBC out of the men's top 10. Kuchar said he was "quite disappointed" with his own run. Madelyn Eybergen, the defending U Sports champion, won the women's race in 29:16. Teammate Marisha Thompson was second in 29:57. Abigail Yakemchuk of UBC Okanagan broke up an all-Victoria podium with third in 30:44. Another Vikes runner took fourth in 31:03, at the front of a group in which fourth to eighth were split by four seconds. Victoria won on 35 points to UBC's 39, with Alberta third on 82. Eybergen called the hilly, muddy course "quite fun" but said it was not a fast one. Despite losing by just four points, the UBC women have fallen from second to sixth in the rankings over three weeks. In Quebec, Xavier Lemaître won the RSEQ men's race in 24:57 and led Sherbrooke, who go to the nationals ranked second. Laval's women filled the podium. Morgane Drouin took the win in 28:35. Léane Baril crossed second at 29:00, with Béatrice Fillion third at 29:30. Laval scored 24 points, with McGill a distant second on 85. At the AUS championships, the UNB Reds men beat Dalhousie 38 to 51. It ended the Tigers' unbeaten season and left them outside the top 10. UNB had raced with a full squad only once this season, at that meeting. The Dalhousie women completed an unbeaten season with the AUS title and rose from tenth to eighth. Two weeks after the nationals, Laval hosts the Canadian Cross Country Championships on the Plains of Abraham in Quebec City on 28 and 29 November.
- [Kenya's 400m record holder Mercy Adongo Oketch provisionally suspended](https://filmmyrun.com/news/kenya-s-400m-record-holder-mercy-adongo-oketch-provisionally-suspended): News Kenya's 400m record holder Mercy Adongo Oketch provisionally suspended Kenya's 400m record holder Mercy Adongo Oketch provisionally suspended 6 November 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Mercy Adongo Oketch , who holds Kenya's national 400m record, has been provisionally suspended by the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya (ADAK). Her sample contained two prohibited substances, trimetazidine and furosemide. She now awaits a hearing with the agency. Her name was not announced separately. It appeared in a list of provisionally suspended athletes that ADAK put out in October. Trimetazidine is a hormone and metabolic modulator mainly prescribed for heart conditions, and it helps the heart use oxygen more efficiently. Furosemide is a diuretic. It thins the urine and can make other banned substances harder to detect, so it is classed as a masking agent. Oketch is 24 and has been the leading figure in Kenyan one-lap running for two seasons. In May 2025 she helped a Kenyan women's 4x400m team set a national record of 3:25.80. Later that month she ran 50.25 for the 400m national record. At the World Athletics Indoor Championships in Toruń, Poland, in March 2026 she set the indoor national record of 51.25. In May she was part of the Kenyan mixed 4x400m team at the World Athletics Relays that finished fourth in an African record of 3:09.87. It is not yet clear whether those marks will stand. The same list included a "Noah Kibet", suspended for triamcinolone acetonide, a glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory. Early reports took him to be the 800m runner of that name, the 2022 world indoor silver medallist. It was later clarified that the athlete concerned is Noah Kibet Cherokony, a half marathoner. World Athletics records show he has not raced since 2018. The cases add to a difficult period for Kenyan athletics. Since the Athletics Integrity Unit was created in 2017, the tally of Kenyan athletes punished for doping has passed 140. The world and Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir was placed under a provisional suspension by the AIU, made public on 23 October. With the 2029 World Championships coming to Nairobi, ADAK says it will greatly increase testing, with more funding and more out-of-competition and overseas tests. Originally reported in Canadian Running ,
- [Dublin Marathon says lifetime bans over swapped bibs were never handed out](https://filmmyrun.com/news/dublin-marathon-says-lifetime-bans-over-swapped-bibs-were-never-handed): News Dublin Marathon says lifetime bans over swapped bibs were never handed out Dublin Marathon says lifetime bans over swapped bibs were never handed out 7 November 2026 Photo: Nick Iwanyshyn / Canadian Running The Dublin Marathon has denied that runners were given lifetime bans after several men ran this year's race on 25 October wearing bibs registered to women. Early reports had said bans for life were handed out. The organisers say those accounts were wrong. Con Sheehan, who looks after communications for the marathon and the wider Irish Life race series, said the reports had been "misconstrued". He said the matter was "ongoing" and that the organisers' wider policy on unofficial number swaps was also under review. Dublin Marathon Group brought in a zero-tolerance rule on unauthorised transfers this year. It said the aim was to protect the integrity of results and the safety of runners. Anyone found to have sold, passed on or otherwise misused a race number faces disqualification from future events. Disqualified performances are struck from the official records. Results are not moved across to the name of the registered entrant afterwards. A man running on a woman's entry can distort the placings in the women's results. The same goes for younger runners using bibs registered to older age groups. There is a safety issue too. A bib links the wearer to a set of registration details and emergency contacts, so medics could struggle to identify a runner who collapses under someone else's number. Dublin does allow official transfers, but its window this year shut on 23 September, a little over a month before race day. The organisers say the deadline is needed to finalise timing and other systems. Some runners have argued that a later cut-off would cut down on unofficial swaps. The organisers say there are practical limits on how late transfers can stay open. Rules differ widely between races. The TCS Toronto Waterfront Marathon lets runners transfer their entries right up to race day. Originally reported in Canadian Running Back to News
- [Caroline Ash and Maximilien Filion honoured after unbeaten conference seasons](https://filmmyrun.com/news/caroline-ash-and-maximilien-filion-honoured-after-unbeaten-conference): News Caroline Ash and Maximilien Filion honoured after unbeaten conference seasons Caroline Ash and Maximilien Filion honoured after unbeaten conference seasons 7 November 2026 Photo: Canadian Running Caroline Ash of St. Francis Xavier University and Maximilien Filion of the University of British Columbia have been named Under Armour Athletes of the Week. Both won their conference cross-country titles on 31 October. Both go into the U Sports Cross Country Championships in Hamilton, Ontario, on 14 November without a defeat this season. Each receives a shoe from Under Armour's Velociti range. Ash won the AUS Championships in Antigonish, Nova Scotia, in 28:11. StFX hosted the race, and she said the local community turned out to support the team. Grace Mack of the Memorial Sea-Hawks was second, 13 seconds back. The title completed an unbeaten conference season for Ash. She was third at the same championship in 2024 and second in 2025. Ash said she is no great fan of big mileage but has raised it slowly over several years. She now averages about 90 kilometres a week. Winning at home meant more because Antigonish was also where she ran her first race for StFX. Her teammate Lalem Sintayehu is also unbeaten on the men's side, and the pair have spent the season teasing each other about who would keep winning. At nationals she hopes to improve on eighth place in 2025. Filion won the Canada West Championships in Calgary on the same day, a year after taking silver there. He trains in Vancouver, 72 metres above sea level. Calgary sits at 1,045 metres. He said he felt good despite the altitude and that his taper had gone to plan. His recent national championship results have been less kind. Filion was 17th at U Sports in 2024 and 20th in 2025, and he said he was nervous before last year's race. This season he is trying to enjoy his racing more. He has a podium place in mind in Hamilton. He also wants his UBC team, 12th last year, to finish in the top 10. Originally reported in Canadian Running Back to News
- [Canada's governing body brings in $5 race-day fee for runners without a membership](https://filmmyrun.com/news/athletics-canada-brings-in-5-race-day-fee-for-runners-without-a-member): News Canada's governing body brings in $5 race-day fee for runners without a membership Canada's governing body brings in $5 race-day fee for runners without a membership 7 November 2026 Photo: Nick Iwanyshyn / Canadian Running Canada's national athletics federation has launched a road and trail programme that will ask recreational runners to pay a $5 membership fee on race day. The governing body announced the plan on 28 October. In most provinces the charge applies to anyone entering a sanctioned race who does not already hold an eligible annual membership. Existing members pay nothing extra. The fee is separate from the sanctioning charges that race organisers already pay. The income will be split between the national body and its provincial branches. It is earmarked for event development, course certification and sanctioning. The body has about 35,000 members and hopes recreational runners could eventually grow that number as much as tenfold. Chris Winter, its Director, Domestic Programs and Safe Sport, said the organisation would have to "earn our place" with organisers and runners. Part of the money is meant for the national mountain and trail team. Canada's road championship teams are already fully funded. Mountain and trail athletes still pay their own way to world championships. The federation took over that team in 2021 and says its annual budget is now above $100,000. It wants to cover the full cost, including athlete travel, by 2029. The programme is also meant to hold every sanctioned race in the country, whether on road, trail or mountain, to one common set of rules. A group set up in summer 2026 is drafting a policy on emergency medical cover, participant safety, course planning, administration and event operations. The draft is due to reach provincial members in December and the board in spring 2027. It would apply to 2028 events at the earliest. Requirements will be scaled to each race's size, resources and setting. Winter said most established races already meet the core standards but smaller events may need help, adding that the aim was not "ruling with an iron fist". On the same day the body created a new post, Coordinator, Road and Trail Program. The holder will run selection and travel planning for Canadian teams at international mountain and trail championships. The job also covers the national course measurement and certification programme, the Road Race Label Program and the national road, trail and mountain championships. The federation is now recruiting for the role. No specific participation targets or full funding plan for the programme have yet been set. The national body recently received an extra $1.7 million in federal funding. Chief executive Mathieu Gentès said the money would help open the sport up to more people, improve road racing infrastructure and back elite athletes. The body has not said whether any of it is set aside for the new programme.
- [Matthew Ramsden recovers from wrong turn to win Cardiff Cross Challenge](https://filmmyrun.com/news/matthew-ramsden-recovers-from-wrong-turn-to-win-cardiff-cross-challeng): News Matthew Ramsden recovers from wrong turn to win Cardiff Cross Challenge Matthew Ramsden recovers from wrong turn to win Cardiff Cross Challenge 9 November 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Matthew Ramsden of Blackburn Harriers took the senior men's title in Cardiff on Sunday 8 November, despite going off course with about 150 metres left. He missed the turn into the home straight and had to hurdle the course tape twice to get back on the route. He still caught James Kingston of Tonbridge AC and took the 9.6km race in 27:26. British runners filled the podium in both senior races at Llandaff Fields, the first of three rounds in the British Athletics Cross Challenge Series. Jacob Cann of Western Tempo led a large pack in the early stages. Ramsden and Kingston were near the front throughout. Kadar Omar of Birchfield Harriers joined them on the last lap before the two broke away. Kingston looked to have the race won when Ramsden took the line used by slower runners who still had a lap to go. Kingston crossed the line two seconds behind in 27:28. Omar was third in 27:39 and Cann fourth in 27:44. Fifth and sixth went to Callum Elson and Jenson Connell, who could not be separated at 27:46. Elson runs for Cambridge & Coleridge AC and Connell for Leeds City AC. Mahamed Mahamed , this year's British marathon champion, came home 11th for Southampton AC. It was Ramsden's first visit to the event. He said he had been told the course was usually dry and good underfoot, and so it proved. He called it "a gutsy course" and said he was happy with the result. The women's race over 6.4km went to Kate Axford of Belgrave Harriers. She and Amelia Quirk of Bracknell AC were given the same time of 20:37 after Axford held off Quirk's late effort. Rebecca Flaherty of Bingley Harriers & AC was third in 20:40. Poppy Tank of City of Plymouth AC was fourth in 20:49, and the Olympic 1500m silver medallist Laura Muir, making a rare cross-country appearance, was fifth in 20:50. Axford had not raced in Cardiff for two years and said she had dealt with a series of setbacks and injuries in that time. She credited her 1500m speed for the decisive final 30 seconds. The meeting carried World Athletics silver label status this year rather than gold, and fewer international contenders came to the front. A year ago both senior titles went to Kenya, through Cynthia Chepkirui and Mathew Kipsang. The series moves on to Liverpool, where Sefton Park stages the next round on 28 November. That race also serves as the selection trial for Britain's squad at this year's European Cross Country Championships in Belgrade.
- [Rodrigue Kwizera wins third Itálica cross country title to match Kenenisa Bekele](https://filmmyrun.com/news/rodrigue-kwizera-wins-third-italica-cross-country-title-to-match-kenen): News Rodrigue Kwizera wins third Itálica cross country title to match Kenenisa Bekele Rodrigue Kwizera wins third Itálica cross country title to match Kenenisa Bekele 9 November 2026 Photo: Athletics Weekly Rodrigue Kwizera won the Cross Internacional de Itálica in Santiponce, near Seville, on Sunday 8 November. It was his third victory in the race and his first cross country win since becoming a Spanish citizen. In 44 editions only Kenenisa Bekele , the winner in 2003, 2004 and 2007, had also won it three times. Kwizera's first two wins came in 2021 and 2025, when he still represented Burundi. The 9.55km course winds around the Roman ruins of Itálica, passing the amphitheatre and the old Roman road. It was a World Athletics Cross Country Tour Gold meeting, run in unusual warmth for November. Kwizera made his move on the final pass through the woods. Charles Kiboino, a 19-year-old Kenyan, went with him and took the lead on the last bend. Kwizera held on to win in 27:36, a second clear. Third went to Frankline Kibet, who holds the world under-20 cross country title, two seconds behind the winner. Denis Kemboi of Kenya was fourth. Thierry Ndikumwenayo , who holds the European cross country title and has twice won at Itálica, was fifth and the next Spaniard home. Miguel Ángel Martínez closed on him late and finished a second behind in sixth. Both were within 23 seconds of the winner. Ethiopia's Berihu Aregawi, a three-time world cross country silver medallist, was ninth. Aaron Las Heras was a late withdrawal with knee pain. Kwizera is 27 and lives in Castellón, where he races for Playas de Castellón. Spain granted him nationality in May, but World Athletics has yet to approve his change of allegiance. Spain's team selector Pepe Peiró said the decision rests on a World Athletics meeting, which he hoped would come before the European Cross Country Championships in Belgrade on 13 December. Kwizera's 58:03 at the Valencia Half Marathon on 25 October was a Spanish record. It was also three seconds inside Europe's best of 58:06, but it will not stand as a European record until World Athletics formally signs off his switch. He plans to race in Soria on 15 November and then at Atapuerca. Likina Amebaw of Ethiopia won the women's race in 30:41. She attacked as the last lap began, with 2.5km to go, and pulled clear on the climb. Uganda's Charity Cherop, the world under-20 5000m champion, had pushed the pace from the start and finished second, eight seconds down. Kenya's Cynthia Chepkirui, 18, was third at 16 seconds. Amebaw, based in Peguerinos in Ávila province, was third here a year ago. September brought her victory over 5000m at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest and the world road 5km crown in Copenhagen, and she won in Amorebieta on 18 October. Her next race is the Cinque Mulini in Italy on 22 November. Carolina Robles of Seville was the first Spanish woman in eighth, 2:10 behind Amebaw, after passing María Forero of Huelva, who was ninth. The meeting, organised by the Diputación de Sevilla, drew a record 5,057 runners across all categories, and four of its races sold out. The Itálica site is Spain's candidate for UNESCO World Heritage status.
- [Damian Hall pulls out of Kendal Mountain Festival over Dacia drive-in cinema](https://filmmyrun.com/news/damian-hall-pulls-out-of-kendal-mountain-festival-over-dacia-drive-in): News Damian Hall pulls out of Kendal Mountain Festival over Dacia drive-in cinema Damian Hall pulls out of Kendal Mountain Festival over Dacia drive-in cinema 7 November 2026 Photo: Julian Herzog / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 Kendal Mountain Festival is facing criticism from parts of the British outdoor community over a new partnership with the car-maker Dacia. The Cumbrian festival announced a Dacia Drive-In Cinema for 2026 in a social media post. Ultrarunner and climate campaigner Damian Hall has since withdrawn from all his events at the festival. The plan offers 12 screenings watched from a private Dacia car, with the sound played through the car stereo. Popcorn and drinks are free. Dacia is also presenting Q&As with endurance cyclist Sarah Ruggins, adaptive adventurer Ed Jackson, and Chief Scout Dwayne Fields alongside WeTwo co-founder Phoebe Smith. Replies to the announcement were largely hostile. Critics questioned a car brand fronting an outdoor festival and pointed to traffic congestion in the Lake District. The festival's own sustainability material asks visitors to cut emissions and ease congestion. Some also said the illustration looked AI-generated. The festival said it was sketched by hand and then coloured in Photoshop. One commenter likened it to UTMB, which lost Dacia as headline sponsor after objections from runners. Hall co-founded The Green Runners, the campaign group that challenged that UTMB deal in 2023. He calls the Kendal arrangement sportswashing but says he still wants the festival to do well. A film featuring him, The F-Word, had been due to show in the Sports Shoes tent. Its makers, Summit Fever Media, have pulled it in support. Hall won the Spine Race outright in January 2023. He is not alone in stepping back. Calum Macintyre, co-founder of the Norwegian climate group Folk Mot Fossilmakta, had been due to speak this year and has also withdrawn. Andy Fìor-Berry, who presents on the endurance stage, shares the concerns but will still host. He wants to help a conservation scientist on the programme reach the audience. An online petition titled "Kendal Mountain Festival: Dump Dacia" asks the festival to drop the sponsor at the next opportunity. It also wants the festival to sign the Cool Down Network's Fossil Free Declaration. The petition accepts that festivals need sponsors. It argues that partnering with Dacia while screening the People's Emergency Briefing is hypocritical. The festival said it was keen to hear "all opinions, sides and views". It has invited athletes, brands and activists to an open discussion at the Abbot Hall Social Centre on Sunday 22 November, from 9.30am to 10.30am. Entry is free but ticketed.
- [Tebogo tells Lyles and Bednarek to be ready to chase in 2027](https://filmmyrun.com/news/tebogo-tells-lyles-and-bednarek-to-be-ready-to-chase-in-2027): News Tebogo tells Lyles and Bednarek to be ready to chase in 2027 Tebogo tells Lyles and Bednarek to be ready to chase in 2027 8 November 2026 Photo: Kevin Morris / Canadian Running Letsile Tebogo has started the 2027 sprint season early, at least online. On 5 November the Olympic 200m champion from Botswana posted a message on X aimed at the Americans Kenny Bednarek and Noah Lyles . He offered both men his respect, then told them they had "better be ready to chase". The post came less than a month after he returned to off-season training on 16 October. Lyles replied the same day. He asked whether Tebogo had decided to "stop playing opossum" and run all the way through the finish. The jibe refers to Tebogo's habit of easing off before the line when the win is out of reach. In the 200m final at the Brussels Diamond League, Bednarek won in 19.62, then the fastest time in the world this year. Tebogo was in contention for second but slowed visibly and dropped to fourth in 20.01. The three men had contrasting seasons in 2026. Bednarek won double gold at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship and set several world leads over 200m. His only defeat to Lyles came in the 100m at the USATF Championships in July, where Lyles ran 9.79, the fastest 100m in the world this season. Lyles pulled up in the 200m final a few days later and did not race again. Bednarek then won four of his five remaining finals. Tebogo won two Diamond League races, but neither included Lyles or Bednarek. Lyles also beat him in Rome on 4 June. He won the 100m in 9.88, with Tebogo third in 9.95 behind Emmanuel Eseme. The rivalry goes back to the Paris 2024 Olympics. Tebogo won the 200m in 19.46 for Botswana's first Olympic gold, with Bednarek second in 19.62 and Lyles third in 19.70. Asked afterwards whether he could become the face of athletics, Tebogo said he was not loud or arrogant "like Noah". Lyles later congratulated him. In 2025 Lyles beat Tebogo over 200m in Monaco in July in 19.88. He beat him again at the Diamond League Final in Zurich on 28 August, where 19.74 earned him a sixth Diamond League trophy. Lyles, an eight-time world champion, has said he is targeting the American 100m record of 9.69, set by Tyson Gay in 2009. His own best is 9.79. He plans to race more and make fewer public appearances over the next two seasons. He calls 2027 "the building block" for the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Originally reported in Canadian Running ,
- [Stephanie Case becomes first woman to finish 100 miles at the Antarctic Ice Ultra](https://filmmyrun.com/news/stephanie-case-becomes-first-woman-to-finish-100-miles-at-the-antarcti): News Stephanie Case becomes first woman to finish 100 miles at the Antarctic Ice Ultra Stephanie Case becomes first woman to finish 100 miles at the Antarctic Ice Ultra 10 November 2026 Photo: peakpixelcafe.de / Canadian Running Stephanie Case has become the first woman to complete the 100-mile race at the Antarctic Ice Ultra. The Canadian finished on Sunday in 17:31:39 and was second overall. China's Yusheng Ni won in 17:02:24. Both ran well inside the previous event record of 22:40:47, which Ni set in 2025. No woman had finished the distance before, so Case now holds the first women's record. Case grew up in Ontario and now lives in Chamonix, France. She had hoped to break the overall record and said she was "ecstatic" with the result. She hopes it shows women, and mothers in particular, that big goals are still possible after having children. Her daughter, Pepper, was only six months old in 2025 when Case took victory over 100km at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia. She paused on the course to breastfeed. Some people said afterwards that she ought to have been at home with her baby, and Case talked publicly about that backlash. The race is held in Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica, with the Schirmacher Oasis at its centre. Runners lap a course of snow and ice around a remote base camp, and temperatures can fall well below -20C. The event began in 2024 and offers distances up to 100 miles, along with a 24-hour relay. This year 28 runners took part across the various races. A large storm was on its way, so the organisers started at 1am local time. Once everyone had finished, the field was flown back to Cape Town ahead of the weather. Case prepared for the cold by spending 20 minutes in a cryotherapy chamber in Geneva, testing her kit under the supervision of an osteopath. A normal session lasts three minutes. She said it showed how small jobs such as drinking from a bottle or opening a gel become difficult. It made her rethink how she would eat and drink with frozen hands. At the covered aid stations runners could change outer layers and take hot drinks. Case still finished with a burnt face, as the area around her nose had to stay uncovered so she could breathe. Her record in long mountain races is substantial. In 2021 she won the women's 450km Tor des Glaciers in Italy and was third overall. She was runner-up at the 2022 Hardrock 100. In 2025 she took second place at Nice Côte d'Azur by UTMB and fifth on her return to Hardrock. In June this year she placed sixth at Trail 100 Andorra by UTMB. Away from racing, Case is a human rights lawyer. In 2014 she founded Free to Run in Afghanistan, a charity that uses running to help women and girls in conflict-affected communities take part in sport and leadership. She used the Antarctic run to raise money for the charity. Pepper, who has just turned two, watched her finish on the livestream. Case said she could not wait to get home and tell her all about it.
- [Habtom Samuel breaks the hour at the Boston Half as Fentaye Belayneh wins for a third year](https://filmmyrun.com/news/habtom-samuel-breaks-the-hour-at-the-boston-half-as-fentaye-belayneh-w): News Habtom Samuel breaks the hour at the Boston Half as Fentaye Belayneh wins for a third year Habtom Samuel breaks the hour at the Boston Half as Fentaye Belayneh wins for a third year 9 November 2026 Photo: World-Track and Field Habtom Samuel of Eritrea won the Boston Half on Sunday 8 November in 59:49. That set an event record and was the first time anyone has broken the hour for a half marathon in Massachusetts. Fentaye Belayneh of Ethiopia took the women's race in 1:09:14. She is the first woman to win it in three consecutive years. The race started and finished in Franklin Park on a cold, clear morning. The course runs over rolling hills through the Emerald Necklace parks. Samuel went through 5K in 14:19 at the head of a four-man group. Morocco's Mohammed El Youssfi was there too, along with two Kenyans, Andrea Kiptoo and Abel Kipchumba. El Youssfi had slipped a few seconds back by 10K, passed in 28:32. Kipchumba, the 2023 winner, lost touch by 10 miles. Samuel moved clear soon after 15K and covered the last 6K alone, finishing more than a minute ahead. Kiptoo was second in 1:01:03 and Kipchumba third in 1:01:16. El Youssfi took fourth in 1:01:29 and Amon Kemboi fifth in 1:01:46. Jack Aho was sixth in 1:01:53, the fastest time by an American in the event's history. Samuel took 45 seconds off the record of 1:00:34 set by Lelisa Desisa in 2013. He said he saw the chance at 10K and decided to "fight for the course record". The win earned him $15,000 plus a $10,000 bonus for the record. He signed with Hoka Northern Arizona Elite last month, having won the NCAA 5000m and 10,000m titles for the University of New Mexico in June. He is unbeaten as a professional. His wins include the Beach to Beacon 10K in 27:40 on 1 August and the Falmouth Road Race in a course record of 30:53 for seven miles. A week before Boston he won the Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K in New York in 13:31. His half marathon best remains 59:01, run in Houston. He said afterwards that he felt tired and had no next race fixed. The women's race began with American Kassie Parker going straight to the front. She ran the first mile in 5:21 and led by 15 seconds at five miles. She still had 11 seconds in hand at 10K before being caught during the seventh mile. She faded to ninth in 1:11:10. Belayneh waited in the chasing group and still had four rivals with her at 11 miles. The final 800 metres climb into Franklin Park, and she kicked clear of Winfred Mbithe of Kenya there to win by two seconds. Mbithe was second in 1:09:16, Sintayehu Lewetegn of Ethiopia third in 1:09:26 and Melat Kejeta of Germany fourth in 1:09:29. Sydney Vaught, the US 10,000m champion, was fifth and first American in 1:09:44 on her half marathon debut. Belayneh also took $15,000 and held up three fingers for the photographs. In the wheelchair races Daniel Romanchuk won the men's title in an event record of 45:53, taking 1:46 off his own mark from 2024. Yen Hoang beat Jenna Ayers in a photo finish, both timed at 1:02:54. More than 7,400 took part and 7,363 runners finished behind the professionals. Heavy rain the day before stopped in time, though the grass staging area in the park was left very muddy.

# Runner profiles (elite and notable runners, not Stephen)
- [Letsile Tebogo: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/letsile-tebogo): Runners / Letsile Tebogo Photo: Ssu / Wikimedia Commons Letsile Tebogo Runs Letsile Tebogo is a sprinter from Botswana, born on 7 June 2003. He races mainly over 100m and 200m and also runs the 4x400m relay for his country. His first international outing came at 17, at the World Athletics Relays in Chorzów, Poland, in May 2021. That August he won the 100m at the World Under-20 Championships in Nairobi and finished second in the 200m. No athlete from Botswana had won a 100m title at any World Championships level before. He came back a year later and produced the same pair of results. His 2022 season rewrote the national record book. On 19 February he ran 10.08 for 100m at the Botswana Athletics Championships, a national record. Two months later he clocked 9.96 at the Gaborone International Meet, becoming the first man from Botswana to go under 10 seconds and setting a world under-20 record. He lowered that mark to 9.94 on 15 July in his first race at a senior World Championships, in Eugene, Oregon. A month later he ran 9.91 to win the under-20 final in Cali, Colombia. He also became African 200m champion that year, the youngest winner in the event's history. At the 2023 World Championships he took silver in the 100m and bronze in the 200m five days later. On 8 August 2024 he won the Olympic 200m title in Paris in 19.46. Kenny Bednarek was second in 19.62 and Noah Lyles third in 19.70. It was the first Olympic gold medal Botswana had ever won. The government declared a public holiday for the afternoon of 9 August and gave him two houses. Earlier that year, on 17 February, he had run 30.69 for 300m at altitude in Pretoria, a world best. He won five Diamond League races in 2024, and his 19.80 at the final in Brussels earned him the first Jesse Owens Rising Star Award for men, though he did not win the race. He was later named best male athlete of Paris 2024 by the Association of National Olympic Committees, and World Athletics Male Athlete of the Year in December. The 2025 World Championships in Tokyo were mixed. He was disqualified from the 100m final for a false start and finished fourth in the 200m behind Lyles, Bednarek and Bryan Levell. On 21 September Botswana took the 4x400m title in 2:57.76. Tebogo ran second in a quartet that also included Lee Eppie, Bayapo Ndori and Collen Kebinatshipi. The following spring he lined up on that same leg at the World Athletics Relays, this time before a home crowd in Gaborone. The team finished in 2:54.47, a competition record and at the time the third fastest performance in history. His 2026 season brought 200m wins at the Bislett Games and in Lausanne, neither against Lyles or Bednarek. In Rome on 4 June he was third over 100m in 9.95, behind Lyles in 9.88 and Emmanuel Eseme. In the Brussels 200m he was in the hunt for second but eased off and slipped to fourth in 20.01 as Bednarek won in 19.62. He returned to training on 16 October. On 5 November he posted a message to the two Americans, offering respect and telling them they had "better be ready to chase" in 2027. Lyles replied the same day, asking whether Tebogo would now "stop playing opossum" and run hard through the line. - [Zouhair Talbi: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/zouhair-talbi): Runners / Zouhair Talbi Photo: Photoguy1212 / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Zouhair Talbi Born 1995 (age 30 or 31) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road, Track Zouhair Talbi is a Moroccan-born American long-distance runner, born on 8 April 1995 in Tighassaline, Khenifra, Morocco. He played football before switching to distance running as a teenager, and competed for Morocco at the U20 race of the 2013 World Cross Country Championships in Bydgoszcz, placing 14th. In 2018 he was fourth over 10,000m at the Bislett Games in Oslo in 28:31. He studied in the United States, first at Northwest Kansas Technical College and then at Oklahoma City University. There he won seven NAIA national titles and took silver in the 5000m at the 2015 World University Games. In May 2021 Talbi won the 10,000m at California's Sound Running Track Meet, improving his personal best from 28:02 to 27:20.61. It was the second-fastest time ever run by a collegiate athlete. He was third with two laps remaining before closing the final 400 metres in 59.41, getting past Emmanuel Bor and Joe Klecker. The run met the Olympic qualifying standard, but Talbi was withdrawn shortly before the Games began after he had not met the drug-testing requirements set for athletes representing Morocco. Talbi turned to the marathon in 2023, finishing fifth at the Boston Marathon in 2:08:35. He also set a half marathon best of 1:01:08 that year, placing fifth at the Houston Half Marathon. In January 2024 he won the Houston Marathon in a course record of 2:06:39. He then ran for Morocco at the 2024 Paris Olympics, placing 35th in 2:11:51. Talbi became an American citizen in 2025. He matched his half marathon best of 1:01:08 to win the 2025 Chicago Half Marathon. On 11 January 2026 he lowered his own Houston Marathon course record to 2:05:45. Only two Americans, Conner Mantz and Khalid Khannouchi, had gone under 2:06 before him where the course counts for records. In March 2026 he ran 59:41 for second place at the New York City Half Marathon. He was fifth again at the Boston Marathon, where his 2:03:45 was the fastest time recorded there by an American. On 13 September 2026 Talbi won the 45th Great North Run, the first American winner in the race's history. He and Kenya's Alex Mutiso, the defending champion, ran shoulder to shoulder on the road from Newcastle over the Tyne Bridge to South Shields for all but the last mile. Talbi opened a gap over that closing stretch and crossed the line in 59:47, with Mutiso 14 seconds back in 1:00:01. On 1 November he was the leading American at the New York City Marathon, sixth in 2:06:43. His eligibility to represent the United States in international championships, held back by his earlier representation of Morocco, opens in August 2027. - [Nick Burmey: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nick-burmey): Runners / Nick Burmey NB 🇨🇦 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Nick Burmey Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra Nick Burmey is a Canadian ultra runner whose results sit at the long end of the sport, from 100-mile trail races to the hourly loops of backyard ultra. He does not currently hold a UTMB Index. His best-documented trail result came in 2024 at the Sulphur Springs Trail Race 100 Mile. The course covers 160 km with 3,920 m of climb. Burmey finished in 29:01:54, which put him 57th among the men. In 2026 he was part of Canada's 15-strong team at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championships. Racing began on a Saturday, with 67 countries each staging their own event at the same time. Canada's runners raced on the B.C. Backyard Ultra course in Sicamous, British Columbia. A 6.706 km loop starts every hour, and any runner who cannot finish it inside the hour is out. Every completed yard counts as a point towards the national total. Burmey was one of seven Canadians still out on the loop as the race moved into its third day on the Monday. By then eight of his teammates had stopped. The furthest of them was Sandra Auger, with 51 yards, or 342 km. Race director Kara Leinweber said Canada stood sixth in the world at that stage and described the team as being in "a really good position". The country had finished eighth at the 2024 edition with 673 yards. - [Stephanie Case: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/stephanie-case): Runners / Stephanie Case Photo: UTMB profile 🇨🇦 Stephanie Case Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 648 (10 November 2026) Stephanie Case is a Canadian ultra runner and human rights lawyer, born in 1982. She grew up in Ontario and is now based in Chamonix. Her legal work has taken her to Afghanistan, Gaza and South Sudan with the United Nations. On the trails she is drawn to the longest and steepest races, and her UTMB Index stands at 648. Her first big win came at the 2009 Vermont 100, where she was first woman in 18:38:42. In 2011 she won the RacingThePlanet Nepal event, covering 75km with 9,700m of climb in 30:15:09. The Tor des Géants then became her race. She was first woman there in 2015, over a 282km course that ran from Courmayeur to Oyace, in 83:12:35. She was second in 2016 in 98:15:27 and fourth in both 2017 and 2018. In 2019 she was second woman at the Ronda dels Cims in Andorra, a 170km route with 13,500m of climb, in 47:00:35. In 2021 she won the women's race at the 450km Tor des Glaciers and was third overall. Hardrock 100 has also suited her. She was second woman in 2022 in 33:52:40 and fifth on her return in 2025 in 32:53:16. That return followed a three-year gap from racing after the birth of her daughter, Pepper. Her comeback race was Ultra-Trail Snowdonia in May 2025, where she won the women's 105km in 16:53:22. She stopped at aid stations along the way to breastfeed her six-month-old daughter. The result drew attention well beyond the sport, and some critics said she should have stayed at home. Case spoke openly about that response. Later in 2025 she was second woman at the 165km Nice Côte d'Azur by UTMB in 25:48:22. In 2026 she became the first woman to finish the 100-mile race at the Antarctic Ice Ultra in Queen Maud Land. Runners lap a snow and ice course around a remote base camp, and the start was moved to 1am to beat an approaching storm. Case finished in 17:31:39 and was second overall, just under half an hour behind China's Yusheng Ni. Both were well inside the previous event record of 22:40:47. To prepare, she spent 20 minutes in a cryotherapy chamber in Geneva to test her kit, against a usual session of three minutes. She still finished with a burnt face where her nose had been left uncovered so she could breathe. Her 2026 season has also included seventh woman at the Transgrancanaria Classic in 18:14:52, sixth at the Trail 100 Andorra 105K in 18:41:53 and 12th at the TDS in 27:54:29. Away from racing, she founded Free to Run in Afghanistan in 2014. The charity uses running to bring women and girls in conflict-affected communities into sport and leadership, and she raised money for it with her Antarctic run. She has said she hopes her results show mothers that ambitious goals remain within reach. - [Tigst Assefa: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/tigst-assefa): Runners / Tigst Assefa Photo: Katie Chan / Wikimedia Commons Tigst Assefa Runs Tigst Assefa is an Ethiopian marathon runner who began her career on the track. Born on 3 December 1996, she was an 800 metres specialist until a persistent Achilles problem stopped her training in spikes. She moved to the roads in 2018 and ran her first marathon in 2022. She has since become one of the fastest women ever over the distance, with four World Marathon Majors wins. Her track years started early. At 12 she took bronze over 400m at the Ethiopian senior championships in 56.70. At 16 she won 800m bronze at the African Junior Championships in Réduit, Mauritius. In 2014 she ran 1:59.24 in Lausanne, won the ISTAF Berlin meeting and was fourth at the African Championships in Marrakesh. She represented Ethiopia at the 2016 World Indoor Championships in Portland and at the Rio Olympics, but went out in the early rounds at both. The marathon brought a sharp change of fortune. Her debut in Riyadh in March 2022 produced seventh place in 2:34:01. Six months later she won in Berlin in 2:15:37, more than 18 minutes quicker, with a second half of 67:24. On 24 September 2023 she returned to Berlin and ran 2:11:53. That cut 2 minutes 11 seconds from Brigid Kosgei's world record and made her the first woman under 2:14, 2:13 and 2:12. She won by almost six minutes, and World Athletics later honoured her as its leading road and non-track athlete that year. Ruth Chepngetich later lowered the record to 2:09:56 in Chicago in 2024, and that mark still stands. At the Paris Olympics on 11 August 2024 she took silver in 2:22:58, three seconds behind Sifan Hassan. The two collided in the closing sprint. Ethiopia lodged a protest, which the Jury of Appeal rejected. Assefa said afterwards that she might have had gold had she not been pushed. London then became her race. She won there on 27 April 2025 in 2:15:50, a world record for a women-only marathon. She came back on 26 April 2026 and took nine seconds off her own mark with 2:15:41. Her third Berlin win, on Sunday 27 September 2026, came at a heavy cost. She reached halfway in 64:57, and at 40km she was on track for 2:09:44, quicker than the world record. Her manager, Gianni Demadonna, said pain in her right foot started at around 31km and the tendon had fully ruptured by the line. She limped home in a course record of 2:11:04, the third fastest time by a woman, and still won by almost six minutes before collapsing past the finish. She missed the podium ceremony and had surgery in Munich the next day, which Demadonna described as a success. He thinks she will need about seven months away from racing. That would still give her a chance to defend her London title on 24 and 25 April 2027. In October she was named among the ten women nominated for the 2026 World Athlete of the Year, and her London run is on the shortlist for the new Moment of the Year award. The winners will be announced in Monaco on 29 November. Personal bests Event Time Where Year 800 m 1:59.24 Lausanne 2014 Marathon 2:11:04 Berlin 2026 From Wikipedia, checked monthly.
