- [Yusheng Ni: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/yusheng-ni): Runners / Yusheng Ni YN 🇨🇳 UTMB Index 638 Film My Run 🇨🇳 Yusheng Ni Country 🇨🇳 China Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 638 (10 November 2026) Yusheng Ni is a Chinese trail and ultra runner whose recorded results go back more than a decade. His UTMB Index stands at 638. He races often and over long distances, in Hong Kong and mainland China, across South-East Asia and in the mountains of Europe. His earliest listed result came at the Vibram Hong Kong 100 in 2013, where he covered 97 km in 15:45:56 for 127th man. He has gone back to that race many times since. His most striking win came at the Antarctic Ice Ultra in Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica. Ni took the 100-mile race in 17:02:24. That was 5:38:23 inside the event record of 22:40:47, which he had set himself in 2025. Runners lap a snow and ice course around a remote base camp near the Schirmacher Oasis, and temperatures can drop well below -20C. Twenty-eight runners took part across all the distances. With a big storm approaching, the organisers started the race at 1am local time. Canada's Stephanie Case was second overall in 17:31:39 and became the first woman to finish the distance. His fastest run on flat ground was a win at the 2024 Brazos Bend 100 Marathon, where he ran 2:59:12 over 42 km with only 30 m of climb. In the mountains his best placings have come in China. He was third at the autumn edition of the Ultra-Trail Huangshan Xihong 168 in 2024, covering 160 km and 7130 m of climb in 28:37:37. At Chongli in 2023 he finished seventh in the 205 km GTC, which climbs 10,660 m, in 39:50:39. He had also been seventh in the Chongli UTC the year before, in 30:15:15. Further afield, he was ninth man in the 118 km Betong 100M at Amazean Jungle Thailand by UTMB in 2025, in 22:16:49. In 2026 he placed sixth at Hallasan100, running 99 km in 14:31:16. He has finished the UTMB itself, taking 34:38:11 for 354th man in 2024. A year later he completed the 153 km TDS in 29:46:29, placing 200th. His 2026 calendar has been crowded. He ran both the HK100 and The Half at the Anta Hong Kong 100, then 79 km at Trail 100 Andorra by UTMB in 12:45:07. At the Marathon du Mont-Blanc he finished the 90 Km in 16:21:10 and the 42 Km in 6:22:29. He took 68th man in the 75 km Termières dera Libertat at Val d'Aran. His most recent listed result is the Restonica Trail UTC100M, 110 km with 7200 m of climb, which he finished in 25:26:44 for 98th man. - [Adam Peterman: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/adam-peterman): Runners / Adam Peterman Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Adam Peterman Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 929 (9 November 2026) Adam Peterman is an American ultra-distance and marathon runner from Missoula, Montana, sponsored by Hoka. He carries a UTMB Index of 930. He ran cross country and track at Hellgate High School before a scholarship took him to the University of Colorado Boulder, where he earned All-Pac-12 honours and an honourable All-American mention in the steeplechase, and graduated magna cum laude in environmental studies and geology. Peterman turned professional and has twice been crowned US national trail champion over the marathon distance. In 2022 he strung together four straight ultra wins, among them the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run on his first attempt at the distance, and took two individual gold medals at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Chiang Mai. USA Track and Field named him one of its 2022 Mountain Ultra Trail Runners of the Year. A sacral stress fracture kept him out of racing for most of 2023. He had surgery, then built back up from walking to cycling before he could run again, returning at the Antelope Island Buffalo Run on 29 March 2024. Later that year he placed third at the CCC in Chamonix in 10:28:50, one of two Americans on the podium. He has stayed near the front of the sport since. In 2025 he won the Gorge Waterfalls 100K, was sixth at the UTMB OCC and eighth at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships long trail race. His 2026 season has brought a win at the Canyons Endurance Runs 100K, second at the Black Canyon Ultras 50K, sixth at Western States and 41st at the CCC. - [Noah Lyles: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/noah-lyles): Runners / Noah Lyles Photo: Aeltegop / Wikimedia Commons Noah Lyles Runs Noah Lyles is an American sprinter who races mainly over 100m and 200m. He was born in Gainesville, Florida, on 18 July 1997 and grew up in Alexandria, Virginia. He was a gymnast before he took up track and field at the age of 12. In July 2016 he turned professional with Adidas, giving up a planned place at the University of Florida. His 19.31 for 200m is the American record and the third fastest time in history. His promise showed early. He won 200m gold at the 2014 Youth Olympic Games, then took the 100m and 4x100m relay titles at the 2016 World U20 Championships. At the 2016 US Olympic Trials he finished fourth in the 200m in 20.09, a national high school record that had stood for 31 years. In 2018 he won the US 100m title in 9.88, passing Ronnie Baker in the final metre. That made him the youngest American champion at the distance since Sam Graddy in 1984. A year later he won the 200m and the 4x100m relay at the World Championships in Doha. The biggest results have come since. At the 2022 World Championships in Eugene he retained his 200m title in 19.31, a hundredth of a second inside Michael Johnson's old national record. In Budapest in 2023 he completed a sprint treble, winning the 100m in 9.83, the 200m in 19.52 and the relay. At the Paris 2024 Olympics he won the 100m by five thousandths of a second from Jamaica's Kishane Thompson, the first American victory in the event since 2004. Later that week he took bronze in the 200m in 19.70, behind Letsile Tebogo of Botswana in 19.46 and Kenny Bednarek in 19.62. In Tokyo in 2025 he was third in the 100m in 9.89, then won a fourth straight world 200m title in 19.52 and anchored the US relay team to gold in 37.29. He now has eight world titles and six Diamond League trophies. Through 2025 he had run under 20 seconds for 200m 47 times without wind assistance, more than any other athlete. His 2026 season was short. He won the 100m in Rome on 4 June in 9.88, with Tebogo third. On 16 June at the Ostrava Golden Spike he ran 14.67 for 150m on a curved track, a world best that beat Thompson's 14.92. At the USATF Championships in July he won the 100m in 9.79, the fastest time in the world this year. A few days later he pulled up in the 200m final and did not race again. The rivalry with Tebogo has carried on into the off-season. On 5 November Tebogo posted on X that Lyles and Bednarek had better be ready to chase. Lyles answered the same day, asking whether Tebogo would "stop playing opossum" and run through the line. Lyles has said he wants Tyson Gay's American 100m record of 9.69, set in 2009. For the next two years he intends to spend more of his time on the track and less of it on promotional work. He treats 2027 as the foundation for a home Olympics in Los Angeles a year later. - [Kenny Bednarek: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kenny-bednarek): Runners / Kenny Bednarek KB Film My Run Kenny Bednarek Runs Kenny Bednarek is an American sprinter who races the 100m and 200m. He was born on 14 October 1998 in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and grew up in Rice Lake, Wisconsin. At Rice Lake High School he collected seven individual state titles. His 20.43 for 200m was the fastest by any US high school runner in 2018. He still holds the Wisconsin all-class records for 200m and 400m. He also played football for the school, and in his final year both the track and football teams won state championships. He races with a tie wrapped round his head, which earned him the nickname "Kung Fu Kenny". He went on to Indian Hills Community College in Ottumwa, Iowa. In May 2019, at the NJCAA championships in Hobbs, New Mexico, he ran 19.49 for 200m in a semi-final at altitude. The tailwind was 6.1 metres per second, far too strong for the time to count. The following day he won the 200m in 19.82 into a headwind and the 400m in 44.73. Isaac Makwala of Botswana was the only other man to have broken 20 and 45 seconds on the same day. Bednarek was 20, the youngest to manage it and the only American. In July 2019 he signed with Nike and moved to Florida to train under Justin Gatlin. His first global medal came at the Tokyo Olympics on 4 August 2021. He took 200m silver in 19.68. That season he won Diamond League races in Gateshead, Doha and Zürich, where 19.70 secured the overall 200m title. He ran under 20 seconds 12 times in 2021, more than anyone in a single year, and finished as World Athletics' top-ranked 200m man. At the 2022 World Championships in Eugene he won silver again in 19.77, behind Noah Lyles's American record of 19.31. He was second to Lyles in both sprints at the 2024 US Olympic trials, setting personal bests of 9.87 and 19.59. In Paris he finished seventh in the 100m final in 9.88. He then took 200m silver in 19.62, behind Letsile Tebogo's 19.46 and ahead of Lyles in 19.70. He joined Michael Johnson's Grand Slam Track for its first season in 2025. He won his sprint category in Kingston, Miami and Philadelphia and was named Racer of the Year. On 1 August 2025 he won the US 100m title in 9.79. That put him level with Lyles and Maurice Greene as the joint sixth-fastest American in history. In 2026 he won the 100m and the 200m at the first World Athletics Ultimate Championship. They were his first individual global titles. His 200m winning time of 19.52 was a personal best and lifted him to seventh on the world all-time list. He also won the 200m at the Brussels Diamond League in 19.62. His only loss to Lyles all year came over 100m at the US championships in July. After that he won four of his five remaining finals. In November Tebogo posted a message on X telling Bednarek and Lyles they had "better be ready to chase" in 2027. - [Kim Collison: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kim-collison): Runners / Kim Collison Photo: Becx Carter 🇬🇧 Kim Collison Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 792 (9 November 2026) Kim Collison is one of British fell running's most decorated all-rounders, with wins and records across ultrarunning, fell racing and mountain marathons. He represented Great Britain at the World Trail Championships twice, helping the team to bronze in 2015. He had earlier competed for a GB adventure racing team at three world championships, finishing sixth in Ecuador in 2014. In 2014 he also won the Lakeland 50 and was crowned British Trail Running Champion. He went on to set ultra records at Hardmoors 55, the Lakeland Trails 110km, Lakes in a Day and the Arc of Attrition. On the fells he has won a British Championship race and finished a close second in an English Championship race. At the Original Mountain Marathon he has won both the Elite and the Long Score categories, and he has twice taken the Elite class of the Dark Mountains Mountain Marathon. Collison has completed both summer and winter Bob Graham Rounds, setting the winter record in 2019 in 15 hours 47 minutes. In July 2020 he broke the Lakeland 24-hour fell record with 78 summits. He then took the Paddy Buckley Round record in April 2021, and the 24-hour Munro record, with 33 tops, that same July. He set a course record at the Northern Traverse in 2022. In 2024 he returned to win the Fellsman, a decade after his first win there. In 2025, on his fourth attempt, he finished and won the Spine Race. He also broke Joss Naylor's 43-year-old record for the Lakes, Meres and Waters challenge. - [Paul Verbnjak: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/paul-verbnjak): Runners / Paul Verbnjak PV 🇦🇹 UTMB Index 721 Film My Run 🇦🇹 Paul Verbnjak Country 🇦🇹 Austria Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 721 (9 November 2026) Paul Verbnjak is an Austrian mountain runner whose recorded results come from vertical races. These are short events where the climb matters far more than the distance. He holds a General UTMB Index of 722. His best result came on Saturday 17 October 2026 at the Beinhoat das Vertical in Dorfgastein, the Grand Finale of the VK OPEN World Cup. He finished second in 40:20, 47 seconds behind his compatriot Christof Hochenwarter, who won in 39:33. Nils Oberauer was third in 40:59, giving Austria every place on the men's podium. Verbnjak also finished one minute and 14 seconds ahead of France's Louis Dumas, who came fourth but still took the overall series title. The Dorfgastein course is a hard test. The direct line climbs 1,200m in 3.3km beneath the cable car to the Fulseck mountain station, which sits at more than 2,000m. Runners may choose their own way up. A longer alternative of 4.1km winds up walking trails and pistes. The race's title is Austrian dialect for brutally hard. It was the 13th edition of the race and the first time Austria had hosted the series final. There were 335 starters. In 2026 he also raced the Vertical at the adidas Innsbruck Alpine Trailrun Festival. That course covers 7km with 1,330m of climb. He finished 40th man in 1:02:50. His runner-up place in Dorfgastein, on home soil and in a field that included the series champion, is the standout result of his season so far. - [Dean Karnazes: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/dean-karnazes): Runners / Dean Karnazes Photo: Narsil at en.wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Dean Karnazes Born 1962 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road, Trail & Ultra (legend) Dean Karnazes is an American ultramarathon runner and author, born Constantinos Karnazes on 23 August 1962. He ran competitively as a teenager in California before giving up the sport for 15 years. He took it up again at the age of 30 and went on to write Ultramarathon Man: Confessions of an All-Night Runner, a memoir that introduced ultra-distance running to a wider public. Karnazes has completed a string of extreme endurance runs. In 2002 he ran a marathon to the South Pole in temperatures of minus 13F, without snowshoes. In 2005 he covered 350 miles without sleep, finishing in 80 hours 44 minutes. The following year he ran a marathon in each of the 50 US states on 50 consecutive days, starting in St Louis in September 2006 and finishing with the New York City Marathon that November. On the racing circuit, Karnazes won the Badwater Ultramarathon across Death Valley in 2004, adding five more top-10 finishes there between 2000 and 2008. He won the Vermont 100 Mile Endurance Run in 2006 and took the overall title at the 4 Deserts Race Series in 2008. At the Western States Endurance Run he earned the sub-24-hour silver buckle eleven times between 1995 and 2006. Over 75 days in 2011 he covered 3,000 miles by road, running from Disneyland to New York City. Karnazes' profile brought him ESPN's ESPY award for Best Outdoor Athlete in 2007 and three wins of Competitor magazine's Endurance Athlete of the Year award. Some in the ultrarunning community have questioned his standing as an elite racer, arguing his fame rests more on self-promotion than results. The president of the American Ultrarunning Association said he was not even in the top 10 of ultrarunners, and former elite runner Weldon Johnson said his biggest achievement was in marketing, not running. - [Fentaye Belayneh: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/fentaye-belayneh): Runners / Fentaye Belayneh FB Film My Run Fentaye Belayneh Runs Fentaye Belayneh is an Ethiopian long-distance runner who has moved from the track to the roads. Born on 15 September 2000, she also appears in results as Fantaye Belayneh Azale or Fentaye Azale. The earliest race on her record is a 5000m at the Ethiopian Athletics Championships of 2021, run that April, and she came home sixth. She was sixth again at the Ethiopian Olympic Trials in Hengelo that year, clocking 14:44.51, and missed out on the team for the Games. Her breakthrough came in 2022. On 2 April she won her first national title at the Ethiopian Championships in Hawassa. Later that month she won a road 10K in Herzogenaurach in 30:25, a time that ranked among the 30 fastest ever run for the distance. In June she took silver in the 5000m at the African Championships, finishing behind Beatrice Chebet. She also won the Beach to Beacon 10K that year in 32:07. Her most notable run since has come in Boston. On 8 November she won the Boston Half in 1:09:14, becoming the first woman to take the race three years running. The course starts and finishes in Franklin Park and rolls over hills through the Emerald Necklace parks. Belayneh let the American Kassie Parker build an early lead and sat in the chasing group. Four rivals were still with her at 11 miles. The race was settled on the final 800 metres, which climb back into Franklin Park. Belayneh kicked away from Kenya's Winfred Mbithe there and won by two seconds. Mbithe finished in 1:09:16, ahead of Ethiopia's Sintayehu Lewetegn in 1:09:26 and Germany's Melat Kejeta in 1:09:29. The win was worth $15,000. Belayneh marked it by raising three fingers for the photographers. - [Fiona O'Keeffe: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/fiona-o-keeffe): Runners / Fiona O'Keeffe Photo: jenaragon94 / Wikimedia Commons Fiona O'Keeffe Runs Fiona O'Keeffe is an American distance runner, born on 24 May 1998 and raised in Davis, California. She made her name on the track and over the country before moving up to the roads. At Davis Senior High School she won the 2016 California state title over 3200 metres and was twice state cross country champion. That summer she ran 15:56.84 for 5000 metres at the USATF Under-20 Championships, a time that put her sixth on the all-time list for American high school runners. She ran for Stanford from 2016 to 2020. In 2019 she won the Pac-12 cross country title in 19:32.7, and she collected eight NCAA Division I All-American honours in her time there. Her best championship placing was third over 5000 metres at the 2019 NCAA indoor meet. She turned professional with Puma in 2021 and finished 20th in the 10,000 metres at the US Olympic Trials in Eugene, Oregon. The road results followed quickly. In January 2022 she was fourth at the Houston Half Marathon in 1:07:42, the quickest half marathon debut by an American woman. In 2023 she lowered her track bests to 15:01.34 for 5000 metres and 30:52.77 for 10,000 metres, and placed sixth in the 5km at the World Road Running Championships. Her first marathon came at the US Olympic Trials in Orlando on 3 February 2024. She had qualified with 1:09:34 at the Raleigh Holiday Half Marathon, then won in 2:22:10. No woman had won the Trials on a marathon debut before, and at 25 she was the youngest woman to win it. Her Olympic marathon in Paris on 11 August 2024 lasted less than 5km before a hip injury forced her out. She came back strongly in New York in 2025, finishing fourth in 2:22:49. She was the first American home that day, and no American woman has run faster on the five-borough course. O'Keeffe, now 28, has had a difficult 2026. She missed the Boston Marathon in April and has withdrawn from the New York City Marathon on 1 November after surgery on her left hamstring in October. - [Gabriela DeBues-Stafford: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/gabriela-debues-stafford): Runners / Gabriela DeBues-Stafford Photo: Lax / Wikimedia Commons Gabriela DeBues-Stafford Runs Gabriela DeBues-Stafford is a Canadian middle- and long-distance runner and a two-time Olympian. She was born in London, Ontario, on 13 September 1995 and grew up in Toronto. Her range runs from 800m on the track to 10km on the road. She won the Ontario schools cross country title in Grade 12. She then studied psychology at the University of Toronto and raced for the Varsity Blues. Her first senior international championship brought a silver medal over 1500m at the 2015 Summer Universiade in Gwangju. Her early championship years were modest. At the Rio Olympics in 2016 she was ninth in her 1500m heat and 25th overall. She took NACAC bronze in Toronto in 2018 in 4:07.36. That summer she met the coach Andy Young at the British Grand Prix and moved to Glasgow to join a training group that included Laura Muir. The move paid off in 2019. She set Canadian records indoors and out, among them 4:17.87 for the mile in Monaco and 14:44.12 for 5000m in Brussels. At the world championships in Doha she reached the 1500m final and finished sixth in 3:56.12, meeting her stated aim of a sub-four-minute run in a final. She then moved to the Bowerman Track Club in Portland, coached by Shalane Flanagan. The delayed Tokyo season of 2021 was her best. She ran 1:58.70 for 800m in Portland, making her one of only three women to have gone under 1:59 for 800m, 3:57 for 1500m and 14:45 for 5000m. In Tokyo she was fifth in the Olympic 1500m final. Her sister Lucia was also in the Canadian team and finished 13th in the semi-finals. On 11 February 2022 in Boston she ran 14:31.38 for 5000m indoors, an area record for North, Central America and the Caribbean. It beat Flanagan's 2009 mark by more than 15 seconds. In her first championship of that year, the World Indoor Championships in Belgrade, she was fourth over 3000m. In April 2022 she left Portland for Victoria. An injury then ended her season early and ruled her out of the Commonwealth Games and the world championships, and her recovery ran on through 2023. She came back to the world championships in Tokyo in 2025, finishing 11th in the 1500m in 3:59.65. She won the 1500m at the Paavo Nurmi Games in 2025 in 4:02 and again in 2026 in 4:04.40. In June 2026 she took her third straight Canadian 5000m title, her seventh national title in all. She was 14th over 5000m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. In September she went to Copenhagen for the global road championships and clocked a personal best of 4:30.59 over the mile, good for ninth place. On 18 October 2026 she won the Jarrow 10K in South Tyneside in 31:37.8. That broke the Canadian road 10km record of 31:44, set by Lynn Williams in Orlando on 11 March 1989. The course begins and ends inside Hebburn's Monkton Stadium, home track of Steve Cram, with two flat laps of Jarrow's streets in between. She took more than two minutes off the course record of 34:08 and only seven men finished ahead of her. It was her first national record for more than four years and gives her eight current Canadian records. She is now based in Scotland and coached by her husband, Rowan. - [Eilish McColgan: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/eilish-mccolgan): Runners / Eilish McColgan Photo: Agência Brasil Fotografias / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Eilish McColgan Born 1990 (age 35 or 36) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road, Track Eilish McColgan is a Scottish middle- and long-distance runner, born in Dundee on 25 November 1990. She won the 10,000 metres at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham. Her winning time set a new Games record, and she added silver in the 5,000 metres. McColgan is coached by her mother, Liz McColgan, a former 10,000 metres world champion and Olympic silver medallist. Eilish has gone on to break several of her mother's British records, including at 10,000 metres and in the half marathon. She holds the European record for the 10 km on the road and the European best for 10 miles. She also holds British records for the 5,000 metres, 10,000 metres, 5 km and half marathon. McColgan has run at four Olympics, in 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024. In 2025 she made her marathon debut at the London Marathon, finishing eighth in 2:24:25 as the leading British runner. She won the Big Half in London in September 2026, then pulled out of the Great North Run a week later after hurting her foot again. She is an ambassador for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, where she will again represent Scotland. - [Cole Hocker: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/cole-hocker): Runners / Cole Hocker Photo: Quejaytee / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Cole Hocker Born 2001 (age 24 or 25) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Track Cole Hocker is an American middle and long-distance runner, born on 6 June 2001 in Indianapolis. He won 1500 metres gold at the 2024 Paris Olympics. His time of 3:27.65 set an Olympic record and a North American record. He came from behind to beat favourites Josh Kerr, Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Yared Nuguse. It was the first US win in the event since 2016. Hocker added a second global title in 2025. He won the 5000 metres at the World Championships in Tokyo in 12:58.30. It made him the first American world champion at the distance since Bernard Lagat in 2007. He is only the fifth man to hold global titles at both 1500m and 5000m, joining Paavo Nurmi, Hicham El Guerrouj, Ingebrigtsen and Lagat. At the same championships he was disqualified from the 1500 metres semifinal after a jostle with Germany's Robert Farken. Hocker went to Cathedral High School in Indianapolis, where he won the 2018 Foot Locker Cross Country Championships. He then ran for the University of Oregon, winning four NCAA titles between 2019 and 2021. In September 2021 he turned professional, signing with Nike and giving up his remaining college eligibility. He is coached by Ben Thomas and remains based in Oregon. In February 2026 Hocker broke the American record for the short track mile, running 3:45.94. That time is the second fastest in indoor history, behind only Ingebrigtsen's world record. He also holds the North American outdoor record for 1500 metres and the second-fastest short track 3000 metres ever run, at 7:23.14. In September 2026 he finished fourth in the 1500 metres at the inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest, behind winner Josh Kerr, Australia's Cameron Myers and American team-mate Hobbs Kessler. - [Hicham El Guerrouj: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hicham-el-guerrouj): Runners / Hicham El Guerrouj Photo: Sebastien from Montreal, Canada / Wikimedia Commons 🇲🇦 Hicham El Guerrouj Born 1974 Country 🇲🇦 Morocco Runs Track (legend) Hicham El Guerrouj is a retired Moroccan middle-distance runner regarded as one of the greatest 1500 metre runners in history. He won four consecutive 1500 metres world titles, at the 1997, 1999, 2001 and 2003 World Championships, and was named World Athlete of the Year three times. He set the 1500 metres world record of 3:26.00 in Rome in 1998, a mark that still stands. The following year, also in Rome, he broke the mile world record with 3:43.13, a time that lasted until Josh Kerr beat it in London in 2026. At the 2004 Athens Olympics, El Guerrouj won both the 1500 metres and the 5000 metres. He beat American Bernard Lagat by 0.12 seconds in the 1500 final, then denied Kenenisa Bekele the 5000m-10,000m double four days later. He was the first man in 80 years to complete that Olympic double, after Finland's Paavo Nurmi in 1924. He had finished second in the 1500 metres at the 1995 World Championships and the 2000 Sydney Olympics, both times behind rivals he later beat, Noureddine Morceli and Noah Ngeny. El Guerrouj retired in 2006 after his years of high-intensity training caught up with him in a series of injuries. - [Ingrid Kristiansen: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ingrid-kristiansen): Runners / Ingrid Kristiansen Photo: Rob Bogaerts for Anefo / Wikimedia Commons 🇳🇴 Ingrid Kristiansen Born 1956 Country 🇳🇴 Norway Runs Road, Track (legend) Ingrid Kristiansen, born Ingrid Christensen on 21 March 1956, was a Norwegian long-distance runner and one of the dominant women in the sport during the 1980s. Before turning to running she competed as a cross-country skier at elite level, taking multiple Norwegian titles and one European junior title. She became the first athlete, male or female, to win World Championship titles on the track, road and in cross country. Kristiansen once held the world record for the 5,000m, 10,000m and marathon at the same time. At the inaugural women's Olympic marathon, in Los Angeles in 1984, she placed fourth, and she was leading the 10,000m final at the 1988 Seoul Olympics when a fractured bone in her foot forced her out of the race. At the Bislett Games in Oslo she set world records for the 5,000m, in 14 minutes 58.9 seconds in 1984, and the 10,000m, in 30 minutes 59.42 seconds in 1985. In 1985 she also won the London Marathon in a world record of 2:21:06, a mark that stood for 13 years. In 1986, her best year, Kristiansen won the Boston Marathon, then lowered her own 10,000m world record to 30:13.74 and her 5,000m record to 14:37.33. She won the London Marathon four times in total, in 1984, 1985, 1987 and 1988, and also won the Boston Marathon again in 1989 and the New York City Marathon that same year, her final marathon. Kristiansen retired from competition in 1993, having started 26 marathons and won 14 of them. Her 1986 10,000m world record stood for five years, and she also won 24 individual Norwegian championship titles. - [Caitriona Jennings: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/caitriona-jennings): Runners / Caitriona Jennings Photo: photographer unknown 🇮🇪 Caitriona Jennings Born 1980 (age 45 or 46) Country 🇮🇪 Ireland Runs Road, Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 813 (9 November 2026) Caitriona Jennings is an Irish runner from Letterkenny, County Donegal, competing across the marathon and ultra distances. She raced the marathon at the 2012 London Olympics and now holds the world record for the women's 100 miles. Her UTMB Index is 813. Jennings started out as a triathlete who represented Ireland at youth level, and has been coached by Terry McConnon since 2007. She ran a marathon personal best of 2:36:14 at the 2012 Rotterdam Marathon, which earned her Olympic qualification. At the London Games she was part of Ireland's first three-woman Olympic marathon team, though plantar fasciitis and a stress fracture left her finishing last, in 3:22:11. She moved up to ultra distances after 2012. She represented Ireland at the 2015 50km World Championships in Qatar, finishing 4th woman. In 2021 she was 3rd woman in the marathon at the Hong Kong Standard Chartered Marathon in 2:51:31, and in 2022 she won bronze at the IAU 100km World Championships in Bernau bei Berlin with an Irish record of 7:07:16. The same year she was 2nd woman at both the JFK 50 Mile and the Lake Sonoma 50. On 9 November 2025 Jennings set the women's 100-mile world record at the Tunnel Hill 100 Mile in Vienna, Illinois, finishing in 12:37:04. She opened 2026 by placing 11th woman at the Canyons Endurance Runs 50K. - [Cameron Myers: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/cameron-myers): Runners / Cameron Myers Photo: Gary Zuccala / Wikimedia Commons 🇦🇺 Cameron Myers Born 2006 (age 19 or 20) Country 🇦🇺 Australia Runs Track Cameron Myers, born 9 June 2006, is an Australian middle-distance runner from Canberra. He trained under Lee Bobbin from the age of ten, then joined Dick Telford's group alongside Olympic 1500m runner Jye Edwards. He now runs for the Bankstown Track Club in Sydney. Myers broke four minutes for the mile in February 2023, aged sixteen, running 3:55.44 at the Maurie Plant Meet in Melbourne. It made him the second youngest person ever to run a sub-four-minute mile and beat Jakob Ingebrigtsen's age-16 record by more than two seconds. That July he ran 1500 metres in 3:33.26 at the Diamond League meeting in Silesia, the fastest recorded by an under-18 athlete. In September he paced Ingebrigtsen to a European mile record of 3:43.73 at the Diamond League final in Eugene, Oregon. Myers took silver in the 1500 metres at the 2024 World Athletics Under-20 Championships in Lima. In February 2025 he broke his own world indoor under-20 mile record, running 3:47.48 at the Millrose Games in New York, then the fifth fastest indoor mile ever run. That June he clocked 3:29.80 for 1500 metres at the Golden Spike meeting in Ostrava, an Oceania mark for his age group, and raced at the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo without reaching the semi-finals. In January 2026 Myers ran the fastest mile recorded that month anywhere, 3:49.81, in Seattle. The following week he ran 7:27.57 for 3000 metres indoors in Boston. That made him only the fourth man under 20 to break 7:28 for the distance, after Eliud Kipchoge, Jacob Kiplimo and Jakob Ingebrigtsen. He won the 1500 metres at the Diamond League final in Brussels that September, edging Phanuel Koech of Kenya by four hundredths of a second. He was runner-up to new mile world record holder Josh Kerr at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, and again at the inaugural World Ultimate Championship in Budapest. - [Matthew Ramsden: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/matthew-ramsden): Runners / Matthew Ramsden Photo: Martin Rulsch, Wikimedia Commons / Wikimedia Commons Matthew Ramsden Runs Matthew Ramsden is a British cross-country runner who races for Blackburn Harriers. His most notable result on these pages came at Llandaff Fields in Cardiff on Sunday 8 November. He won the senior men's title at the Cardiff Cross Challenge there. The 9.6km race opened the three-round Cross Challenge Series run by British Athletics. In the early stages a big group gathered behind Western Tempo's Jacob Cann, who set the pace. Ramsden and James Kingston of Tonbridge AC stayed close to the front from start to finish. Kadar Omar of Birchfield Harriers went with them on the final lap before Ramsden and Kingston pulled clear. With about 150 metres to run, Ramsden missed the turn for the home straight. He followed the line meant for slower runners still on their penultimate lap and had to jump the course tape twice to get back on the right route. Kingston appeared to have the race won. Ramsden still caught him and crossed the line in 27:26. Kingston was two seconds back in 27:28. Third place went to Omar in 27:39. Cann came home five seconds later in 27:44 to take fourth. It was Ramsden's first time at the Cardiff race. He had heard the ground there was usually firm and dry, and that was how he found it. He called the course "gutsy" and said he was pleased with the outcome. The series continues at Sefton Park in Liverpool on 28 November. That round is also the trial for Britain's team at the European Cross Country Championships in Belgrade. He shares his name with an Australian middle-distance runner, born in 1997, who won the 1500m at the 2019 Oceania Championships in Townsville. That athlete also ran the 1500m at the World Championships the same year. - [Rory Linkletter: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rory-linkletter): Runners / Rory Linkletter Photo: 4300streetcar / Wikimedia Commons Rory Linkletter Runs Rory Linkletter is a Canadian distance runner who races the marathon and the half marathon on the roads. He was born in Calgary, Alberta on 12 August 1996 and moved to Herriman, Utah when he was five. He only started running as a freshman at Herriman High School, after a friend took him along to a summer practice. From there he went to Brigham Young University and raced track and cross country for the Cougars. He lives and trains in Flagstaff, Arizona. His college years took him around the world. He was 84th in the junior race at the 2015 World Cross Country Championships in Guiyang, China. Two years later he was 76th in the senior race in Kampala, Uganda. On the track he finished second over 10,000m at the 2017 NCAA Championships, 1.42 seconds behind Marc Scott. In his final season for BYU he lowered his bests to 13:36.41 for 5000m and 28:12.42 for 10,000m. He turned professional in 2019 with Hoka and joined the Northern Arizona Elite group under Ben Rosario. That summer he was sixth over 10,000m at the Pan American Games in Lima. Ten weeks later he made his marathon debut in Toronto in 2:16:42. He took four minutes off that with 2:12:54 at the Marathon Project in Chandler, Arizona in December 2020. A difficult Boston in 2021 ended in 33rd place in 2:23:34. He answered it with second place at the California International Marathon in 2:12:52. In 2022 he signed with Puma and began working with coach Ryan Hall, still based in Flagstaff. He ran a Canadian half marathon record of 1:01:08 in Houston that January. At the World Championships in Eugene he was 20th in 2:10:24, the second Canadian home behind Cam Levins and his national record of 2:07:09. In the humid heat of Budapest a year later he finished 18th in 2:12:16. He also broke four minutes for the mile that autumn, running 3:59.05 in Boston to become the 74th Canadian under the barrier. In February 2024 he ran 2:08:01 in Seville, inside the Olympic standard of 2:08:10. The best results have come in 2026. He lowered the Canadian half marathon record to 59:49 in Houston. He then ran 2:06:04 at the Boston Marathon, which puts him second on the Canadian all-time list behind Levins, whose national record stands at 2:05:36. On Sunday 11 October he appeared at the Chicago Marathon despite not being on the elite start list. He was there as a pacer for the American Dakotah Popehn, who ran a personal best of 2:24:00. Linkletter was timed at 2:23:59. - [Kate Axford: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kate-axford): Runners / Kate Axford Photo: Hildreth gazzard / Wikimedia Commons Kate Axford Runs Kate Axford is a British cross country and distance runner from Bedford who races for Belgrave Harriers. Born on 31 March 1999, she came to athletics late. Hockey came first, and she was good at it. She played for England at under-16, under-18 and under-21 level and won European bronze with the under-21 side in Valencia in 2017. She later played in the Premier Division for Wimbledon and was contracted to the senior Great Britain squad in 2022. After leaving hockey she went back to a sport she had last tried at school nine years before. Belgrave coaches noticed her at a 5km in Battersea Park. Her first track 5000m came at the Comeback 5000 in Battersea that April of 2023, and she won it in 15:48.79. Later that year she won a 3000m on her Team England debut at Loughborough. It was also her first race over the distance. In November she was eighth for England at the Cross Italica in Seville. Her progress in 2024 was quick. At the UK Indoor Championships that February, held in Birmingham, she ran a 3000m personal best of 9:08.43 to finish third. In June she ran 15:19.40 for fourth in the 5000m at the British Championships in Manchester. That November she was third at the Cardiff Cross Challenge, then won the senior women's race at the Liverpool Cross Challenge, which also served as the British trial for the European Championships. In Antalya she finished tenth and helped Britain to team silver. Since then she has been a fixture of the Belgrave relay squad. She ran the last leg in Mansfield as the club won a third straight English national relays title, and she ran in all three of those wins. On 18 September 2026 she lowered her mile best to 4:26.96 at Athlos in London. Eight days later she won the UK and English road mile titles at the Westminster Mile in 4:23. That equalled the course record held by Katie Snowden and put her ahead of the defending champion, Holly Dixon. On 8 November 2026 she returned to Cardiff and won the 6.4km senior women's race at Llandaff Fields. She and Amelia Quirk of Bracknell AC were both given 20:37 after Axford resisted a late push. Rebecca Flaherty was third in 20:40 and Laura Muir fifth in 20:50. It was her first race in Cardiff for two years, a period she said had brought a run of setbacks and injuries. She put the decisive last 30 seconds down to her 1500m speed. The series next moves to Sefton Park in Liverpool on 28 November, the trial for Britain's team at the European Cross Country Championships in Belgrade. - [Likina Amebaw: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/likina-amebaw): Runners / Likina Amebaw Photo: Ssu / Wikimedia Commons Likina Amebaw Runs Likina Amebaw is an Ethiopian long-distance runner, born on 30 November 1997. She races cross country, road and track, and she has won on all three. She is based in Peguerinos, in the Spanish province of Ávila, and competes for the Playas de Castellón club. In September 2026 she won two global titles in the space of six days. Her early wins came over the country. She won the Almond Blossom Cross Country in Albufeira in April 2021 and won there again in February 2023. In October 2023 she took the first Gold event of the World Athletics Cross Country Tour season at the Cross Zornotza in Amorebieta. A month later she won the Cross Internacional de Soria. She was second at the San Silvestre Vallecana in January 2024 and won a 10km road race in Paris that April in a personal best of 29:56. On the track she was runner-up over 3000m at the Bislett Games in Oslo in May 2024, in 8:24.29. In 2025 she won the Monaco Run 5km in 14:33 and lowered her 5000m best to 14:30.54 at the Xiamen Diamond League. She finished second to Faith Kipyegon over 3000m in Poland in 8:34.53, then second to Agnes Ngetich over 5000m in Brussels. On 28 August she took third over 3000m when the Diamond League season ended in Zurich. The winter brought a run of fast road times. Her 14:23 to win the Cursa dels Nassos 5km in Barcelona on 31 December put her fifth on the all-time list. On 11 January 2026 she ran 29:30 for 10km in Valencia, second to Brenda Jepchirchir and sixth on the world all-time list. She won the Berlin Half Marathon on 29 March in 1:05:07. On the track in 2026 she ran a 5000m best of 14:24.21 in Shanghai, again behind Kipyegon. She improved it to 14:18.41 to win at the Golden Gala in Rome on 4 June. She was second at the Diamond League Final in Brussels on 4 September, between Freweyni Hailu and Senayet Getachew in an Ethiopian clean sweep. Nine days later she won the 5000m at the first World Ultimate Championship in Budapest in 14:30.36, a Hungarian all-comers' record, pulling well clear in the closing stages. On 19 September in Copenhagen she won the 5km at the World Athletics Road Running Championships, ahead of Kenya's Caroline Gitonga. She added mixed team gold with Aleshign Baweke, Addisu Yihune and Mezgebu Sime. She was runner-up in the overall standings when the 2025-26 cross country tour wrapped up, and she is back on the country this autumn. She won in Amorebieta again on 18 October. On 8 November she won the Cross Internacional de Itálica at Santiponce, near Seville, on a course that loops past the Roman amphitheatre. She had been third there a year earlier. This time she attacked at the start of the last lap, with 2.5km left, and broke away on the climb to win in 30:41. Uganda's Charity Cherop was eight seconds back in second. Next up for her is the Cinque Mulini, the Italian cross country classic, on 22 November. His UTMB win in 2023 was a first for an American man, and he set a course record of 19:37:43 doing it. His general UTMB Index is 961. He came to the trails from the track. At the Air Force Academy, between 2008 and 2012, he captained the cross country team and ran 13:52 for 5000m. Western States is his race. In May 2019 he ran 50 miles in 4:50:07, a world best that beat Bruce Fordyce's time by 14 seconds. He was named UltraRunner of the Year four years running from 2016, then again in 2023 and 2025. In 2025 he won the long trail race at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, 81 km in 8:35:11, and the OCC at Chamonix. - [Steve Ovett: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/steve-ovett): Runners / Steve Ovett Photo: Jeremy Gilbert aka Canada Jack / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Steve Ovett Born 1955 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track (legend) Steve Ovett was a British middle-distance runner who won 45 consecutive 1500m and mile races between 1977 and 1980. He set five world records at 1500m and the mile, plus a world best at two miles, and formed one half of British athletics' defining rivalry of the era with Sebastian Coe. Ovett won 800m gold at the 1978 European Championships, beating Coe into third, then took gold in the 1500m at the same meeting. He arrived at the 1980 Moscow Olympics unbeaten over 1500m and the mile for three years. He won the 800m final by outsprinting Coe in the closing metres, then had to settle for 1500m bronze six days later as Coe took gold. He pushed his mile world record to 3:48.8 in 1980 and matched Coe's 1500m mark of 3:32.1 before setting a new record of 3:31.36 later that year. In 1981 he and Coe traded world records over the mile three times inside nine days without racing each other. A world record of 3:30.77 for 1500m followed in Rieti in 1983. Injury and illness disrupted his later career. He finished eighth in the 800m at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics after suffering respiratory problems, then collapsed and was hospitalised, and dropped out of the 1500m final days later. He won 5000m gold at the 1986 Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh before retiring in 1991. Ovett has worked as a track and field commentator for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation since 1992 and lives in Australia. A statue of him stands in Brighton, his home city. - [Judith Wyder: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/judith-wyder): Runners / Judith Wyder Photo: Dnikitin / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇭 Judith Wyder Born 1988 (age 37 or 38) Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 818 (9 November 2026) Judith Wyder is a Swiss trail and sky runner, born on 25 June 1988. She was a leading orienteer before switching to trail running in 2019. As a junior she won medals in both orienteering and ski orienteering. She later became Switzerland's leading female orienteer after Simone Niggli's retirement. Wyder won relay gold at the 2012 World Orienteering Championships in Lausanne. Two years later she took individual gold in both the sprint and the long distance at the European Orienteering Championships in Portugal. That same year she added three more golds and a bronze at the World Orienteering Championships. She won further medals at the 2018 World Orienteering Championships in Riga, taking sprint bronze and sprint relay silver. Wyder moved into trail and skyrunning in 2019 and made an immediate impact. She won the Ring of Steall Skyrace in a course record and set another course record at the DoloMyths Run. She was runner-up at Sierre-Zinal, then won the Annapurna Trail Marathon to clinch the women's title in that year's Golden Trail World Series. She won silver, individually and with the Swiss team, in the short trail race at the 2023 World Trail Running Championships in Innsbruck-Stubai. She has since been a regular podium finisher at UTMB Mont-Blanc's OCC race, taking second in both 2024 and 2025. In 2026 she won the trail race at the European Off-Road Running Championships and finished second at the Chianti Ultra Trail. He won the Skyrunner World Series Vertical Kilometre title in 2015 and the Golden Trail Series overall in 2022. Bonnet has won some of the sport's biggest single races. In 2025 he added the uphill title at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. Bonnet remains a regular winner in the sport's shorter mountain races. He won the Restonica Trail in Corsica in 2024 and opened 2026 by winning the Marathon du Mont-Blanc 42km again, in 3:33:14. At Sierre-Zinal, one of the sport's classic races, his best finish is third, from 2020. - [John Birmingham: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/john-birmingham): Runners / John Birmingham Photo: CraigPRichmond / Wikimedia Commons John Birmingham Runs John Birmingham is a cross-country runner with Salford, the club that dominates the North of England relay scene. His sources on record are thin. The one race documented here is a two-mile relay leg in Sheffield, and it was a useful one. The race was the Cutlers Relay at the North of England cross-country relays, held at Graves Park on Saturday 17 October 2026. The men's event is four legs of two miles each. The ground was dry and the sky bright, though the wind made itself felt. Birmingham was given the first leg for Salford A and came back in 10:08. Only three men in the field ran a quicker lap all afternoon. His teammates then had some work to do. Salford's own B team took the lead on the second leg through Sam Hopkins, who ran 10:11 and gained 26 seconds on the A team's Bryn Lawrence. Harry Wakefield put Salford A back in front over the next two miles. Nobody in the field went quicker than his 9:42. David Barratt brought the A team home in 10:26 with Thomas Manton chasing for the B team. Salford A finished in 40:54, just seven seconds clear of their clubmates. Gateshead were third in 41:31 and 47 teams completed the course. The win meant Salford's men kept the title they already held. For Birmingham it is the first and only result on these pages so far. Readers searching his name will also find a Liverpool-born Australian novelist, born in 1964 and known for He Died with a Felafel in His Hand. That is a different John Birmingham, and nothing in the record links the writer to the Salford relay runner. - [Marco Olmo: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/marco-olmo): Runners / Marco Olmo Photo: Francesco Canu / Wikimedia Commons 🇮🇹 Marco Olmo Born 1948 Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra, Road (legend) UTMB Index 500 (9 November 2026) Marco Olmo is an Italian ultra-trail runner born on 8 October 1948. He worked as a labourer throughout his life while racing on the side, and began winning major ultra-distance events in 1996. Olmo finished third at the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc in 2005, in 21 hours 49 minutes and 57 seconds. He won the race outright in 2006, aged 58, in 21 hours 6 minutes and 6 seconds. He won again in 2007, aged 59, clocking 21 hours 31 minutes and 58 seconds. He also won the Transgrancanaria in the Canary Islands in 2008. Olmo ran the Marathon des Sables across the Sahara almost every year from 1996, finishing 11th overall in 2011 at the age of 62. In November 2017, aged 69, he won the Africa Race, a record age for the event. Olmo's personal best over 24 hours on the road is 199.931km, set at the IAU 24 Hours in Gravigny, France. He kept competing into his late seventies, running local Italian trail races such as the Garda Trentino Castle Run in 2026. - [Hannah Allgood: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hannah-allgood): Runners / Hannah Allgood Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Hannah Allgood Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra Hannah Allgood is an American ultrarunner based in Colorado Springs, Colorado. She works as a physical therapist, a background she credits with helping her avoid injuries. Running came late for her. As a child she played soccer and basketball rather than running competitively. She moved to Colorado in 2016 and took up trail running only after that. She won the Blue Sky Marathon in Fort Collins in 2022, setting a course record of 3:33. Her first 100-mile race was the Javelina Jundred in Arizona in 2024, where she finished second. In 2025 she finished seventh in the women's race at the Western States 100, in 17:39:02. Allgood returned to the Western States 100 in June 2026, finishing 10th in 16:45:56. Weeks later she won the Run Rabbit Run 100 in Steamboat Springs, setting a course record of 19:01:59. Her time beat the previous record, set by Canada's Emilie Mann in 2024, by about 46 minutes. It was only her fourth 100-mile race. The win earned Allgood $20,000. She said the result felt affirming, and that getting back into the mountains was what she loves most about the sport. Run Rabbit Run's organisers have since raised the prize fund, so future winners of the race will earn $100,000 each in 2027 and 2028. - [Scott Jurek: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/scott-jurek): Runners / Scott Jurek Photo: Windriverwild / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Scott Jurek Born 1973 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Scott Jurek is an American ultramarathon runner who dominated trail racing in the 2000s. He won the Western States 100 Mile Endurance Run seven years running, from 1999 to 2005. He beat five-time champion Tim Twietmeyer on his first attempt in 1999. In 2004 he lowered his own course record to 15 hours 36 minutes, a mark that stood for six years. He won the Badwater Ultramarathon twice, in 2005 and 2006, in temperatures of 49C. Jurek dealt with the heat by stopping to cool off in an ice-filled cooler. He then won the Spartathlon three years running, from 2006 to 2008, over the 246km route from Athens to Sparta. The Hardrock Hundred fell to him in 2007, with a new course record that stood for a year. In 2010, Jurek won silver at the 24-Hour World Championships, held that year in Brive-la-Gaillarde, France. He ran 165.7 miles (266.7km), an American record, finishing behind Japan's Shingo Inoue. Four years earlier he had narrowly lost a Copper Canyon race to Tarahumara runner Arnulfo Quimare. Christopher McDougall wrote about the race in his bestselling book Born to Run. Jurek returned to the Copper Canyon in 2007 and won it. Rickey Gates joined Jurek in 2014 to become the first North Americans to finish the Lake District's Bob Graham Round in under a day. The following year he set a supported speed record on the 2,168-mile Appalachian Trail. He finished in 46 days, 8 hours and 7 minutes, three hours faster than the previous mark. Jurek gave up meat in 1997 and turned vegan in 1999, crediting plant-based eating as central to his performance and recovery. - [Mary Denholm: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mary-denholm): Runners / Mary Denholm 🇺🇸 Mary Denholm Born 1987 (age 38 or 39) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 784 (27 September 2026) Mary Denholm is an American ultrarunner from Sparks, Maryland, now based in Colorado. She ran collegiately at Saint Michael's College and was the 2008 Vermont state cross country champion across all divisions. She spent six years away from competitive running during law school and an early career as a trial attorney, before returning to the sport in 2015. She is a two-time qualifier for the US Olympic Trials Marathon, finishing 51st in 2020. Qualifying again for the 2024 trials took three attempts. She ran the 2022 Boston Marathon, was unable to compete at Grandma's Marathon in 2023, and qualified that December at the California International Marathon, clocking her marathon best of 2:36:28. Denholm made an immediate impact when she moved to trail ultrarunning in 2024, her first year at the distance. She won the Leadville Trail Marathon and the Leadville Silver Rush 50 that summer, then took the Leadville Trail 100 in August in 18:23:51, the second-fastest women's time in the race's history behind Ann Trason's 1994 mark. She finished more than three hours ahead of the runner-up. She was second woman at the JFK 50 Mile in November 2024, in 06:04:15, then won the women's race at the Kodiak 100K in October 2025, in 09:28:28. Ultra Running Magazine ranked her the seventh-best US ultrarunner of 2024. Denholm coaches for Lift Run Perform alongside her own racing, and fuels her ultras aggressively, taking on more than 100 grams of carbohydrate an hour. - [Jake Wightman: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jake-wightman): Runners / Jake Wightman Photo: Sandro Halank / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Jake Wightman Born 1994 (age 31 or 32) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track Jake Wightman is a British middle-distance runner, born on 11 July 1994, who competes mainly over 1500 metres. He won the world title at the 2022 Championships in Eugene, Oregon. His time of 3:29.23 was a personal best and beat Olympic champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen. It was the first global middle-distance gold for a British man since Seb Coe's 1500 metres win in 1984. Wightman was troubled by injury for the two years after his world title. He withdrew from the 2023 World Championships in Budapest with Achilles, shin and hamstring problems, handing his title to training partner and childhood friend Josh Kerr. He also pulled out of the 2024 Paris Olympics 800 metres with a hamstring injury. In 2025 he returned to form, winning silver in the 1500 metres at the World Championships, becoming the first British athlete to win two medals in the event there. Wightman was born in England but grew up in Linlithgow and represents Scotland internationally. His father Geoff Wightman is a former marathon runner who commentated on his son's 2022 world title race from the stadium. His mother Susan Tooby and aunt Angela Tooby both competed for Great Britain at the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Wightman is engaged to the former Irish international runner Georgie Hartigan. Wightman holds Scottish records over 800 metres, 1000 metres and the mile. In July 2026 he ran 2:12.77 for 1000 metres at the Monaco Diamond League, finishing second to Emmanuel Wanyonyi's world record. In September 2026 he was ninth in the 1500 metres at the inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest, in 3:31.56. - [Andreas Almgren: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/andreas-almgren): Runners / Andreas Almgren Photo: Frankie Fouganthin / Wikimedia Commons 🇸🇪 Andreas Almgren Born 1995 (age 30 or 31) Country 🇸🇪 Sweden Runs Road, Track Andreas Almgren is a Swedish long-distance runner born on 12 June 1995. He started out as an 800m runner and has moved steadily up in distance. In 2026 he won the European 10,000m title, the world half marathon title and the New York City Marathon. Away from the track he has had a job analysing data for Svexa, a firm working in sports technology. His first podium came as a teenager, with 800m bronze at the 2014 World Junior Championships in Eugene, Oregon. He qualified for the 5,000m at the 2024 Olympics and travelled to Paris, but a lingering shinbone injury forced him out before he could race. In June 2025 he ran 12:44.27 over 5,000m in Stockholm, a European record. He also took bronze in the 10,000m at the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo. In August 2026 he took the European 10,000m crown in Birmingham, running 27:23.44 to set a championship record. The world half marathon in Copenhagen followed in September 2026. Almgren was only ninth at 5km and worked his way forward as the pace rose. With 3km left it was down to him, Kenya's Nicholas Kipkorir and Uganda's Joshua Cheptegei. Cheptegei fell away first and Almgren beat Kipkorir in the sprint. His 58:06 was a European record and took 35 seconds off the 58:41 he had run in Valencia the year before. He became the first man from outside Africa to win the title since Italy's Stefano Baldini in 1996. Rodrigue Kwizera ran 58:03 in Valencia in October, but World Athletics has yet to clear his switch to Spain, so the European record stays with Almgren. On 1 November 2026 Almgren ran his first marathon, in New York, aged 31. He had never covered 26.2 miles before, even in training. Fifteen men were together at 35km until the defending champion Benson Kipruto ran the 24th mile in 4:38. That left Almgren, Kipruto and Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa. Almgren hit the front for the first time just before 40km, then surged again on Central Park South to drop Crippa. He jogged the last few metres, waving to the crowd, and finished in 2:06:01, 13 seconds clear. He was the first European-born man to win the race since Italy's Giacomo Leone in 1996. He said it was probably the most emotional he had ever been at the end of a race. His other bests include 3:32.00 for 1500m, Swedish records of 7:26.48 for 3000m and 26:52.87 for 10,000m, and 26:45 for 10km on the road in Valencia, a European record. He chose New York for his debut because the course races like a championship. The Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 are the target he had in mind. - [Charlie Lawrence: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/charlie-lawrence): Runners / Charlie Lawrence Photo: photographer unknown 🇺🇸 Charlie Lawrence Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road Charlie Lawrence is an American road ultrarunner who holds the world record for 50 miles, 4:48:21, and the American record for 100km, 6:07:10. In September 2026 he won the IAU 100km World Championships in Ames, Spain, in 6:09:25, going past early leader Masato Tanaka of Japan on the tenth of nineteen 5km laps. He reached halfway in 3:00:34 and briefly looked capable of chasing down Aleksandr Sorokin's outright world record of 6:05:35, before his own laps slowed past the 15th. He still held off Sorokin, the Lithuanian world record holder, who finished second and also took the World Masters Athletics 100km title contested within the same race. The event drew 147 men from 44 countries in temperatures that rose from 16C to 32C. Lawrence had already raced South Africa's Comrades Marathon in 2026, finishing sixth over the roughly 89km course. - [Emil Zátopek: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/emil-zatopek): Runners / Emil Zátopek Photo: Roger Rössing / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇿 Emil Zátopek Born 1922 Country 🇨🇿 Czechia Runs Track, Road (legend) Emil Zátopek was a Czech long-distance runner known as the "Czech Locomotive" for his relentless, grimacing running style. At the 1952 Helsinki Olympics he won gold in the 5,000 metres, the 10,000 metres and the marathon, a treble no one else has matched at a single Games. He entered the marathon on a last-minute whim, having never raced the distance before, and won it by more than two minutes. Zátopek broke the 10,000 metres world record five times between 1949 and 1954, becoming the first runner to go under 29 minutes for the distance in 1954. In 1951 he became the first to run more than 20 kilometres inside an hour. He also set world records at 5,000 metres, 20,000 metres, 25,000 metres and 30,000 metres. He is credited with popularising interval training after the Second World War, and trained through all weathers, at times in heavy work boots rather than running shoes. At the 1948 London Olympics he won the 10,000 metres and took silver in the 5,000 metres. He tried to defend his Olympic marathon title in 1956, but a groin injury in training left him hospitalised for six weeks. He finished sixth, behind his rival and friend Alain Mimoun, and retired from competition in 1957. Zátopek was known for his generosity to fellow athletes. In 1966 he gave one of his 1952 Olympic gold medals to the Australian Ron Clarke, a multiple world record holder who had never won Olympic gold. Zátopek died in Prague in 2000, aged 78. - [Joss Naylor: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joss-naylor): Runners / Joss Naylor Photo: Torpenhow3 / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Joss Naylor Born 1936 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Joss Naylor was an English fell runner and sheep farmer from the Lake District, known as the King of the Fells. Born Joseph Naylor on 10 February 1936, he grew up on his family's farm at Wasdale Head and left school at 15 to work the land. Knee surgery at 19 and back surgery at 22 followed injuries in his youth. He took up running in 1960, aged 24, and won his first race, the Mountain Trial, in 1966. Naylor completed the Bob Graham Round in 1971, becoming only the sixth person to do so. That year he also set a new peak-bagging record within the round, covering 61 peaks in 23 hours 37 minutes. He extended it to 63 peaks in 1972 and then to 72 peaks in 1975, a route of more than 100 miles and about 38,000 feet of climbing completed in 23 hours 20 minutes. The 1975 record stood for 13 years and Naylor called it his greatest achievement. Naylor set records across a range of British endurance challenges. In 1973 he ran the 14 peaks of the Welsh 3000s in 4 hours 46 minutes, and in 1974 he covered the Pennine Way in 3 days, 4 hours and 36 minutes. At 50, in 1986, he completed the Wainwrights round in 7 days, 1 hour and 25 minutes, a record that stood until 2014. He kept setting fell challenges into old age, running 60 Lakeland tops in 1996 at 60 and 70 tops in 2006 at 70. Naylor was appointed MBE in 1976 for services to fell running. Chris Brasher, co-founder of the London Marathon, called him 'the greatest of them all' after his 72-peak run. Naylor later created his own event, the Joss Naylor Lakeland Challenge, a 48-mile route for runners over 50 with 17,000 feet of climbing. He died on 28 June 2024, aged 88, at a care home in Gosforth, Cumbria, after a period of ill health. - [Masai Russell: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/masai-russell): Runners / Masai Russell Photo: Quejaytee / Wikimedia Commons Masai Russell Runs Masai Russell is an American sprint hurdler and the world record holder for the 100m hurdles. She was born on 17 June 2000. She went to Bullis School and then the University of Kentucky, where she graduated in Health Science in 2023. The short hurdles are her event, though she has also raced the 400m hurdles to a best of 54.66. Indoors she has run 7.74 for the 60m hurdles. Her college years built steadily. In 2021 she was sixth in the NCAA Division I 100m hurdles final and fourth over 400m hurdles in 56.18. A year later she was third and fourth over the same two events. In 2023 she ran 7.75 for the 60m hurdles, taking the collegiate record from Grace Stark's 7.78. That April, at the Texas Relays, she set a collegiate 100m hurdles record of 12.36. She then turned professional and placed third at the US championships. At the World Championships in Budapest she reached the semi-finals but hit a hurdle and did not finish. In 2024 she was fourth over 60m hurdles at the World Indoor Championships. She won the US Olympic Trials in a personal best of 12.25. In Paris she took Olympic gold in 12.33, just ahead of France's Cyréna Samba-Mayela. On 2 May 2025 she ran an American record of 12.17 at the Grand Slam Track meeting in Miami. She won the US title in 12.22 in August. At the World Championships she won her heat and semi-final but finished fourth in the final. This year has gone rather better. She ran 12.14 to win in Xiamen in May. She then won in Los Angeles in 12.26 and at the Prefontaine Classic in 12.24, equalling the meet record. On 27 August at the Zürich Diamond League she ran 12.09. That took 0.03 seconds off the 12.12 Tobi Amusan set in 2022. It was her 11th straight win in the event. Afterwards she reckoned a 1.9 wind behind her could have produced a "sub-12 race". She also said she believes she can be the first woman under 12 seconds. In September the Diamond League Final came to Brussels, and she took that title for the first time with 12.20. She then won the inaugural World Ultimate Championship in Budapest in 12.22. She was unbeaten over 100m hurdles all year, broke 12.30 nine times and ran nine of the season's ten fastest times. On 6 October she was named among the ten women nominated for World Athlete of the Year. Voting closes on 17 October, and the winners will be announced in Monaco on 29 November. - [Abebe Bikila: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/abebe-bikila): Runners / Abebe Bikila Photo: Anefo Derivative work MagentaGreen / Wikimedia Commons 🇪🇹 Abebe Bikila Born 1932 Country 🇪🇹 Ethiopia Runs Road (legend) Abebe Bikila was an Ethiopian marathon runner who became his country's first Olympic gold medallist. At the 1960 Rome Olympics he won the marathon running barefoot, clocking 2:15:16.2 and breaking the world record. Four years later in Tokyo he defended his title, this time in Puma running shoes, finishing in 2:12:11.2. He remains one of only three men to win consecutive Olympic marathon titles, alongside Waldemar Cierpinski and Eliud Kipchoge. Bikila served in Ethiopia's Imperial Guard before his running career began, and was trained by the Swedish coach Onni Niskanen. He ran 16 marathons in total, winning 12 of them. His only defeat in an international marathon came at the 1963 Boston Marathon, where he finished fifth in 2:24:43 after fading in the Newton hills. A hamstring injury sustained in July 1967 troubled him for the rest of his career. His last completed marathon was the 1966 Incheon-Seoul race. At the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, racing with a fractured fibula, he dropped out after about 16 kilometres while chasing a third consecutive gold. His teammate Mamo Wolde went on to win the race. Bikila is credited as a pioneer of East African distance running. The New York Road Runners' Abebe Bikila Award, given since to Mamo Wolde, Tegla Loroupe, Paul Tergat and Haile Gebrselassie among others, recognises the athletes who followed him. A car accident in March 1969 left him paralysed, and he never competed again. He died in 1973, aged 41, and Ethiopia held a state funeral in his honour. - [Jemima Farley: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jemima-farley): Runners / Jemima Farley Photo: James Mackenzie / Inverness Courier 🇬🇧 Jemima Farley Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 748 (9 November 2026) Jemima Farley is a British trail runner and family doctor living in Malta. Before 2026 she was better known on the UK fell and cross-country circuits than on the international trail scene, but her results around the Mediterranean have steadily changed that. Gozo has become something of a home course. She has won the 52km XTERRA Gozo Trails race, with 1,450m of climb, four times. Her winning time has fallen with each win, from 4:56:04 in 2021 to 4:43:22 in 2024, 4:27:56 in 2025 and 4:20:01 in 2026. In the 2026 race she started cautiously through the early technical descents. She then pulled away from New Zealand's Charlotte McMeeken from around 35km and won by just over four minutes. Her biggest title came in Wales in 2025. She won the 44km XTERRA Snowdonia Trail Marathon, which doubled as the XTERRA World Championship Marathon, in 4:34:37 over 1,694m of climb. She has also won the 24km Etna Trail Sicilia twice, in 2:48:53 in 2022 and 2:45:53 in 2024. Her other wins include the Akamas Trail Running Festival 38k in 2022 in 3:16:05, the Valtellina Wine Trail 21km in 2024 in 1:46:43 and the Arezzo Wild Trail 23K in 2025 in 2:00:12. She was fourth at the 50km Castellaneta Underground Trail at Puglia by UTMB in 2025, in 4:25:59. In 2026 she won the 54km Ultra Malta Trail in 4:49:21. She then stepped up to the 60km HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc OCC, finishing 22nd woman. The course carried 3,500m of climb, more than double anything in her Gozo wins, and she finished in 6:59:11. - [Buze Diriba: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/buze-diriba): Runners / Buze Diriba Photo: Erik van Leeuwen, attribution: Erik van Leeuwen (bron: Wikipedia). / Wikimedia Commons Buze Diriba Runs Buze Diriba Kejela is an Ethiopian distance runner, born on 9 February 1994. She has raced on the track, on the roads and over cross country. She came through as a teenager on the track, spent years on the American road circuit and is now among the quickest marathon runners in history. Her junior record was strong. She was world junior champion in 2012. At the IAAF World Cross Country Championships she ran the junior race twice. She was 10th in 2011, when Ethiopia took team gold without her counting among the scorers. Two years later she was ninth and helped her country to team silver. She was sixth at the 2012 African Cross Country Championships, where Ethiopia won the junior team title. Senior results followed quickly. On her Diamond League debut in 2012 she was third over 3000m at the Herculis meeting, and she finished that season by winning the Giro Podistico di Pettinengo. In 2013 she placed in the top six at Diamond League meetings in Shanghai, Eugene, Oslo and Paris. She was fifth in the 5000m at the 2013 World Championships. Her track bests include 8:39.65 for 3000m from 2012 and 14:50.02 for 5000m from 2013. Her times stalled on the track in 2014 and she moved to the roads, mostly in the United States. In 2015 she won the Shamrockin' Run and the Parkersburg Half Marathon. She also made the top three at the Freihofer's Run for Women and the Carrera de la Mujer. In 2016 she won the Crescent City Classic and was second at the Cherry Blossom Ten Mile Run, the BAA 5K and the Peachtree Road Race. She also won the Rock 'n' Roll Philadelphia Half Marathon that year in 1:11:49, ahead of Neely Spence Gracey. Her biggest win came on Sunday 18 October 2026 at the Amsterdam Marathon. In cold rain she ran 2:16:12 to win by almost a minute. That took 40 seconds off the course record of 2:16:52 set by Yalemzerf Yehualaw in 2024. It was also a Dutch all-comers' record. She ran the second half faster than the first, pulling away from the defending champion Aynalem Desta after 30km. She arrived in Amsterdam with a best of 2:19:34, so the gain was over three minutes. Within a year she had now broken 2:20 on three occasions. The run moved her, at 32, to 16th on the world all-time list. - [Karlie Janes: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/karlie-janes): Runners / Karlie Janes KJ 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 526 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Karlie Janes Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 526 (9 November 2026) Karlie Janes is a Canadian trail runner from Guelph, Ontario. She races everything from short, hilly loops to 50K mountain courses. Her general UTMB Index stands at 526. Her best result on the longer trails came at the Sulphur Springs Trail Race in 2025. She finished the 50K in 4:47:57 and took third place among the women. That course covered 50 km with 1,225 m of climb. In 2026 she lined up for the Eryri 50K at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia by UTMB. The race measured 56 km and carried 3,400 m of ascent, almost three times the climbing of Sulphur Springs. Janes reached the finish in 10:35:58 and placed 51st woman. Closer to home, she won the women's 12.5K at the first Hustle at Pinehurst in 52:18. The race revives the old Run for the Toad at the Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area near Cambridge, Ontario. Each 12.5K lap has more than 250 metres of climb on rolling, cross-country style ground. A new event has no earlier times to beat, so her 52:18 is now the women's record for the distance. The event is run by Straw Dog Racing, the same team behind Sulphur Springs. - [Lemi Berhanu: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lemi-berhanu): Runners / Lemi Berhanu LB Film My Run Lemi Berhanu Runs Lemi Berhanu Hayle is an Ethiopian marathon runner, born on 13 September 1994. He is also known as Berhanu Lemi. He has raced the marathon since 2014 and has won major city races on three continents. His start was quick. He won his debut marathon in Zürich in 2014 in 2:10:40. In Dubai the following year he took five minutes off that time and won in 2:05:28. Behind him were Lelisa Desisa, then the Boston champion, and Feyisa Lilesa, runner-up in Chicago. The win was worth US$200,000. Later in 2015 he won in Warsaw in 2:07:57, his third marathon victory from three starts. The run ended at the World Championships in Beijing in 2015, where he was 15th. He went back to Dubai in 2016 and ran 2:04:33. That was still only good enough for second. Tesfaye Abera beat him in a sprint by nine seconds. In April 2016 he won the Boston Marathon in 2:12:45. Further wins followed in Xiamen in 2017 and at Hengshui Lake in 2018. He won the Mumbai Marathon in 2023 and again in 2024. He also won in Prague in 2024 and 2025. At 32 he produced the best run of his career. He won the Amsterdam Marathon on Sunday 18 October 2026 in 2:03:33, in wet and cold weather. The leaders went through halfway in 1:02:24. Justus Kangogo of Kenya took over the pace at 30km once the pacemakers had gone. Nicholas Kipkorir pushed on near the Vondelpark and Berhanu went with him. The pair were level at 40km in 1:57:25 before Berhanu pulled away. His second half took 1:01:09. Kipkorir was second in 2:03:39 and Patrick Mosin third in 2:03:58. Berhanu finished three seconds outside the course record of 2:03:30, set in 2025 by Geofry Toroitich Kipchumba. Kipchumba dropped out soon after halfway. Berhanu's time was about a minute quicker than the personal best he had run in January. - [Billy Bland: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/billy-bland): Runners / Billy Bland Photo: photographer unknown 🇬🇧 Billy Bland Born 1947 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Billy Bland is an English fell runner, born in 1947 in Borrowdale in the Lake District. His father Joe Bland raced professionally as a guides racer, and his brothers Stuart and David also took up the sport. Bland began in professional guides races himself before turning amateur in about 1974, when Borrowdale held its first fell race. He climbed through the British rankings fast, placing eighth at the 1976 British Championships and winning the title outright four years later, in 1980. He is widely regarded as the finest long-distance fell runner the sport has seen, at his best from the mid-1970s through the late 1980s. His most famous run came on the Bob Graham Round, a Lake District test that covers about 66 miles and takes in 42 peaks. He finished it in 13 hours and 53 minutes on 19 June 1982, a mark that nobody beat for 36 years until Kilian Jornet finally went quicker in 2018. Only three weeks after that round he broke the Wasdale Fell Race record too, clocking 3:25:21, and the year before he had run 2:34:38 to win at Borrowdale. A book about his life, All or Nothing at All, written by Steve Chilton and carrying a foreword from Jornet himself, came out in 2020. - [Naomi Lang: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/naomi-lang): Runners / Naomi Lang Photo: Salomon 🇬🇧 Naomi Lang Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 810 (9 November 2026) Naomi Lang is a British trail and mountain runner from northeast Scotland. She races for Carnethy Hill Running Club and holds a UTMB Index of 810. She grew up loving the outdoors and represented Aberdeen AAC as a teenager. She first made her name on the track and in cross country, winning national titles over 1500 metres and 5000 metres. She studied sport science at the University of Edinburgh, then earned a Great Britain vest for a world mountain running championships staged in Thailand. She then took a job at a Lake District hostel, and found herself drawn increasingly into hill racing there. In 2026 she won the Arc of Attrition's Arc 25 race in Cornwall, finishing in 3:09:16. She has also won the Rab Scafell Sky Race and the EcoTrail Paris, and taken third at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc in both 2025 and 2026. At the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships she won bronze in the short trail race. She works two jobs alongside her running, driving a coffee van and working at Go Ape, and plans to study medicine. She has said the hills suit her lifestyle and that she still has unfinished business on them.
