- [Steve Jones: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/steve-jones): Runners / Steve Jones Photo: Whoisjohngalt / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Steve Jones Born 1955 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road, Track (legend) Steve Jones is a Welsh former runner who set the marathon world record in his first completed race at the distance, winning the 1984 Chicago Marathon in 2:08:05. Raised in Ebbw Vale, he ran his first race aged 15 as an Air Training Corps cadet, later working as an RAF aircraft technician and joining its running team in 1976. Jones specialised in the 5,000m and 10,000m before moving up in distance. He had dropped out of the 1983 Chicago Marathon through injury, and ran the 1984 Olympic 10,000m in 28:28.08 for eighth place, before returning to Chicago that October to break Robert de Castella's world record by 13 seconds. He said he did not know he was on record pace until two miles from the finish, since he never wore a watch. He also won the 1985 London Marathon in 2:08:16 after stopping mid-race, and said he had barely trained for it beforehand. That August he set a half marathon world record of 61:14 in Birmingham, then ran a personal best of 2:07:13 to win Chicago again in October. That time stood as the fastest by a British runner for 33 years, until Mo Farah went quicker in 2018. Jones led the 1986 European Championships marathon by more than two minutes at 20 miles before fading badly over the closing six miles, but refused to drop out as rivals passed him. He won the 1988 New York City Marathon by over three minutes in 2:08:20, and took bronze in the 10,000m at the 1986 Commonwealth Games. He was appointed MBE in 2019 for services to sport and now lives in Boulder, Colorado. Ebbw Vale Leisure Centre unveiled a statue in his honour in September 2025. - [Joyciline Jepkosgei: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joyciline-jepkosgei): Runners / Joyciline Jepkosgei Photo: Luzifiga / Wikimedia Commons Joyciline Jepkosgei Runs Joyciline Jepkosgei is a Kenyan distance runner, born on 8 December 1993. She races everything from 10,000m on the track up to the marathon, and is a member of the Kenya Defence Forces. Her first result of note came at the 2015 Nairobi Half Marathon, where she was fifth in 1:14:06. A year later she ran 1:09:09 for second behind Valentine Kipketer at the First Lady's Half Marathon in Nairobi. She then won the Karlovy Vary Half Marathon two seconds quicker. On the track she took 10,000m bronze at the 2016 African Championships in Durban in 31:28.28, having qualified with third at the Kenyan championships. She closed that year with a win at the Marseille-Cassis Classique Internationale. The following spring changed her standing. She finished third at the RAK Half Marathon in 66:08, behind Peres Jepchirchir and Mary Keitany, cutting almost three minutes from her best. About six weeks later she won the Prague Half Marathon in 1:04:52 and became the first woman to go under 65 minutes. Along the way she passed 10km in 30:05, 15km in 45:37 and 20km in 1:01:25, all world record marks. She returned to Prague that September and ran 29:43 for 10km with a male pacer. That made her the first woman under 30 minutes for the distance, with Fancy Chemutai second in 30:06. Her official marathon debut came in New York in November 2019. She won in 2:22:38, the second fastest women's time on that course. She had also won the New York City Half Marathon that year. In 2021 she won the London Marathon in 2:17:43, taking the lead around 22 miles, which put her seventh on the all-time list. In 2022 she was seventh at Boston in 2:24:43, then second in London behind Yalemzerf Yehualaw in 2:18:07, 24 seconds outside her best. Her quickest running has come later. In 2025 she lowered her half marathon best to 1:04:13 in Barcelona. In November that year she won Valencia in 2:14:00, a course record and at the time the fourth fastest women's marathon ever run. She is still winning. On Sunday 4 October, aged 32, she set a women's course record of 1:05:40 at the Cardiff Half Marathon, taking 12 seconds off Edith Chelimo's mark from 2017. Ethiopia's Wede Kefale stayed with her for most of the race. Jepkosgei went clear with three miles left, near Roath Park Lake, and Kefale finished second in 1:05:54. Jepkosgei said the late hills made it hard but that she "kept fighting". - [Robin Juillaguet: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/robin-juillaguet): Runners / Robin Juillaguet Photo: UTMB profile 🇫🇷 Robin Juillaguet Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 901 (9 November 2026) Robin Juillaguet is a French trail runner who has spent more than a decade working his way up from short mountain races to the long ultras. His recorded results begin in 2013 with the Cross du Mont-Blanc and the Altispeed at the Ice Trail Tarentaise. For several seasons he raced mostly between 20km and 45km, often on steep ground. He holds a general UTMB Index of 893. His early wins came on that shorter terrain. In 2015 he won the YCC at the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc week, 16km with 1,130m of climb, in 1:39:48. In 2017 he took the 36km Transju'Trail in 3:08:37. The following year brought three more victories: the 23km race at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc in 2:16:42, La Venasque at Luchon Aneto Trail in 4:22:08, and the Argeles Nature Trail in 3:24:12. He won at Argeles again in 2019, covering 36km in 3:14:50. The step up in distance followed. He was fifth at the Grand Trail des Templiers in 2023, running the 81km course with 3,486m of climb in 7:09:50. In 2025 he finished fourth at both the Chianti Ultra Trail, in 6:19:22, and the High Trail Vanoise, in 8:00:41. He also ran the 82km long trail at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships that year, finishing 91st in 11:35:45. In 2026 he won the Marathon de la Toureille at Ceven'Trail in 3:39:58 and was eighth at Transvulcania in 7:00:41. He took second place in the Lavaredo 80K, 80km with 4,600m of climb, in 7:51:31. He then finished 13th in the CCC at Chamonix in 11:16:39. His biggest result so far came on Réunion in October. On his first attempt at the Diagonale des Fous, he finished second in 23:51:54. The 34th edition took the longest route in the race's history, 180km with 10,200m of climb from Saint-Pierre to La Redoute stadium in Saint-Denis. He was only 13th at Hell-Bourg and worked through the field from there. He finished just under an hour behind the winner, Hugo Deck, and ahead of Jérôme Vanderschaeghe, who was third in 24:10:35. - [Kazuhiro Kawahata: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kazuhiro-kawahata): Runners / Kazuhiro Kawahata KK 🇯🇵 UTMB Index 683 Film My Run 🇯🇵 Kazuhiro Kawahata Country 🇯🇵 Japan Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 683 (9 November 2026) Kazuhiro Kawahata is a Japanese trail and ultra runner whose racing has been built almost entirely on home ground. His results run back to 2017, when he finished 27th in the long race at the Senba Coastal Cliff Trail Running Race. Since then he has worked steadily up through the 100 km and 100 mile fields at Japan's big mountain events. He holds a general UTMB Index of 691. His outright wins have come over shorter ultra distances. In 2018 he won the 100 km at Trainic-World in Sainokuni in 17:50:51, a 109 km course with 6,830 m of climb. In 2023 he took the OSJ KAMI100 74K in 8:48:50. The Sainokuni 100 mile has suited him too. He was third there in 2019 in 29:16:59 and fourth in 2024 in 27:39:19, his quickest time on a course carrying 9,550 m of ascent. His longest race on record is the Shiga1 Round Trail in 2022. He covered 438 km and 30,000 m of climb in 142:11:10 to finish fourth. He is a fixture at two of Japan's established 100 milers. At Lake Biwa 100, which climbs 10,500 m over 169 km, he finished every year from 2021 to 2025. His best was sixth in 2024 in 29:27:43. At the OSJ Ontake 100 miles he was ninth in 2024 in 18:42:04 and ninth again in 2026 in 19:54:33. Further afield on the Japanese calendar, he finished 31st at the Ultra-Trail Mt. Fuji full course in 2019 in 26:30:43. Kawahata has also become one of Japan's leading backyard ultra runners. At the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship he was the last Japanese runner left after Kengo Takahashi dropped out partway through yard 105. That made Kawahata the national winner on 105 yards. Each yard is 6.706 km and starts on the hour, so he covered a little over 704 km. The total was one yard short of his national best of 106. It was the second team championship in which he had been Japan's last man out. When the overall standings were last checked, Japan sat third on 1,038 yards, behind the United States and Australia. - [Hannah Irwin: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hannah-irwin): Runners / Hannah Irwin Photo: Athletics Northern Ireland Hannah Irwin Runs Hannah Irwin is a British long-distance runner who races on the track and the road. She was born in Cambridge on 23 June 1998 and runs for Cambridge & Coleridge AC. She represents Northern Ireland internationally and holds its national records for 10km and the half marathon. She studied English with Creative Writing at Surrey University. Her breakthrough came at Parliament Hill in May 2022. At the Night of the 10,000m PBs she ran 32:25.34, a personal best and a new Northern Irish record. A month later she pulled on a British vest for the first time over 10,000m, and the team she was part of finished third. That June she also lowered her 5000m best to 15:45.87 at Woodside Stadium in Watford. She was picked for Northern Ireland over 10,000m at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham but did not finish the race. In August 2023 she ran 1:11:05 in County Antrim to set the Northern Irish half-marathon record. She was sixteenth in the half marathon at the European Running Championships in Leuven on 12 April 2025, finishing in 73:54. On the last day of 2025 she was second at the Battersea 5K in 15:27, a personal best on the road. In Valencia on 11 January 2026 she took the Northern Ireland 10km record down to 31:32. She was third in the British 10,000m championship in Loughborough on 17 May, behind Izzy Fry and Poppy Tank. On Sunday 18 October she won the UK 10-mile title at the Great South Run in Portsmouth, a mainly flat course that runs from the seafront past the Spinnaker Tower and the naval base to Southsea Castle. The race stayed close for most of the way before Irwin moved away to finish in 53:34. The defending champion, Verity Ockenden, was three seconds back in 53:37. - [Joshua Cassidy: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joshua-cassidy): Runners / Joshua Cassidy Photo: Katie Chan / Wikimedia Commons Joshua Cassidy Runs Josh Cassidy is a Canadian wheelchair racer, born in Ottawa on 15 November 1984. He races the middle and long distances, from 800m on the track up to the marathon. He has won 31 Canadian titles and has held national records at 800m, 1500m, 5000m, 10,000m and the marathon. Away from racing he works as a motivational speaker, an artist and an actor. He studied illustration at Sheridan College. He was first carded to the Canadian national team in 2005. A year later he made his world championship debut in Assen, in the Netherlands. At the 2008 Paralympics he was 10th over 5000m, 12th over 1500m and 17th in the 800m. The London Games four years later brought a 10th place in the 1500m. Over 5000m he came home 20th, and the marathon ended in 12th. His best result there came in the 800m. He was caught up in a crash and still finished fifth. Road marathons have brought most of his wins. He won London in 2010 in 1:35:21. In 2012 he took the Boston wheelchair race in 1:18:25, the quickest wheelchair marathon anyone had recorded at that point. Boston's course is not eligible for records, so the time never counted as an official world best. Nobody went faster for five years, until Marcel Hug of Switzerland lowered it in 2017. Cassidy also won Chicago in 2012. He then took bronze over 10,000m at the 2013 World Championships in Lyon. Los Angeles has brought him two victories. The first, in 2019, came after his racing chair broke in two on the eve of the race. A friend flew a spare out to him overnight, and he won with it a few hours later. He won in Los Angeles again in 2023, and took the Sydney Marathon in both 2023 and 2024. At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham he shared flag duties for Canada at the opening ceremony with the weightlifter Maude Charron. He finished fourth in the T54 marathon. He is still racing at the top level. In 2026 he won the professional men's wheelchair race at the BOLDERBoulder in 23:36. On 27 September he was sixth in the wheelchair race at the 52nd Berlin Marathon, a course known for fast times, in 1:31:31. - [Ron Hill: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ron-hill): Runners / Ron Hill Photo: Bert Verhoeff for Anefo / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Ron Hill Born 1938 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road, Track (legend) Ron Hill was a British marathon runner and one of the leading marathon runners of his era. He was the second man to break two hours ten minutes for the marathon, running 2:09:28 at the 1970 Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh, a pace he himself called suicidal. He won the Boston Marathon in 1970 in a course record of 2:10:30, the first British winner of that race. He also won marathon gold at the 1969 European Championships and the 1970 Commonwealth Games. Hill competed in two Olympic marathons, finishing 19th in Tokyo in 1964 and sixth in Munich in 1972 at the age of 33. He also ran the 10,000 metres at the 1964 and 1968 Olympics, placing 18th and seventh. Over his career he set world records at 10 miles, 15 miles and 25 kilometres, twice lowering the 10-mile record within the same year, 1968. He completed 115 marathons in total, winning 21 of them, with 112 finishes under 2:50 and 29 under 2:20. His final marathon was the 100th running of Boston, in 1996. Between December 1964 and January 2017 he ran at least a mile every day, a streak of more than 52 years that he ended after chest pains during a run. Hill trained as a textile chemist and used that background to design running gear, founding the company Ron Hill Sports in 1970. It introduced wrap-over shorts, mesh vests and reflective strips that became standard running kit. He was appointed MBE in 1972 for services to athletics. Hill died in 2021, aged 82. - [Eliud Kipchoge: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/eliud-kipchoge): Runners / Eliud Kipchoge Photo: Denis Barthel / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Eliud Kipchoge Born 1984 (age 41 or 42) Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Road, Track Eliud Kipchoge is a Kenyan long-distance runner regarded as one of the greatest marathon runners of all time. Before moving to the roads in 2012, he specialised in the 5000 metres, becoming world champion in 2003 at the age of 18 and adding Olympic and World Championship medals in the event over the next decade. He set the marathon world record twice in Berlin, running 2:01:39 in 2018 and improving it to 2:01:09 in 2022. That record stood until 2023, when fellow Kenyan Kelvin Kiptum broke it at the Chicago Marathon. In October 2019, Kipchoge became the first person to run a marathon distance in under two hours. He completed the Ineos 1:59 Challenge in Vienna in 1:59:40.2, though the run did not count as an official record because of its pacing and fluid support. He has won the Berlin Marathon a record five times and the London Marathon four times, and was crowned World Marathon Majors series champion five times, in 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2022. His first marathon win came at the 2013 Hamburg Marathon, and his first World Marathon Major victory followed at the Chicago Marathon in 2014. Kipchoge won Olympic marathon gold at the 2016 Rio Games and defended his title at the pandemic-delayed Tokyo Olympics in 2021, becoming only the third man to win consecutive Olympic marathon titles, after Abebe Bikila and Waldemar Cierpinski. He won that race by 80 seconds, the largest margin in an Olympic marathon in 49 years, at the age of 36. Kipchoge's dominance faded after 2022. He finished sixth at the 2023 Boston Marathon, his third defeat over the distance, then won a record fifth Berlin Marathon that October in 2:02:42. He dropped out of the marathon at the 2024 Paris Olympics after about 30 kilometres. It was the first time he had failed to finish a marathon, and he said afterwards he would not compete at another Olympics. In 2025 he finished 17th at the New York City Marathon, completing all six World Marathon Majors. He then launched Eliud's Running World, a plan to run seven marathons on seven continents over two years to raise money for libraries and education in Kenya. - [Claire Sumner: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/claire-sumner): Runners / Claire Sumner Photo: Tim Huebsch / Canadian Running Claire Sumner Runs Claire Sumner is a Canadian distance runner from Calgary, born on 10 March 1995. She came up through cross country and the 10,000 metres on the track before moving up to the marathon. Her first senior international vest came at the 2017 World Cross Country Championships in Kampala, Uganda. She placed 51st in the senior women's race. A few months later she lined up over 10,000 metres at the Summer Universiade in Taipei, Taiwan, and finished eighth. She returned to the World Cross Country Championships in 2019, this time in Aarhus, Denmark, and came home 66th in the senior women's race. Her standout road result came at the Chicago Marathon on Sunday 11 October. She ran 2:32:21 to finish 18th in the women's race and was the first Canadian woman across the line. The next Canadian, Katarina Mayer of Toronto, was nearly seven minutes back in 2:39:14. More than 55,000 runners started the 48th edition of the race, which Ethiopia's Hawi Feysa won in 2:13:33 to keep her title. That Chicago run is the most recent result on record for Sumner. It puts her at the front of the Canadian women's marathon field from that weekend in a race that also saw Thomas Nobbs move to third on the Canadian men's all-time list. - [Alex Milne: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/alex-milne): Runners / Alex Milne Photo: photographer unknown 🇬🇧 Alex Milne Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road Alex Milne is a British road ultrarunner. In March 2026 he won the IAU 50km World Championships in New Delhi, completing ten laps of a 5-kilometre course that started at 4am in poor air quality and near 21C heat. He took the front at around the 35-kilometre mark and crossed the line in 2:46:09, a European record and well over five minutes quicker than his previous best. Six months later, in September 2026, he took individual bronze at the IAU 100km World Championships in Ames, Spain, finishing in 6:17:50 after sitting tenth and over four minutes off the pace early on. He clawed his way up a course of a 4.8km opening loop and nineteen 5km laps, reaching fourth by lap 16 and reaching the podium two laps later as the heat climbed from 16C to 32C. His 100km time broke Steve Way's 2014 British road record of 6:19:20 and ranks him second among UK runners of all time, only behind Don Ritchie's track run of 6:10:20 from 1978. The run also carried Great Britain & Northern Ireland's men's team to silver, with team-mates Hugh Tibbs and Henry Hart both finishing inside their previous best times. Milne called the result "pleased and surprised". - [Lucy Gossage: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lucy-gossage): Runners / Lucy Gossage Photo: Lucy Gossage 🇬🇧 Lucy Gossage Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 734 (9 November 2026) Lucy Gossage is a British ultrarunner, former professional triathlete and doctor. She studied medicine at Cambridge and now works as a cancer specialist at a Nottingham hospital trust. She was European duathlon champion in 2012 and 2013 before turning to full-time Ironman racing at 34. She won Ironman UK and Ironman Wales in 2013, then Ironman Lanzarote in 2014 and Ironman UK again in 2015 and 2016. She reached the 2016 Ironman World Championship and placed ninth there, having broken her collarbone only two months before the race. She then retired from professional triathlon to focus on medicine, with 2020 set as her final competitive year. Gossage has since moved into ultrarunning, finishing third on her debut at the Montane Winter Spine Race in 2024 and winning it outright in 2025. In September 2026 she set the women's record for the Pennine Way, completing it in 2 days, 22 hours and 47 minutes. She won the 2026 Orsieres-Champex-Chamonix, the UTMB World Series Finals race, run that year over 60 km, in 06:08:07. She was a scoring member of their 2019 NCAA Cross Country Championship team, and helped them win the NCAA Indoor Championships in 2019, 2021 and 2023. At Fort Collins High School in Colorado she won three state cross country titles and four individual track titles. She placed third at the Nike Cross Nationals, behind another Colorado runner, Brie Oakley. She also won the Golden Trail Series overall title in 2025, and has taken further trail wins at the Speedgoat Mountain Races 50K and the Gorge Waterfalls 30K in 2026. - [Jimmy Gressier: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jimmy-gressier): Runners / Jimmy Gressier Photo: Sandro Halank / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇷 Jimmy Gressier Born 1997 (age 28 or 29) Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Track, Road Jimmy Gressier is a French runner over middle and long distances, born on 4 May 1997. He is the surprise 2025 world champion over 10,000 metres, and also took bronze in the 5000 metres at the same championships in Tokyo. He holds the European record for the 5km road race. Gressier's early career was built on cross country. He won U20 team gold twice at the European Cross Country Championships, in 2015 and again in 2016, then took the individual U23 title three years running, in 2017, 2018 and 2019. At the 2019 European U23 Championships he also added gold in both the 5000m and 10,000m. He stepped up to the seniors with bronze at the 2021 European Cross Country Championships in Dublin, finishing behind Jakob Ingebrigtsen. On the roads he set a European 5km record of 13:12 in Monaco in 2023, then lowered it further to 12:51 at the Urban Trail de Lille in April 2026, missing the world record by two seconds. In June 2026 he broke the French 3000m record with 7:28.67 at the Meeting de Montreuil. He also won the half marathon title at the 2025 European Running Championships, clocking a personal best of 59:45 in Brussels for his first senior crown, and took the 3000m at the 2025 Diamond League final in Zurich. His biggest result came at the 2025 World Athletics Championships in Tokyo, where he won the 10,000m in 28:55.77 with a late finishing burst. He became the first French winner of the event, only the third European champion, and just the second winner not born in Africa since Italy's Alberto Cova in 1983. He added bronze in the 5000m on the championships' final day, then took silver in the 2025 European Cross Country Championships, held that year in Lagoa, Portugal. He won bronze over 10,000m at the 2026 European Championships in Birmingham. Gressier has become known for his finish-line celebrations, from a knee slide that ended in a fall at the 2018 European Cross Country Championships to eating a crepe before crossing the line at the 2023 French Cross Country Championships. He celebrated his 2025 European half marathon title by hurdling the finish tape. - [Hannah Gapes: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hannah-gapes): Runners / Hannah Gapes Photo: NC State Athletics Hannah Gapes Runs Hannah Gapes is a New Zealand distance runner who is at her best over cross country. Born on 28 November 2003, she grew up in Rotorua in the Bay of Plenty and took up running at primary school. She later attended John Paul College and raced for Lake City Athletics Club. In 2020 she took the senior girls' 1500m title at the New Zealand Secondary Schools Track and Field Championships in Tauranga. By the age of 17 she was the national under-20 champion over 5000m. She then moved to the United States to race in the college system for North Carolina State University. Her first big college result came in November 2024, when she finished eighth at the NCAA Cross Country Championships. She followed it with tenth in the 3000m at the 2025 NCAA Division 1 Indoor Championships, though she was ruled out of that year's outdoor season. Back home in August 2025 she won the senior women's 10km at the New Zealand Cross Country Championships in Christchurch. It was her first national senior cross country title. It also gave her an automatic place at the 2026 World Athletics Cross Country Championships. The autumn of 2025 was a busy one. She won the Sean Earl Loyola Lakefront Invitational in Chicago on 3 October, then placed fifth at the ACC championships on 31 October as NC State took the team title. She was second at the NCAA Southeast regional on 14 November, with her team winning again. On 22 November she finished fifth at the NCAA Cross Country Championships in Missouri, and NC State were crowned team champions. She came 19th at the World Cross Country Championships in Tallahassee on 10 January 2026. Her form carried into the summer. At the 2026 NCAA Outdoor Championships in June she set a 5000m personal best of 15:25.93. In September she placed ninth in the 5km at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen. Now a senior at NC State, Gapes opened her autumn account in emphatic style on 16 October 2026. The race was the Pre-National Invitational, held in the Indiana city of Terre Haute. Running alone at the front on the LaVern Gibson Championship Cross Country Course, she covered the 6km in 18:57.6. No woman had run faster over the distance there. The old best of 19:14.0 had stood for less than a month. Auburn's Faith Chelangat was next home in 19:15.5. NC State still lost the team contest to BYU by four points, 84 to 88, their first cross country defeat in almost two years. The NCAA Championships follow on 21 November. - [Tove Alexandersson: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/tove-alexandersson): Runners / Tove Alexandersson Photo: Torben Utzon / Wikimedia Commons 🇸🇪 Tove Alexandersson Born 1992 (age 33 or 34) Country 🇸🇪 Sweden Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 870 (9 November 2026) Tove Alexandersson is a Swedish orienteer, ski orienteer, skyrunner and trail runner, born on 7 September 1992. She has won world championship gold in six different sports. In orienteering alone she has won 23 world titles, the most of any woman in the sport's history. Her orienteering career took off in 2016, when she topped the world rankings for the first time. In 2021 she won gold in all five events at the World Orienteering Championships, the first person to do so. Between 2018 and 2022 she won 11 world titles in a row, a record for the sport. Alexandersson turned to skyrunning almost by accident. In 2017, only her second such race, she won the Limone Extreme Skyrace by 12 minutes. The following year she won the Sky discipline at the Skyrunning World Championships on the Ring of Steall course in Scotland, setting a course record. In 2023 she added a trail running world medal, taking silver in the Up and Downhill class at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. In September 2025 Alexandersson won her first trail running world title, taking Short Trail 45K gold at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships by 34 minutes. She has also won ten world titles in ski orienteering. In 2021 she won the combined title at the World Championships of Ski Mountaineering. In 2024 she won all three gold medals on offer at the first SkySnow World Championships, a sport she had never competed in before. Her trail running results have kept coming since. In 2026 she won the Marathon du Mont-Blanc, the Zegama-Aizkorri mountain race and the Grand Raid Ventoux's Mistral Marathon Trail, all as outright women's winner. She has worked as a dietitian and coach alongside her own racing. She has moved to Annecy, France, to be closer to Europe's main trail racing calendar. She joined the adidas Terrex team in 2022. In 2023 she won the UTMB OCC over 55 kilometres, and in 2024 she won the full UTMB CCC on her first attempt at the 100 kilometre distance. That made her one of only a few runners with wins in two different UTMB World Series finals. She has stayed close to unbeaten since, winning the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 50K and the Tenerife Bluetrail in 2025, and the MaXi-Race Tour du Lac d'Annecy 100K in 2026. She was runner-up at the 2026 CCC. She has said she wants to complete the full set of UTMB finals victories, with the 100 mile race in Chamonix as her next target. She won her first big titles at home, including the Ultra-Trail Drakensberg 30K in 2018 and 2019. - [George Scholey: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/george-scholey): Runners / George Scholey GS 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 George Scholey Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra George Scholey is a British-born runner whose racing is bound up with the Rubik's Cube. He has been solving cubes for 11 years but has only been running for three. He took a job as an associate brand manager at Rubik's Cube and relocated to Toronto in 2025. He was 24 when he set his latest record, and his marathon best is 2:34. His most notable run came at Central Tech Stadium in Toronto on 12 October, when he completed a Rubik's Cube mile in 5:09.25. The previous best belonged to the American Jake Hanson, who ran 5:22.75 in June, so Scholey went 13.5 seconds quicker. The rules require one solve before the start and another after each of the first three laps. Each cube arrives scrambled and unseen. After four laps there are 9 more metres to run to complete the mile. Scholey's solves averaged nine seconds, with the fastest at around 8.5 seconds. His laps averaged 67 seconds, and the final 409m took the same. He said he was confident of the record by halfway, after his second solve. He called it "objectively the most difficult" of his records. Guinness World Records has yet to ratify the time. If approved, it would be his fourth Guinness record. In 2022 he solved 6,931 cubes in 24 hours. He has also solved 500 while riding a skateboard and 520 while running the 2024 London Marathon. On the trails, UTMB results show him 36th man in the 10 Km du Mont-Blanc in 2024. That course covers 10km with 270m of climb, and he finished in 46:37. He does not currently hold a UTMB Index. Scholey ran the Boston Marathon in April and then shifted his training towards the mile, with the emphasis on pace. December brings his next big race, The Marathon Project in Chandler, Arizona. He wants to finish there in under 2:30. - [Alison dos Santos: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/alison-dos-santos): Runners / Alison dos Santos Photo: Anass Sedrati / Wikimedia Commons Alison dos Santos Runs Alison dos Santos is a Brazilian hurdler who specialises in the 400m hurdles. His birth date is 3 June 2000 and his home town is São Joaquim da Barra, in São Paulo state. He did judo from the age of six until he was 14, then a childhood friend talked him into trying athletics. He started in 2013 at a state technical school in his home town, coached by Ana Fidélis. By 16 he was already racing against adults. Early on, teammates gave him the nickname "Piu", and it stuck. His international results came quickly. He was fifth in the 400m hurdles final at the 2017 World U18 Championships. A year later he took bronze at the World U20 Championships in 49.78. In 2019 he won the event at the World University Games, then took gold at the Pan American Games in Lima at the age of 19. His 48.45 there was a South American under-20 record. That September he reached the world final in Doha, the first Brazilian to do so since Eronilde de Araújo in 1999. He finished seventh in 48.28. The Tokyo Olympic final in 2021 is regarded as the strongest 400m hurdles race ever run. Dos Santos took bronze in 46.72 behind Karsten Warholm and Rai Benjamin. All three went under Kevin Young's old world record, which had stood for almost 30 years until a month earlier. On 19 July 2022 he became world champion in Eugene in 46.29, a championship record. It was the first men's world title in Brazil's history. He was fifth at the 2023 worlds in Budapest after clipping the eighth and tenth barriers. He won Olympic bronze again in Paris in 2024 in 47.26, took the Diamond League title in 2022 and 2024, and won world silver in 2025 in 46.84, behind Benjamin. In May 2025 he also set a world best of 21.85 in the rarely run 200m hurdles. His 2026 season has been his best. On 27 August at the Zürich Diamond League he broke the world record with 45.80, finishing ahead of Warholm, the previous holder. He is only the second man to run under 46 seconds. He put it down to changes in training, saying he was "starting faster" and "finishing stronger". In September he won the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in 45.98, the third fastest time in history, beating Warholm and Benjamin again. He has won six Diamond League races this year. On 6 October he was one of 20 athletes shortlisted for this year's World Athlete of the Year award. Voting closes on 17 October and the winners will be announced in Monaco on 29 November. - [Yared Nuguse: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/yared-nuguse): Runners / Yared Nuguse Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Yared Nuguse Born 1999 (age 26 or 27) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Track Yared Nuguse is an American middle-distance runner who specialises in the 1500 metres and the mile, born 1 June 1999 in Washington D.C. He races for the On Athletics Club, coached by Dathan Ritzenhein, and won the 1500m at the 2019 NCAA outdoor championships while at the University of Notre Dame. In 2023 he set the North American outdoor 1500m record of 3:29.02 at the Bislett Games in Oslo. He also ran the second-fastest indoor mile in history, 3:47.38, at that year's Millrose Games, and broke the American mile record with 3:43.97 at the Prefontaine Classic, finishing second to Jakob Ingebrigtsen. Nuguse won bronze in the 1500m at the 2024 Paris Olympics, running a personal best of 3:27.80. It gave the United States two medals in the event at the same Games for the first time in 112 years. He also won the 1500m at that year's Weltklasse Zurich meeting, beating Ingebrigtsen. In February 2025 he set a world record in the indoor mile, running 3:46.63 to win his third Wanamaker Mile title, though Ingebrigtsen took the record back five days later. He also set an 800m personal best of 1:44.77 that year, racing in the Grand Slam Track series. At the Ultimate Championship in Budapest in September 2026, Nuguse led the 1500m field at the bell before losing a shoe with about 600m to go. He still finished fifth, in 3:30.76, behind winner Josh Kerr. - [Kathrine Switzer: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kathrine-switzer): Runners / Kathrine Switzer Photo: Marathona / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Kathrine Switzer Born 1947 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road (legend) In 1967, Kathrine Switzer became the first woman to complete the Boston Marathon on an official race number, entering as "K.V. Switzer" and given bib 261. During the race, co-director Jock Semple tried to physically pull her from the course and grab her number, an attack captured by press photographers and reported around the world. Her coach Arnie Briggs and fellow runner Tom Miller shielded her, and she went on to finish in around 4 hours 20 minutes. The Amateur Athletic Union responded by explicitly banning women from races against men. Switzer and other female runners campaigned against the rule, and in 1972 the Boston Marathon introduced an official women's race. She finished third in that race, receiving her trophy from Semple himself. Switzer went on to win the 1974 New York City Marathon in 3:07:29 and set her personal best of 2:51:37 at the 1975 Boston Marathon. Runner's World named her Female Runner of the Decade for 1967 to 1977. She later became a sports broadcaster and won an Emmy for her commentary. She also founded a global series of women's road races, sponsored by Avon, that helped bring the women's marathon into the 1984 Olympics. In 2017, on the 50th anniversary of her first Boston Marathon, Switzer ran the race again wearing bib 261, this time among more than 13,700 women finishers. The Boston Athletic Association retired that number afterwards in her honour. For her work opening the sport to women, the National Women's Hall of Fame added her name to its ranks in 2011, and in 2015 she founded 261 Fearless, a non-profit that uses running to support women worldwide. - [François D'Haene: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/francois-d-haene): Runners / François D'Haene Photo: France 3 Corse ViaStella / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇷 François D'Haene Born 1985 (age 40 or 41) Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra Born in Lille on 24 December 1985, François D'Haene races ultra distances and mountains for France. He worked as a physiotherapist before becoming a wine-grower in 2012, and now lives in the Beaujolais wine region. D'Haene has won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc four times, in 2012, 2014, 2017 and 2021. He also won Réunion's Grand Raid three times, in 2013, 2014 and 2016, and took the first Ultra-Trail World Tour title in 2014. He set the UTMB course record in 2012, running 20 hours 11 minutes 44 seconds over 167km, then lowered it in 2017, covering an extended 170km route in 19 hours 1 minute 32 seconds. In October 2017 he ran California's John Muir Trail in two days, nineteen hours and twenty-six minutes, a new record for the route. The mark stood until September 2026, when Joe McConaughy lowered it by three hours and 26 minutes. In July 2021, D'Haene won the Hardrock 100, breaking both the counter-clockwise and outright course records, both previously held by Kilian Jornet, with a time of 21:45:51. The following month he won the UTMB again, in 20:45:59. D'Haene set a record for Corsica's GR20 in June 2016, completing the route in 31 hours and 6 minutes. Lambert Santelli broke that record in 2021 with 30 hours 25 minutes. D'Haene reclaimed the record in July 2026, the first ever sub-30-hour crossing of the trail, in 29 hours and 46 minutes. - [Taiju Goto: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/taiju-goto): Runners / Taiju Goto Photo: Daily Sports Taiju Goto Runs Taiju Goto is a Japanese hurdler who specialises in the 400 metres hurdles. He was born on 5 May 2009. In 2026, still aged 17, he became Japan's senior national champion and lowered the world under-18 best more than once. His season began to gather pace in May, when he ran 49.34 seconds in Osaka. At the Asian U20 Athletics Championships he clocked 49.25 to set a meeting record. That took the mark from Qatar's Ismail Doudai Abakar, who had set it in 2023. The following month Goto went to the Japanese Athletics Championships in Aichi Prefecture and ran 48.31, a world under-18 best. He then went quicker again, 48.09, to take the senior title against athletes considerably older than him. In August he reached the final of the 400 metres hurdles at the World Athletics U20 Championships. He won silver there in 49.23. The Asian Games in Nagoya followed in September. Goto was fastest through the heats in 48.60. In the final he ran shoulder to shoulder with Qatar's Bassam Hemeida for most of the single lap. Hemeida won in 47.82. Goto took silver in 47.93, which improved his own world under-18 record and made him the first under-18 athlete on record to run under 48 seconds. He ends the 2026 season as Japan's national champion and the holder of the world under-18 record, with silver medals from both the world under-20 championships and the Asian Games. - [Camille Herron: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/camille-herron): Runners / Camille Herron Photo: Runcamille / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Camille Herron Born 1981 (age 44 or 45) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road Camille Herron is an American ultramarathon runner, born in 1981 in Norman, Oklahoma. She holds a bachelor's degree in exercise and sports science from the University of Tulsa and a master's from Oregon State University. At Tulsa she began studying the stress fractures that had troubled her as a young runner. She trains under coach Conor Holt, a former elite runner who now coaches at college level. She has also worked as a research assistant in bone imaging at the University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center. Herron has set 13 world records at ultramarathon distances. Racing outright against the men in February 2022, she won the Jackpot 100 in 12:41:10, a race that doubled that year as the US 100 Mile Championship. Two months later she passed 100,000 lifetime running miles, the youngest woman on record to do so. In 2023 she added 14.8 miles to the women's 48-hour world record, covering 270.505 miles, a mark beaten at the time only by two men. That year she also became the first woman to run under 24 hours at the 153-mile Spartathlon, winning in a course record of 22:35:31. The win made her the first athlete to win both Comrades and Spartathlon. In March 2024 Herron broke 12 world records across distances from 48 hours to six days, including a six-day world mark that Sandy Barwick had held since 1990. She has also excelled on trails, with wins at the JFK 50 Mile, Bandera 100K, Black Canyon 100K and Tunnel Hill 100. Her wins there also include the Javelina Jundred and the Tarawera Ultramarathon at both 100K and 100 miles. She won the Tarawera 100 Mile title in 17:20:52, a course record set two weeks after she survived a rollover car accident. Herron has qualified for the Olympic Marathon Trials three times and won 21 marathons outright. Running for the United States at the Pan American marathon in 2011, she placed 9th. She became the third American ever to win the Comrades Marathon, doing so in 2017, and that same year Ultrarunning Magazine named her its Female Ultrarunner of the Year. She also holds the Guinness World Record for running the fastest marathon by a woman dressed as a superhero, finishing in 2:48:51 as Spiderwoman. She has been named IAU International Ultra Runner of the Year four times. The Road Runners Club of America inducted her into its Distance Running Hall of Fame in 2024. Herron partnered with Lululemon on product development, including a women's trail shoe, but the brand ended its sponsorship in September 2024. That came after several accounts were found editing Wikipedia to favour her over other athletes such as Kilian Jornet and Courtney Dauwalter, edits Herron was accused of making. In 2026 she began selling content through OnlyFans, saying the move let her sponsor herself and that elite athletes should draw income from more than one source. - [Joshua Cheptegei: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joshua-cheptegei): Runners / Joshua Cheptegei Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇬 Joshua Cheptegei Born 1996 (age 29 or 30) Country 🇺🇬 Uganda Runs Track, Road Joshua Kiprui Cheptegei is a Ugandan long-distance runner born on 12 September 1996 in Kapchorwa District, Uganda. He is the current world record holder for both the 5000 metres and the 10,000 metres. He set both records within months of each other in 2020, making him only the tenth man in history to hold both simultaneously. He is the reigning Olympic 10,000m champion and a three-time world champion at that distance. Cheptegei studied procurement and logistics management and is employed by the Uganda National Police. He is coached by Addy Ruiter. He turned to running after trying football, long jump and triple jump as a boy. He finished ninth in the 10,000m at the 2015 World Championships and eighth and sixth in the 5000m and 10,000m at the 2016 Olympics. He won 10,000m silver at the 2017 World Championships, then took both the 5000m and 10,000m titles at the 2018 Commonwealth Games. He also won the World Cross Country Championships in Aarhus, Denmark, in 2019, leading Uganda to the team title ahead of teammate Jacob Kiplimo in second. In late 2019 and 2020, Cheptegei set a string of world records on the road and track. He ran a 10km road record of 26:38 in Valencia in December 2019, then a 5km road record of 12:51 in Monaco in February 2020. That August, racing in Monaco again, he broke Kenenisa Bekele's 16-year-old 5000m world record with a time of 12:35.36. Two months later in Valencia he set a 10,000m world record of 26:11.00, improving on another Bekele mark that had stood for 15 years. Cheptegei won gold in the 5000m and silver in the 10,000m at the 2020 Summer Olympics. He won 10,000m gold again at the 2022 and 2023 World Athletics Championships, and took bronze at the 2023 World Athletics Cross Country Championships behind Jacob Kiplimo and Berihu Aregawi. He made his marathon debut at the Valencia Marathon in 2023, finishing 37th in 2:08:59. At the 2024 Olympics in Paris he won 10,000m gold in an Olympic record of 26:43.14, beating Bekele's mark from 2008. He said afterwards that he would not defend his 5000m title from Tokyo, citing his recovery from the 10,000m. He signalled he would focus on road racing rather than further Olympic track races. Cheptegei has also won the Zevenheuvelenloop 15km road race in Nijmegen four times. He set the 15km road world record there in 2018, before it was broken by fellow Ugandan Jacob Kiplimo in 2022. In September 2026 he placed third in the half marathon at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen, running a personal best of 58:26. He was among the three leading men with about 3km left before fading from contention as Andreas Almgren and Nicholas Kipkorir fought for the win. - [Hayden Hawks: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hayden-hawks): Runners / Hayden Hawks Photo: Gianina Lindsey / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Hayden Hawks Born 1991 (age 34 or 35) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 935 (9 November 2026) Hayden Hawks is an American trail and ultramarathon runner for HOKA, born in 1991 in St. George, Utah, with a general UTMB Index of 935. He took up cross-country in high school after playing basketball, won state titles in the 1600m and 3200m, and went on to compete on Southern Utah University's Division I cross-country squad. He turned heads as a trail runner with his win at the Speedgoat 50k in 2016, and joined the United States team at the International Association of Ultrarunners' Trail World Championships the following year. In 2017 he also won the UTMB CCC in 10:24:30. The following year he won the full Lavaredo Ultra Trail over 120 km in 12:16:20, and the Tour en Terre Du Jura in France in 13:35:57. He has finished on the podium at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run twice, taking second in 2022 and third in 2024, and finished eighth there in 2021. His recent wins include the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 2020 and 2024, and the Ultra-Trail Kosciuszko 100 in Australia in 2022. In 2025 he won the Kodiak Ultra Marathons 100M in 16:40:37 and the Tarawera Ultra-Trail T50 in 03:18:46, before finishing third at the Canyons Endurance Runs 100K in 2026. - [Natalie Beadle: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/natalie-beadle): Runners / Natalie Beadle Photo: Merrell Skyrunner World Series 🇬🇧 Natalie Beadle Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 735 (9 November 2026) Natalie Beadle is a British skyrunner who grew up in the English Lake District, where she learned to move across fell terrain. She now represents Arc'teryx on the international skyrunning circuit and is known for performing well in technical, wet and challenging conditions. She trains between sailing trips, often living aboard a 40 foot sailboat between races. In September 2026 Beadle won the MAGA Skymarathon in Italy's Val Serina, a 39 kilometre race with 3,000 metres of climbing, in 5 hours 27 minutes. She also finished 2nd at the Beast of Big Creek Skyrace and 1st at the After Shock 24km race that year. Her results across the Skyrunner World Series calendar have placed her among Britain's strongest current skyrunners. Beadle has raced widely across Europe, including the SIERRE-ZINAL classic and the Matterhorn Ultraks Extreme. In 2025 she took a podium at the UTNP 2 Peaks Skyrace in South Korea. Her UTMB Index of 734 reflects a wide-ranging season across technical mountain terrain. Wilson also won the Faultline Ultra's After Shock 24km race in 2025. Her UTMB Index of 746 reflects a consistent run of podium finishes across middle and long distance trail races. She continues to race predominantly on the UTMB World Series circuit in Australasia. - [Davide Magnini: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/davide-magnini): Runners / Davide Magnini Photo: UTMB profile 🇮🇹 Davide Magnini Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 920 (9 November 2026) Davide Magnini is an Italian mountain runner sponsored by New Balance, with a UTMB Index of 920 built over a career stretching back to 2016. He has been one of Europe's most consistent short mountain racers, with a best of fifth at Sierre-Zinal in 2021 in 02:34:38 across ten appearances there since 2018. The Marathon du Mont-Blanc has been a particular strength. Magnini won its 43 km race outright in 2019 in 03:47:13, was runner-up there in 2021 and 2022, and returned to win again in 2025 in 03:42:55. He also won the Giir di Mont in 2025 in 03:14:04. He has raced widely across the Alps and beyond, taking second at Zegama-Aizkorri in 2022, second at the Annapurna 100 Trail Marathon in 2019 and eighth at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' Short Trail 45K. He has also won at the Vibram Ultra Trail Lago d'Orta, La Skyrhune and twice at the Dolomyths Run Sellaronda Ultra Trail Sky. - [Madalina Florea: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/madalina-florea): Runners / Madalina Florea Photo: Frank Haug / Wikimedia Commons 🇷🇴 Madalina Florea Country 🇷🇴 Romania Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 825 (9 November 2026) Madalina Florea is a Romanian trail and mountain runner. In 2026 she won the Sierre-Zinal mountain race in Switzerland, one of the sport's classic events, in 02:55:46. It capped a steady climb up that race's results. She had finished seventh in 2023, third in 2024 and twelfth in 2025. Florea's 2026 season also included wins at the Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail, a stop on the Golden Trail World Series, and at the Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K in California. She had finished second at the Broken Arrow race the year before. She won the short HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc ETC race in 2025. In 2024 she was runner-up at both the Marathon du Mont-Blanc and the Mammoth Trail Fest, and took third at the European Off-Road Running Championships. In 2023 she won the Golfo dell'Isola race, a Golden Trail World Series final. Florea has raced internationally since at least 2019, when she won the Predeal Forest Run in Romania. She has also raced at altitude and over longer distances, including the Bucovina Ultra Rocks race in 2020 and the Pikes Peak Ascent in the United States. - [Jared Campbell: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jared-campbell): Runners / Jared Campbell Photo: Jared Campbell / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Jared Campbell Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Jared Campbell is an American mountain ultrarunner from Utah and the first person to finish the Barkley Marathons three times. He completed the Tennessee race in 2012, 2014 and 2016, then added a fourth finish in 2024. He also won the Hardrock 100 in 2010. Raised in Olympus Cove, on the eastern edge of Salt Lake City, he began as a rock climber. Running came later, while he was studying mechanical engineering at the University of Utah. He ran his first 100-miler at the Wasatch Front 100 in 2003, aged 24, and has kept working as an engineer. Hardrock in Colorado became a fixture. He first ran it in 2004 and has finished it ten times, winning in 2010 in 27:18. He was a regular at the Wasatch 100 too, with a best of 21:48:32 for fourth in 2009. In 2014 he won the Plain 100 in Washington state, an unmarked race that rewards route finding. Barkley suited his taste for navigation on unmarked ground. He first finished in 2012 in 56:00:16 and went back in 2014 to finish in 57:53:20, this time doing all of his own navigation. In 2016 he was the only finisher, in 59:32:30. In 2024 he finished again in 59:30:32. He has also completed Nolan's 14, a line over 14 Colorado peaks above 14,000 feet, three times. His winter training for Barkley led him to found Running Up For Air, a mountain endurance event that raises money for cleaner air along Utah's Wasatch Front. - [Roger Bannister: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/roger-bannister): Runners / Roger Bannister Photo: User:Pruneau / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Roger Bannister Born 1929 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track (legend) Roger Bannister was an English middle-distance runner who became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes. He set the record on 6 May 1954 at Iffley Road in Oxford, clocking 3 minutes 59.4 seconds with pacing from Chris Chataway and Chris Brasher. The run came two years after he finished fourth in the 1500 metres at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, where he set a British record of 3:46.30. That near-miss convinced him to target the four-minute mile instead. His record lasted just 46 days before Australia's John Landy broke it in Turku, running 3:58.0. The two met later that year in Vancouver, at the British Empire and Commonwealth Games, in a race billed as the Miracle Mile. Bannister won in 3:58.8, overtaking Landy on the final bend, with Landy eight tenths of a second behind. He went on to win the 1500 metres at the European Championships in Bern later that season with a championship record of 3:43.8. Bannister retired from athletics at the end of 1954, at the age of 25, to concentrate on a career as a doctor. He was appointed CBE in 1955 for services to athletics. He went on to chair the newly formed Sports Council, now Sport England, as its first chairman, and was knighted for that work in 1975. In the role he introduced the first testing for anabolic steroids in British sport. Away from athletics, Bannister spent forty years as a neurologist, publishing more than eighty papers on the autonomic nervous system. He said in a 2014 interview that he was prouder of that work than of the four-minute mile. Bannister died in 2018, aged 88. - [Ben Dhiman: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ben-dhiman): Runners / Ben Dhiman Photo: The Adventure Bakery / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Ben Dhiman Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 965 (9 November 2026) Ben Dhiman is an American ultra-trail runner with a general UTMB Index of 965, competing for ASICS. He set a UTMB Mont-Blanc course record of 18:16:29 in 2026, the first man to get under 19 hours on the course and only the second American to win the race outright. He came to the sport by way of long hikes rather than a running scholarship. After graduating from Sycamore High School in Ohio in 2010 and playing soccer at Emory University, he hiked the length of the Appalachian Trail in 2012 and, four years later, the Continental Divide Trail. His results built steadily across Europe's biggest 100-mile-plus races. He won MIUT on Madeira in 2024 in 13:52:46, then the Lavaredo Ultra Trail and the Grand Raid Ventoux in 2025, both in under 12 hours. He was runner-up at UTMB itself in 2025, in 19:51:37, the year before his win, and finished third at La Réunion's Diagonale des Fous in both 2022 and 2024. He now lives and trains in Soues, in the French Pyrenees. - [Bruce Fordyce: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/bruce-fordyce): Runners / Bruce Fordyce Photo: Claidheamhmor / Wikimedia Commons 🇿🇦 Bruce Fordyce Born 1955 Country 🇿🇦 South Africa Runs Road (legend) Bruce Fordyce is a South African ultramarathon runner, born in Hong Kong on 3 December 1955, who moved to Johannesburg as a boy. He first ran the Comrades Marathon in 1977, finishing 43rd out of 1,678 starters. He climbed to 14th in 1978, 3rd in 1979 and 2nd in 1980, before winning for eight consecutive years from 1981 to 1988. Fordyce won the Comrades again in 1990, taking his total to nine victories, a record no other runner has matched. He completed 30 Comrades Marathons in all, once posting identical finishing times in 1985 and 1987. In 1986 he ran the 'down' route, from Pietermaritzburg to Durban, in 5 hours 24 minutes and 7 seconds. That mark stood for 21 years until Russia's Leonid Shvetsov beat it in 2007. Between 1981 and 1983 Fordyce also took the London to Brighton Ultramarathon title three times in a row. In 1984 he set a world record for 50 miles, clocking 4 hours 50 minutes and 21 seconds at the AMJA 50 Mile Ultramarathon in Chicago. Jim Walmsley finally broke that mark on 5 May 2019. Fordyce also held the world record for 100km. Fordyce was an outspoken opponent of apartheid. At his first Comrades win in 1981 he wore a black armband to protest the regime's 20th anniversary, drawing boos and thrown tomatoes from the crowd. He later called it one of the proudest moments of his life. In 2011 he brought parkrun to South Africa, and had run his 500th free weekly 5km event, at Johannesburg's Delta Park, by October 2023. His general UTMB index of 924 is among the highest in Chinese trail running, built from results since 2019. He won the Adidas Terrex Chongli 168's CTC over 131 km in 2023, in 14:39:24, and the Doi Inthanon by UTMB's Cliffs100 in 2022. He also won the TSAIGU Trail's 115K in 2023 and its 105K in 2025. He opened 2026 with a win at the Nike ACG Ultra-Trail Chongli 168's Xueruyi 70 and a second place at the Amazean Jungle Thailand's 50K. His other wins include the TSAIGU Trail's 85K in 2022 and the Xihu Qingzhiwu Longdong Trail's Wangjue42K in 2024. He was third at Mount Yun's MMY50K in 2023. - [Patrick Kipngeno: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/patrick-kipngeno): Runners / Patrick Kipngeno Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Patrick Kipngeno Born 1993 (age 32 or 33) Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 976 (9 November 2026) Patrick Kipngeno is a Kenyan mountain runner born on 18 June 1993 in Bomet County, Kenya. He is based in Austria and competes mainly on the mountain and trail circuits of Italy, France, Switzerland and Austria. His technical sponsor is On, and he holds a UTMB index of 976. Kipngeno has finished on the podium at Sierre-Zinal every year from 2022 to 2026. He was second in 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026, and third in 2024, with times consistently between 2:26 and 2:30. He has been especially strong at Trofeo Nasego, winning in 2022 in 01:30:46 and 2024 in 01:31:26, and finishing second in 2023 and 2026. He also won The Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K in 2024 in 01:45:37 before taking third in both 2025 and 2026. Other wins include the Montée du Nid d'Aigle in 2022 and 2023, the Val Bregaglia Trail in 2024, and the Four Sisters Mountain Trail in 2024. In 2025 he won the Jinshanling Great Wall Trail Race in 02:13:02. In 2026 he was third in the Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail on the Golden Trail World Series and third again at The Broken Arrow Skyrace. - [Catherine Debrunner: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/catherine-debrunner): Runners / Catherine Debrunner Photo: Tobi swiss / Wikimedia Commons Catherine Debrunner Runs Catherine Debrunner is a Swiss wheelchair racer who competes in the T53 class. She was born on 11 April 1995 in Mettendorf, Switzerland, and has raced for the Swiss team since 2008. Her range is unusually wide. She wins on the track over 100m and over 5000m, and on the road over the full marathon. She holds nine World Para Athletics world records. These are the T53 100m, 200m, 400m and 800m, the T53/T54 1500m and 5000m, and the 10K, half marathon and marathon on the road. She met her first coach, Paul Odermatt, at a sports camp in Nottwil. The Dutchman Arno Mul has coached her since 2021. Her international debut came at the IWAS World Youth Games in New Jersey in 2008. She won five golds there. Her first senior world medal followed in 2015, in the T53 200m, in 30.64. She was seventh in the 400m at the Rio Paralympics in 2016, then stepped away from the sport to concentrate on her studies. She came back for the 2019 world championships in Dubai and took gold in the T53 400m and silver in the 800m. In Tokyo she won bronze over 800m behind Madison de Rozario and Zhou Hongzhuan, then gold in the 400m. The world championships of 2023 brought four golds and a silver. In 2025 she won all five events she entered, from 100m to 5000m. The marathon came almost by accident. With the 2022 world championships cancelled, she switched to the roads for the rest of that year. She won her first marathon, in Berlin, in 1:36:47. The result ended Manuela Schär's run of five Berlin titles. A week later she won London. Back in Berlin in 2023 she set a world record of 1:34:16. Course records followed in Chicago, in 1:38:44, and in New York, in 1:39:32. She added London, Berlin and Chicago in 2024, then Tokyo and London in 2025. She was second in Boston in both 2025 and 2026. She has topped the overall World Marathon Majors standings in 2023, 2024 and 2026. Paris 2024 was her biggest championship. She left with five golds and a silver. One of the golds came in the T54 marathon, which she led from the start. De Rozario of Australia was second and Susannah Scaroni of the United States third. In May 2023 the Laureus awards named her the year's leading athlete with a disability. She was nominated again in 2025. Her 2026 season has been her strongest on the roads. She won Tokyo, London and Berlin before going to Chicago on 11 October. There she took a full minute off her own world record, finishing in 1:33:16. Three weeks later, on 1 November, she won the 50th anniversary New York City Marathon in 1:40:02, 30 seconds outside her course record. Tatyana McFadden was more than eight minutes back in second, four seconds ahead of Scaroni. Her most unusual win came off the course. London will run over two days in 2027, and on 30 September she played the men's champion, Sabastian Sawe, at rock, paper, scissors for the traditional Sunday slot. She won two games to nil in front of a Guinness World Records adjudicator. That result puts the elite women and the women's wheelchair field on the Sunday, 25 April 2027. Debrunner, a four-time winner there, will line up as the reigning champion. - [Ashley Paulson: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ashley-paulson): Runners / Ashley Paulson Photo: Guinness World Records 🇺🇸 Ashley Paulson Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 702 (9 November 2026) Ashley Paulson is an American ultrarunner who has built most of her record on 100-mile races. She has also moved up to the 200-mile distance and beyond. Her general UTMB Index stands at 702. Her first listed win came in 2019 at the Red Mountain 55k, where she covered 54km and 1,600m of climb in 5:16:46. In 2020 she won the Squaw Peak 50 Mile, an 83km course with 3,360m of ascent, in 9:22:01. Later that year she won the Bear 100 in 22:42:37. That race runs to 163km with 6,460m of climbing. She added the Antelope Island Buffalo Run 100 Mile in 2021, winning in 18:26:45. More wins followed. She took the women's title at the Zion 100 in 2023 in 23:04:52 and at the Antelope Canyon 100 Mile in 2024 in 23:23:30. Also in 2024 she finished ninth woman at the Cocodona 250 in 91:20:00. That course runs to 401km with 12,236m of climb. In 2025 she won the Buffalo Run 100 Miler in 16:13:38 on a route with 3,096m of ascent. She then returned to Zion and won again in 21:18:14, 1 hour 46 minutes and 38 seconds quicker than her 2023 time. She was also 62nd woman over 101km at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K that season, in 13:07:19. In 2026 she set out to complete the Triple Crown of 200s. She had already raced the Tahoe 200 and the Bigfoot 200. At the Moab 240 she was leading the women's race when organisers Destination Trail stopped the event on Sunday 11 October. The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel had brought flooding, freezing rain and strong winds. Cottonwood Creek became impassable beyond the Bridger Jack aid station at about 96 miles, and around 70 runners and volunteers spent the night there. All were brought out by bus on the Sunday. No runner was officially recorded as a finisher. The race is a single loop of about 240 miles from Moab, with nearly 9,500m of climbing. - [Rory Bosio: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rory-bosio): Runners / Rory Bosio Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Rory Bosio Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Rory Bosio is an American mountain ultrarunner who won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc in 2013 and 2014. Her 2013 win in 22:37:26 took almost two hours and 20 minutes off the women's course record. She was seventh overall that day, beaten by only six men. She is from Truckee, California, and ran her first one-mile race at the age of eight. After graduating from the University of California, Davis in 2007 she worked as a paediatric intensive care nurse at its medical centre in Sacramento. The North Face and CamelBak have sponsored her. Western States was an early focus. She was fourth there in 2010 and second in 2012 in 18:08:06. Later that summer she was fourth in a shortened UTMB. In 2014 she won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail in Italy in 14:29:54, then defended her UTMB title in 23:23:20. In 2015 she spent ten months filming the third season of the series Boundless. In 2017 she crossed Corsica on foot via the 125-mile GR20. She was second at the 2018 TDS, won Ushuaia by UTMB in Argentina in 2019 and placed eighth at that year's UTMB. - [William Boffelli: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/william-boffelli): Runners / William Boffelli Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇮🇹 William Boffelli Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 938 (9 November 2026) William Boffelli is an Italian skyrunning specialist who races for Kailas Fuga. His UTMB Index of 938 is one of the highest in this batch, built almost entirely on short, steep mountain races. His biggest win came at the 2026 Trofeo Kima, one of skyrunning's toughest races, 48km with 3,800m of climbing, which he won in 6:07:43. He has also won the Matterhorn Ultraks Extreme three times, in 2020, 2021 and 2025. He races frequently on the vertical kilometre circuit, winning the VTMB Vertical VK2 in 2021, its successor VK 2000 in 2024, and the 2026 VK2. He placed 16th at the Golden Trail Championship's 112km GTC Azores race in 2020, and won the Ultra Supramonte's Ultra Sky Supramonte in 2023. He opened 2026 with wins at the Maga Skymarathon, the Pizzostella Skymarathon and the Trail del Centenario, alongside 2nd place at the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg's Walserwaeg Trail, a race where he was also runner-up in both his 2025 outings. - [Lucija Krkoc: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lucija-krkoc): Runners / Lucija Krkoc Photo: UTMB profile 🇸🇮 Lucija Krkoc Country 🇸🇮 Slovenia Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 759 (9 November 2026) Lucija Krkoc is a Slovenian mountain and skyrunner with a UTMB Index of 759. Her results stretch back to 2006 on home trails around Ljubljana. She has been near-unbeaten domestically in recent years, winning the Ultra Trail Vipava Valley 30 km LEGIONAR three times running, in 2023, 2025 and 2026, and the KNAP Trail T' Sredna in both 2024 and 2026. In 2025 she also won the Julian Alps Trail Run by UTMB's Kranjska Gora 25K, the International Skyrace Carnia and the Kočevsko Outdoor Festival's Wolf Trail 30K, and was 4th woman at the Monte Zerbion Skyrace. She represented Slovenia at the 2024 European Off-Road Championships, finishing 7th woman in the Elite Up & Down, and won that year's Dolomythsrun Skyrace. Her career includes wins going back to the Smarna Gora Race near Ljubljana, which she has raced regularly since 2006, and the Collio-Brda Trail Marathon in 2017. - [Hugh Chatfield: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hugh-chatfield): Runners / Hugh Chatfield Photo: UTMB profile 🇬🇧 Hugh Chatfield Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 886 (9 November 2026) Hugh Chatfield is a British ultrarunner who races for Team Altra and the Elite Trail Team. His biggest win came in 2023 when he took first place in the Dragon's Back Race, a five day, 380 kilometre traverse of the mountains of Wales. He has built a wide range of results across skyrunning, ultra distance and mountain marathon events. Chatfield has twice finished fourth in the Ultra-Trail Snowdonia 100K, in 2023 and 2024, over a course of around 104 kilometres. He also placed fourth at the Transgrancanaria Advanced race in 2024 after finishing 23rd there the year before. At the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships he finished 12th in the Long Trail 82km event. He has won several British sky and trail races outright, including the Rab Helvellyn Sky Ultra and the SkyRun Eryri 14 Peaks Ultra. In 2026 he added a win at the Chianti Ultra Trail's shorter race and a seventh place finish at the full distance event. His UTMB Index of 880 places him among the leading British ultra racers on the current circuit. - [Ryan Sandes: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ryan-sandes): Runners / Ryan Sandes Photo: iRunFar 🇿🇦 Ryan Sandes Born 1982 (age 43 or 44) Country 🇿🇦 South Africa Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 800 (9 November 2026) Ryan Sandes is a South African trail runner, born in Cape Town on 10 March 1982. In 2010 he was the first person to win all four races in the 4 Deserts series. He won the Leadville Trail 100 in 2011 and the Western States 100 in 2017. He races for Salomon. Sandes holds degrees in construction and quantity surveying from the University of Cape Town. His desert campaign began in 2008, when he won both the Gobi March and the Sahara Race. A year later he won the Jungle Ultra in Brazil in a course record and was second in Namibia. In 2010 he completed the set, finishing in Antarctica, after also winning in Chile's Atacama Desert. Each is a self-supported stage race of about 250 km. In 2011 he won the Leadville Trail 100 by more than 30 minutes from Dylan Bowman, in 16:46:54. In 2012 he was second at Western States in 15:03:56. That year he also won The North Face 100 in Australia and the Hong Kong 100. He then lowered Russell Pasche's record for the 90 km Fish River Canyon trail to 6:57. The old mark was 10:54. In 2014 he won Transgrancanaria, the second race of the Ultra-Trail World Series, and was second at the Ultra-Trail Mt. Fuji. With Ryno Griesel he set a fastest known time on the Drakensberg Grand Traverse that year, about 200 km with 9,000 m of climbing. The pair took on the Great Himalaya Trail in 2018. Their time for the 1,504 km route was 24 days, 4 hours and 24 minutes. He won Western States in 2017 in 16:19:37. He won the Ultra-Trail Drakensberg 160 in 2021 and the MUT Miler in 2023. In 2025 he was second at the Cocodona 250, a 413 km race, in 61:21:04. She works as a landscape architect. She did not go up a mountain until she was 25, climbing Snowdon, and only took up running to join two friends training for a half marathon in Conwy. - [Thomas Fafard: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/thomas-fafard): Runners / Thomas Fafard Photo: Kevin Mackinnon / Canadian Running Thomas Fafard Runs Thomas Fafard is a Canadian distance runner from Quebec, born on 6 December 1998. He made his name on the track over 5000m and on the country before moving up to the marathon. He has represented Canada at the Olympic Games. His first international medal came as a junior. At the 2017 Pan American U20 Championships in Trujillo, Peru, he took silver in the 5000m. Five years later he won his first senior medal of note, another 5000m silver, at the NACAC Championships in Nassau in the Bahamas. He added a second silver that year at the Pan American Cross-Country Championships in Brazil. 2024 was his breakthrough season. He won the Vancouver Sun Run in April. In May he lowered his 5000m best to 13:05.07, missing the Olympic qualifying standard by seven hundredths of a second. A month later he was second over 5000m at the Canadian trials. His world ranking then secured him a place in the Canadian team for the Paris Olympics in July. He has since taken to the roads. His marathon debut in Chandler, Arizona produced 2:10:29, a Quebec record. The Chicago Marathon on 11 October was harder going. He finished 38th in 2:16:23, almost six minutes outside his best, in a race that drew more than 55,000 runners. Personal bests Event Time Where Year 13 05.07 28 39.29 From Wikipedia, checked monthly. - [Marianne Hogan: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/marianne-hogan): Runners / Marianne Hogan Photo: Meghan Hicks / iRunFar 🇨🇦 Marianne Hogan Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 810 (9 November 2026) Marianne Hogan is a Canadian ultrarunner who races for Salomon. She started out as a competitive triathlete, racing on Triathlon Canada's junior national team as a teenager and reaching as high as 11th at a World Championships in Hamburg, Germany. She kept racing track and cross country through five years of college in California. After college she switched to trail running, tired of the rigid pacing of triathlon, and was drawn quickly into the ultrarunning scene around 2017. That year a fall on a trail run left her with a spiral fracture of her tibia and fibula, needing two surgeries and years away from racing, though she stayed involved through coaching, crewing and pacing. She returned to racing in 2021 with Ultra-Trail Harricana and Ultra-Trail Cape Town, then won the Bandera 100k outright in 2022, earning a Golden Ticket to the Western States 100. Hogan made her Western States debut in 2022 and finished third, then took second at UTMB later that year. She was third again at UTMB in 2024, and third at Western States in both 2025 and 2026, a run of three straight podiums at the race. The 2026 Western States was her best run there, in far cooler conditions than her two previous, hotter editions. Hogan led through a rolling high country section before digestion problems slowed her in the middle miles, then fought a close battle over the closing six miles from Pointed Rocks with Caitlin Fielder of New Zealand. She finished third for the third year running, just under an hour quicker than in 2025, and without needing a headlamp, a goal she had held since her first Western States. Asked about taking third place again, Hogan said it would be a shame to feel disappointed by another Western States podium finish, calling that a way of letting life pass her by. - [Nathan Maguire: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nathan-maguire): Runners / Nathan Maguire Photo: Encirc Nathan Maguire Runs Nathan Maguire is a British wheelchair racer who competes in the T54 class. He was born in Salford on 27 July 1997 and has lived in Chester and, as of 2022, in Elton, Cheshire. He came to sport through wheelchair basketball at the age of eight, coached by Josie Cichockyj. At 15 he switched to racing at Greenbank Sports Academy. He now trains with Kirkby Athletics Club. His range runs from 100 metres on the track to the half marathon on the road. His early wins came on the streets of London. He took the under-17 wheelchair mini-marathon over 3 miles at the London Marathon in both 2014 and 2015. In 2016 he was in the British 4 x 400 metres T53/T54 squad at the Rio Paralympics, where the team finished second in its heat. At the 2017 World Para Athletics Junior Championships he collected two silvers and a bronze. The following year he raced for England at the Gold Coast Commonwealth Games and placed fourth over 1500 metres. At the 2018 European Championships he left with four medals: relay gold and bronze in the 100, 200 and 800 metres T54. The delayed Tokyo Paralympics brought his biggest team result. Great Britain took silver in the mixed 4 x 100 metres relay. He also reached the 400 metres T54 final and finished sixth, though he went out in the 800 metres heats. Earlier that summer he won bronze in both the 400 and 800 metres T54 at the European Championships, edging fellow Briton Danny Sidbury in the shorter race. The high point came in 2022. He won the 1500 metres T54 at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games, a few weeks after taking the 400 metres wheelchair title at the British Championships. He has won the British 400 metres mixed class race more than once. The results since have been consistent rather than golden. He was fifth in the 400 and 800 metres and seventh in the 1500 metres at the 2023 World Championships. In 2024 he took world bronze over 800 metres. At the Paris Paralympics that year he finished fourth in both the 400 and 800 metres, a place off the podium twice, and fifth in the 1500 metres. Away from the track he has spoken up for his sport. In 2019 he criticised funding cuts to British para sport and the gap with able-bodied events. Since Paris he has argued for more international competitions to give para athletics a bigger stage. On the road he remains quick. On Sunday 4 October he won the men's wheelchair race at the Manchester Half Marathon in 47:01, a course record, on a route that drops downhill out of Trafford and makes the field climb back up it to the finish on Talbot Road. - [Lizzy Hawker: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lizzy-hawker): Runners / Lizzy Hawker Photo: EpicTVAdventure / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Lizzy Hawker Born 1976 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Lizzy Hawker is a British endurance runner, born Elizabeth Hawker on 10 March 1976. In 2000 she ran the London Marathon, her first long-distance event, before turning to trail ultramarathons. Hawker won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc at her first attempt in 2005, despite having owned a pair of trail shoes for only 10 days beforehand. She went on to win UTMB five times in total, a record for a male or female runner. The North Face began sponsoring Hawker in 2005, and she won the IAU 100km World Championships the following year. Until 2007 she was employed by the British Antarctic Survey as a researcher, before relocating to a training base in the Swiss Alps. That year she also set a record for the 199-mile route between Everest South Base Camp and Kathmandu, completing it in 77 hours 36 minutes. At the 2010 IAU 100km World Championships, Hawker led for much of the race before fading to take bronze behind Ellie Greenwood and Monica Carlin. In 2011 she set a women's 24-hour world record of 153.5 miles in Llandudno, Wales, and cut her Everest to Kathmandu record to 71 hours 25 minutes. The following year she won UTMB again, added the 100-mile Run Rabbit Run in Colorado, and set a women's record at the Spartathlon while finishing third overall. Hawker lowered her Everest Base Camp to Kathmandu record again in 2013, completing the route in 63 hours. Training runs along the Tour de Monte Rosa inspired her to create her own race, the 93-mile Ultra Tour Monte Rosa, which she launched with a Zero Edition in August 2015. In 2016 she covered 1,600km across Nepal's Himalayas on foot, combining running, hiking and climbing. Hawker holds a PhD in physical oceanography and has written a book about her running, Runner: A Short Story About a Long Run.
