- [Grete Waitz: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/grete-waitz): Runners / Grete Waitz Photo: Shannon / Wikimedia Commons 🇳🇴 Grete Waitz Born 1953 Country 🇳🇴 Norway Runs Road, Track (legend) Grete Waitz was a Norwegian marathon runner, born Grete Andersen in Oslo on 1 October 1953. She competed as a middle-distance runner before her marathon breakthrough, running the 1500m at the 1972 Munich Olympics as a 19-year-old. In 1978 Fred Lebow invited her to run the New York City Marathon, and she won on debut, taking two minutes off the women's course record in 2:32:30. Waitz went on to win the New York City Marathon nine times between 1978 and 1988, more victories than any runner has taken in a single major marathon. In 1979 she became the first woman to break two and a half hours for the marathon, winning in New York in 2:27:33. She set the marathon world record four times in total, lowering it to 2:25:29 in London in 1983. She won gold in the marathon at the 1983 World Championships in Helsinki and silver at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, behind Joan Benoit. She took the London Marathon title in 1983 and again in 1986, when she ran her personal best of 2:24:54, and she also won the Stockholm Marathon in 1988. Across track and cross country she also won the World Cross Country Championships five times and set world records over 3000m, 8km, 10km and 15km. Waitz retired from top competition after a knee injury forced her out of the 1988 Seoul Olympic marathon. She later coached Liz McColgan and served as ambassador for the JPMorgan Chase Corporate Challenge for more than 25 years. In 2007 she founded the cancer care charity Aktiv mot Kreft, and in 2008 King Harald V made her a Knight, First Class, of Norway's Royal Order of St Olav. Waitz died on 19 April 2011, aged 57. Norway honoured her with a state funeral, and she is commemorated with statues in Oslo and at Walt Disney World's EPCOT, as well as the annual Grete's Great Gallop race in New York. - [Laura Hottenrott: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/laura-hottenrott): Runners / Laura Hottenrott Photo: Ninaninaninanina / Wikimedia Commons 🇩🇪 Laura Hottenrott Born 1992 (age 33 or 34) Country 🇩🇪 Germany Runs Road, Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 799 (9 November 2026) Laura Hottenrott is a German runner who moved from the road marathon into mountain and trail racing. Born 14 May 1992, she races for ASICS and holds a UTMB Index of 799. On the road she ran a marathon personal best of 2:24:32 at the 2023 Valencia Marathon. She won bronze in the marathon at the 2017 German Athletics Championships, and lined up in the women's half marathon at the 2020 World Championships for that distance, held in Gdynia, Poland. At the 2018 European Athletics Championships in Berlin she started the marathon but did not finish. She has since built one of the strongest records at the Jungfrau-Marathon in Switzerland, winning the mountain race outright in 2021, 2022, 2025 and 2026, and taking 3rd in 2024. In June 2023 she finished 4th in the vertical race at the World Mountain and Trail Championships, and 2nd in the team classification alongside Hanna Gröber, Laura Hampel and Domenika Meyer. Her other wins include the Salomon Cappadocia Ultra-Trail's CST race in 2024 and the Eiger Ultra Trail's E51 Panorama Trail in 2025. At Sierre-Zinal she has placed 5th in 2025 and 10th in 2026, and she opened 2026 with a win at the Davos X-Trails Silver Run. - [Roberto Delorenzi: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/roberto-delorenzi): Runners / Roberto Delorenzi Photo: Roberto Delorenzi / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇭 Roberto Delorenzi Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 931 (9 November 2026) Roberto Delorenzi is a Swiss trail and skyrunning specialist for Brooks Trail Runners, with a general UTMB Index of 933. He races widely across the European skyrunning circuit, from short vertical races up to full marathons. In 2026 he won the Istria 100 by UTMB 42K in 02:50:48, and was runner-up at both the Wildstrubel Wild 25 in Leukerbad and the Val d'Aran by UTMB Sky race in Baqueira Beret. He also finished 11th at Zegama-Aizkorri and 20th at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc that year. His best season came in 2024, when he won the European Off-Road Championships Up and Down race, the Lozere Trail Skyrace, the Calamorro SkyRace and the Marato dels Dements. He also ran his fastest Sierre-Zinal that year, finishing fifth in 02:32:26, and was third at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc. He has raced Sierre-Zinal every year since at least 2021, and won the Dacia UTMB Mont Blanc ETC and the Classic Greina Trail K27 in 2023. - [Alain Santamaria: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/alain-santamaria): Runners / Alain Santamaria Photo: ISF / iancorless.com 🇪🇸 Alain Santamaria Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 934 (9 November 2026) Alain Santamaria is a Spanish trail and mountain runner who competes on the biggest skyrunning and ultra circuits in Europe. He carries a UTMB Index of 929 and has raced for the X-Bionic Integrity team. In 2024 Santamaria won both the vertical kilometre and Sky races at the Desafio Urbion round of the ISF Skyrunning World Championships, taking two world titles in a single week. That year he also won the Ultra Trail Cote d'Azur Mercantour outright and finished eighth at Zegama-Aizkorri, one of the sport's toughest mountain marathons. He carried that form into 2025, finishing fourth in the short trail race at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. He raced often across the season, taking in more than a dozen events in Spain, France and further afield, though he did not finish that year's Zegama-Aizkorri. 2026 has brought a heavy European schedule. Santamaria finished fifth at the UTMB Mont-Blanc OCC over 60 km, fourth at the European Off-Road Running Championships trail race, and won the CAMOVI Montes de Viveiro race outright. He has also helped set up Open Trail Team, a project pairing traditional running sponsors with backers from outside the sport, and has spoken publicly about the need for clearer minimum pay standards in professional trail running. - [Kyle Brotherton: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kyle-brotherton): Runners / Kyle Brotherton KB 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Kyle Brotherton Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road, Track Kyle Brotherton is a Scottish wheelchair racer from Port Glasgow. He won the men's wheelchair 10K at the 2026 Great Scottish Run in Glasgow, finishing in 31:17. He first took part in sport at the age of seven, at an inclusive club at Greenock Sports Centre. He went on to race in the pool and on the track. In 2014 he won the Mini London Wheelchair Marathon. Two years later, aged 16, he was third over 200m at the Swiss Open Nationals and fourth at 100m, 400m and 800m. At the time he named the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics as his goal. At the 2018 School Games National Finals at Loughborough, racing for Scotland, he took silver in the wheelchair 800m in 2:04.28. It was his fourth School Games and his first medal there. He admitted afterwards that he had gone off too quickly and had to hold on over the second lap. Later that year he was named Para athlete of the year at the Inverclyde Sports Awards. He raced in the T54 class for Red Star Athletics Club and swam for Port Glasgow Otters. - [Robbie Britton: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/robbie-britton): Runners / Robbie Britton Photo: Zoe Salt / iRunFar 🇬🇧 Robbie Britton Born 1986 (age 39 or 40) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 787 (9 November 2026) Robbie Britton is a British ultra-distance coach and athlete based in northern Italy. On 25 and 26 February 2023 he set a new British record for 24 hours on the track, covering 277.439 kilometres at the Turin 24 hour race. That beat David Dowdle's mark of 274.48 kilometres, which had stood since 1982. Britton had run on the same Turin course before, finishing with an individual bronze medal at the 2015 World 24 Hour Championships. His distance there, 261.14 kilometres, remained his personal best for almost eight years and helped the Great Britain team to gold. He holds a Masters degree in Performance Coaching from the University of Stirling and a postgraduate diploma in sports nutrition from the International Olympic Committee. On the trails Britton has raced widely across Europe, North America and Asia. In 2026 he won the Campo dei Fiori Trail 50K in Italy and finished second at both the Maremontana K50 and the 304 kilometre Terra de Gigantes. In 2024 he finished 6th at the Leadville Trail 100 Run in Colorado, and in 2023 he took 6th place at the KAT100 by UTMB, a 160 kilometre race with almost 9,820 metres of climbing. He now coaches other athletes through his own business and has written the book 1001 Running Tips: The Essential Runner's Guide, published by Vertebrate Publishing. He draws on more than a decade of racing at the top level of ultra distance and track running. His UTMB Index of 788 reflects his continuing form on trail courses alongside his track record. - [Eszter Csillag: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/eszter-csillag): Runners / Eszter Csillag Photo: iRunFar 🇭🇺 Eszter Csillag Country 🇭🇺 Hungary Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 795 (9 November 2026) Eszter Csillag is a Hungarian ultrarunner who works as an art historian. She grew up in Budapest and now spends much of her time in Hong Kong. She took up trail running there after a friend invited her out onto the Twin Peaks, two steep hills above the city, and started racing ultramarathons in 2016. Csillag first drew wider attention in August 2021, when she finished fourth at the CCC race at UTMB, a striking result for a runner with no major sponsor at the time. She began working with coach Ida Nilsson that year, training six days a week. She placed fifth at the Transgrancanaria 129k in 2022 and fifth at UTMB itself that year, then finished third at the Western States 100 in both 2023 and 2024. Her 2024 Western States run was faster still. She moved into second place after Dusty Corners and was passed by Fu-Zhao Xiang after Michigan Bluff. By Foresthill she had slipped to fifth and was struggling on the drop down to the river. Cold water at the crossing revived her, and on her coach Jason Koop's plan she pushed up the climb to Green Gate, caught back up to Emily Hawgood and held on to finish third again, about half an hour faster than the year before and the fourth-fastest women's time in the race's history. Csillag also sits on the Pro Trail Runners Association's women's committee. In 2024 the group ran a campaign to bring more attention to the women's race at Western States and UTMB, selling T-shirts printed with the words For the women's race. The first batch sold out within a day. - [Rebecca Bunting: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rebecca-bunting): Runners / Rebecca Bunting Photo: UTMB profile 🇬🇧 Rebecca Bunting Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 733 (9 November 2026) Rebecca Bunting is a British ultrarunner who has built a strong record on courses over 40 kilometres since 2021. She won her first major ultra at the TSUNAMI Clovelly Marathon in 2021 and followed it with victory at the Endurancelife Exmoor Marathon in 2022. Both wins came over technical coastal and moorland terrain in the south west of England. In 2024 Bunting won the South Downs 50K, and in 2026 she added the Centurion South Downs Way 50km title in a time of 3 hours 49 minutes. That same year she finished third at the Vietnam Mountain Marathon's 50km World Trail Majors race. Her results show a consistent record of winning domestic ultras before testing herself further afield. Bunting's UTMB Index of 733 reflects her run of podium finishes across British and international ultra distance races. She continues to race on courses combining significant climbing with technical terrain. Her recent form places her among the leading British women at the 50 kilometre distance. - [Nicky Spinks: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nicky-spinks): Runners / Nicky Spinks Photo: Nicky Spinks / runbg.co.uk 🇬🇧 Nicky Spinks Born 1967 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) UTMB Index 608 (9 November 2026) Nicky Spinks is a British fell runner, born Nicola Spinks on 22 April 1967, who is now a farmer in Yorkshire. She began competitive running in 2001, in a four-mile fell race, and first completed the Bob Graham Round in 2005. She lowered the women's record for the round to 18 hours 12 minutes in 2012, then to 18 hours 6 minutes in 2015. Spinks also set the women's record for the Paddy Buckley Round, at 19 hours 2 minutes, in 2013, and for the Ramsay Round, at 19 hours 39 minutes, in 2014. From 2014 to 2016 she held the women's record for all three major 24-hour British mountain rounds at once, a feat no man has managed. Jasmin Paris broke her individual records in 2016, setting a combined time of 50 hours 10 minutes across the three. Spinks became the fourth person ever, and only the second inside 48 hours, to complete a double Bob Graham Round, finishing in 45 hours 30 minutes on 15 May 2016. Her time beat the record Roger Baumeister had set in 1979 by more than an hour. She went on to complete a double Ramsay Round in 55 hours 56 minutes in 2018 and a double Paddy Buckley Round in 57 hours 27 minutes in 2019, becoming the only person to complete doubles of either round. In 2011 Spinks set a new women's record of 64 Lakeland peaks climbed within 24 hours, beating Anne Johnson's 1994 mark of 62. The record passed to Carol Morgan in 2020, but Spinks reclaimed it in 2021 by covering the same 65 peaks in a faster time. She also ran the Joss Naylor Lakeland Challenge in 11 hours 2 minutes in April 2017, another women's record, and has won the Fellsman four times. Spinks has continued to compete at ultra distances into her fifties. She won the Arc of Attrition 100 miles in 2022, and in 2025 won both the Montane Winter Spine Challenger North and the 388km SwissPeaks Trail. She has twice entered the Barkley Marathons, in 2019 and 2023. - [Dave Phillips: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/dave-phillips): Runners / Dave Phillips Photo: Rasselbock Running 🇬🇧 Dave Phillips Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Dave Phillips is a British ultrarunner who has won some of the hardest long trail races in the country. He also holds the UK men's backyard record. He set it at the 2026 Backyard Ultra World Team Championship, running 90 yards as the last British runner standing. That is about 603 km in 90 hours. He won the Montane Summer Spine Race in 2023 in 76:59:33. Peter Mortimer, in second, was more than 16 hours behind. The next April he won the SILVA Northern Traverse, crossing England from coast to coast over 300 km. He finished in 47:32:14 despite the gales of Storm Kathleen. He was second to Kim Collison at the 2025 Montane Winter Spine Race in 85:58:08. In January 2026 he won the 303 km Terra de Gigantes in Portugal in 40:51:33. Between races he chases records on Britain's long-distance paths, with 13 fastest known times listed. In May 2022 he ran the whole South West Coast Path in 10 days 8 hours 24 minutes. In 2025 he ran the Thames Path from Woolwich to its source in 33:20:45. That year he also set times on the Essex Way and the North Downs Way. In 2026 he added Glyndwr's Way and Offa's Dyke, the second in 1 day 20 hours 13 minutes. His first published backyard result came at Suffolk in June 2026. He won with 65 yards, one more than Sam Mayhew. At Sherwood Pines that October the hosts, Rasselbock Running, called him "the cool cucumber from day one". Matthew Blackburn stayed with him until yard 90, which he could not finish. That left Phillips to run the last lap alone. His 90 yards went three past the previous best by a British man. The team finished on 939 yards, a national record and fifth in the world. After his final lap his first thought was for Blackburn. He said Blackburn had pulled him out of "a dark place" during the race. - [Matt Blackburn: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/matt-blackburn): Runners / Matt Blackburn Photo: Rasselbock Running 🇬🇧 Matt Blackburn Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra, Road Matt Blackburn is an ultrarunner from New Mills who specialises in backyard and fixed-time races. He came to the sport late, entering a marathon with no racing behind him and moving on to ultras in 2015. He has twice been the assist in the longest races ever run at Suffolk. He won the UK race at the 2022 Backyard Ultra World Team Championship with 47 yards. At Suffolk he dropped out after 35 yards in 2020. He came back in 2021 and ran 80 yards alongside John Stocker, whose 81 was a world best at the time. Blackburn called it "three and a half days for a DNF". In 2024 he went further, reaching 87 yards as the assist to Lukasz Wrobel's 88. That stood as the best by a British man. He is just as strong over fixed time. He won the UMF Winter Edition 48-hour race in Italy in 2022 and 2023. His 48-hour best is 368.330 km, eighth overall at the 2025 GOMU World Championship in Poland. He was second at the Sparta City Ultra 24-hour in 2024 with 228.619 km, and second again in 2026. Earlier he ran 218.257 km for fourth at the Tooting Bec 24-hour track race in 2017. He has finished the Spartathlon three times. His fastest was his first, 29:48:11 in 2018, and he ran 31:00:10 in 2024. He has raced Big's Backyard Ultra in Tennessee twice, reaching 63 yards in 2025. At the 2026 Backyard Ultra World Team Championship at Sherwood Pines he went past his own British best. He reached 89 yards before stopping in yard 90 as the assist to Dave Phillips. Britain's 939 yards was a national team record and ranked fifth in the world. - [Damian Hall: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/damian-hall): Runners / Damian Hall Photo: David Miller / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Damian Hall Born 1975 (age 50 or 51) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Damian Hall is a British ultrarunner, author and climate activist who grew up in the Cotswolds. He did not begin running as an adult until 2011, aged 36, and completed his first marathon dressed as a toilet the following year. In 2016 he represented Great Britain at the IAU Trail World Championships in Portugal. Hall holds several Fastest Known Times on long British trails. He ran the 230 mile Cape Wrath Trail self supported through a Scottish winter alongside Beth Pascall, and has also held records for the South Wales Traverse and Wainwright's Coast to Coast. A 2020 bid to hold the Pennine Way FKT ended when John Kelly went faster. He won the Spine Race outright in January 2023 and the Ultra Tour Monte Rosa four years earlier. His best finishes on the world stage came in the same era, placing fourth in the Tor des Geants and fifth at UTMB. He has twice made the final loop of the notoriously secretive Barkley Marathons without completing it. Away from racing, Hall is vegan and a founding member of The Green Runners, campaigning against races sponsored by high carbon companies. His books include In It For The Long Run and We Can't Run Away From This, alongside walking guidebooks to the Cotswolds and the Pennine Way. Three documentaries, Wrath, Underdog and Totally FKT, have followed his record attempts and races. - [Hans Troyer: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hans-troyer): Runners / Hans Troyer Photo: JanSternagel / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Hans Troyer Born 2000 (age 25 or 26) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 930 (9 November 2026) Hans Troyer is an American ultrarunner, born on 16 February 2000. He is from Newnan, Georgia, and took up running to stay fit for football. He went to Trinity Christian High School, then to Augusta University on a running scholarship, where he raced as a steeplechaser. At Augusta he broke the school's 10,000m record, along with several other school records, and made the All-Region team as a steeplechaser in 2023. After time away from the sport, working as a graduate assistant, he made a rapid return to running in 2024 and set course records in his first two ultramarathons. He then broke the USA Track and Field 50 Mile Championship course record by 12 minutes, a run that became the subject of a documentary about his rise. He set another course record that year at the Bandera 100k. In 2025 Troyer ran the second-fastest time ever recorded at the JFK 50 Mile to win it, and was called arguably America's best ultramarathon athlete. He also won the Bandera 50k, the Blue Ridge 50k and the Way Too Cool 50k, and was runner-up at the Canyons 100k. Those results earned him a first start at the Western States 100, where he finished eighth, and fifth place in Ultra Running's 2025 Ultrarunner of the Year. Troyer kept the form going into 2026, winning the Black Canyon 100k that February and setting a course record by more than five minutes. Later that year he finished third at the CCC race at UTMB, leading through the Champex-Lac checkpoint at 54km before Italy's Cristian Minoggio pulled clear of him on the climb toward Trient. - [Nadir Maguet: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nadir-maguet): Runners / Nadir Maguet Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇮🇹 Nadir Maguet Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 931 (9 November 2026) Nadir Maguet is an Italian trail and skyrunner who races for La Sportiva. His career stretches back to at least 2012, when he finished second at the Gran Trail Valdigne. In 2026 he finished second at the Lavaredo Ultra Trail's 50K race, in 04:06:42, and third at Transvulcania on La Palma. The Lavaredo Ultra Trail, in Italy's Dolomites, has been a regular target for Maguet. He won its 20K race in 2024 and was runner-up there in 2025. He also finished second in the longer 50K race in both 2023 and 2026. He won the MAGA Skymarathon and the Skyrace des Matheysins in 2024, and the HOKA Val d'Aran PDA race in 2025. In 2023 he won the ultraKtrail UKT 32K. Earlier in his career Maguet won the Ring of Steall Skyrace in Scotland in 2019, having been runner-up there in 2018. He also won the Misurina Sky Marathon and the Matterhorn Cervino Xtrail, both in 2016. - [Merijn Geerts: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/merijn-geerts): Runners / Merijn Geerts Photo: Merijn Geerts / Strava 🇧🇪 Merijn Geerts Country 🇧🇪 Belgium Runs Trail & Ultra Merijn Geerts is a Belgian backyard ultra runner from Wilsele. He has set the format's world record four times, and three of those records he shared with his compatriot Ivo Steyaert. The first came in May 2022 at the Backyard Masters in Germany. Its Race of the Champions only took runners who had already done 45 laps at another backyard. Geerts outlasted Ireland's Keith Russell, who stopped after 89 laps, and finished a 90th to reach 603.5 km. That beat the 85 laps Harvey Lewis ran at Big's Backyard Ultra in 2021. Five months later he ran for Belgium at the World Team Championships. He and Steyaert kept going for 101 hours, more than 420 miles and then retired together. In 2024 the pair did it again with Frank Gielen, and all three stopped together after 110 hours. In October 2026 Geerts and Steyaert each completed 124 laps at the Belgian race, 831.5 km in a little over five days. That passed the 119 laps Australia's Phil Gore ran at Dead Cow Gully in 2025. Because both chose not to start lap 125, the rules gave the race no winner. He races on his own too. He was sixth at Big's Backyard Ultra in 2023 with 100 yards, third at Dead Cow Gully in 2025 with 102 and third at Legends Backyard Ultra in 2026 with 110. - [Evi Gudelius: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/evi-gudelius): Runners / Evi Gudelius EG 🇩🇪 UTMB Index 691 Film My Run 🇩🇪 Evi Gudelius Country 🇩🇪 Germany Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 691 (9 November 2026) Evi Gudelius is a German mountain and trail runner. Her racing covers a wide range, from a 3.3km vertical kilometre to a 71km trail with almost 4,000m of climb. She holds a general UTMB Index of 691. Her standout result of 2026 came in Dorfgastein, Austria, on Saturday 17 October. She finished second in the women's race at the Beinhoat das Vertical in 49:55. That event closed the 2026 VK OPEN World Cup season as its final round, in the series run by the International Skyrunning Federation. Her compatriot Sophia Reuss won in 48:16, so Germany took the top two places. Gudelius finished 1:39 behind Reuss and 2:04 ahead of Serbia's Sladjana Zagorac, the 2025 champion, who was third in 51:59. The direct route climbs 1,200m beneath the cable car to the Fulseck mountain station, which sits above 2,000m. The race takes its name from an Austrian dialect phrase meaning brutally hard. She has also reached the podium in longer trail races in the Alps. At the Zugspitz Ultra Trail by UTMB she was second woman in the Mittenwald Trail, covering 44km and 2,110m of climb in 4:31:55. She was third woman in the MOUNTAINMAN Nesselwang XXL-Trail, a 71km course with 3,952m of ascent, in 8:02:42. At the Alpenplus Ötzi Trailrun in Naturns she was third woman in the Sunny Mountain Trail, running the 30km course and its 2,100m of climb in 3:31:25. That runner-up finish in Dorfgastein closed the 2026 World Cup season for her. Taken together, her results show a runner who can hold her own on short, steep vertical climbs as well as on long mountain trails. - [Sabrina Verjee: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sabrina-verjee): Runners / Sabrina Verjee Photo: Steve Ashworth 🇬🇧 Sabrina Verjee Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 673 (9 November 2026) Sabrina Verjee is a British fell runner who works as a vet. She studied human sciences at Oxford before training in veterinary medicine at Cambridge, where she also rowed and took up modern pentathlon and adventure racing. Her first ultramarathon win came at the Grand Tour of Skiddaw in 2014, a race she went on to win again in 2015, 2016 and 2018. In summer 2019 Verjee won the Spine Fusion, a summer race along a route similar to the Pennine Way, in 81 hours 19 minutes. The following January she was fifth overall and first woman in the winter Spine Race, in 108 hours 7 minutes. In September 2020 she set a new female record for the Pennine Way of 3 days 2 hours 28 minutes, a mark that stood for almost a year before Anna Troup ran faster. Verjee also chased a round of the 214 Wainwright summits, a 325 mile route with 36,000 metres of climbing. Her first attempt in July 2020 was completed in 6 days 17 hours but was not ratified as a record because she received assistance during the effort. She succeeded on her third attempt in June 2021, completing the route in 5 days 23 hours 49 minutes, the fastest time by anyone at that point. The overall record was later broken by John Kelly in May 2022. On the UTMB circuit Verjee races for La Sportiva and has completed some of the toughest events on the calendar. In 2026 she won the 292 kilometre Centurion Sea to Sea 300km and finished 21st in the multi day Ultra Tour Monte Rosa Stage Race. She also won the Arc of Attrition 100 miles in 2024 and finished first woman at Garda Trentino Trail Extra, a 150 kilometre race with 11,000 metres of climbing. - [Sladjana Zagorac: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sladjana-zagorac): Runners / Sladjana Zagorac Photo: Alexander Valchev / International Skyrunning Federation 🇷🇸 Sladjana Zagorac Country 🇷🇸 Serbia Runs Trail & Ultra Sladjana Zagorac is a Serbian mountain runner who specialises in vertical kilometre racing. She also competes over longer trail distances. She does not currently hold a UTMB Index. Her strongest results have come in the International Skyrunning Federation's vertical series. She was champion in 2025, when the series still went by the name VK OPEN World Championships. It was renamed the VK OPEN World Cup for 2026, and she came close to defending her title. She finished the season second overall on 334 points, ten behind Irina Chernova, who competes as an Individual Neutral Athlete. The title was settled at the Grand Finale, the Beinhoat das Vertical in Dorfgastein, Austria, on Saturday 17 October 2026. The direct line climbs 1,200m in 3.3km beneath the cable car to the Fulseck mountain station, which sits above 2,000m. Zagorac was third woman in 51:59. Germany's Sophia Reuss won in 48:16 and Evi Gudelius was second in 49:55. Chernova finished fourth in 53:16, but two earlier wins gave her the edge in the standings. The final carried double points. Over longer ground, Zagorac was fourth woman in the 34K at the 2024 World Masters Mountain Running Championships. That race covered 34km with 1967m of climb, and she finished in 4:01:26. In 2022 she was second woman in the 21K at Trail 100 Andorra by UTMB, a 21km course with 1750m of climb, in 3:10:40. - [Hugh Tibbs: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hugh-tibbs): Runners / Hugh Tibbs Photo: Centurion Running 🇬🇧 Hugh Tibbs Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 882 (9 November 2026) Hugh Tibbs is a British ultrarunner who races for Cambridge Harriers. In October 2025 he won the Centurion Running Autumn 100, breaking the previous course record and setting a new British 100 mile trail record of 13 hours 3 minutes. He has become one of the country's leading 100 mile racers on both road and trail. At the Centurion South Downs Way 100 in June 2026, Tibbs nearly missed the start after being held up by road closures. He sprinted the final distance and jumped several fences to reach the starting pen with 38 seconds to spare. He led the race for long spells before finishing third in 13 hours 46 minutes, his third podium there in three years. Tibbs won the Arc of Attrition in January 2026 in a time just outside the course record, and finished fourth at the ACP British 100km Championships in 6 hours 37 minutes. He also won the Race to the Stones 100km non-stop event in 2025. His results place him among Britain's fastest ultra-distance runners on the trails. - [Frank Gielen: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/frank-gielen): Runners / Frank Gielen Photo: dplusdinsdag 🇧🇪 Frank Gielen Country 🇧🇪 Belgium Runs Trail & Ultra Frank Gielen is a Belgian backyard ultra runner from Kortenberg, near Leuven. Known as Frank the Tank, he shares the 2024 backyard world record with Merijn Geerts and Ivo Steyaert. He also founded dplusdinsdag, a running group with weekly runs around Leuven. His first backyard win came at Legends Backyard Ultra in April 2022, where he lasted 42 yards. That October he ran 67 yards for Belgium at the World Team Championships, third at the Belgian venue. He was fifth at Legends in 2023 with 53 yards. In October 2023 he went to Big's Backyard Ultra in Tennessee for the individual world championship. He ran 97 yards, about 650 km, and finished eighth. His biggest week came at the 2024 World Team Championships in Retie. Gielen, Geerts and Steyaert were the last three on the Belgian course and stopped together after 110 yards, 737.7 km. That set a new world record, and Belgium took the team title. On lap 109 he was filmed doing a set of push-ups. He has also raced the six-day format. At the GOMU Six-Day World Championship in April 2025 he covered 900.5 km, third overall and second man. - [Zak Hanna: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/zak-hanna): Runners / Zak Hanna Photo: UTMB profile 🇮🇪 Zak Hanna Country 🇮🇪 Ireland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 784 (9 November 2026) Zak Hanna is an Irish mountain runner who races for New Balance. He specialises in short, steep events, from vertical kilometres to skyraces of around 20km. His UTMB Index stands at 784. His results stretch back to 2016, when he finished 76th at a WMRA race in Sapareva Banya. He was 52nd at the WMRA race in Premana a year later. His best win came at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc Km Vertical in 2021. He climbed the 1,000m over 4km in 36:17 to take first place. The previous year he was second at the Vertikal Nasego in 36:22 on a course of the same length and climb. In 2019 he placed fourth at the Snowdon International Race in 1:08:09 and seventh at the Drei Zinnen Alpine Run in 1:29:19. He was also 35th in the WMRA senior race at the K42 Adventure Marathon in Argentina that year. He has gone back to some races several times. At the Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K he was 14th in 1:46:32 in 2023 and 19th in 2:02:51 in 2024. At home he was second at the Ecotrail Wicklow 19k in 2024 in 1:31:23. In 2024 he also ran Sierre-Zinal, 31km with 2,190m of climb, in 3:19:05 for 165th. His 2026 season has centred on the vertical. He was 11th at the Transvulcania kilómetro vertical on La Palma in 52:16 and eighth at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc Km Vertical in 39:43. On 17 October he finished eighth in 44:30 at the Beinhoat das Vertical in Dorfgastein, Austria. That race was the Grand Finale of the VK OPEN World Cup, run by the International Skyrunning Federation. Its direct line gains 1,200m in 3.3km beneath the cable car to the Fulseck mountain station. The result lifted Hanna to second in the season standings on 292 points, behind France's Louis Dumas on 332. She also improved her time at the Trofeo Nasego from 2:08:41 in 2025 to 2:09:53 in 2026 while moving up the field. Her UTMB Index of 742 reflects a fast rise through international trail and fell running. - [Josh Kerr: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/josh-kerr): Runners / Josh Kerr Photo: jenaragon94 / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Josh Kerr Born 1997 (age 28 or 29) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track Josh Kerr is a Scottish middle-distance runner from Edinburgh, born on 8 October 1997. He holds the mile world record. He ran 3:42.66 at the London Diamond League on 18 July 2026, beating Hicham El Guerrouj's 3:43.13 from 1999. No men's mile record had stood longer. He went through 1500m in 3:27.62 on the way, which was also a British record. He started at Edinburgh Athletics Club aged eight and later took a scholarship to the University of New Mexico in Albuquerque. There he won three NCAA titles and set a collegiate 1500m record of 3:35.01. He turned professional in 2018 with the Brooks Beasts, coached by Danny Mackey. The global medals came quickly. Bronze in the Olympic 1500m in Tokyo in 3:29.05. World champion in Budapest in 2023, beating Jakob Ingebrigtsen in a sprint in 3:29.38. Silver at the Paris Olympics in 2024 behind Cole Hocker, where his 3:27.79 was a British record. He has also won the world indoor 3000m twice, in 2024 and 2026, and took the British 5000m title in 2025. 2026 has been his best year yet. On 1 August he won the Commonwealth Games mile in front of a home crowd in Glasgow in 3:54.12, pulling away from Cam Myers and Jake Wightman over the last 200m. Then on 13 September he won the first Ultimate Championship 1500m in Budapest in 3:29.35, the same stadium where he became world champion. It was his first 1500m of the year. He got in on an invitation from World Athletics, passed Yared Nuguse with about 250m left and held off Myers, who ran 3:29.68. The win made him Britain's first champion at the event and was worth $150,000. He chose not to race the European Championships in Birmingham, which drew criticism from Ingebrigtsen. Kerr answered that he is "not a robot" and will keep to a handful of meetings a season. He trains in the US with the Brooks Beasts and is now taking an end-of-season break. El Guerrouj's 1500m world record of 3:26.00 is reported to be a likely target for next year. - [Ruti Aga: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ruti-aga): Runners / Ruti Aga Photo: nakashi from Chofu, Tokyo, JAPAN / Wikimedia Commons Ruti Aga Runs Ruti Aga is an Ethiopian long-distance runner, born on 16 January 1994, who made her name over the marathon. She came through on the track and the country as a junior. At the 2012 World Junior Championships in Barcelona she took silver in the 5000m. A year later she was fifth in the junior women's race at the World Cross Country Championships in Bydgoszcz, Poland. She then won the 5000m at the 2013 African Junior Championships in Bambous, Mauritius. Both of her track bests date from that season: 15:13.48 for 5000m in Shanghai and 33:38.39 for 10,000m in Addis Ababa. Berlin was where she first showed at the sharp end of the World Marathon Majors. She was third there in 2016, then runner-up in 2017. In 2018 she was second in Tokyo and second again in Berlin. That Berlin run of 2:18:34 remains her fastest marathon. The same year she ran 1:06:39 for the half marathon in Houston. Her biggest win came at the 2019 Tokyo Marathon, which she took in 2:20:40. Later that year she ran the marathon at the World Athletics Championships. She was then third at the New York City Marathon. That gave her a Tokyo victory and five further top-three places across the Majors. In more recent years she has taken the Xiamen Marathon twice in a row. The race holds Platinum Label status from World Athletics. Her latest victory there came on 11 January 2026 in 2:22:45. On 15 March she won the Meishan Renshou Half Marathon in China in 1:08:04. The sample taken at that Chinese race tested positive for methylprednisolone, a glucocorticoid banned in competition when taken by injection, by mouth or rectally. On 22 October the Athletics Integrity Unit announced a six-year ban, running from 15 March 2026. Two years were for the positive test and four for tampering. The AIU found, with the help of the Ethiopian Anti-Doping Authority, that the prescription she supplied had been forged. It named a clinic that does not exist and was written by someone with no medical registration. The tampering charge covered false information given to investigators on 21 April and a forged document she produced on 4 May. She had been provisionally suspended on 17 September. She did not respond when the forgery evidence was put to her, so the case went ahead with no hearing. Brett Clothier, the AIU's chief executive, said such attempts to cheat "will be exposed". - [Mark Kiptoo: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mark-kiptoo): Runners / Mark Kiptoo Photo: Marie-Lan Nguyen / Wikimedia Commons Mark Kiptoo Runs Mark Kiptoo is a Kenyan distance runner, born on 21 June 1976 in Lumino Village in the Lugari District. He came to the sport late. After finishing school in 1996 he joined the Kenyan Armed Forces, and he began racing only after being posted to Laikipia Air Base in 2002. He served with the United Nations peacekeeping mission in Burundi in 2005 and 2006. He returned home in May 2006 and started training seriously at the age of 30. His first years at the top were spent on the track and over the country. He won the 5000m at the Military World Games in 2007, then defended the title in Rio de Janeiro in 2011 with a games record of 13:06.17. In 2010 he took 5000m bronze at the African Championships and again at the Commonwealth Games, where Moses Kipsiro and Eliud Kipchoge finished ahead of him. That summer he won the 5000m at the DN Galan Diamond League meeting in 12:53.46, which remains his best. He ran 27:14.67 for 10,000m in Eugene in 2008 and 7:32.97 for 3000m in Doha in 2009. In 2012 he became African 5000m champion and added silver over 10,000m. He was seventh at the 2009 World Cross Country Championships. He moved up to the marathon in 2013. On his debut in Frankfurt that October he pushed Vincent Kipruto all the way and finished second, one second behind, in 2:06:16. His marathon best is 2:06:00, run in Eindhoven in 2015. His half-marathon best is 1:00:29, set when he was 34. Age has done little to slow him. Back in Frankfurt in 2018 he ran 2:07:50, a world record for men aged 40 and over. He also holds the M45 marathon record of 2:09:12. Now 50, he is still winning races. In March this year, aged 49, he won the Azkoitia-Azpeitia Half Marathon in 1:03:17, a race he had also won in 2013. On Sunday 4 October, on rain-soaked roads in San Sebastián, he was first to the line at the Rural Kutxa half in 1:03:57. Nobody in the field, of any age, was quicker. The time is a world best for men aged 50 and over. It takes 2 minutes 26 seconds off the 1:06:23 run by Titus Mamabolo of South Africa in 1991. Iraitz Arrospide, a former world 50km champion, was the nearest to him in 1:04:51. - [Kate Storey: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kate-storey): Runners / Kate Storey KS 🇦🇺 Film My Run 🇦🇺 Kate Storey Country 🇦🇺 Australia Runs Trail & Ultra Kate Storey is a cross country runner who competes in the Start Fitness North East Harrier League. The league runs over the autumn and winter, and its fields are sent off in separate starting packs. That means the order across the line and the order on net time do not always match. Her best-documented result came at the league's opening fixture of the new season, held at Thornley in County Durham on 26 September. Storey started in the M pack, while the first woman home had set off in the S pack. Alex Sneddon, a W35, finished first in 27:01 and Amy Fuller second in 27:22. Storey came through for third place on the line in 28:59. Her net time told a different story. Storey covered the course in 26:38, the quickest time recorded by any woman in the race. That put her 28 seconds clear of A Pigford, who was third fastest on net time in 27:06. That run puts her at the front of the women's field as the 2026/27 North East season gets going. A runner of the same name is listed as Australian on the UTMB database, with no current UTMB Index. The records available do not show whether that is the same athlete. He races for Brooks and holds a general UTMB Index of 916. Growing up in Georgia he played baseball and ran cross country, later running for the club team at Miami University. A spell working for a bike company in France followed college, before he completed a master's degree in mathematics. He took up ultra distances in 2023, finishing runner-up on his very first attempt, at the Silver Rush 50 Mile. In 2024 he was 8th man at the Chuckanut 50k in 3:48:11. He then finished 5th man in his 100-mile debut at the Leadville Trail 100, in 17:29:07, on a course with 4,230m of climb. At the 2025 Black Canyon Ultras 100K he was 2nd man in 7:26:53, earning a place at the Western States 100. He returned to Chuckanut that year and was 8th man again, in 4:00:57. His standout result came at the 2025 Javelina Jundred in Arizona. The race runs over five loops in McDowell Mountain Regional Park, near Fountain Hills, and Murray won it in 12:10:12, a course record. That mark survived the next edition on 31 October, when Rob Molke won in 12:11:30, just 78 seconds slower. In 2026 he was 11th man at The Canyons Endurance Runs 100K in 9:16:41. He then made his Western States debut and finished 9th man over the 162km course, in 15:23:12. He still combines racing at the front of American 100-milers with teaching and coaching at Blair Academy. - [Beth Pascall: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/beth-pascall): Runners / Beth Pascall Photo: Matt Bennett / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Beth Pascall Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 693 (9 November 2026) Beth Pascall is a British ultrarunner and paediatrician. She took up rowing while studying medicine at Nottingham, then turned to trail running because it fitted more easily around her medical career. She won the Spine Race on her ultra debut in 2015 and took bronze in the team standings at the 2016 Trail World Championships in Gerês, finishing eighth individually. In 2018 she and Damian Hall set a fastest known time on the Cape Wrath Trail in winter, self-supported, a journey later made into the documentary Wrath. In 2019 she dominated the Ultra-Trail Cape Town 100km, winning in a new course record after the race's other favourites withdrew. In 2020, with racing paused by the pandemic, she trained specifically for the Bob Graham Round and beat Jasmin Paris' women's record by 50 minutes, finishing in 14:34:26, the fourth-fastest time ever recorded by anyone. She won the Canyons 100k in 2021, then went on to the Western States Endurance Run that year. She led from early on to win outright in 17:10:42, the second-fastest women's time in the race's history. A pelvic injury later took her into gravel racing and mountain biking, where she finished second in Scotland's Raiders Gravel race in 2022 and set the speed record for the 200km Lakeland mountain-biking route. She has since returned to trail racing, finishing second at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia's Eryri 50K in 2026. - [Lucy Austin: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lucy-austin): Runners / Lucy Austin LA 🇬🇧 UTMB Index 317 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Lucy Austin Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 317 (9 November 2026) Lucy Austin is a British runner whose name appears in two quite different corners of the sport. One is a trail ultra in England. The other is a new coaching group led by Geoff Wightman. The available records do not confirm that both belong to the same athlete, so they are set out separately here. On the trails, a British woman named Lucy Austin finished the Ultra X 50 England in 2026. The course covered 50km and took in 1,987m of climbing. She completed it in 11:19:12 and was the 71st woman home. Her general UTMB Index stands at 317. A Lucy Austin was also one of four young women chosen by Wightman, the former marathon runner who coached his son Jake to the 1500m world title in Eugene in 2022. Jake won that final in a personal best of 3:29.23. Wightman found his new athletes by putting out a call on Instagram. Around 60 people replied. He drew up a shortlist, interviewed the candidates and then offered places to Austin, Pippa Roessler, Annie Testar and Ella Fryer. The four met for the first time on camera, with the meeting filmed for YouTube. The group are in their early to mid twenties, and none has yet reached the standard for lottery funding. Wightman picked them on potential and because athletes of that age usually take well to a fresh approach to training. Most of them work alongside their running. They train together on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Wightman describes his role as keeping the four "in one piece" while they continue to improve, and he hopes everyday runners will recognise something of themselves in how the group gets on. - [Yenenesh Shimket: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/yenenesh-shimket): Runners / Yenenesh Shimket YS Film My Run Yenenesh Shimket Runs Yenenesh Shimket is an Ethiopian distance runner who has made her name in cross country and is now moving onto the track and the roads. Born on 9 February 2007, she also appears in results as Yenenesh Shimeket. She is still only 19. Her first continental medal came in 2024, when the African cross country title races were held at Hammamet. She was runner-up among the under-20 women there, with fellow Ethiopian Robe Dida the only one ahead of her. That November, aged 17, she won two World Athletics Cross Country Tour races, the French meeting known as the Festival du Cross and Italy's Cinque Mulini, with Sheila Jebet and Nadia Battocletti among those she beat. In January 2025 she won the International La Mandria Cross and was second to Jebet at the Tour Gold race in Hannut, Belgium. She finished seventh in the overall Tour standings. In November 2025 she returned to San Vittore Olona and won the Cinque Mulini for a second time. The track has come along quickly. At the Diamond League meeting in Rabat in May 2025 she was fifth over 3000m in a personal best of 8:32.01. Later that month she ran 15:51.75 for a top-ten place over 5000m at the Kip Keino Classic. A year on she had taken that 5000m best down to 14:48.02 at the Shanghai Diamond League. Before that she placed fifth in the under-20 race at the 2026 World Athletics Cross Country Championships. At the Urban Trail de Lille on 4 April 2026 she ran the 5km road race in 14:24 for third place, behind Marta Alemayo and Hawi Abera. That run ranked her among the ten fastest women ever over the distance. Her latest outing came at the tRUNsylvania 10km in Brasov, Romania, a World Athletics Elite Label race, on 4 October 2026. It was 8°C at the start. Seven women passed 5km together in 15:11 before Shimket went clear with Asefu Abreha and Aynadis Mebratu over the following kilometre. Mebratu pushed on from 7km, and Shimket held on until the final kilometre. Abreha won in 30:16 and Mebratu took second in 30:19. Shimket was third in 30:21, a world under-20 best for 10km, as Ethiopians filled all six podium places across the two races. She was born on 9 September 1999 and studied at Sheffield Hallam University. She once competed for Oxford City AC. She has also shown real ability in the long jump on its own. Her rise began as a junior. In 2018 she broke into the world's top 40 heptathletes. That same year she placed seventh at the World U20 Championships. Her first major senior medal came at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, where she took heptathlon bronze. She also wore a Great Britain vest at the 2022 European Championships and finished seventh. Two years later she placed seventh again at the 2024 European Athletics Championships. In 2024 she won the long jump title at the British Athletics Championships. Selection for the Great Britain heptathlon team at the Paris Olympics followed, and she finished 10th at the Games. In February 2025 she took long jump silver at the British Indoor Championships. Alice Hopkins, also from Oxfordshire, beat her to the title. Her latest major result came at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Four years after her bronze in Birmingham, she improved to heptathlon silver. Later that year he added a Commonwealth Games bronze, finishing behind Moses Kipsiro and Eliud Kipchoge. At the 2012 African Championships he won 5000m gold and 10,000m silver. His other track bests are 7:32.97 for 3000m, run in Doha in May 2009, and 27:14.67 for 10,000m, run in Eugene in June 2008. Away from the track he was seventh at the 2009 World Cross Country Championships and second to Deriba Merga at the World 10K Bangalore that year. He moved up to the marathon in 2013 after missing selection for that year's World Championships. His debut came in Frankfurt in October, where he pushed Vincent Kipruto all the way and finished one second behind him in 2:06:16. Frankfurt has been a recurring venue ever since. He returned in 2018 and ran 2:07:50, a world record for the over-40 age group. He is now setting records in the M50 category. In March 2026, still aged 49, he won the Azkoitia-Azpeitia Half Marathon in 1:03:17, a race he had also won in 2013. On 3 October he ran 1:03:57 for the half marathon, beating the M50 best of 1:06:23 set by South Africa's Titus Mamabolo as a split in 1991. Three weeks later he took Mamabolo's other record. On Sunday 25 October, in his fifth Frankfurt Marathon, he finished 13th overall in 2:15:24. Mamabolo's M50 mark of 2:19:29 had been set in Durban at the South African championships and had stood for 35 years. Kiptoo beat it by 4:05. - [Jacob Adkin: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jacob-adkin): Runners / Jacob Adkin Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Jacob Adkin Born 1996 (age 29 or 30) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 934 (9 November 2026) Jacob Adkin is a British mountain and sky runner born on 18 May 1996 in Edinburgh. He tried swimming as a boy before following his older sister Scout into fell running, around 2008. He won the Scottish junior hill running title in 2014 and again in 2015. He broke through at senior level by winning the Mont-Blanc Vertical Kilometre in 2018. The following year he won the European mountain running title in Zermatt. He beat Norway's Stian Ovegaard Aarvik by 25 seconds and helped Great Britain to team gold. He took silver in the uphill race at the 2024 European Championships in Annecy, again with team gold for Great Britain. In 2026 he won a second European title, in the uphill race at Kamnik in Slovenia. He carries a UTMB Index of 934 and was fourth at Sierre-Zinal that year, his best finish there. He trains in Chamonix, coached by fellow Briton Robbie Simpson. Early in his career he balanced university study with athletics. He has also won the Mozart Half Marathon in Salzburg, in 2023. - [Keely Hodgkinson: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/keely-hodgkinson): Runners / Keely Hodgkinson Photo: Erik van Leeuwen, attribution: Erik van Leeuwen (bron: Wikipedia). / Wikimedia Commons Keely Hodgkinson Runs Keely Hodgkinson is an 800m runner from Atherton in Greater Manchester, born on 3 March 2002. She joined Leigh Harriers at nine and won county titles in middle-distance events and cross country as a junior. Trevor Painter and Jenny Meadows have coached her in Manchester since 2019. She is part of the city's M11 Track Club. Her first international gold came at 16, at the 2018 European Under-18 Championships in Győr, Hungary. She won there in 2:04.84, a championship record. Her senior breakthrough came quickly. In 2021 she won the European indoor 800m title in Toruń, Poland, the youngest woman ever to do so. At the delayed Tokyo Olympics that summer, aged 19, she took silver behind Athing Mu in 1:55.88. That run removed Kelly Holmes's British record of 1:56.21, which had stood since 1995. She closed the season by winning the Diamond League final in Zürich. Silver became a familiar colour for a while. She was second at the 2022 World Championships in Eugene, 0.08 seconds behind Mu in 1:56.38, and second again at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and the 2023 World Championships. In between she won the European outdoor title in Munich in 1:59.04 and retained her European indoor crown in Istanbul in 2023. A 1:55.77 at the Paris Diamond League in June 2023 lowered her British record. The breakthrough came in Paris in 2024. She led the Olympic final from early on and pulled clear in the last 100 metres, finishing ahead of Tsige Duguma and Mary Moraa. She also won a second European outdoor title that year, was voted BBC Sports Personality of the Year and received an MBE in the 2025 New Year Honours. The 2025 season was disrupted by injury, but she still left the World Championships with bronze. In February 2026 she ran 1:54.87 at Liévin for an indoor world record over 800m. She then won the world indoor title in Toruń. Outdoors she set another British record in Stockholm in June, though Audrey Werro beat her there. Werro finished ahead of her again at both the European Championships and the World Athletics Ultimate Championship, with Hodgkinson second and Femke Broeders-Bol behind her each time. She was left off the 20-strong shortlist for the 2026 World Athlete of the Year awards despite that indoor world record. UK Athletics has put her at the head of its lottery-funded World Class Programme for 2026-27, alongside Josh Kerr, with the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 the stated target. - [Jacob Fincham-Dukes: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jacob-fincham-dukes): Runners / Jacob Fincham-Dukes Photo: Sandro Halank, Wikimedia Commons / Wikimedia Commons Jacob Fincham-Dukes Runs Jacob Fincham-Dukes is a British long jumper, born on 12 January 1997. He grew up in Harrogate, North Yorkshire, and went to school and sixth form in the town. He then crossed the Atlantic to Oklahoma State University. There he set the school's indoor and outdoor long jump records and reached the NCAA Championships. Between the ages of 15 and 22 he collected six England junior long jump titles. His first international medal came in 2015. At the European Athletics Junior Championships he took silver behind Anatoliy Ryapolov, with a personal best of 7.75m. His senior championship debut followed in March 2021 at the European Indoor Championships at the Arena Toruń in Poland. He finished seventh in the final, shortly after jumping a personal best of 8.08m at the British trials at Lee Valley. A year later, on 26 March 2022, he won the Texas Relays with a wind-assisted 8.45m. The wind reading was 3.6, and the mark was listed as the second longest jump in British history. The summer of 2022 brought his first English title, won with 7.58m at the Bedford Athletic Stadium on 31 July. At the European Championships in Munich that August he qualified for the final, then criticised television coverage for paying too little attention to field events. In the final he opened with a season's best of 8.06m to lead after the first round. He finished second and appeared to have his first senior major medal. The French federation then appealed against that opening jump. The appeal was upheld and the jump was ruled a foul. A British counter-appeal failed, and he was moved from second to fifth. National titles followed. He won the British Outdoor Championships in Manchester in July 2023 with 7.86m, set in the second round. In April 2024 he jumped 8.20m, with a wind of 1.2, to win the Texas Invitational. That followed an 8.02m indoors, met the UK Athletics Olympic qualifying standard and took him to sixth on the UK all-time list. He was fourth at the European Championships in Rome and retained his British title in Manchester in June. At the 2024 Olympic Games he finished fifth with 8.14m. He added the British Indoor title in Birmingham in 2025. His funding status has since changed. UK Athletics put forward 62 names for lottery support over the 2026-27 cycle, aiming at the Los Angeles Games in 2028. Fincham-Dukes was no longer on the podium level. His removal and heptathlete Jade O'Dowda's promotion were the only changes to that 21-strong group. Performance director Paula Dunn acknowledged the work of those left out and said development "looks different for everyone". - [Marc Scott: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/marc-scott): Runners / Marc Scott Photo: Sandro Halank, Wikimedia Commons / Wikimedia Commons Marc Scott Runs Marc Scott is a British long-distance runner, born on 21 December 1993, who races on the track and the roads. He started running at 11 and played football as a boy. He went to the University of Tulsa in the United States after contacting the cross country coach, Steve Gulley, himself. Gulley later said Scott had "talked his way into a scholarship" and a place on the team. In 2017 he won the NCAA Division I 10,000 metres in 29:01.54, running his final lap in 55.44 seconds. After Tulsa he joined the Bowerman Track Club. On the track he ran the 5000 metres for Great Britain at the 2017 World Championships in London, the 2019 edition in Doha and the Tokyo Olympics. He was fifth in the 5000 metres final at the 2018 European Championships. He has won the British 5000 metres title three times, in 2018, 2020 and 2022. His 2020 win came in 13:32.98. He won his first global medal in Belgrade in 2022, taking third over 3000 metres at the World Indoor Championships. Only one British man had medalled over that distance at the championships before him. That year he also became British indoor 3000 metres champion. In Boston in 2022 he ran 12:57.08 for 5000 metres indoors, a European record. Outdoors his bests are 13:05.13 for 5000 metres and 27:10.41 for 10,000 metres, both set at San Juan Capistrano in 2021. His road record is just as solid. He won the Great South Run in 2019, and his 10-mile best of 46:58 dates from Portsmouth that year. He was first home at the Great North Run in 2021 and also won the 10K in Manchester that year, setting his 10K best of 28:03 there. His half marathon best is 60:39, from Larne in 2020. He became UK Athletics 5K road champion in September 2024, and that month finished runner-up to Abel Kipchumba at the Great North Run. He won the Great South Run again in October 2025, clocking 47:21. This autumn he was eighth at the 45th Great North Run, the route from Newcastle over the Tyne Bridge to South Shields. He was the first Briton home in 1:02:10. On 18 October he ran the Amsterdam Marathon in wet and cold weather. He finished 27th in 2:10:14 and was the leading British man. He was on the podium potential level of UK Athletics' Olympic World Class Programme last year but was left out of the 2026-27 list. - [Mahamed Mahamed: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mahamed-mahamed): Runners / Mahamed Mahamed Photo: Ian Robertson from East Lothian, Scotland / Wikimedia Commons Mahamed Mahamed Runs Mahamed Mahamed is a British long distance runner who made his name in cross country before moving up to the marathon. He was born in Jarso, Ethiopia, on 18 September 1997. He moved to Southampton with his family in 2011, aged 13, and later studied sports coaching and sports development at Southampton Solent University. He raced for Southampton AC and has represented Great Britain at senior level. His early titles came on the country. He took the national under-17 cross country title at Parliament Hill in London on 25 February 2015. In 2018 he won both the English under-20 national title and the Inter-Counties. He was senior English National Cross Country champion in 2019 and again in 2022. In between, he ran for Great Britain at the 2019 World Cross Country Championships in Aarhus. He also won the British universities title in Edinburgh in February 2020. On the roads he took second place at the Big Half in London in September 2023. Only Jack Rowe beat him, and Andrew Butchart and Mo Farah both finished further back. His marathon debut came in Valencia that December, where he ran 2:08:42. That put him seventh on the UK all-time list. Four months later he was fourth in London in 2:07:05, the third-fastest time by a Briton. It earned him a place at the Paris Olympics, where he finished 57th. He was ninth in London in 2025. 2026 has been his strongest season. He ran a half marathon best of 61:09 in Barcelona in February. At the London Marathon in April he finished tenth in 2:06:14, the race in which Sabastian Sawe ran a world record 1:59:30. That run took the British marathon title and moved him to second on the British all-time list. He was second in the British 10km road championships at the Great Manchester Run on 31 May, in 28:28. On 16 August he placed seventh in the European Championships marathon in Birmingham, in 2:09:43. UK Athletics has moved him up from the confirmation tier to podium potential on its lottery-funded World Class Programme for 2026-27. His next target is likely to be London in April 2027. The men's elite race there, on Saturday 24 April, doubles as the British trial for the 2027 World Championships in Beijing and the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. The first two British men will be eligible for Beijing if they have run the qualifying time of 2:06:00. His best stands 14 seconds outside that mark. He took up trail running in 2019 and races for Altra and the Elite Trail Team. Wigley has reached the podium at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia's 100K three times in four years, finishing third in 2023, 2025 and 2026 and fourth in 2024. He has also been on the podium at the Arc of Attrition's Arc50, placing third in 2025 and second in 2026. He won the British Trail Running Championships in 2022 and the Elite category at the Original Mountain Marathon in 2023. In 2025 he was selected for Great Britain's Long Trail squad at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, held that year in Canfranc, Spain, finishing the 82km long trail race in 11:05:10. Away from trail racing, Wigley has run a road marathon in 2:26 at Seville in 2024 and completed the 200-mile Race Across Scotland in 2022. He began coaching other runners in 2025. - [Joe Steward: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joe-steward): Runners / Joe Steward Photo: England Athletics 🇬🇧 Joe Steward Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 880 (9 November 2026) Joe Steward, born on 19 August 1996, is a British mountain runner from Salford. He runs for Salford Harriers and Athletic Club and has been based in Austria for several years, training on Alpine terrain. He holds a UTMB Index of 890 and specialises in short, steep mountain and vertical races. Steward made his name on the Mountain Running World Cup's vertical circuit in 2023, finishing third at the Piz Tri Vertical and second at the Vertical Nasego. He won the Canfranc-Canfranc Vertical in Spain that September, his first World Cup victory, and also won the Sky Gran Canaria race, going on to finish third overall in the season's World Cup standings. His best season came in 2024. He won the British mountain running title at Keswick in April, then took the European title in the uphill event at Annecy in May, beating training rival Jacob Adkin by more than a minute. In July he defended his European crown at the Snowdon International Mountain Race, winning in 1:05:41 despite a difficult, wet descent. Steward has also raced further afield on the UTMB circuit. In 2025 he won the After Shock 24km race at New Zealand's Faultline Ultra, then took the Tarawera Ultra-Trail's T21 event in 1:18:47. - [Puripol Boonson: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/puripol-boonson): Runners / Puripol Boonson Photo: Chensiyuan / Wikimedia Commons Puripol Boonson Runs Puripol Boonson is a Thai sprinter who concentrates on the 100m and 200m. He was born on 13 January 2006. He first came to notice in Vietnam, winning the 100m, the 200m and the 4x100m relay at the Southeast Asian Games of 2021, held in Hanoi. In Almaty, Kazakhstan, on 26 June 2022 he ran 20.19 for 200m with a legal tailwind of 1.7 metres per second. That was a Thai record and an Asian best for both under-20 and under-18 athletes. Among youth sprinters, only Erriyon Knighton and Usain Bolt had gone quicker. At the World Athletics U20 Championships in Cali that August he clocked 10.09 in a 100m semi-final, then a world under-18 best, and placed fourth in the final in 10.12. Senior honours soon followed. In July 2023 he helped Thailand win the 4x100m relay at the Asian Athletics Championships in Bangkok in 38.55, a national and championship record. At the Asian Games in Hangzhou that autumn he won 100m silver in 10.02, though the wind was too strong for the time to count as a record. He carried the Thai flag at the Paris Olympics in 2024, sharing the job with the 12-year-old skateboarder Vareeraya Sukasem. On the track he was third in his 100m heat in 10.13, behind Oblique Seville and Abdul Hakim Sani Brown. His semi-final ended in last place in 10.14. Later that year he won 100m silver at the world under-20 championships in Lima in 10.22, a first medal for a Thai athlete in that category. He then took the baton for the relay final with Thailand second to last and hauled them up to bronze in 39.39, four hundredths ahead of France. The 2025 season brought a run of silver medals. He was second in the 100m at the Asian Athletics Championships in Gumi in 10.20 and added another silver in the relay in 38.78. At the World University Games he finished second in 10.22 behind Bayanda Walaza, the 2024 world champion. His World Championships in Tokyo ended in the 100m semi-finals, where he ran 10.17. The breakthrough came at the Southeast Asian Games on home soil. On 11 December he ran 9.94, and no Southeast Asian athlete had broken 10 seconds before. He won the final in 10.00, then took the 200m in 20.07 and the relay in 38.28. Both were Thai records. This year he won the 60m at the Asian Beach Games in Sanya, China, on 25 April in 6.62. At the Asian Games in Nagoya he opened with 9.95 in the 100m heats and a Games record of 9.91 in the semi-finals. In the final on 25 September he lowered the Thai record to 9.90. The last Thai to win the Asian Games 100m title was Suchart Jairsuraparp, in 1978. Only China's Su Bingtian, with his Asian record of 9.83, has run faster among Asian men. Two days later he completed the sprint double. He had already set a Games record of 20.10 in the opening round of the 200m. The final was run on a wet track into a headwind of 0.3 metres per second. Boonson crossed the line in 19.88, the only man in the field under 20 seconds. The time matched the Asian record set by China's Xie Zhenye in 2019 and made him just the third Asian man to dip below 20 seconds. Huang Youwen of China was a distant second in 20.45. He is 20 years old. Personal bests Event Time Where Year 100 m 9.90 NR Nagoya 2026 200 m 19.88 NR Nagoya 2026 From Wikipedia, checked monthly. - [Success Eduan: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/success-eduan): Runners / Success Eduan SE Film My Run Success Eduan Runs Success Eduan is a British sprinter from Blackley in Manchester. She was born on 27 September 2004 and races mainly over 200m, with a growing record as a 4 x 100m relay runner. Her speed was first noticed in school cross-country races at St Matthew's Roman Catholic High School in Moston, where she was also head girl. She moved on to Loreto College and then the University of Salford, fitting a midwifery course around her training. Her first international medals came at the European Under-20 Championships in Tallinn in July 2021. She took bronze in the 200m and brought the British 4 x 100m team home for gold on the final leg. A year later she was national under-20 champion at 200m and earned a place at the World Under-20 Championships. In February 2023 she won the senior British indoor 200m title in Birmingham in 23.49 seconds. That August, in Jerusalem, she collected another European under-20 bronze in the 200m and a relay silver. In May 2024 she ran 11.52 for second behind Joy Eze in the 100m at the BUCS Championships, racing for Salford. The 2025 season was her breakthrough. On 11 May she ran the last leg as Great Britain won the women's 4 x 100m at the World Athletics Relays. At the European Under-23 Championships in Bergen she won the 200m in 22.74 seconds. She then anchored the British quartet to gold in 42.92, a championship record. Back in Birmingham she was fourth at the UK Championships in a personal best of 22.53, and she was named in the relay pool for the World Championships in Tokyo. She has kept moving up in 2026. In Gaborone she anchored the British women's 4 x 100m team as they booked a place at the 2027 World Championships. In June she became UK 200m champion with another personal best, 22.43 seconds. She ran 22.53 at the London Athletics Meet on 18 July and finished seventh in the 200m final at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. On 15 August she won European gold in Birmingham alongside Dina Asher-Smith, Amy Hunt and Imani-Lara Lansiquot. The four clocked 42.05, more than a second ahead of the next team. She also reached the individual 200m final there, was seventh at the Diamond League Final in Brussels in September, and a week later helped the British mixed 4 x 100m team to third at the first World Ultimate Championship in Budapest. UK Athletics has now put her forward for a step up from confirmation level to podium potential on its Olympic World Class Programme for 2026-27. The scheme is paid for by the National Lottery through UK Sport and is built around the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Her nomination, like every other, still needs to be signed off by UK Sport. - [Ja'Kobe Tharp: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ja-kobe-tharp): Runners / Ja'Kobe Tharp Photo: youthrunnermag / Wikimedia Commons Ja'Kobe Tharp Runs Ja'Kobe Tharp is an American sprint hurdler and the world record holder for the 110m hurdles. He was born in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, on 30 September 2005 and went to Rockvale High School in the same state. He raced for Auburn University before turning professional. His events are the 110m hurdles outdoors and the 60m hurdles indoors. His rise was quick. In 2024 he won the Southeastern Conference title in Gainesville, Florida, in 13.18. That broke a US under-20 record held by Renaldo Nehemiah since 1978. He was second at the NCAA Championships that June, then won the US under-20 title in Eugene, Oregon. At the World U20 Championships in Lima, Peru, he took gold in 13.05 into a 0.5 metres per second headwind over the 99cm junior hurdles. In 2025 he won the NCAA indoor 60m hurdles in 7.45 in Virginia Beach on 15 March. He added the NCAA outdoor 110m title in Eugene in 13.05. He was third in Monaco on his Diamond League debut on 11 July in 13.17. On 3 August he won the US title in 13.01, ahead of Cordell Tinch. He was sixth in the world final in Tokyo that September and one of three finalists for the Bowerman Award, which went to Jordan Anthony. 2026 has been his year. At the NCAA indoor championships he ran 7.36 in his heat on 13 March. He won the final the next day in 7.32, taking down Grant Holloway's collegiate record of 7.35. Only Holloway and Colin Jackson have run faster. Then came the outdoor NCAA Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene. In a preliminary heat he ran 12.75 with a 1.0 metre per second tailwind, beating the 12.80 Aries Merritt ran in 2012. The record is awaiting ratification. Nobody had set a world record at that meeting since 1976, when Dwight Stones did so in the high jump. Tharp admitted it had not been on his "bingo chart" for the meeting. On 12 June he won the final in 12.90 into a headwind, with Kendrick Smallwood second in 12.95. He then gave up his remaining college eligibility and turned professional. He was second at the Prefontaine Classic on 4 July in 12.91. In Budapest on 14 July he won the István Gyulai Memorial in 12.85, the fifth fastest time in history, despite easing up to celebrate before the line. Four days later he won in London with a meeting record of 12.89. He won in Silesia, Poland, on 23 August in 13.05. On 4 September he took the Diamond League title in Brussels in 13.03, ahead of Jamal Britt and Trey Cunningham. A week later he won the first World Ultimate Championship, leading an American clean sweep ahead of Tinch and Bradley Franklin. On 6 October he was named among the ten men nominated for the 2026 World Athlete of the Year award. Public voting closes at midnight CEST on 17 October. Three male finalists will be announced in November, and the winners will be revealed in Monaco on 29 November. He turned 21 last month. - [Winfred Yavi: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/winfred-yavi): Runners / Winfred Yavi Photo: Martin Rulsch, Wikimedia Commons / Wikimedia Commons Winfred Yavi Runs Winfred Yavi is a Bahraini steeplechaser and the reigning Olympic champion over 3000m steeplechase. She was born in Kenya on 31 December 1999 and comes from Ukia in Makueni County. She switched to Bahrain at 15 and became eligible to represent her new country in August 2016. The barriers and water jump are her speciality, but she has also won major titles on the flat from 1500m up to 10,000m. Her rise was steady rather than sudden. At 17 she reached the 2017 World Championships final and placed eighth in 9:22.67. A year later she took bronze at the World Under-20 Championships and lowered her best to 9:10.74 in Monaco. In 2019 she won the 5000m and the steeplechase at the Asian Championships, added bronze in the 1500m, and finished fourth at the World Championships in Doha. She was tenth in the Tokyo Olympic final. Her first run under nine minutes came at the 2022 Prefontaine Classic, where she clocked 8:58.71. She won the Paris Diamond League in 8:56.55 soon afterwards. The major titles followed. Yavi became world champion in 2023 with a personal best of 8:54.29. She then won in Zurich and at the Prefontaine Classic in Eugene, where her 8:50.66 was an Asian record. She took the Diamond League title that season and won both the 1500m and the steeplechase at the Asian Games. In Paris in 2024 she claimed Olympic gold in an Olympic record of 8:52.76. At the Rome Diamond League that summer she ran 8:44.39, taking more than six seconds off her own national record. It left her 0.07 seconds short of the world record and second on the all-time list. She was runner-up to Faith Cherotich at the Diamond League final in Brussels. She has kept winning since. Yavi took the steeplechase in Eugene in 2025 and in Lausanne in 2026. Her other bests include an Asian indoor record of 8:39.64 for 3000m, set in Val-de-Reuil in 2020, and 14:41.99 for 5000m from Liège in 2024. This month she was busier than ever at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan. She arrived having placed third at the Diamond League Final in Brussels. On the Thursday she stepped up to 10,000m and won in 32:39.18. On the Sunday she took the steeplechase in a Games record 9:04.36, ahead of Kazakhstan's Norah Jeruto in 9:06.82. The next day she won the 5000m in 15:10.18. That made three gold medals in five days. - [Mariam Kareem: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mariam-kareem): Runners / Mariam Kareem MK Film My Run Mariam Kareem Runs Mariam Kareem is a sprinter and hurdler from the United Arab Emirates, born on 25 January 2008. Her first international results came over 100m and 200m. Her biggest have come over the 400m hurdles. At 18 she is the Asian Games champion in that event. She was 16 when she ran the 100m for the UAE at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris. She clocked a personal best of 13.26 but did not get through the preliminary round. That September she went to the Arab Junior Athletics Championships for under-18s in Taif, Saudi Arabia. She won the 100m there and ran 24.30 for 200m, a UAE junior record. Her 2025 season brought two golds at the Asian U18 Championships in Saudi Arabia in April, one in the 200m and one in the 400m hurdles. The Asian Athletics Awards later named her Best Asian Under-18 Female Athlete. A month after those titles she stepped up to the senior Asian Championships in Gumi, South Korea, and finished eighth in the 400m hurdles final. In September she ran 57.66, which led the world under-18 rankings. In November she took silver at the Islamic Solidarity Games in 57.42. In August 2026 she reached the 400m hurdles final at the World Athletics U20 Championships in the United States. The following month she travelled to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. She set a UAE record of 55.14 in her heat. In the final she went quicker still and won in 54.31, a Games record and the fastest under-20 time in the world this year. That took more than three seconds off her Islamic Solidarity Games time in about ten months. Both 400m hurdles titles in Nagoya went to young athletes. Qatar's Bassam Hemeida won the men's race in 47.82, with 17-year-old Taiju Goto of Japan second in 47.93. Kareem, still a junior, now holds the Asian Games record in the women's event. He has competed at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, finishing 11th in the long trail event in 2025 and 17th at the 2023 championships in Innsbruck-Stubai. His other results include 4th at the Lavaredo Ultra Trail in 2022 over 121 km, and wins at races including the Grand Raid Ventoux and Trail des Hauts Forts.
