- [Gianmarco Tamberi: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/gianmarco-tamberi): Runners / Gianmarco Tamberi Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons Gianmarco Tamberi Runs Gianmarco Tamberi is an Italian high jumper, born on 1 June 1992. He is an Olympic champion, a world champion and a four-time European champion. Until 2022 he was coached by his father, Marco Tamberi, who set an Italian indoor record of 2.28m in 1983. At major championships he is known for keeping a full beard through qualifying and then shaving off half of it for the final. His rise came quickly. In 2015 he broke the Italian record twice, first with 2.34m in Cologne and then with 2.37m in Eberstadt, where he finished second to Derek Drouin. He was eighth at the World Championships in Beijing that summer with 2.25m. He won every competition he entered in the winter of 2016. That run included 2.38m at Hustopeče on 13 February, still the Italian indoor record, and the world indoor title in Portland in March with 2.36m. On 15 July 2016 he cleared 2.39m in Monaco, which remains the Italian outdoor record. An injury earlier that season kept him out of the 2016 Olympics. The biggest prizes followed. On 1 August 2021 he and Qatar's Mutaz Essa Barshim both cleared 2.37m at the delayed 2020 Olympics and agreed to share the gold medal, a rare outcome between athletes of different nations. Barshim marked the moment by telling him it was "History, my friend". Tamberi became the first Italian to win the Diamond League title in 2021 and won it again in 2022 and 2024. In Budapest in 2023 he took the world title on countback from JuVaughn Harrison of the United States, after both had cleared 2.36m. He added European titles in 2016, 2022 and 2024, the last of them in Rome. He also carried the Italian flag at the Paris 2024 Olympics alongside the fencer Arianna Errigo, and he has won nine national titles. The years after Rome were harder. Tamberi has spoken of injuries and health problems and said that 2025 left him wondering whether his career was nearly over. He answered that in 2026. In Birmingham he won a record fourth European high jump title, his third in a row. He then went to Budapest and won the Ultimate Championship. His winning clearance of 2.37m has not been bettered by any high jumper in 2026, and it sits two centimetres below his own national record. On 24 October 2026, at the age of 34, he was named European Athlete of the Year at the Golden Tracks ceremony in Lausanne. He finished ahead of Armand Duplantis and Miltiadis Tentoglou and became the first Italian to win the award since it began in 1993. His 2.37m in Budapest is also among 18 nominees for the World Athletics Moment of the Year, with the winner to be announced in Monaco on 29 November. - [Mondo Duplantis: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mondo-duplantis): Runners / Mondo Duplantis Photo: Quejaytee / Wikimedia Commons Mondo Duplantis Runs Armand Duplantis, known to almost everyone as Mondo, is a pole vaulter. He was born in Lafayette, Louisiana, on 10 November 1999 and holds both American and Swedish citizenship. In June 2015 he announced that he would represent Sweden. He holds the world record of 6.31m, set in 2026, and is widely considered the finest vaulter the event has produced. He won his first world title at 15. At the 2015 World Youth Championships in Cali, Colombia, he cleared 5.30m at the first attempt and took gold on countback. The world U20 title followed in Tampere, Finland, in July 2018 with a championship record of 5.82m. On 12 August that year he went over 6.05m at the European Championships in Berlin. It added 12cm to his best, set a world U20 record and won his first senior title. At 18 years and 275 days, he became the youngest man to clear six metres. The senior titles have not stopped since. He now has ten at global level. He won Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2020 and again in 2024. He has three world outdoor titles, from 2022, 2023 and 2025, and four world indoor titles, from 2022, 2024, 2025 and 2026. He also won the first World Ultimate Championship in 2026. He has been European champion four times and won the Diamond League final in five straight years from 2021 to 2025. His 2022 season brought three world records and 22 clearances at six metres or higher. The numbers on the bar tell the rest. Renaud Lavillenie's 6.16m had stood since 2014 until Duplantis cleared 6.17m in 2020. He has set 15 world records in all, including 6.25m at the 2024 Olympics. Only three other men have cleared 6.10m: Emmanouil Karalis, Lavillenie and Sergey Bubka. By September 2026 he had gone over six metres in 91 competitions, a run stretching across nine seasons back to Berlin. He was named World Athlete of the Year in 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2025, and Laureus World Sportsman of the Year in 2025. On 6 October 2026 he was named among the 20 nominees for this year's World Athlete of the Year award. Voting closes at midnight CEST on 17 October. The winners will be announced in Monaco on 29 November. Personal bests Event Time Where Year Pole vault 6.31 WR Uppsala 2026 100 m 10.37 Zurich 2024 From Wikipedia, checked monthly. - [Yan Ziyi: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/yan-ziyi): Runners / Yan Ziyi Photo: Ssu / Wikimedia Commons Yan Ziyi Runs Yan Ziyi is a Chinese javelin thrower, born on 22 May 2008. At 18 she holds the world under-20 record and the Asian record with 71.74m. That mark put her second on the world all-time list. In 2026 she has also won the Diamond League title and Asian Games gold. Her rise began in 2024. In March that year she took the Chinese women's title in Tianjin with 61.31m. She went beyond 60m in four of her five competitions that season. In April she threw 62.23m in Chengdu. Later that month she won at the China Athletics GP with 64.28m, a new world under-20 record. It beat Yulenmis Aguilar's 63.86m from 2015. World Athletics' age limit kept her out of the 2024 Olympics. On 30 August 2024 she won the world under-20 title in Lima, Peru. She pushed the under-20 record out to 64.83m in Chengdu in March 2025. On 3 May she was fifth at the Shanghai Diamond League with 60.54m. In August she won the Chinese Championships with 65.89m, improving the under-20 record again. Her age ruled her out of the 2025 World Championships, although she was regarded as a favourite for the title. That November World Athletics named her among the contenders for its women's Rising Star award. The big throw came on 23 May 2026 at the Xiamen Diamond League, a day after her 18th birthday. She sent the spear 71.74m, and World Athletics ratified the under-20 record on 23 July. Her first Diamond League outing outside China followed on 10 June at the Bislett Games in Oslo, where her opening 67.11m won. She won in Paris on 28 June with a first-round 67.44m. In Monaco on 10 July she saved her best for the final round, winning the Herculis meeting with 68.75m. The season's Diamond League Final came in Brussels on 5 September. Her 68.42m there took the trophy, with Japan's Haruka Kitaguchi behind her. Kitaguchi turned the tables at the World Ultimate Championship in Budapest. Yan led with 68.05m but withdrew after her second attempt, and that first throw was enough for second. Her latest title came at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, on 27 September. Her opening throw of 70.46m was a Games record and the second-best of her career. Kitaguchi took silver with 62.70m, almost 8 metres behind. - [Audrey Werro: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/audrey-werro): Runners / Audrey Werro Photo: Quejaytee / Wikimedia Commons Audrey Werro Runs Audrey Werro is a Swiss 800m runner from Fribourg, in the west of the country. Born on 27 March 2004, she took up athletics at the age of nine with Club Athlétique Belfaux. Her first coach there, Christiane Berset Nuoffer, still guides her as a professional. Werro has won nine Swiss 800m titles, four outdoors and five indoors, and holds national records at U18, U20 and senior level. Her junior record was strong. At 17 she won the European U20 800m in Tallinn in 2021, beating athletes up to two years older. A year later she took silver at the World U20 Championships in Cali in 1:59.53, behind Roisin Willis. She retained her European U20 title in Jerusalem in 2023. In 2025 she added the European U23 crown in Bergen with a championship record of 1:57.42. That senior season she missed a world indoor medal in Nanjing by 0.01 seconds, finishing fourth in 1:59.81. She then won the Diamond League Final in Zurich on 28 August in 1:55.91, ahead of Georgia Hunter Bell, and placed sixth at the World Championships in Tokyo in 1:56.17. In October she was named European Rising Star of the Year. Her 2026 season went further still. Indoors she took world silver in Toruń in 1:56.64 behind Keely Hodgkinson. Outdoors she was not beaten. On 7 June in Stockholm she beat Hodgkinson in 1:53.98, the quickest 800m by anyone for 43 years. She improved to 1:53.80 in Paris on 28 June. At the European Championships in Birmingham she went down while leading in the last 120 metres of her semi-final, after Anaïs Bourgoin's hand caught her foot. She was reinstated on appeal and won the final the next day in a championship record of 1:54.81. Hodgkinson was second and Femke Broeders-Bol third. Zurich brought her best yet. On 27 August she ran 1:53.70, a Diamond League record and the third fastest time in history, 0.42 seconds outside Jarmila Kratochvílová's world record. She is only the third woman to break 1:54 and has run three of the five fastest times ever. On 5 September in Brussels she kept her Diamond League title, edging Broeders-Bol by 0.06 seconds in 1:54.75 and removing Pamela Jelimo's 18-year-old meeting record. A week later in Budapest she became the first World Ultimate champion in 1:55.88, with Hodgkinson and Broeders-Bol again second and third. On 24 October Werro was voted European Athlete of the Year at the Golden Tracks ceremony in Lausanne. She is the first Swiss woman to win it. The only Swiss athlete to take either senior award before her was another 800m runner, André Bucher, in 2001. She is also on the 20-strong shortlist for World Athlete of the Year, with the winners due to be named in Monaco on 29 November. The world record is something she thinks about constantly, she has said, though she accepts there is still work ahead of her. - [Avery Pearson: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/avery-pearson): Runners / Avery Pearson Photo: University of Colorado Athletics Avery Pearson Runs Avery Pearson is a Canadian middle-distance runner from Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan, born on 24 May 2003. The 800 metres is her main event, though she has collected titles over 600 metres, 1000 metres and the rarely raced 600 yards. Her start was unpromising. Meadow Lake had no track team. Her father did some of the coaching, and the vice-principal at her school did the rest. She began running during the COVID period without realising it could become a career. She first raced for Canada at the 2021 World Athletics U20 Championships in Nairobi, where she reached the 800m final and placed seventh. She then spent four years with the University of Saskatchewan Huskies, where she studied kinesiology and was named U Sports Female Rookie of the Year. At the 2023 U Sports Indoor Championships she was second over 600m in a personal best of 1:28.83. In March 2024 she won the national 1000m title indoors in Manitoba. At the same championships she was runner-up over 600m and ran the anchor leg as Saskatchewan won both the 4x400m and 4x800m. The 2025 season brought senior progress. She opened in January with a meeting record of 1:30.25 over 600m at the University of Alberta Golden Bear Open. In June she ran 2:03.17 for 800m at the Portland Track Festival. In August she finished third at the Canadian Athletics Championships in Ottawa in 2:03.18. At the Junior Pan American Games in Asunción, Paraguay, she took silver in the 800m. She also won gold in the 4x400m with Isabella Goudros, Emily Martin and Dianna Proctor, in a Games record of 3:31.73. She spent her last season of college eligibility at the University of Colorado, where Sean Carlson was her coach. In February 2026 she ran 2:00.76 indoors, which put her sixth on the Canadian indoor all-time list. A week later at the Big 12 Indoor Championships in Texas she set a meet record of 1:17.92 over 600 yards in the heats, then improved it to 1:17.48 to win the final. She went on to the World Athletics Indoor Championships in Toruń, Poland, where she did not progress beyond the opening round of the 800m. She earned All-American status and qualified for the NCAA Outdoor Championships in June. On 6 October 2026 the On Athletics Club announced that Pearson had signed a professional contract. She joins its Global Team as the first Canadian on the Boulder squad, which trains more than 1,600 metres above sea level under Dathan Ritzenhein. She will race as a professional from 2027. Her 800m best stands at 2:00.76 and her next aim is to break two minutes. According to the club, competing for Canada at the Olympics is another ambition. For her first season as a professional she has said she intends to stay "humble" and learn from those around her. - [Ruth Chepngetich: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ruth-chepngetich): Runners / Ruth Chepngetich RC Film My Run Ruth Chepngetich Runs Ruth Chepngetich is a Kenyan road runner who made her name over the marathon. She was born in Kericho on 8 August 1994 and went to school at Sigowet Primary and Momoniat Secondary. She holds the women's marathon world record of 2:09:56 and won the world title in 2019. At home she has taken national titles at 10,000 metres in 2022 and in the senior women's race at the Kenyan Cross Country Championships in 2023. Her rise came quickly. She won the women's race at the 2018 Istanbul Marathon in 2:18:35, a course record and at that point the seventh fastest time ever run. A year later she lowered the Dubai course record to 2:17:08. On 28 September 2019 she became world champion in Doha. The race began at midnight to avoid the worst of the heat, and only 40 of the 68 starters reached the finish. Her 2:32:43 was the slowest winning time in the history of the women's event. Bahrain's Rose Chelimo took silver in 2:33:46, with Namibia's Helalia Johannes third in 2:34:15. She was third in London on 4 October 2020. In Istanbul on 4 April 2021 she ran the half marathon in 1:04:02, a world record by 29 seconds at the time. That mark has since been beaten. Chicago became her race. She won there on 10 October 2021 in 2:22:31, her first World Marathon Major, after reaching halfway in 67:34 and fading to a 74:57 second half. She still had nearly two minutes to spare. In Nagoya on 13 March 2022 she ran a negative split for a course record of 2:17:18 and collected $250,000. That October she kept her Chicago title in 2:14:18, 14 seconds outside Brigid Kosgei's world record of the day. On 13 October 2024 she went back to Chicago and ran 2:09:56. It removed almost two minutes from Tigst Assefa's 2:11:53 and made her the first woman to go under 2:11 and then 2:10. She dedicated the run to Kelvin Kiptum, the Kenyan men's world record holder, who died in February 2024. Within about five months of that run she failed a drugs test for hydrochlorothiazide, a prohibited diuretic. After a provisional suspension, the Athletics Integrity Unit gave her a three-year ban in October 2025, backdated to April 2025. The usual four years was reduced by one because she admitted the violation. Her world record still stands, as the positive sample came after Chicago. London Marathon chief executive Hugh Brasher has called the time "entirely dubious" and said that was his personal opinion, based on what the AIU has said. The record came under real threat in Berlin on 27 September 2026. Assefa was projected to finish in 2:09:44 at 40km before a ruptured Achilles slowed her to 2:11:04, 68 seconds short of the Kenyan's mark. - [Salwa Eid Naser: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/salwa-eid-naser): Runners / Salwa Eid Naser Photo: Erik van Leeuwen, attribution: Erik van Leeuwen (bron: Wikipedia). / Wikimedia Commons Salwa Eid Naser Runs Salwa Eid Naser is a Bahraini sprinter whose event is the 400m. She was born Ebelechukwu Agbapuonwu in Onitsha, Nigeria, on 23 May 1998, and took up Bahraini nationality in 2014. She won the 100m and the 400m in her first school race at the age of 11. A teacher told her the longer sprint suited her, and she has concentrated on it ever since. Her rise was quick. At the 2014 Youth Olympics she took silver in 52.74, finishing behind Australia's Jessica Thornton. A year later she won the World Youth title in 51.50, reeling in the American Lynna Irby late in the race. In October 2015, still only 17, she won the Military World Games in 51.39 for her first senior title. At the Rio Olympics in 2016 she ran 50.88 in the semi-finals, finished equal ninth and missed the final by a single place. The big results followed. At the 2017 World Championships in London she was last at halfway and fourth off the final bend on a wet track. She came through to take silver in 50.06, behind Phyllis Francis and 0.02 ahead of Allyson Felix. In 2018 she won 10 of her 11 races at the distance. That run included 49.55 in Paris to break Ma Yuqin's Asian record from 1993. It also included 49.08 in Monaco behind Shaunae Miller-Uibo's 48.97 and Asian Games gold in Jakarta. She won the Diamond League title in Brussels in 49.33, having flown in overnight after a relay final in Jakarta. She took the Diamond League title again in 2019. On 3 October that year she won the world title in Doha in 48.14. She was the youngest woman to win the event and the first representing an Asian nation to do so. At the time only Marita Koch, with 47.60, and Jarmila Kratochvílová, with 47.99, had gone faster. She added bronze in the mixed 4x400m relay in an Asian record and finished the season unbeaten. Then came a long absence. In June 2020 the Athletics Integrity Unit provisionally suspended her over whereabouts failures, with one filing failure and three missed tests in a 12-month period. A World Athletics Disciplinary Tribunal threw out the charges that October. World Athletics and WADA appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport. On 30 June 2021 CAS upheld that appeal and banned her for two years, with credit for the provisional suspension, so the ban ran until February 2023. Her results between 25 November 2019 and 30 June 2021 were disqualified. She has been back among the medals since. At the 2024 Olympics she took silver behind Marileidy Paulino in 48.53, the second-quickest run of her career. She signed for the first season of Michael Johnson's Grand Slam Track and won the 400m at the 2025 Kingston Slam in 48.67. Most recently she won the 400m at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, in a Games record of 49.20. Iran's Zara Zarei Manoujan was second in 52.38, more than three seconds back. - [Andreas Reiterer: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/andreas-reiterer): Runners / Andreas Reiterer Photo: photographer unknown 🇮🇹 Andreas Reiterer Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 930 (9 November 2026) Andreas Reiterer is an Italian trail and ultra-running specialist who races for La Sportiva. His UTMB Index stands at 930, built on more than a decade of results across the Dolomites, the Alps and races further afield. Reiterer's biggest ultra win came at the 2024 Eiger Ultra Trail, where he took the 101km E101 route in 11:05:32 with 6,541m of climbing. The same year he won the Chianti Ultra Trail's 103km route in 8:40:33. He has also taken outright victories at the Grossglockner Ultra-Trail in 2021, the Garda Trentino Trail in 2022, and repeated wins at the Alpenplus Ötzi Trailrun and the Innsbruck Alpine Trailrun Festival. On the bigger UTMB World Series stages he has been a consistent podium finisher rather than a winner. He placed 3rd in the 99km UTMB Mont Blanc CCC in 2022 and 4th in the same race in 2021. At the Lavaredo Ultra Trail's 120km route he has finished 2nd and 3rd across three separate years between 2024 and 2026. He was 2nd man at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' long trail race in Innsbruck-Stubai in 2023, an 87km course with over 6,000m of climbing. His 2026 season opened with more of the same pattern. He was 2nd at the Wildstrubel by UTMB Wild 110 in Crans-Montana, 2nd at the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 120K and took a win at AIM Trail Extreme. - [Nico Young: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nico-young): Runners / Nico Young NY Film My Run Nico Young Runs Nico Young is an American distance runner, born on 27 July 2002, who races from 3000m up to 10,000m on the track. He holds the American outdoor 5000m record of 12:45.27. He first came to notice at Newbury Park High School in California. In 2019 he ran 13:39.7 for three miles of cross country at the Woodbridge Classic, a national high school record. He also lowered the high school indoor 3000m record to 7:56.91. That autumn he won Nike Cross Nationals in a course record of 14:52 and Newbury Park took the team title. He went on to Northern Arizona University. As a true freshman he was fourth at the 2020 NCAA cross country championships, covering 10km in 29:58.3. At the 2021 Drake Relays he ran 13:24.26 for 5000m, an American junior record. That time took him to the Olympic Trials, where he finished ninth. In May 2022 he clocked 13:11.30 in San Juan Capistrano. No American teenager had run 5000m faster. He was second at the 2022 NCAA cross country championships in 28:44.5. His big year came in 2024. On 26 January in Boston he ran 12:57.14 behind Adrian Wildschutt, breaking 13 minutes and setting an NCAA record. In March he won the NCAA indoor 5000m and then the 3000m the following day in 7:41.01. Parker Wolfe was second both times. A week later Young ran his first track 10,000m and finished behind Grant Fisher in 26:52.72. That took the collegiate record from the 27:08.49 set by Sam Chelanga. He signed with Adidas on 25 March and turned professional. After placing second to Wolfe in the NCAA outdoor 5000m, he outsprinted Drew Hunter for third in the Olympic Trials 10,000m. In Paris he was 12th in 26:58.11. The 2025 season brought more. On 2 March he ran 12:51.56 for 5000m on a short track, the second fastest by an American. He won the 3000m at the Philadelphia Slam on 1 June in 8:01.03. Eleven days later he won the 5000m at the Bislett Games in 12:45.27, an American record. On 31 July he took the US 10,000m title, edging Fisher by a quarter of a second in 29:02.12. Three days later he was third over 5000m behind Fisher and Cole Hocker. His next race is on the road. Organisers announced 24 elite entries on 27 October, and Young is among them. The Kalakaua Merrie Mile reaches its tenth edition in Honolulu on 12 December. It is held on the eve of the Honolulu Marathon, on a stretch of Kalakaua Avenue next to Waikiki Beach. The women start first with a head start, and prize money is paid on the combined order of finish. Ethan Strand and Oliver Hoare are also in the men's field. The men's course record is 3:53.3, set by Edward Cheserek in 2019. - [Alex Yee: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/alex-yee): Runners / Alex Yee Photo: Rz98 / Wikimedia Commons Alex Yee Runs Alex Yee is a British triathlete who also races seriously on the track and road. He was born on 18 February 1998 and grew up in Lewisham, London. He later studied Sport and Exercise Science at Leeds Beckett University, which gave him an honorary doctorate in July 2025. He has long called himself a triathlete first. His running times would stand up on their own. His triathlon record is the strongest of any athlete in Olympic history. He took individual silver and mixed relay gold at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021, and he was the man who brought the relay team home. In Paris in 2024 he won the individual title. Beth Potter, Sam Dickinson and Georgia Taylor-Brown then joined him for relay bronze. He was also world champion over the standard distance that year. He is only the second man to win both titles in the same season. At the 2022 Commonwealth Games he came out of the water 15th and won the opening gold by 13 seconds from Hayden Wilde. The margin was argued over, because Wilde had served a 10-second penalty for unbuckling his helmet before his bike was racked. Yee also won the mixed relay at those Games and was appointed MBE in the 2022 New Year Honours. On foot he won the British 10,000m title in 2018, at the Night of 10,000m PBs on Parliament Hill. That same year he ran 27:51.94 for the distance on 19 May, under five seconds slower than the British under-23 record Dave Bedford set in 1971. Earlier in 2018 he ran 13:57 at Dulwich parkrun, then the second fastest time recorded at any parkrun. In August 2020 he clocked 13:26 for 5km at Barrowford in Lancashire, six seconds behind Marc Scott. It was the second quickest 5km by a British athlete at the time. Later that month he ran 7:45.81 for 3000m at the Bromley Twilight Meeting. He moved up to the marathon after his 2024 double. At London on 27 April 2025 he ran 2:11:08 for 14th place. He was the second Briton home, which also earned him silver at the British Championships. On 7 December that year he finished seventh in Valencia in 2:06:38. Only Mo Farah has run faster among British men. He has not been shy about the direction of his sport. When triathlon's world governing body signed a deal in October making Hyrox a recognised discipline, he put the question to his 227,000 followers. After a couple of hours, 82% of those who voted were against it. - [Viktoria Angelova: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/viktoria-angelova): Runners / Viktoria Angelova VA Film My Run Viktoria Angelova Runs Viktoria Angelova is a Bulgarian jumper who competes in both the long jump and the triple jump. She was born on 25 April 2009. She is based in Greece, where she is coached by Georgi Pomashki. The triple jump was a new event for her in 2026, and it quickly became her best. Her breakthrough came at the European Athletics U18 Championships in Rieti, Italy. She won the triple jump with 13.98m, a championship record. It was only the fifth triple jump competition of her career. The mark was 40 centimetres further than her previous best and lifted her to eleventh on the Bulgarian all-time list. In August she travelled to Eugene in the United States for the World Athletics U20 Championships. She came home with the world U20 triple jump title. That gave her a European and a world crown in her first season in the discipline. Her 13.98m from Rieti stood as her best for the year. Those results earned her the European Athletics women's Rising Star award for 2026. She was 17 when she collected it in Lausanne on 24 October, at the Golden Tracks awards evening. Czechia's Michal Rada, the world U20 400m hurdles champion, took the men's award. - [Oliver Hoare: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/oliver-hoare): Runners / Oliver Hoare OH 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Oliver Hoare Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Oliver Hoare is an Australian middle-distance runner whose best events are the 1500m and the mile. His biggest title came in 2022, when he won Commonwealth gold over 1500m. His best time for the mile is 3:47.48. On 12 December he races the Kalakaua Merrie Mile in Honolulu, one of 24 elite runners named for the event's 10th edition. The fields were announced on 27 October. The race is a road mile along Kalakaua Avenue, with Waikiki Beach alongside, and is held the day before the 53rd JAL Honolulu Marathon. It is a chase format. The women start first with a set head start, 31 seconds last year, and prize money is paid on the combined finishing order. The winner collects $15,000 from a guaranteed $39,000. The men's field is a strong one. Ethan Strand, the 2025 USATF 1500m champion, arrives with a mile best of 3:46.97, quicker than Hoare's. The line-up also includes Nico Young, who won the 2025 USATF 10,000m title, and US 5000m champion Vince Ciattei, who was second in this race in 2023. The men's course record is 3:53.3, set by Edward Cheserek in 2019. A runner of the same name, listed as a British man, finished the 2023 Salomon Serpent Trail 50k in 5:47:20 for 133rd man. That course covered 50 km with 1190 m of climb. He holds no current UTMB Index. The nationalities in the two records differ, and the available sources do not confirm that the trail result belongs to the Australian miler. - [Benjamin Roubiol: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/benjamin-roubiol): Runners / Benjamin Roubiol Photo: UTMB profile 🇫🇷 Benjamin Roubiol Born 1999 (age 26 or 27) Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 939 (9 November 2026) Benjamin Roubiol is a French trail runner born on 6 November 1999 in Moutiers, Savoie. He grew up in a sports-minded family in the mountains and started out in climbing before switching to trail running, where results came quickly. He races for the ASICS Fuji Trail team and holds a UTMB Index of 941. His early wins came close to home, including the Parcours des Cretes race in 2020, which he finished in 6:49:51, and the High Trail Vanoise in 2022. He reached the 2023 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Innsbruck after finishing runner-up at the French selection race, then launched a late attack around the 70 kilometre mark of the long trail race to overhaul Italy's Andreas Reiterer and take the individual title in 9:52:59, adding team gold for France. Roubiol has since become a two-time French long trail champion. At the 2024 European Trail Championships in Annecy he finished second behind his French teammate Thomas Cardin, with France again taking the team title. Also in 2024 he was runner-up at the European Off-Road Championships trail race. At the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships long trail he took silver, with France's team again winning gold alongside Louison Coiffet. His 2026 season has opened with a win at the Restonica Trail 100K in Corsica and a second place at the French short trail championship on the Trail du Ventoux. - [Jack Kavanagh: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jack-kavanagh): Runners / Jack Kavanagh 🇬🇧 Jack Kavanagh Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track, Road Jack Kavanagh is an English distance runner who races for Holland Sports AC and is coached by Neil Danby. He came to the sport late, taking up running during the Covid-19 pandemic because he enjoyed being outside. He later left his job as a teacher to train full-time. The gamble paid off quickly. He has run for England, and at the UK Athletics Championships in 2025 he finished second over 5000m, beaten only by Josh Kerr. He is a regular at the SportsShoes Podium road races, with outings in Battersea Park, Dulwich and Leicester. In September 2026 he won the UK 5km road title in Cardiff's Bute Park. He arrived as favourite with a best of 13:34 and led after the first lap. Joseph Tuffin passed him on the final lap, but Kavanagh found another gear in the closing metres to win in 13:50. He said days like that made leaving teaching worth it, and turned straight to the cross-country season. - [Dorcus Ewoi: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/dorcus-ewoi): Runners / Dorcus Ewoi DE Film My Run Dorcus Ewoi Runs Dorcus Ewoi is a Kenyan middle-distance runner who lives and trains in the United States. She was born in Kitale on 2 October 1996, and her name is sometimes written as Dorcas. The 800m has long been her main event. Her biggest medal so far came over 1500m. Her American career began at junior college level with South Plains between 2018 and 2020. In 2019 she won the NJCAA Division I indoor mile and the outdoor 1500m. She retained the indoor mile title in 2020, shortly before the pandemic shut down college athletics. A move to Campbell University followed. At the 2022 NCAA Division I outdoor championships she ran 2:03.17 in her 800m semi-final and went no further. A year later she reached the final and finished fifth in 2:02.13, moving up from the chasing group in the closing stretch. She turned professional with Puma Elite Running in 2024 and took her 800m best from 2:01.12 to 1:58.19 that season. She won the Olympic Development 800m at the Penn Relays. In July 2024 she took the Holloway Pro Classic, a World Athletics Continental Tour Silver meeting in Florida, finishing ahead of the reigning Olympic champion Athing Mu. At the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo she took silver in the 1500m. On 12 December Ewoi leads the women's entry for the Kalakaua Merrie Mile, which reaches its tenth edition this year. The road mile is staged in Honolulu on Kalakaua Avenue, with Waikiki Beach alongside, on the eve of the city's 53rd JAL Honolulu Marathon. She arrives with a mile best of 4:17.62 and has never been to Hawaii before. Addy Wiley, the US road mile champion, looks her most likely challenger. The race is run as a chase. The women start first with a set head start, which was 31 seconds last year, and the men try to reel them in. The overall winner collects $15,000. The women's course record is 4:21.66, set by Sinclair Johnson in 2025. Personal bests Event Time Where Year 800 m 1:58.19 2024 1500 m 3:54.92 2025 From Wikipedia, checked monthly. - [Melissa Courtney-Bryant: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/melissa-courtney-bryant): Runners / Melissa Courtney-Bryant Photo: Dave Atkinson / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Melissa Courtney-Bryant Born 1993 (age 32 or 33) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track, Road Melissa Courtney-Bryant is a British middle and long-distance runner from Poole, Dorset, who represents Wales. She started out as a swimmer before switching to running, and joined Poole Athletic Club, where Mark Pauley coached her from the age of twelve. She later studied sports psychology at Brunel University London and moved to Loughborough in 2017 to train under Rob Denmark. Her breakthrough came at the 2018 Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast. Running for Wales, she took 1500m bronze in a personal best of 4:03.44, behind only Caster Semenya and Beatrice Chepkoech. A year earlier she had won gold in the first mixed relay at the European Cross Country Championships. The 3000m indoors has been her strongest event. She won European indoor bronze in 2019 and 2023, then silver in 2025, and is a two-time British indoor champion over the distance. Her indoor best of 8:28.69 came in New York in 2025. Outdoors she has run 4:01.81 for 1500m and 14:53.82 for 5000m. On Christmas Eve 2022 she ran 15:31 at Poole parkrun, an unofficial women's parkrun world record at the time. In 2026 a calf tear at the London 5000 in June ended her hopes of the European Championships. She recovered in six and a half weeks to captain Wales at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, then won the UK 5km road title in Cardiff in September in 15:40. - [Habtom Samuel: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/habtom-samuel): Runners / Habtom Samuel HS Film My Run Habtom Samuel Runs Habtom Samuel is an Eritrean distance runner, born on 30 November 2003. He made his name on the track and over the country before moving to the roads in 2026. He spent his college years at the University of New Mexico, which he joined in 2023. His first medals came at junior level. He took bronze over 3000 metres at the 2021 World Athletics U20 Championships, then another bronze over 5000 metres at the same championships a year later. In 2022 he also finished 17th in the senior 10,000 metres at the World Athletics Championships. A year later he placed 17th again, this time among the senior men at the global cross country championships of 2023. In America he collected five NCAA titles. The first came on his NCAA Outdoor debut in 2024, when he won the 10,000 metres in 28:07.82. He had gone down about 900 metres from the line. The NCAA Division I Cross Country title followed in 2025. That year he was also second in both the 5000 and 10,000 metres outdoors, and second over 5000 metres indoors. His final college season brought the full set. He won the indoor 5000 metres, then the 5000 and 10,000 metres at the 2026 NCAA Outdoor Championships. No man had managed that outdoor double since Ky Robinson in 2023. His track bests are 12:57.22 for 5000 metres, run in Los Angeles in 2026, and 26:51.06 for 10,000 metres, set in San Juan Capistrano in 2025. Indoors he holds Eritrean records of 7:40.63 for 3000 metres and 13:04.92 for 5000 metres, both set in Boston. On the road he has run 59:01 for the half marathon in Houston and 27:40 for 10K in Cape Elizabeth, Maine. He has not been beaten since turning professional. He won the Beach to Beacon 10K and the Falmouth Road Race, and set course records at Falmouth and the Houston Half Marathon. On 31 October he won his first New York Road Runners race, the Abbott Dash to the Finish Line, covering the 5K in 13:31. He led for much of it and broke clear around 10 minutes in. Edwin Kurgat was seven seconds back in 13:38 and Amon Kemboi third in 13:40. Samuel had been aiming for "13:10" and the course record. A headwind in midtown Manhattan put paid to that, so he raced for the win instead, finishing on the New York City Marathon finish line in Central Park. - [Rachael Rudel: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rachael-rudel): Runners / Rachael Rudel RR 🇺🇸 Film My Run 🇺🇸 Rachael Rudel Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra Rachael Rudel is an American distance runner. Most of her best results have come on the roads, at distances from 5km to 20km. She also has a trail win to her name, and she has no current UTMB Index. Her first notable result on trails came in 2019 at the Black Squirrel Trail Half Marathon. The course covers 21km with 591m of climb. Rudel was first woman home in 1:42:36. Her most prominent win came in Manhattan on Saturday 31 October, in the Abbott Dash to the Finish Line 5K. It was her first New York Road Runners race. She made her move in the last 400 metres and won by six seconds in 15:35, a personal best. Americans took all three podium places. Josette Andrews was second in 15:41 and Ednah Kurgat third in 15:42. Rudel's win stopped Annie Rodenfels at three consecutive victories in the race. Afterwards Rudel said she had arrived with "no expectations". The race drew more than 11,500 runners over 3.1 miles and forms part of New York City Marathon weekend. The route started on the East Side near the United Nations and went along 42nd Street past Grand Central Terminal. It then turned up Sixth Avenue past Radio City Music Hall before an undulating stretch through Central Park. Runners crossed the same line the marathon field would use the following day. - [Gemma Steel: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/gemma-steel): Runners / Gemma Steel Photo: AdamKR / Wikimedia Commons Gemma Steel Runs Gemma Steel is a British long-distance runner who races on the roads and over the country. Born on 12 November 1985, she runs for Charnwood Athletic Club in Loughborough and is coached by Liz Nuttall. She has worn a Great Britain vest on the country, the road and the track. Her start was modest. In 2005 she took up low-key racing on the roads, wearing the colours of Hermitage Harriers, the Whitwick club. Between 2006 and 2009 she cut her 10k best from more than 40 minutes to 34:34 and her ten-mile time from 67:05 to 58:03. The breakthrough came in 2010. Third place at the UK Cross Challenge in Liverpool earned a first Great Britain call-up. She was 27th at that year's European Cross Country Championships and came home with a team silver. In 2011 she won the Hannut Lotto CrossCup and made her world debut at the World Cross Country Championships, finishing 54th. On the roads she won the Bristol Half Marathon, the Great Yorkshire Run and the Great Birmingham Run. At the European Cross Country Championships that year she ran near the front throughout. Portugal's Ana Dulce Félix passed her late on, but Steel held on for individual bronze. The British women took the team title, only their second at the event. In 2012 she won the English National Cross Country Championships at Parliament Hill Fields and the inter-counties title at Cofton Park. She was ninth in the 10,000 metres at the European Athletics Championships and seventh at the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships. A year later she won the Great Birmingham Run again, setting a course record of 70:19. The summer of 2014 in New England brought one of her best-known wins. She beat Shalane Flanagan at the TD Beach to Beacon 10km in 31:26.5, still her road 10K best. She followed it with 68:13 at the Great North Run. That season ended with gold at the 2014 European Cross Country Championships. Later wins included the 2017 Great South Run in 55:25 and the 10K at the 2018 Great Scottish Run in 34:00. She now races as a master, and is still winning. At Betley Court Farm on Saturday 26 September she became one of the first English Masters Cross Country champions. The titles were decided within a North Staffs League fixture. Steel won the 4.8km women's race in 17:58. Katie Latham, who had beaten her at Leeds a year earlier while racing as a W35, was 19 seconds behind in 18:17 for W40 silver. The race also served as selection for the England against Ireland Masters International in Dublin in November. Steel won the W40 race at that fixture last year, and a top-three finish in her age group guaranteed her a place on the team again. - [Rodrigue Kwizera: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rodrigue-kwizera): Runners / Rodrigue Kwizera RK Film My Run Rodrigue Kwizera Runs Rodrigue Kwizera is a Burundian-born long-distance runner who now holds Spanish nationality. Born on 10 October 1999, he made his name in cross country and on the track before moving to the half marathon, where he has become one of the quickest men in the world. He moved to Spain in 2019 and races for the Playas de Castellón club. His first senior World Cross Country Championships came in Kampala in 2017, where he was 39th. Two years later in Aarhus he finished 11th. He also ran in Rabat at the 2019 African Games, placing 16th in the 5000 metres, and was 16th in the 10,000 metres at the 2019 World Championships in Doha. He won the World Cross Country Tour in 2021-22, taking five races that winter, among them Soria, San Sebastián, Itálica and the Almond Blossom Cross Country. Four more tour wins followed in 2022-23, including Campaccio. On the track he was 16th again over 10,000 metres at the 2022 World Championships in Eugene. His best marks all date from 2022: 13:20.17 for 5000 metres in Castellón, 27:25.47 for 10,000 metres in Maia and a national record of 26:56 for 10km on the road in Herzogenaurach. The half marathon has brought his biggest results. He won in Prague in April 2025 in 58:54, a Burundian record, then ran 58:39 for second in Valencia that October behind Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha. He went back to Prague in March 2026 and defended his title in 58:16, a course record that took down the previous best set by Sabastian Sawe in 2024. On 25 October 2026 he won the Valencia Half Marathon in 58:03, a Spanish record that cut 1 minute 36 seconds from the 59:39 Carlos Mayo ran on the same course in 2023. He had built up for the race at altitude in Addis Ababa alongside his clubmate Thierry Ndikumwenayo. The pair were among five men still at the front at 15km. Kwizera pushed on with two kilometres to go and got clear in the final 500 metres to finish alone on Avenida de Tarongers. Ndikumwenayo was second in 58:09. Kwizera said afterwards that he had led every kilometre and paid for it near the end. He stopped representing Burundi in 2023 so that he could serve the three years required before switching countries. He applied for Spanish nationality in 2025 and Spain's Council of Ministers granted it in May 2026. He can now race as a Spaniard in national events, but World Athletics has yet to approve his change of international allegiance. That is why his Valencia run, three seconds faster than the 58:06 Andreas Almgren of Sweden ran in Copenhagen this year, will not be ratified as a European record. Kwizera expects to have another go at that mark. - [Marcel Hug: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/marcel-hug): Runners / Marcel Hug Photo: Margot Murphy (Massachusetts Governor’s Press Office) / Wikimedia Commons Marcel Hug Runs Marcel Hug is a Swiss wheelchair racer who competes in the T54 class on the track and on the roads. He was born on 16 January 1986 in Pfyn. At ten a sports teacher bought him an old racing chair, and he won the first race he entered, a 3km youth event held alongside the Schenkon Marathon. He went on to join the Swiss Paraplegic Centre in Nottwil, where he worked with the coach Paul Odermatt. He races in a silver helmet, and that earned him the nickname "The Silver Bullet" at the 2011 world championships in Christchurch. Switzerland selected him for the 2004 Paralympics in Athens before he was part of the national team. He came home with two bronze medals, in the 800m in 1:32.66 and the 1500m in 3:05.48. His first world title followed in Assen in 2006, where he won the 10,000m in 23:06.71. Beijing in 2008 was a letdown. He missed the podium in every event and crashed in both the 1500m and the marathon. Between 24 and 27 June 2010, at a meeting in Switzerland, he set T54 world records at 800m (1:31.12), 1500m (2:54.51), 5000m (9:53.05) and 10,000m (19:50.04). For several years his track results were tied up with Britain's David Weir. Weir beat him to gold in the 800m, 1500m and 5000m in Christchurch in 2011, though Hug still won the 10,000m. At the London Paralympics in 2012 Hug took silver behind Weir in the 800m. The marathon there was decided by a single second across the medals, with Weir first, Hug second and Kurt Fearnley third. Weir stayed away from the 2013 world championships in Lyon, and Hug won five golds. Only Kim Gyu-Dae beat him, in the 800m. His first Paralympic titles came in Rio in 2016, in the 800m and the marathon, along with silver in the 1500m and 5000m. On the roads his record is longer still. His first big city win came in Berlin in 2011, and he has since won there 11 times. His Wikipedia record also lists nine Boston wins, eight in London, four in Tokyo and one in Sydney, in 2025. He had been second in London in 2010, 2012 and 2013 before beating Weir there in April 2014, a week after he had won in Paris. His first Boston title in 2015 came by more than six minutes over Ernst Van Dyk. In London in 2022 he finished in 1:24:38, two seconds clear of the American Daniel Romanchuk. He holds the course records in Boston, Chicago, New York and London. Hug has shown no sign of easing off in 2026. On 11 October he was first home in Chicago for the seventh time. His 1:21:34 set a new mark for the course, 63 seconds quicker than the 1:22:37 he recorded there in 2023. Three weeks later, on 1 November, he won his eighth New York City Marathon in 1:28:14. Romanchuk was one second behind and Weir third. It was the race's 50th anniversary edition, on a course that runs through all five boroughs from Staten Island to Manhattan. Earlier in the year he had also won in Tokyo, Boston, London and Berlin. - [Ted Higgins: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ted-higgins): Runners / Ted Higgins TH Film My Run Ted Higgins Runs Ted Higgins is a British middle-distance and cross-country runner, born on 20 September 2001. He races for Tonbridge Athletics Club, as does his twin brother Jack, who also runs middle distance. His range runs from 800 metres on the track to the mud of the English National and the road relays. His results picked up in December 2025. He won the South of England indoor 3000 metres title in 7:57.31. On 31 December he ran his first official 5km on the roads, in Battersea, and finished second in 13:38 behind Joe Wigfield. He started 2026 with an indoor 1500 metres personal best of 3:39.52 in Sheffield. The margin over his brother Jack was three hundredths of a second. In February he ran 3:57.05 for the indoor mile at Lee Valley. Later that month he lowered his 3000 metres best to 7:53.21 and took third at the British Indoor Championships in Birmingham, behind Tom Keen and Henry McLuckie. Soon after came a place in the first five at Sedgefield, where the English National cross-country was held. The spring and summer were busy. In April he ran the third fastest time of the day at the national road relays, where Tonbridge finished second. In May he was third over 1500 metres at the Belfast Classic in 3:39.73 and won the 800 metres for Tonbridge at the National Athletics League opener in Derby. Selected for England at the Loughborough International, he took second in the Gandy Mile, with Freddie Rowe the winner. A month later he was the 1500 metres winner at Prague's Josef Odložil Memorial and placed fourth in the British Championships final. In July he was runner-up to Reuben Reina in the mile at Cork City Sports. He has since been part of a strong run of relay wins for Tonbridge. At the South of England road relays at Aldershot's Rushmoor Arena on 26 September, he ran the anchor leg in 17:54 over the undulating 6km course. That held the lead James Kingston had built, and the club won the six-stage title in 1:48:16 after five runner-up finishes since 2016. On 31 October the national cross-country relays were held in Mansfield's Berry Hill Park. Higgins produced the fastest lap of the day there, 14:32, on the third stage. Tonbridge kept their senior men's title in 59:07. - [Megan Keith: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/megan-keith): Runners / Megan Keith Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons Megan Keith Runs Megan Keith is a Scottish distance runner who races on the track, on the roads and over the country. Born in Inverness on 23 April 2002, she runs for Inverness Harriers and studied Sport Science at Edinburgh University. She came to running from orienteering. In 2018, at her first international event, she won the sprint at the European Youth Orienteering Championships in Bulgaria by 34 seconds, the first gold for a British woman at those championships. A year later she helped a British relay team to Britain's first gold at the Junior World Orienteering Championships in Denmark. Running became her focus at around 16 or 17. The junior titles soon followed. She won the European U20 cross country race in Dublin in December 2021 and was runner-up in the U23 race in Turin a year later. In July 2023 she took the European U23 5000m title in Espoo, finishing ahead of Spain's Maria Forero and her British teammate Eloise Walker. That same month she ran 14:56.98 at the London Diamond League, and in August she was in the British team for the World Championships in Budapest. In December 2023 she won the U23 race at the European Cross Country Championships in Brussels and added a team gold. She opened 2024 with 31:22 at the Valencia 10K, a European U23 record. Her first 10,000m on the track came in March in San Juan Capistrano, California. She ran 30:36.84, which put her fourth on the UK all-time list. A British U23 5000m record of 14:43.24 followed in Shanghai in April. Victory in London on 18 May, at the meeting known as the Night of the 10,000m PBs, sealed her Olympic place. She then took bronze at the European Championships in Rome in 31:04.07, in only her third track 10,000m. The Paris Olympics went badly. She finished last in the 10,000m final in 33:19 after hurting her ankle. In 2025 she kept her British 10,000m title in Birmingham in 31:19.88, clocked 4:26.85 over the Monument Mile in Stirling for the fastest time by a Scottish-born woman, and placed tenth over 10,000m at the World Championships in Tokyo. She got up from an early fall at the European Cross Country Championships in Portugal that December to take silver behind Nadia Battocletti, and led Britain to team silver. The 2026 season has been her busiest yet. She was the first British finisher at the World Cross Country Championships in Tallahassee, in 25th. On 22 February in Castellón she ran 30:07 for 10km, a European record by one second over the mark held by Eilish McColgan. She was third at the New York City Half Marathon in 67:13 and lowered her 3000m best to 8:28.35 at the Bislett Games. At the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow she was ninth in the 10,000m. Then she went to the front with four laps left in the 5000m final on 30 July and held on for bronze in front of a home crowd. At the European Championships in Birmingham she led in the 10,000m but faded to eighth. She said afterwards she was still "proud of myself" for trying. In Copenhagen on 19 September she was 15th in the 5km at the World Road Running Championships in 15:19. On 27 September she was back in Inverness for the Baxters River Ness 10K, which finishes at Bught Park and drew around 3,000 runners. Her winning time of 31:24 was 96 seconds inside the 33:00 that Mhairi Maclennan ran in 2022, the previous best for the course. She had also won the race in 2019 and 2021, so this made three. She was almost five minutes clear, and Inverness Harriers filled the podium, with Charlotte-Rose Burton second in 36:17 and Helen Leigh third in 36:30. Keith had only decided a couple of days earlier to "jump in" while in town to support the event. These are her training roads when she comes home, and she conceded they have not got any easier. The crowd shouting her name near the finish made "a world of difference", she said. Winter training is next, with any road races yet to be settled. - [Katie Snowden: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/katie-snowden): Runners / Katie Snowden Photo: Erik van Leeuwen, attribution: Erik van Leeuwen (bron: Wikipedia). / Wikimedia Commons Katie Snowden Runs Katie Snowden is an English middle-distance runner who has represented both England and Great Britain. Born on 9 March 1994, she has made the 1500 metres her main event, although her first international success came over two laps. That came in 2011, when she won the girls' 800m at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Douglas on the Isle of Man. Four years later she was sixth over 800m at the European Under-23 Championships in Tallinn. By 2018 she had moved up to the 1500m, which she ran for England at the Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast in Australia. Her senior record has grown steadily since. She was sixth in the 1500m at the 2021 European Indoor Championships in Toruń, Poland. At the delayed Tokyo Olympics later that year she ran a personal best of 4:02.77 in the third heat and went through to the semi-finals. In 2022 she finished fourth at the European Championships, just outside the medals. A year later she won the 1500m at the British Athletics Championships to become national champion. She has also turned out for her club on grass. England's national cross-country relay meeting went to Mansfield on 31 October, and she ran the final leg for Herne Hill in the women's 3x3km. The team won in 28:43 and ended Belgrave Harriers' run of three straight titles. Snowden's lap was the third fastest of the race. She had come back from the World Road Running Championships only two weeks earlier, and she described the Nottinghamshire course as "brilliant underfoot". - [Thierry Ndikumwenayo: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/thierry-ndikumwenayo): Runners / Thierry Ndikumwenayo TN Film My Run Thierry Ndikumwenayo Runs Thierry Ndikumwenayo is a distance runner born in Burundi on 26 March 1997 who now represents Spain. He made his name in cross country but has raced with distinction on the track and, lately, the road. He took up athletics in 2012 after a friend challenged him to a race. Two years later, aged 17, he won silver in the boys' 3,000m at the 2014 Summer Youth Olympics in Nanjing. That run brought an invitation to train in Spain through a scheme for Burundian and Sudanese athletes. He joined the Playas de Castellón club, which paid for his accommodation. He kept racing for Burundi in those early years. He was seventh over 5,000m at the 2015 African Junior Championships and ninth at the 2015 All-Africa Games. In 2016 he was seventh over 5,000m at the African Championships. His first World Cross Country Championships, in Kampala in 2017, ended in 95th place. In Aarhus two years later he finished ninth, 86 places higher. That earned him a 10,000m start at the 2019 World Championships in Doha, which he did not finish. Later that year he won the Cross Internacional de la Constitución in Alcobendas. The pandemic kept him inside the Iberian Peninsula through 2020 and 2021, when he won the Almond Blossom Cross Country. His breakthrough came in 2022. He opened with a 10km best of 28:04 in Castellón. In May he cut almost 19 seconds from his 5,000m best with 13:06.58 at the Desafío Nerja, then ran 13:06.46 for third in Huelva three weeks later. His first Diamond League race, the Golden Gala in Rome, brought 12:59.39 for eighth. He was second over 5,000m in Paris in 13:05.24 and fifth over 3,000m at the Bauhaus-Galan in a personal best of 7:34.91. Injury then ruled him out of the World Championships in Oregon. He returned to win the 3,000m at the Herculis meeting in 7:25.94, a Burundian record, a world lead and a Diamond League record. That winter he won the Soria, Atapuerca and Italica cross country races in succession, at about the time he became a Spanish citizen. On Sunday 25 October 2026 he finished second at the Valencia Half Marathon in 58:09. He had arrived with a best of 59:42, so the run took 1 minute 33 seconds off it. According to the organisers it is the second-fastest half marathon by a European. He was one of five men left at the front at 15km, reached in 41:31. His Playas de Castellón clubmate Rodrigue Kwizera broke clear in the final 500 metres to win in 58:03. Kenya's Victor Kipruto was third in 58:12. The pair had prepared together at altitude in Addis Ababa, and the organisers described them as "almost brothers". - [Christof Hochenwarter: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/christof-hochenwarter): Runners / Christof Hochenwarter CH 🇦🇹 UTMB Index 825 Film My Run 🇦🇹 Christof Hochenwarter Country 🇦🇹 Austria Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 825 (9 November 2026) Christof Hochenwarter is an Austrian mountain runner who does his best work on short, steep ground. Vertical kilometres, hill climbs and fast up-and-down courses make up most of his record. He holds a general UTMB Index of 825. His biggest win came in Dorfgastein on Saturday 17 October 2026. He took the Beinhoat das Vertical in 39:33. It was the last round of the 2026 VK OPEN World Cup and the first final staged in Austria. Paul Verbnjak followed in 40:20, with Nils Oberauer next across the line in 40:59, so the men's podium was all Austrian. The direct line climbs 1,200m in 3.3km. It tracks the cable car to the top station on the Fulseck, which sits above 2,000m. France's Louis Dumas, who won the season title, finished fourth in 41:34. Before that, the Grossglockner had been a regular test. He was seventh at the Grossglockner Berglauf in 2022 in 1:14:33, over 13km with 1,365m of climb. Two years later he placed 13th at the Grossglockner Mountain Run in 1:17:30. In 2021 he was third at the Nassfeld-Mountain-Skytrails Skyrace, 25km with 2,140m of ascent, in 3:36:16. He also ran the elite up-and-down race at the 2024 European Off-Road Championships, finishing 61st over 16km in 1:34:13. In 2025 he was tenth in the vertical at the Innsbruck Alpine Trailrun Festival, 7km and 1,350m of climb, in 59:16. The Obertauern Trailrun Summit has been a happy hunting ground. In 2024 he won the 9km short trail in 57:25 and the 2km sprint in 7:39. In 2025 he was second in the Seekarspitz Vertical in 25:15 and third over the 26km half marathon trail in 2:39:40. He went back in 2026 and won the Seekarspitz Vertical, 5km with 467m of climb, in 24:18. He has also tested himself against a deeper field on the Golden Trail World Series. At the Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail, 24km with 1,700m of climb, he was 39th in 2025. He improved to 33rd in 2026 in 2:46:28. He also raced at the Trail World Championships in 2017, finishing 128th over a 49 km course with almost 3,000 m of climbing. - [Sabastian Sawe: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sabastian-sawe): Runners / Sabastian Sawe Photo: Leonhard Lenz / Wikimedia Commons Sabastian Sawe Runs Sabastian Sawe is a Kenyan long-distance runner, born on 16 March 1995, who holds the world record for the marathon. He went to St Patrick's High School in Iten and began as a middle-distance runner. His first 5,000m came in 2019 more or less by accident. He arrived late to an athletics meeting, found it was the only race still open, and won it in 13:56. He went on to train with Abel Mutai, an assistant coach at the 2Running Club in Nandi County, which Claudio Berardelli founded. The half marathon made his name. In Seville in January 2022 he started as a pacemaker, carried on and won in 59:02, well inside the old course record of 1:00:44. Two months later he ran 58:02 at the Rome-Ostia Half Marathon, though that course does not count for records. A win in Bahrain followed in 58:58. In September 2022, at the Memorial Van Damme in Brussels, he ran 21,250 metres in sixty minutes. That set a Kenyan record and fell narrowly short of the world mark. He finished seventh of the senior men at the world cross country championships in 2023. That year he also ran 26:49 for 10K in Herzogenaurach and won the Montferland Run in 's-Heerenberg over 15km in 42:35. His best legal half marathon, 58:05, came with victory in Copenhagen in September 2024. He stepped up to the marathon in Valencia on 1 December 2024 and won in 2:02:05. It was the fastest marathon of 2024. Only Kelvin Kiptum had run a quicker debut, and by just 12 seconds. Sawe won London on 27 April 2025 in 2:02:27. In Berlin that September he improved to 2:02:16, finishing the job alone after the last of seven pacemakers stepped off at 23km. London on 26 April 2026 is the race he will be remembered for. Sawe won in 1:59:30, the first time anyone had gone under two hours in a record-eligible marathon. He took 65 seconds off Kiptum's official record. He was also ten seconds quicker than Eliud Kipchoge's run in 2019, which was never ratified because it was not run under race conditions. Yomif Kejelcha of Ethiopia, in his first marathon, was second in 1:59:41. Sawe had averaged 200km a week for the six weeks before, wore the Adidas Pro Evo 3 and collected £740,000 in prize money. Paula Radcliffe described two hours as an "iconic barrier". Canadian Running pointed out that his last defeat of any kind had come in 2024, when he took second place in a 10K at adizero Road to Records, held in Germany. He withdrew from the defence of his Berlin title in August, and Guye Adola won the race on 27 September in 2:02:50. On 30 September Sawe lost a best-of-three game of rock, paper, scissors 2-0 to Catherine Debrunner, the wheelchair marathon world record holder. A Guinness World Records adjudicator watched the contest. Both wanted the traditional Sunday, so his loss means the elite men will race on Saturday 24 April 2027, at a London Marathon spread over two days for one year only. He is expected back on the Greenwich-to-Westminster course to defend his title. - [Amos Kipruto: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/amos-kipruto): Runners / Amos Kipruto Photo: Katie Chan / Wikimedia Commons Amos Kipruto Runs Amos Kipruto is a Kenyan marathon runner, born on 16 September 1992. He made his name on the European and Asian road circuit before becoming a regular contender at the World Marathon Majors. His shorter bests include 1:00:24 for the half marathon, set in Gothenburg in 2017, and 28:37 for 10km in Bolzano in 2019. His first big wins came in Rome in 2016 and Seoul the following year. In 2018 he reached the podium at two majors. He was third in Tokyo in 2:06:33 and second in Berlin in 2:06:23. A year later he took bronze in the marathon at the World Athletics Championships in Doha. He then ran for Kenya at the Tokyo Olympics, held a year late. The postponed 2021 Tokyo Marathon took place in March 2022. Kipruto finished second there in 2:03:13, beaten only by Eliud Kipchoge's 2:02:40. Seven months later he won the London Marathon in 2:04:39. That was his first major title. He returned to London in April 2026 and ran 2:01:39 for fourth place. The time took three minutes off his winning mark from 2022. It equalled the seventh fastest marathon on record and put him sixth on the all-time list for men. Chicago had been close for some time. He was third there in 2024 and second in 2025. On 11 October 2026 he finally won it, aged 34. The leaders passed halfway in 60:21 and reached 30km in 1:25:28, with only Kipruto and the Ugandan defending champion Jacob Kiplimo still on two-hour pace. Kipruto pulled clear near 20 miles and finished in 2:01:09, a personal best. Only Kelvin Kiptum's 2:00:35 from 2023 has been faster on the Chicago course. Ethiopia's Tadese Takele was second in 2:02:56, Milkesa Mengesha third in 2:03:46 and Kiplimo fourth in 2:04:18. Kipruto collapsed to the ground after the line. He described this year as "win or die". - [Zeineba Yimer: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/zeineba-yimer): Runners / Zeineba Yimer ZY Film My Run Zeineba Yimer Runs Zeineba Yimer is an Ethiopian long-distance runner, born on 17 June 1998. She has raced on the track, over the half marathon and over the full marathon, and has worn Ethiopian colours at continental, world and Olympic level. Her first notable win came in 2017 at the Great Ethiopian Run in Addis Ababa. A year later she was fifth at the IAAF World Half Marathon Championships in Valencia. That run also counted towards the team event, where she, Netsanet Gudeta and Meseret Belete took gold with a combined 3:22:27. In 2019 she went to the African Games in Rabat, Morocco, and came away with silver in the 10,000 metres. She returned to world half marathon competition in Gdynia, Poland, at the 2020 championships. She then ran the women's marathon at the Tokyo Olympics, the Games held a year late after being postponed from 2020. Her biggest marathon win so far came in Frankfurt on 25 October, when the city staged its marathon for the 43rd time and she lined up as favourite at 28. Rain and wind made fast times unlikely. She ran at the front from the start with fellow Ethiopian Siranesh Yirga, who could not hold on beyond 30km. Yimer had to dig in over the final kilometres before finishing at the Festhalle in 2:19:45. Only five women have run faster in the race's history. The German debutant Blanka Dörfel closed to finish second in 2:20:46, and Beriha Gebreslasie of Ethiopia was third in 2:22:46. Afterwards Yimer said the wet conditions had cost her time but that she was happy with her run. A sub-2:20 win in a German city marathon, on a course partly under water, makes her one to watch on the big-city circuit. - [Pier-Alexandre Beaulieu: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/pier-alexandre-beaulieu): Runners / Pier-Alexandre Beaulieu PB 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 625 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Pier-Alexandre Beaulieu Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 625 (9 November 2026) Pier-Alexandre Beaulieu is a Canadian trail and ultra runner. His racing has taken him from short, steep mountain courses to 100 km events and, most recently, to the backyard format. His general UTMB Index stands at 627. His one recorded win came in 2022 at the Ultra Trail Chic-chocs. He took the Mont Xalibu 26k, a 26 km course with 1,290 m of climb, in 2:26:33. In the same year he ran the Saint-Siméon 42 km at the Ultra-Trail Harricana du Canada. That route climbs 1,545 m, and he came home sixth man in 4:58:46. In 2025 he moved up to 100 km at The Canyons Endurance Runs by UTMB. The course carries 3,750 m of climb. Beaulieu finished in 11:55:05, which placed him 52nd man. In 2026 he was one of 15 runners on Canada's team at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championships. The Canadians raced on the B.C. Backyard Ultra course in Sicamous, British Columbia. A 6.706 km loop starts every hour, and anyone who fails to finish one inside the hour is out. Each completed yard adds a point to the national total. The championships began on a Saturday. When racing moved into a third day on the Monday, Beaulieu was still out on the loop. He was one of seven Canadians left, after Sandra Auger had stopped at 51 yards. Canada was sixth in the world at that stage. - [Amanal Petros: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/amanal-petros): Runners / Amanal Petros Photo: Ailura / Wikimedia Commons Amanal Petros Runs Amanal Petros is a German long-distance runner who holds the national records for both the half marathon and the marathon. He was born on 17 May 1995 in Assab, a port city on the Eritrean coast. He left Eritrea aged two, while the country was fighting Ethiopia over their shared border. He reached Germany alone as a refugee in January 2012. He became a German citizen in 2015. His early results came on the track. He took bronze over 5000m at the 2015 German Championships in Nuremberg. Two years later he won silver in the 10,000m at the European Under-23 Championships in Bydgoszcz, Poland, and finished fourth in the 5000m. In 2019 he ran at the European 10,000m Cup in London. Later that year he won silver medals over both 5000m and 10,000m at the Military World Games in Wuhan, China. He also won the half marathon at the Cologne Marathon that year. In 2020 he raced at the World Athletics Half Marathon Championships in Gdynia, Poland. The road has since become his main event. At the 2025 Berlin Half Marathon he ran 59:31, a German record. Later that year he took the national marathon record at Valencia with 2:04:03. In 2026 he became European champion over the marathon in Birmingham. He won gold in 2:09:11, a championship record. Two and a half months after Birmingham, on 25 October 2026, he lined up at the Frankfurt Marathon. He had hoped to lower his own national record alongside Samuel Fitwi, but rain and wind made fast times unlikely. With about 10km to go Petros and Kenya's Benard Biwott, the 2024 winner, pushed clear. Ethiopia's Jirata Dinki closed the gap on the pair near 37km. Petros pressed once more and Biwott could not follow. Dinki could, and Petros cracked with roughly 2km left. Dinki won in 2:05:26. Petros crossed the line second in 2:05:46. No German had ever run quicker on the Frankfurt course. He was also the first German man on the Frankfurt podium in more than 25 years. Afterwards he conceded that he had probably attacked too early. - [Finlay Wild: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/finlay-wild): Runners / Finlay Wild Photo: Paul Dobson / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Finlay Wild Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 906 (9 November 2026) Finlay Wild is a Scottish fell runner and mountaineer, born in Thurso in September 1984. He grew up in Fort William and works there as a general practitioner. His general UTMB index stands at 906. Wild is the most successful runner in the history of the Ben Nevis Race, having won it twelve times since his first victory in 2010. He has also won the British Fell Running Championships twice, in 2015 and 2022, and holds records at races including the Isle of Jura, the Glamaig Hill Race and Buckden Pike. He holds several of Scotland's classic round records. He completed the Ramsay Round in 14:42:40 in 2020 and the Paddy Buckley Round, solo and unsupported, in 15:14 in 2022. He has repeatedly lowered his own Tranter's Round time, reaching 8:27:53 in 2024. In 2019 he broke the long-standing Welsh 3000s record with a time of 4:10:48. He completed the Bob Graham Round in 12:59 in 2021, then again in January 2024 in 15:35, the fastest time recorded for a winter round. On the international skyrunning circuit, Wild won the Trofeo Kima in 2022 and again in 2024, setting a course record of 6:05:04. He finished third in the Extreme category of the 2016 Skyrunner World Series after results at the Tromsø SkyRace and the Glen Coe Skyline. - [Gary Cantrell: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/gary-cantrell): Runners / Gary Cantrell Photo: Michael Hodge / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Gary Cantrell Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Gary Cantrell, known to runners as Lazarus Lake, is the American race director behind some of the toughest events in ultrarunning. They include the Barkley Marathons, Big's Backyard Ultra and the Last Annual Vol State Road Race. He put on his first ultra in 1979, the Strolling Jim 40 in Tennessee. It is named after a champion Tennessee Walking Horse and still runs every year, one of the oldest ultras in the American South. He started the Barkley Marathons in 1986. The 100-mile race mixes navigation with off-trail scrambling, and he says its purpose is to find where human endurance runs out. In 2012 he invented the backyard ultra. Runners cover a 4.167-mile loop every hour, on the hour, until only one is left. From 2020 his Big Dog's Backyard also held a team championship between countries, with 37 nations taking part by 2022. A 2014 documentary about the Barkley made him known far beyond the sport. In 2018 he crossed the United States on foot, from Rhode Island to Oregon. He joined the American Ultrarunning Hall of Fame in 2023. - [Elhousine Elazzaoui: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/elhousine-elazzaoui): Runners / Elhousine Elazzaoui Photo: UTMB profile 🇲🇦 Elhousine Elazzaoui Country 🇲🇦 Morocco Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 964 (9 November 2026) Elhousine Elazzaoui is a Moroccan trail and skyrunner from Zagora, in the Saharan south of the country. He grew up in a nomadic family whose small tourism business ran camel treks. He started running at 12 while fetching the camels. He won his first race in 2006 and later qualified as an official guide with Morocco's tourism ministry. He prefers the mountains to the road, though his 10K road best stands at 29 minutes. He moved to Switzerland in 2018 to develop his talent and gain experience on the international circuit. He has said he found good people there who love the sport and helped him grow. He turned professional the same year, winning the Morocco Race over 80 kilometres. He won the Swiss Golden Trail national series in 2019 and Swissalpine Davos K43 in 2021. In 2024 he set a new course record at the Marathon du Mont Blanc, finishing in 3:30:10. He added back-to-back wins that year at the Headlands and Mammoth Trail Fest races. That year he also won the overall Golden Trail World Series, the first African man to take the title. He called it a proud moment for African running. He has stayed near the top since. He won the Zegama-Aizkorri Marathon in both 2025 and 2026, and took the Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K in 2025. - [Julie-Anne Staehli: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/julie-anne-staehli): Runners / Julie-Anne Staehli Photo: JStaehli / Wikimedia Commons Julie-Anne Staehli Runs Julie-Anne Staehli is a Canadian distance runner who specialises in the 5,000 metres. She was born on 21 December 1993 and runs professionally for Team New Balance Boston. She grew up on a farm outside Lucknow, a small town in Ontario, and started running on the backroads near home. As a teenager she also did skiing, snowboarding, triathlon and football. Running took over in her final year of high school. That year her school's cross country squad won the OFSAA title with Staehli at its head. She also took gold in the 1,500m steeplechase. In 2012 she moved to Kingston to study at Queen's University. Over five years as a varsity athlete she collected 12 podium finishes. She became the first athlete in the school's history to earn All-Canadian honours five times. Her first national team came in 2014, at the FISU World University Cross Country Championships. That same year she took bronze in the 3000m steeplechase at the NACAC U23 Championships in Kamloops. Staehli has since made five senior Canadian teams. She won the 2021 Olympic Trials and ran the 5,000m at the Tokyo Games. In the autumn of 2021 she moved to Boston to train full time. She went on to compete at the 2022 World Indoor Championships and the Commonwealth Games. She also holds the Canadian indoor record for 2 miles. She has been ranked second on the Canadian indoor 3,000m list and fourth on the national all-time 5,000m list. Her international vests also include the World Cross Country Championships and the Pan American Cross Country Cup. On the roads she has made the national 5K title her own. She first won it in 2022. Her fourth straight win came in Montreal, where she finished in 15:49. The championship was held as part of the Marathon Beneva de Montréal weekend, which drew around 35,000 participants. Her margin was slim. Makenna Fitzgerald, from Cochrane, Alberta, was two seconds back in 15:51. Siona Chisholm was third in 15:59. Away from racing she holds three degrees from Queen's and Western universities, including a master's in sport psychology. She has coached cross country as an assistant with the Queen's Gaels in 2017 and with the Western Mustangs in 2018-19. Her research on how university coaches plan their programmes was published in the International Sport Coaching Journal. In 2016 she co-founded The ReRUN Shoe Project with Kurtis Marlow. It collects lightly used running shoes at drop-off points and passes them on to Canadians who need a decent pair. - [Gordy Ainsleigh: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/gordy-ainsleigh): Runners / Gordy Ainsleigh Photo: FartherFaster / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Gordy Ainsleigh Born 1947 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Gordy Ainsleigh is the American runner whose solo run through the Sierra Nevada in 1974 led to the Western States 100. Born in 1947, he later qualified as a chiropractor, in 1983. He first rode the Western States Trail Ride, the 100-mile Tevis Cup, in 1971 at 23. He was big for a rider, so he ran long stretches ahead of or behind his horse to spare it. In 1973 his horse went lame at Robinson Flat, 30 miles in. He had no horse for 1974. Drucilla Barner, who had been the first woman to take the Tevis Cup, urged him to try the trail on foot instead. He trained by running from Michigan Bluff to Auburn four times in six weeks. He started ahead of the horses and struggled in 107-degree heat at Devil's Thumb, close to quitting. He reached Auburn in 23 hours 42 minutes, finishing with a somersault. Seven soldiers had walked the trail in 1972, but he was the first to cover it on foot inside a day. When the run became an official race in 1977, he was its race director. He kept racing it too, with 22 finishes by 2007 and a best of 20:55 in 1984. In 1973 he had also run 2:52:07 for the marathon, briefly a record for runners over 200 pounds.
