- [Joe McConaughy: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joe-mcconaughy): Runners / Joe McConaughy Photo: Caroline Himbert / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Joe McConaughy Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 905 (9 November 2026) Joe McConaughy, known as "Stringbean", is an American ultrarunner and long-distance hiker based in Seattle. In September 2026 he ran California's John Muir Trail northbound quicker than any supported man before him, taking 2 days and 16 hours. It was his third crack at the record, having come up short in 2022 and 2024. He beat the previous mark, set by François D'Haene in 2017, by 3 hours and 26 minutes. He started at 1.47pm on Sunday 20 September and matched D'Haene's old schedule for the first 100 miles. By mile 135 he had edged two miles clear, and by nightfall on the Tuesday he led by more than nine miles. He finished before 6am on the Wednesday, about 13 miles up on record pace, climbing more than 14,000 metres over a route that crosses Mount Whitney. His crew supplied food and water along the way, which made the run a supported one. McConaughy earned his trail name for his tall, lanky build during his thru-hiking days. Away from that run he holds speed records on the Appalachian Trail, Vermont's Long Trail, the Arizona Trail and the Pacific Crest Trail, and he still owns the men's unsupported north-south John Muir Trail mark from 2022. On the race circuit he won the Cocodona 250 in Arizona in 2022, then returned to finish fourth in 2024 and fourth again in 2026. In 2025 he was third at the Black Canyon 100k and 14th at the Western States 100. - [Cristian Minoggio: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/cristian-minoggio): Runners / Cristian Minoggio Photo: photographer unknown 🇮🇹 Cristian Minoggio Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 953 (9 November 2026) Cristian Minoggio is an Italian skyrunner who works as a dam keeper. Runners call him Braccio di Ferro, Italian for Popeye. He is a two-time Ultra SkyMarathon world champion and a three-time European champion in the discipline. He did not reach the top tier of the UTMB World Series until his forties. In 2025 he was runner-up at OCC. The following year, at 42, he won the CCC at UTMB Mont-Blanc, his first victory in the race. Minoggio moved into second place before the Champex-Lac checkpoint at 54km, level with race leader Hans Troyer and fellow frontrunner Eli Hemming. On the climb toward Trient, at around 80km, he pulled clear of Troyer and took the lead for good. By Vallorcine, the last crew access point at 90km, Minoggio led by more than seven minutes. He held that lead all the way to Chamonix, finishing in 10 hours 21 minutes and 48 seconds, 5 minutes and 37 seconds clear of Portugal's Miguel Arsenio. His results stretch back to 2013 and include repeated wins at races such as the Trofeo Kima, the Pierra Menta and the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg trail. In 2024 he also won the ultra race at the ISF Skyrunning World Championships, and he finished fourth in the long trail at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. - [Aleksandr Sorokin: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/aleksandr-sorokin): Runners / Aleksandr Sorokin Photo: Augustas Didžgalvis / Wikimedia Commons 🇱🇹 Aleksandr Sorokin Born 1981 Country 🇱🇹 Lithuania Runs Road, Track (legend) Aleksandr Sorokin is a Lithuanian ultrarunner, born in 1981, who has rewritten the world records for running fast over very long distances. By May 2023 he held seven of them across road and track, from 100 km to 24 hours. He came to running late. He paddled kayaks and canoes for Lithuanian teams until a shoulder injury in his mid-twenties. He took up running in 2013, aged 31, and raced his first 100 km that same year. Two years later he set Lithuanian records for 100 km and 24 hours at world championships. His first big title was the Spartathlon in Greece in 2017. Two years later he became 24-hour world champion in Albi, France, with a championship record of 278.972 km. The records followed quickly. In April 2021 he took the 100-mile and 12-hour marks on the track at the Centurion event in England. That August in Pabianice, Poland, he ran 309.4 km in 24 hours, ending a record Yiannis Kouros had held since 1997. In January 2022 in Tel Aviv he became the first runner to go 100 miles in under 11 hours, clocking 10:51:39. Later in 2022 he set a 100 km world record of 6:05:41 and won the European 24-hour title in Verona with 319.614 km. In September 2026 he was second at the IAU 100k World Championships in Spain in 6:12:41, and took the World Masters Athletics 100k title in the same race. - [Jerome Vanderschaeghe: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jerome-vanderschaeghe): Runners / Jerome Vanderschaeghe Photo: UTMB profile 🇧🇪 Jerome Vanderschaeghe Country 🇧🇪 Belgium Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 870 (9 November 2026) Jerome Vanderschaeghe is a Belgian trail and ultra runner. His UTMB record holds 52 results going back to 2015. They range from a 17 km sprint up to 175 km mountain ultras. His general UTMB Index stands at 857. The early years were modest. In 2015 he was 330th in La 6000D, 64 km in 9:26:24, though he also took 2nd in Les Doux Dingues 60 km in 5:45:15. He was 18th in the OCC at UTMB in 2017 in 5:48:01. A year later he came to Scotland for the Ben Nevis Ultra at Salomon Skyline Scotland, finishing 22nd over 47 km and 1,640 m of climb in 4:28:48. In 2019 he was 44th at the Trail World Championships at Abutres and 147th in the CCC in 16:10:31. The wins started in 2020, at the Trail des Cabanes and the Trail Vallée de Joux 51K, where he ran 4:43:14. In 2021 he added three more, including the Trail du Petit Saint-Bernard 60 km in 6:50:01. His longest races have brought his best results. At the Diagonale des Fous on Réunion he was 6th in 2022, covering 168 km and 10,250 m of climb in 25:33:33. He went back in 2025 and finished 5th over 175 km in 25:35:50. He won the Échappée Belle Traversée Nord in 2022, 84 km with 6,150 m of climb, in 12:36:30. In 2023 he won the Montreux MXALPS in 8:32:27 and took 2nd at the Ultra-Trail di Corsica, 109 km in 16:40:42. In 2024 he was 3rd at Ultra-trail Cape Town over 163 km in 22:33:19 and won the 74 km Grand Raid 73 in 8:21:55. He keeps returning to familiar races. He has won the Trail du Besso twice, most recently the 59K in 2025, when he ran 9:46:40 over 5,800 m of climb. He has run Sierre-Zinal four times, with a best of 52nd in 2:55:08 in 2021. His 2026 season has produced his biggest win to date. He took the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg, 120 km with 8,200 m of climb, in 15:33:44. At the Wildstrubel 70 he was 13th over 72 km from Kandersteg in 7:49:52. That was 17 minutes 8 seconds quicker than the time that earned him 2nd there in 2025. - [Aya Tomioka: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/aya-tomioka): Runners / Aya Tomioka AT 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 399 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Aya Tomioka Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 399 (9 November 2026) Aya Tomioka is a trail runner from Toronto, Canada. The results on record come from shorter races, on courses built around rolling woodland and steady climbing rather than mountain summits. Tomioka holds a general UTMB Index of 399. The best known result came at the first Hustle at Pinehurst, held at the Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area near Cambridge, Ontario. The event revives the old Run for the Toad under a new name, and nearly 400 runners took part across distances from 12.5K to 50K. Tomioka won the non-binary division of the 12.5K in 1:18:07. Because it was the event's first running, that time also stands as the course record. One lap of the course carries more than 250 metres of climb over ground that feels closer to cross-country than to groomed trail. In 2026 Tomioka also won a category at the Sulphur Springs Trail Race 20k, finishing in 2:22:51. That course covers 20 km with 490 m of climb. Sulphur Springs is put on by Straw Dog Racing, the same organisers behind the Pinehurst revival, so Tomioka has now won at two of their races. The organisers have said they already have ideas for the 2027 edition at Pinehurst, which gives Tomioka a course record to defend. - [Pam Reed: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/pam-reed): Runners / Pam Reed Photo: HarrisRose / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Pam Reed Born 1961 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road, Track (legend) Pam Reed is an American ultrarunner, born in Michigan in 1961, who is best known for winning Badwater outright. In 2002 she became the first woman to take the overall title in the 135-mile race through Death Valley, and she won it again in 2003. She started running long distances in 1989 while training for Ironman triathlons. Her first 100-miler was the Wasatch Front 100 in 1992, and she has finished at least one every year since. In 1998 she completed the Grand Slam of Ultrarunning. Badwater became her race. She finished it 11 times and was on the podium every time. That first win took 27:56:47, a women's best for the course back then. She was just as strong on flat ground. In 2003 she ran 138.96 miles in 24 hours in San Diego, an American women's record that lasted 25 years. In 2005 she covered 301 miles in 79 hours without sleeping, on a frontage road beside Interstate 10 near Tucson. In 2015 she finished Western States, Hardrock and Badwater within 33 days. Her 100th 100-mile finish came in February 2021, three weeks short of her 60th birthday. She entered the American Ultrarunning Hall of Fame in 2022. - [Blandine L'Hirondel: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/blandine-l-hirondel): Runners / Blandine L'Hirondel Photo: Anna & Mathieu - Trail de La Chaussée des Géants / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇷 Blandine L'Hirondel Born 1991 (age 34 or 35) Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 814 (9 November 2026) Blandine L'Hirondel is a French trail and ultramarathon runner. She was born on 3 March 1991 in Caen. She works as an obstetrician-gynaecologist alongside her running career. In August 2026 she won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc in 21:54:49. She was the first French woman to take the title since Caroline Chaverot in 2016. The win completed a set of victories at UTMB Mont-Blanc's three feature races. She had already won the OCC in 2021 and the CCC in 2022. Only Ruth Croft had won all three races before her. L'Hirondel grew up in Normandy. She took up mountain running while studying medicine on Réunion, then continued in the Pyrenees after returning to mainland France. Her breakthrough came in 2019, when she won the Trail World Championships in Portugal in 4:06:17 and helped France to the team title. In 2022 she won the European Off-Road Running Championships trail race, and went on to win the CCC and a world long-trail title that same year. The French athletics federation voted her female athlete of the year for 2022. In 2023 she finished third at UTMB on her first attempt at the 100-mile distance. She then won La Réunion's Diagonale des Fous in 2025, crossing the line in roughly 27 hours and 26 minutes. Her 2026 season began with a course record at Transvulcania on La Palma, where she ran 7:43:47 in May. She then won the UTMB itself in August, finishing ahead of Americans Rachel Entrekin and Emily Schmitz. - [Zach Miller: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/zach-miller): Runners / Zach Miller Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Zach Miller Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 903 (9 November 2026) Zach Miller is an American ultrarunner with a UTMB Index of 904. His results run from 2013 to 2026, making him one of the sport's most consistent competitors over more than a decade. He has finished UTMB itself five times, taking 2nd man in 2023 in 19:58:58 and finishing inside the top 10 in 2016, 2017 and 2022. He won the Tarawera Ultramarathon by UTMB's 165 km Miler race in 2023 in 14:41:41 and the Trail 100 Andorra by UTMB's Ultra 105K in 2022. More recently he was 5th man at both Hardrock 100 in 2025 and the 2026 Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run, and 2nd at The Canyons Endurance Runs by UTMB 100K in 2026. Earlier in his career he won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc's CCC race in 2015 and the Madeira Island Ultra Trail in 2016, and won the JFK 50 Mile in 2013 before finishing 2nd there in 2018. He was also a repeat winner of The North Face Endurance Challenge California 50 Mile, taking the title in both 2015 and 2016. - [Caitlin Schindel: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/caitlin-schindel): Runners / Caitlin Schindel Photo: University of Saskatchewan 🇨🇦 Caitlin Schindel Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 685 (9 November 2026) Caitlin Schindel is a Canadian trail and ultra runner. Her results run from 50km mountain races to 100km in the desert, with a road marathon added this autumn. She holds a general UTMB Index of 741. Her best results came in 2023. She won the Nakawé 50K at Puerto Vallarta México by UTMB, covering 49km and 2,300m of climb in 5:40:11 to finish first woman. Closer to home she was third woman at the Nesters Market Squamish 50 50km, a 51km course with 2,450m of ascent, in 5:38:43. She has since tested herself in deeper fields. At the 2024 HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc OCC, 57km with 3,500m of climb, she was 23rd woman in 6:54:06. In 2025 she ran 9:58:23 for 18th woman at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K, a 101km race with only 1,600m of climb. Later that year she represented the step up to world level. She finished the Long Trail at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, 81km with 5,413m of ascent, in 13:43:20 for 74th woman. Her 2026 season started on the trails of Québec. She was 11th woman in the QMT 80 at the Québec Mega Trail, running the 77km and 3,370m of climb in 10:47:00. She then turned to the road. At the 52nd Berlin Marathon on Sunday 27 September she was the second Canadian woman to finish. Her time was 2:51:02, which put her 125th. - [Lewis Mills: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lewis-mills): Runners / Lewis Mills LM 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Lewis Mills Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Lewis Mills is a British runner who has turned up in both road relay and trail results this year. Neither source gives his age, his event of choice or how long he has been running. His most notable run came for Tonbridge at the South of England road relays on Saturday 26 September, at Aldershot's Rushmoor Arena. Each leg was 6km over two undulating 3km laps. Mills took the third of six stages. He received the baton with Tonbridge in second and passed it on in third at the halfway point. His individual split has not been published. James Kingston then moved the team into the lead on the fourth leg with 17:07, equalling a course record set by Andy Bristow in 1989. Will Beeston and Ted Higgins held on from there. Tonbridge won in 1:48:16, 46 seconds ahead of Cambridge & Coleridge. It ended a long wait for the club, which counts five second places since 2016. The UTMB results database lists a British man named Lewis Mills in the Adidas TERREX 10k Trail Race at the Keswick Mountain Festival in 2026. The course was 10 km with 380 m of climb. He finished in 1:02:22, 69th man. The sources do not confirm that the relay runner and the trail runner are the same person. That Lewis Mills has no current UTMB Index. Nothing has been reported about his plans for the rest of the season. He also lined up in the 10,000 metres at the Paris Olympics in 2024. He landed two silvers at the 2025 edition of the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Spain, taking individual silver in the mountain classic and helping Uganda to team silver, clocking 1:03:14 for second in the Classic 14K. - [Karl Meltzer: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/karl-meltzer): Runners / Karl Meltzer Photo: Hoka One One 🇺🇸 Karl Meltzer Born 1967 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) UTMB Index 596 (9 November 2026) Karl Meltzer is an American ultrarunner and coach from Sandy, Utah, born in 1967 and known as "Speedgoat Karl". No one has won more 100-mile races. By December 2021 his tally at the distance stood at 45. He turned professional in 1999 and started coaching in 2007. Hardrock was the race he made his own, with five wins. The fastest of them came in 2009 in 24:38:02. He also won the Wasatch Front 100 six times and Massanutten four times. His best year was 2006, when he won six 100-milers, four of them in record times. The last four came inside eight weeks. That season brought Runner of the Year honours from USATF, Ultrarunning Magazine and the RRCA. He has also chased records on long trails. He ran the Appalachian Trail from Maine to Georgia in 2008 in just under 55 days. In 2016 he went back and set a record of 45 days, 22 hours and 38 minutes for its 2,190 miles. The run became the 2017 film "Made To Be Broken". He has also held the speed record for the Pony Express Trail. His win at the No Business 100 in October 2020 made it 19 years in a row with a 100-mile victory. He is the race director of the Speedgoat 50K at Snowbird. - [Arthur Newton: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/arthur-newton): Runners / Arthur Newton Photo: photographer unknown / Ultrarunning History 🇬🇧 Arthur Newton Born 1883 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road (legend) Arthur Newton was an English-born distance runner who won South Africa's Comrades Marathon five times in the 1920s. Born on 20 May 1883, he only took up running seriously at the age of 38. He went on to hold world records at 50 miles, 100 miles and 24 hours. He died on 7 September 1959. After school at Bedford, he went to South Africa in 1901 and worked as a teacher. In 1911 he bought a farm in Natal. During the First World War he was a dispatch rider with the Natal Light Horse. He came home to a neglected farm and a dispute with the government over his land. He entered the 1922 Comrades to win publicity for his case, after just 20 weeks of training. He won that first "up" race in 8:40:00. A year later he won the "down" run by 52 minutes in 6:56:07, over two hours inside the old record. Two officials timed him off a nearby post office clock. Further wins followed in 1924, 1925 and 1927, with a down record of 6:24:54 in 1925. That year he moved to Rhodesia, where he founded the Bulawayo Harriers. In 1928 he set a 100-mile record of 14:22:10 on the road from Bath to London. He then raced as a professional in the United States, Canada and Britain. In 1931, at an indoor race he staged in Hamilton, Ontario, he covered 152 miles and 540 yards in 24 hours. That world record stood for 22 years. His last 100-mile run came in 1934, at 51, from Bath to London in 14:11:30. He championed high mileage at gentle speeds, later known as long slow distance, and wrote several books on training. When the London to Brighton race became an annual event in 1951, its trophy was named the Arthur Newton Cup. - [Lotti Brinks: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lotti-brinks): Runners / Lotti Brinks Photo: iRunFar / Eszter Horanyi 🇩🇪 Lotti Brinks Country 🇩🇪 Germany Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 807 (9 November 2026) Lotti Brinks is a German-born ultrarunner now based in Boise, Idaho, with a UTMB Index of 808. Running was part of her college years at Savannah College of Art and Design, but she stepped away afterwards, only picking the sport back up once the Covid-19 pandemic hit, while she was living in Austin, Texas. Her comeback moved fast. Early in 2021 she took wins at the Bandera 50K and the HOKA Rocky Raccoon 100K, and in 2023 a victory at the Grindstone 100K earned her a Golden Ticket entry to the Western States 100. She debuted there in 2024, finishing 15th, before climbing to 5th in 2026 in 16:04:38. Coach Tyler Green oversees her training. HOKA signed her as a professional at the start of 2025, work she balances with a full-time marketing job. In 2026 she won Snowbasin by UTMB's 58K race in 05:18:56 and repeated an earlier win at the Gorge Waterfalls 100K, this time in 09:06:23. She has raced the CCC, the support race at HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc, twice, improving from 9th in 2024 to 6th in 2025. Her other wins include the Tillamook Burn 50 Miler in 2023 and the Javelina Jundred 100K in 2022. - [Sylvie Abel: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sylvie-abel): Runners / Sylvie Abel Photo: @sylvie.abel / Instagram 🇺🇸 Sylvie Abel Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 784 (9 November 2026) Sylvie Abel is an American trail runner with a UTMB Index of 784, built almost entirely on races around the San Francisco Bay Area over an eight-year career. She won the Quicksilver Endurance Runs 100k in 2026 in 9:25:41, more than two hours quicker than her 2021 win over the same course, and finished third woman at The Big Alta 100K the same year. In 2024 she won the Quad Dipsea in 4:38:36 and the Mammoth Trail Fest 50 km in 5:23:14, and was third at the Javelina Jundred 100 km. Her 2025 season was quieter by comparison, with a third place at the Quad Dipsea and an eighth at the Mammoth Trail Fest. She has raced consistently since 2018, when she finished fourth woman at the Rodeo Beach 50K, a race she improved to third the following year. - [Ellie Greenwood: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ellie-greenwood): Runners / Ellie Greenwood Photo: Ben Zengerink / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Ellie Greenwood Born 1979 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra, Road (legend) Ellie Greenwood is a Scottish-born ultrarunner with British and Canadian citizenship. Born in Dundee on 14 March 1979, she won the world 100 km title in 2010 and 2014. In 2014 she became the first British woman to win the Comrades Marathon. Ultrarunning Magazine made her its North American female ultrarunner of the year in 2011, 2012 and 2014. She moved to Canada in 2001 after university and began racing ultras in 2005. Her breakthrough came in 2010. At her first 100 km, the Elk-Beaver race on Vancouver Island, she won in a course record of 7:36. Later that year she became world 100 km champion for Great Britain in 7:29:05, after a long battle with Lizzy Hawker. Britain took the team gold too. Western States made her name in the United States. She won it in 2011 and returned in 2012 to run 16:47:19. That cut more than 50 minutes from Ann Trason's course record, which had stood since 1994. In 2012 she also broke the women's record at the JFK 50 Mile, finishing tenth overall, and won the 101 km CCC in Chamonix. At Comrades she was fourth in 2011 and runner-up in 2012, beaten by only 72 seconds. Injuries wrecked her 2013 season. She returned for Comrades in 2014 and was eight minutes down with 18 km left. She caught the leader and won in 6:18:15. In November she won her second world 100 km title in 7:30:48, eight minutes clear, as Britain again won the team event. Her other wins include the Vancouver Marathon in 2:42:15 in 2012 and the Les Templiers 75k in 2015. She became a Canadian citizen in 2015 and was coaching runners full-time by 2023. - [Ross Gollan: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ross-gollan): Runners / Ross Gollan Photo: Gollan Coaching 🇬🇧 Ross Gollan Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 858 (9 November 2026) Ross Gollan is a Scottish mountain and sky runner who represents Nike ACG and coaches other athletes through Gollan Coaching. He also works part time as an ecologist at the Kyle of Sutherland Rivers Trust, having graduated with a geography degree from the University of Glasgow. He has raced internationally for both Scotland and Great Britain and Northern Ireland in mountain running. In 2025 Gollan won the British long distance mountain running championship at Stuc a'Chroin in Scotland, part of a season that took him from a 5k road race in Northern Ireland to altitude racing in Mexico. He broke 14 minutes for 5k at Armagh and ran 64 minutes for the half marathon in Den Haag the same year. He also raced the Mexico Sky Challenge, a 35 kilometre course with 3,600 metres of climbing, as part of the Skyrunner World Series. On the UTMB circuit Gollan has won races including the Trail des Hauts Forts Trail des Mines d'Or in France and the Shotover Moonlight Mountain Marathon in New Zealand. He regularly competes at Sierre-Zinal, the classic Swiss mountain race, and has raced there every year from 2016 to 2026. His UTMB Index of 862 places him among Scotland's strongest current mountain runners. - [Courtney Dauwalter: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/courtney-dauwalter): Runners / Courtney Dauwalter Photo: Heike Maria Seitz / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Courtney Dauwalter Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 854 (9 November 2026) Courtney Dauwalter is an American ultramarathon runner, born on 13 February 1985. She is widely regarded as one of the best trail runners in the world. In 2023 she won Western States 100, then Hardrock 100, and finally the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc, all within a few months, a feat no one had managed before. Dauwalter grew up in Hopkins, Minnesota, and was a four-time state Nordic skiing champion in high school. She studied biology at the University of Denver on a skiing scholarship. She later trained as a teacher at the University of Mississippi and taught science in Denver. She became a full-time professional runner in 2017. She now lives and trains above 10,000 feet in Leadville, Colorado. She set a course record at the 2016 Javelina Jundred 100K and won that year's Run Rabbit Run 100 by 75 minutes. In 2017 she won Run Rabbit Run again despite temporary blindness over the final 12 miles. She also won the Moab 240 outright, beating the runner-up by more than 10 hours. Dauwalter is known for her upbeat attitude in races and for wearing distinctively baggy long shorts, later sold by Salomon as her 'Shortney' range. She won the Western States 100 in 2018 and the UTMB in both 2019 and 2021, setting a women's course record on her second UTMB win. In 2022 and 2023 she won the Hardrock 100 in both race directions, breaking Diana Finkel's long-standing course records by more than an hour each time. Her 2023 season was historic. She also won Western States that year, breaking Ellie Greenwood's 2012 record, then completed the treble by winning UTMB again that September. She has kept winning since, taking the Mt. Fuji 100 Mile and Transgrancanaria in 2024, and Hardrock and the Chianti Ultra Trail in 2026. In December 2025 she ran a marathon personal best of 2:38:55 at the California International Marathon. She has been named Ultra Runner of the Year five times and carried the Olympic flame across Italy ahead of the 2026 Winter Olympics. In 2024, rival runner Camille Herron was found to have edited Dauwalter's Wikipedia page, along with Kilian Jornet's, to play down their results and talk up her own. - [Anton Krupicka: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/anton-krupicka): Runners / Anton Krupicka Photo: Juan Ramón Rodríguez Sosa / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Anton Krupicka Born 1983 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Anton Krupicka is an American ultrarunner who won the Leadville Trail 100 in 2006 and 2007. Born on 2 August 1983, he grew up near Niobrara in Nebraska. He ran his first marathon at 12. Long hair, a beard, no shirt and the lightest of shoes made him one of the most recognisable runners in the sport. He graduated from Colorado College in 2005 in physics and philosophy, then took a second degree in geology in 2006. Through college and his early twenties he often ran more than 200 miles a week. He left graduate studies at the University of Colorado to run as a professional. The film Indulgence followed his build-up to Leadville in 2007. His other wins include Rocky Raccoon 100 in 2007, the Miwok 100K and White River 50 Mile twice. At White River in 2010 he set a course record of 6:25:29. The same year he finished second at Western States in 15:13:53, a time that would have been a course record. In 2014 he won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail. Injuries interrupted much of his racing, and he turned more and more to climbing, skiing and cycling. He has set 28 fastest known times, among them the Maroon Bells Four Pass Loop in 2009. In 2016 he and climber Stefan Griebel set the Longs Peak Triathlon record of 9:06:00, cycling from Boulder, running and then climbing the Diamond. He returned to 100-mile racing with third place at Leadville in 2021. Second place at Grindstone in 2024 earned him a start at UTMB in 2025, his first appearance at the Chamonix final since 2014. - [Joaquin Lopez: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joaquin-lopez): Runners / Joaquin Lopez Photo: UTMB profile 🇪🇨 Joaquin Lopez Country 🇪🇨 Ecuador Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 925 (9 November 2026) Joaquin Lopez is an Ecuadorian ultra-trail runner racing for Kailas Fuga. His UTMB Index of 925 is one of the strongest in this group. He has raced the UTMB Mont Blanc itself five times, finishing 6th in 2019, 2nd in the TDS distance in 2022, 11th in 2023 and 3rd in 2024. In 2026 he placed 5th, covering the 174km course in 19 hours 6 minutes. - [Wally Hayward: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/wally-hayward): Runners / Wally Hayward WH 🇿🇦 Film My Run 🇿🇦 Wally Hayward Born 1908 Country 🇿🇦 South Africa Runs Road, Track (legend) Wally Hayward was a South African endurance runner whose career spanned 60 years. He took five Comrades Marathon titles and ranks among the finest 100-mile runners there have been. Born in Durban on 10 July 1908, he died in Edenvale on 28 April 2006. Hayward served an apprenticeship as a carpenter and began running at 19, through a boys' club. He read about Comrades in 1929 and sent a letter to its director, Vic Clapham. He entered in 1930 and won at his first attempt, aged 21. A broken foot in training the next year halted him, and he was back racing by 1938. He won bronze over six miles at the 1938 Empire Games in Sydney and placed fourth over three miles. In the Second World War he fought in North Africa and Italy. He received the British Empire Medal in 1942 for bravery near El Alamein. Two decades after his first Comrades win he took the title again in 1950, 1951, 1953 and 1954. In 1952 he ran the Olympic marathon in Helsinki instead and finished tenth. He set down-run records in 1951 and 1953, the second time becoming the first runner under six hours. His 1954 win brought the up-run record, and at 45 he was the oldest winner until Vladimir Kotov in 2004. In 1953 he also set records from London to Brighton in 5:29:40 and Bath to London over 100 miles in 12:20:28. He covered 159 miles 562 yards in a 24-hour track race. That year the South African Athletics and Cycling Association ruled him a professional for accepting a small travel donation in Britain. The ban on amateur racing was lifted in 1974. He went back to Comrades in 1988 and ran 9:44, ahead of half the finishers. In 1989, aged 80, he finished 1 minute 57 seconds inside the cut-off, an age record that stood for 34 years. She ran the 20km course, which carries 490 metres of climb, in 2:12:17 and finished 29th woman. She returned to the same race in 2026 and clocked 2:14:31, which was good for 33rd woman. Her biggest result came over the longer distance. She won the women's 50K at the first Hustle at Pinehurst, the revived version of the old Run for the Toad, at the Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area near Cambridge, Ontario. The course is a 12.5K loop with more than 250 metres of climb a lap over cross-country style ground, so the 50K runners went round four times. Maher finished in 5:30:36. Because it was the first edition of the new race, that time stands as the women's course record. Behind her, Hamilton's Nicki Tober took second in 5:32:08, seven seconds ahead of Patricia Halligan of Niagara Falls. Robert Brouillette won the race overall in 3:34:36. Nearly 400 runners took part across the distances that day. The organisers have said they already have ideas for a 2027 edition. If it goes ahead, the women's 50K record the field will be chasing is Maher's. - [Fuzhao Xiang: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/fuzhao-xiang): Runners / Fuzhao Xiang Photo: Arc'teryx 🇨🇳 Fuzhao Xiang Country 🇨🇳 China Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 822 (9 November 2026) Fuzhao Xiang is a Chinese trail and ultra runner from a mountain village in Wanzhou, Chongqing, with a UTMB Index of 823. She took up trail running in 2012 as a late substitute in an adventure race while studying at Zunyi Medical University, and ran her first 100 km trail race in 2015 in Zhangye, Gansu province, finishing 3rd. She has built one of the deepest records in the sport, racing UTMB Mont-Blanc itself four times. She finished 20th in 2018, 11th in 2019, 7th in 2022 and 4th in 2023, her best result there and the highest UTMB Mont-Blanc finish by a Chinese runner. In 2019 she also became the first Asian woman to win the Ultra-Trail Mt. Fuji, in 24:20:00. Xiang has twice finished 2nd at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run, in 16:20:03 in 2024 and 16:47:09 in 2025, before placing 7th in 2026 in 16:25:59. She has also won major races including the Vibram Hong Kong 100, TransLantau 140 and Panda Trail by UTMB. China's Golden Rhino Awards, dubbed the country's outdoor-sports Oscars, named her its 2024 Trail Runner of the Year. - [Andrea Mayr: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/andrea-mayr): Runners / Andrea Mayr Photo: Steindy / Wikimedia Commons 🇦🇹 Andrea Mayr Born 1979 (age 46 or 47) Country 🇦🇹 Austria Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 767 (9 November 2026) Andrea Mayr is an Austrian runner, born in 1979, who has competed on the road, on mountain courses, in cycling and in ski mountaineering. No other athlete has won more world mountain running titles: she has seven, the most in the championship's history. She won her first, in 2010, beating Valentina Belotti into second by more than 30 seconds over 8.5km, and also took that year's WMRA Grand Prix series. She has repeatedly won Slovenia's Smarna Gora Race, taking the title in 2008, 2009, 2010, 2014, 2016 and 2017. On the road, Mayr set her marathon best of 2:30:43 winning the Vienna City Marathon in 2009, a time that still stands as the Austrian record alongside her Austrian half marathon record. She represented Austria in the marathon at the 2012 London Olympics, finishing 54th, and in the 3000m steeplechase at the 2005 and 2007 World Championships in Athletics. She has continued competing into her forties, racing Italy's Trofeo Nasego most years since 2021 and finishing 7th there in 2026. - [Xavier Thévenard: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/xavier-thevenard): Runners / Xavier Thévenard Photo: ESM / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇷 Xavier Thévenard Born 1988 Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) UTMB Index 722 (9 November 2026) Xavier Thévenard is a French trail runner and the only athlete to have won all four individual races at the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc. Born in Nantua on 6 March 1988, he grew up in the ski resort of Les Plans d'Hotonnes. He won the UTMB itself in 2013, 2015 and 2018. He came to running from cross-country skiing and biathlon, using it to train through the summer. He started racing ultras in 2010 and won the 99 km CCC in Chamonix that August in 11:57:13. A year later he took the 105 km Endurance Trail at the Festival des Templiers. His first UTMB win came in 2013, in 20:34:57. He added the TDS in 2014 and a second UTMB title in 2015. Victory in the 55 km OCC in 2016 completed the set of Chamonix races. That July he was also third at the Hardrock 100 in Colorado in 23:57:10. Victory in the Mont-Blanc 80 km followed in 2017, and a third UTMB title came in 2018 in 20:44:16. In 2019 he took Ultra-Trail Mt. Fuji and the Mont-Blanc 90 km, then finished second at the UTMB. He was still racing in 2026, when he took second place at the Gruyère Trail Charmey 54 km. - [Josh Wade: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/josh-wade): Runners / Josh Wade 🇬🇧 Josh Wade Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 918 (9 November 2026) Josh Wade is a British trail and ultra runner from Kendal in the Lake District, sponsored by The North Face. His UTMB Index stands at 918. He grew up fell walking as a child before switching to running around 2017. He also works as a gardener, and reckons a day spent shoving mowers up slopes adds to his mileage. His 2023 Ultra-Trail Snowdonia 100 Mile win stands out, a course record built on an almost 90 minute margin. He has also topped the podium at the Montane Spine Challenger and twice at the shorter Ultra-Trail Snowdonia 100k. His UTMB Mont-Blanc results have improved each year, from 11th in 2024 to third in 2025, his best finish there. Strong climbing on the way to Grand Col Ferret set up that podium spot, which left him, in his own words, chuffed. In 2026 he added the Ultra-Trail Snowdonia Eryri 80K to his wins and finished third again at Transgrancanaria. He wants more years at UTMB and has named Hardrock 100 and the Diagonale des Fous as future targets. - [Caroline Kimutai: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/caroline-kimutai): Runners / Caroline Kimutai Photo: Christian David / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Caroline Kimutai Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 801 (9 November 2026) Caroline Kimutai is a Kenyan mountain and trail runner from Iten, racing for Milimani Runners. Her UTMB Index stands at 802. She ran as a young athlete but stopped during high school. Kimutai took the sport up again in 2022, stepped away, then recommitted to focused training. She moved into trail racing in October 2024 and won her first race, a 25 km event in her home town of Iten. Her rise continued through 2025. She won the Jinshanling Great Wall Trail Race in China in 2:39:14, over 24 km with 1,800 m of climbing. She also won the Restonica Trail 50K in Corsica in 3:42:25, and finished 7th in 1:56:56 at the Golden Trail World Series stop at Pitz Alpine. At Sierre-Zinal in August she crossed the line second in 2:55:31 on the 31 km course, which climbs 2,190 m. Joyline Chepngeno was ahead of her. Chepngeno was later given a two-year ban by the Athletics Integrity Unit, starting 8 September 2025, after testing positive for the corticosteroid triamcinolone acetonide. Her Sierre-Zinal result was annulled and Kimutai was promoted to the win. Kimutai went back to Sierre-Zinal in 2026 and finished second in 2:56:31. On 27 September she returned to Jinshanling as defending champion and took third in 2:43:33, a little over four minutes slower than her winning time a year earlier. Ruth Gitonga of Kenya won in 2:39:47, with Germany's Hanna Gröber second in 2:41:13. This year's course ran 23.1 km with 1,667 m of climbing, much of it on the stone stairs of the wall. The race closed the seven-event 2026 Golden Trail World Series calendar before its finale. That decider is the Muju Trail Grand Finale in South Korea on 24 October. - [Matt Carpenter: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/matt-carpenter): Runners / Matt Carpenter Photo: Matt Carpenter / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Matt Carpenter Born 1964 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Matt Carpenter is an American mountain runner whose times still fill the record books of Colorado's high-altitude races. Born in North Carolina on 20 July 1964, he has won the Pikes Peak Marathon 12 times. His 2005 course record at the Leadville Trail 100 lasted 19 years. He took up running at high school in Mississippi and went on to the University of Southern Mississippi. Frequent trips to Colorado led him to move there after graduating, first to Vail in 1987 and later to Manitou Springs. In 1990 the US Olympic Training Center measured his VO2 max at 90.2, the highest it had recorded. Fila Skyrunners signed him in 1993, and he won most of the 17 high-altitude marathons he entered. He set records at both 14,350 and 17,060 feet. On Pikes Peak he has won 18 races, six ascents and 12 marathons, including both on consecutive days in 2001. His 1993 marathon time of 3:16:39 is still the outright best. His ascent split from that 1993 race, 2:01:06, stood as the fastest ascent for 30 years until Rémi Bonnet ran 2:00:20 in 2023. Carpenter also holds the course records at the Vail Hill Climb, which he won eight times, and the Imogene Pass Run, which he won six times. Later he turned to ultras. He set a course record at the San Juan Solstice 50 in 2004. At Leadville in 2005 he ran 15:42:59, beating Paul DeWitt's mark of 17:16:19 by more than 90 minutes. David Roche finally broke that record in 2024. In October 2013 Carpenter became the first distance runner in the Colorado Springs Sports Hall of Fame. - [Heather Jackson: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/heather-jackson): Runners / Heather Jackson Photo: Heather Jackson Racing 🇺🇸 Heather Jackson Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 761 (9 November 2026) Heather Jackson, born 24 April 1984, is an American endurance athlete who made her name as a professional triathlete before moving into trail and ultrarunning for HOKA. She played ice hockey at Princeton University and was twice captain of the women's team. She also raced on the US track cycling programme, finishing third in both the individual pursuit and the omnium at the 2009 US Elite Track National Championships. As a professional triathlete she was third at the 2012 Ironman 70.3 World Championship and runner-up a year later. She won her first full-distance race at Ironman Coeur d'Alene in 2015, recovering from an 8-minute deficit after the swim on an unusually hot day. She was fifth on her Ironman World Championship debut that year. On 24 July 2016 she won Ironman Lake Placid in 9:09:42, a female course record. Her ultrarunning record began to build at the Javelina Jundred 100 Miles, where she was 5th woman in 2022 in 15:42:18 and won in 2023 in 14:24:47. In 2023 she also won the Three Sisters Skyline 50K in 04:10:20 and The Canyons 50K in 04:09:36, and was second at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 08:47:59. In 2024 she was 5th woman at the CCC, 101 km with 6,050m of climb, in 12:50:55, and 7th at the Western States 100 in 17:16:43. She stepped up to the full 174 km UTMB in 2025 and finished 19th woman in 29:33:00. Her 2026 season has been her busiest yet. She won the Desert RATS 100K in 09:45:12 and was 4th woman at the Cocodona 250, 408 km with 11,824m of climb, in 69:36:34. She retained her Three Sisters Skyline 50K title in 04:27:36. On 31 October she won Javelina for a second time in 13:48:29, 55 seconds ahead of Britain's Carla Molinaro. The race runs over five loops in McDowell Mountain Regional Park in Arizona, with 1,919m of climb, and heavy overnight rain had left the trails muddy. Jackson was 8min 15sec behind Molinaro at mile 71 and still 3min 21sec down at mile 95.3. She went past late on, in the dark and the rain. The win earned her a Golden Ticket for the 2027 Western States 100. She holds a UTMB Index of 761. - [Ruth Croft: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ruth-croft): Runners / Ruth Croft Photo: iRunFar / Eszter Horanyi 🇳🇿 Ruth Croft Born 1989 (age 36 or 37) Country 🇳🇿 New Zealand Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 820 (9 November 2026) Ruth Croft is a New Zealand ultramarathon and trail runner who races for adidas TERREX, with a UTMB Index of 820. Born on 15 January 1989 in Greymouth, she grew up in the small West Coast town of Stillwater and was schooled in Christchurch, competing there in track and cross country. As a junior she was under-20 national champion. She ran the 3000m steeplechase for New Zealand at the 2006 World Junior Championships, and appeared for her country at the World Mountain Running Championships in 2005 and 2007. An athletic scholarship took her to the University of Portland in Oregon. After graduating she moved to Taiwan to teach English, staying five and a half years and eventually working in marketing for Garmin, whose sponsorship she picked up as she raced more trail events there. In Malaysia she was twice victorious at the Mt. Kinabalu International Climbathon, over 50K, first in 2013 and again the following year, then won the 100 km CCC race at UTMB in 2015 and was 4th at the North Face 50 in San Francisco. From 2017 she began splitting her year between Europe and New Zealand. That season alone brought wins over 50K near Hong Kong, over Tarawera's 62 km course, and at the 73 km Templiers race in France. Chamonix's 55 km OCC fell to her twice, in 2018 and 2019, and she added a silver medal at the 2019 Trail World Championships behind France's Blandine L'Hirondel, the first trail world championship medal won by a New Zealander. She made a winning start over 100 miles, finishing 2nd at Western States in 2021 behind Beth Pascall, then won the race outright in 2022 in 17:21:30. She won the 100 km Ultra-Trail Cape Town in November 2023, but did not start UTMB that year. Croft returned in 2024 to finish 2nd behind Katie Schide, then won UTMB itself in 2025, becoming the first woman and only the second runner ever to win OCC, CCC and UTMB. She also races Tarawera in New Zealand almost every year, winning in 2021 with a course record of 9:21:03, again in 2024, in 2025 with another course record, and again in 2026. Away from racing she ran the length of Greenland's 125-mile Arctic Circle Trail in 2022, and the historic Nakasendo Trail in Japan in 2023 alongside Tim Tollefson, Magda Boulet and Desiree Linden. - [Cassandra de Winter: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/cassandra-de-winter): Runners / Cassandra de Winter Photo: Athletics Illustrated 🇨🇦 Cassandra de Winter Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 694 (9 November 2026) Cassandra de Winter is a Canadian road and trail runner who lives in Lethbridge, Alberta. She grew up in the nearby town of Vulcan. She came to distance running from rugby and powerlifting, and only started racing seriously in 2025. She coaches herself. Her rise on the roads was quick. She ran 2:52 at the Calgary Marathon in May 2025 to place second woman. Five months later she won the Royal Victoria Marathon in 2:39:52. In April 2026 she ran Boston from the professional field and clocked 2:34:43. That made her the first Canadian woman home, in only her third marathon. She has also run 1:12:55 for the half marathon, in Mesa, Arizona. She races trails in the summer. In 2025 she won the women's race at the Black Spur Ultra 54K in 5:26:00, setting a course record, and finished a 100 km in 10:03:12. In 2026 she won the Sinister 7 Ultra 50K in July in 5:10:19. In September she took the Lost Soul Ultra 50K in Lethbridge outright in about 4:12. Both of those wins were women's course records. Her biggest result came at the Javelina Jundred 100K in Arizona on 31 October 2026. She held back from a fast start and caught the leading men late in the race. She won outright in 7:44:45, ahead of Juan Rocha in 7:50:28. That took more than 28 minutes off Anna Louden's women's course record of 8:13:07 from 2023. Only two faster times have been recorded on the course. Her Javelina time was eight minutes outside Julie Hamulecki's Canadian women's 100K road record of 7:36:39. De Winter said she would love to have a go at it. Her general UTMB Index is 694. - [Don Ritchie: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/don-ritchie): Runners / Don Ritchie Photo: Mark Shearman / Scottish Athletics 🇬🇧 Don Ritchie Born 1944 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road, Track (legend) Don Ritchie was a Scottish ultrarunner who set a string of world bests on track and road in the 1970s and 1980s. Born at Haddo House in Aberdeenshire on 6 July 1944, he covered 100 km in 6:10:20 on the track at Crystal Palace in October 1978. He held that world record for the rest of his life. He was first pushed towards the quarter-mile but soon moved up to longer distances. His first ultra was the 36-mile Two Bridges race in 1970. He won the London to Brighton race in 1977 and 1978. At Crystal Palace in October 1977 he ran 100 miles in 11:30:51, the fastest ever recorded, and that time lasted until 2002. In 1979 he set a world road best for 100 miles, running 11:51:11 at Flushing Meadows in New York. He also set track world bests at 50 km, 40 miles and 50 miles. At Coatbridge in 1983 he covered 200 km on the track in 16:32:30. In 1989 he ran from John o' Groats to Land's End in a record 10 days, 15 hours and 27 minutes. Ritchie won the global 24-hour championships in Milton Keynes in 1990 with 166 miles, an indoor world record. His style suited road and track more than trails, yet in 1991 he won the West Highland Way Race, 95 miles of trail. He was made an MBE in 1995 for services to athletics. Ritchie died at his home in Lossiemouth in June 2018, aged 73. Days later Nao Kazami ran 6:09:14 at the Lake Saroma 100 km, finally beating the time Ritchie had set almost 40 years before. - [Andy Douglas: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/andrew-douglas): Runners / Andy Douglas Photo: scottishathletics 🇬🇧 Andy Douglas Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 869 (9 November 2026) Andy Douglas is a Scottish mountain runner who switched from road and cross country racing in 2014. He had been chasing a marathon qualifying time for the 2014 Commonwealth Games but was repeatedly held back by injury. Having grown up in a rural part of northern Scotland, he turned to the hills instead and made the Great Britain mountain running team at his first attempt. Douglas won his first British Mountain Running title in that debut season of 2014 and has represented Great Britain at the European and World Mountain Running Championships every year since. He finished 6th at the World Championships in 2015. On the road he set his half marathon personal best in 2016, two years after taking up hill racing, showing the two disciplines could work together. He has been a regular podium finisher at Sierre-Zinal and the Laugavegur Ultra Marathon, winning the Icelandic race outright in 2021. In 2024 he won the World Masters Mountain Running Championships Classic 17K. He continues to race across Europe on the WMRA circuit, coached by Sophie Dunnett. - [Elena Nurgalieva: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/elena-nurgalieva): Runners / Elena Nurgalieva Photo: Ben Zengerink / Wikimedia Commons 🇷🇺 Elena Nurgalieva Born 1976 Country 🇷🇺 Russia Runs Road (legend) Elena Nurgalieva is a Russian ultrarunner who won the Comrades Marathon eight times, more than any other woman. Born in Perm Krai on 9 January 1976, she also took four wins at the 56 km Two Oceans Marathon. With her identical twin Olesya she ruled South Africa's two great ultras from 2003 to 2014. The twins grew up in the Urals as cross-country skiers. They had taken marathon running seriously for only four years when they arrived at Comrades in 2003. It was their first race outside Russia. They ran together for 70 km before Elena broke clear to win in 6:07:46, with Olesya second. Earlier that year she had been second at the Russian 100 km championships in 7:31:14. In 2004 she won the Two Oceans for the first time and defended her Comrades title with an up-run record. That season she also ran her marathon best of 2:29:49 at Frankfurt, one second behind her sister. She won the Two Oceans again in 2005 and set another up-run record at Comrades in 2006. Further Comrades wins came in 2008 and 2010, while her other Two Oceans titles came in 2009 and 2012. Across her career she earned 13 Comrades gold medals, a women's record. Her last Comrades was in 2015, when she finished third. - [George Hopkins: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/george-hopkins): Runners / George Hopkins GH 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 George Hopkins Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra George Hopkins is a British runner. The available record of his running is thin. His one reported result comes from university cross-country relay racing in Manchester. A George Hopkins of Great Britain is also listed on the UTMB database, though without a current UTMB Index. The sources do not show whether this is the same runner. His notable run came at the Ron Hill Manchester University Relays at Wythenshawe in late October, on a weekend when Storm Austen and Storm Boelo hit the British cross-country calendar. Organisers said the conditions were the worst in the event's 60 editions. Bruce Green, speaking for them, called it "the worst that I have officiated in". Hopkins ran for the University of Manchester in the mixed race. His strong final leg helped the team win in 64:33, five seconds ahead of Manchester Metropolitan University. It was a home win in a big field. A total of 45 mixed teams finished, alongside 71 men's and 96 women's teams. Birmingham's runners filled the top two places in the men's event and did the same again in the women's. Manchester's victory in the mixed event was the one title that stayed in the city. Leg distances and individual split times for the mixed race have not been reported, so Hopkins's own time is not known. Nothing further has been published about his recent racing or his plans. - [Jakob Ingebrigtsen: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jakob-ingebrigtsen): Runners / Jakob Ingebrigtsen Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons 🇳🇴 Jakob Ingebrigtsen Born 2000 (age 25 or 26) Country 🇳🇴 Norway Runs Track, Road Jakob Ingebrigtsen is a Norwegian middle- and long-distance runner, born on 19 September 2000. He is a two-time Olympic champion, winning 1500 metres gold at the Tokyo Olympics and 5000 metres gold at the Paris Olympics. He has won seven senior global titles in total and holds world records over several distances. Ingebrigtsen was born in Sandnes, the youngest of three running brothers alongside Henrik and Filip. Their father, Gjert, coached all three until 2022, when Jakob became self-coached with input from his brothers. At 16, in 2017, he became the youngest man in history at the time to run a mile under four minutes, in 3:58.07. That age record has since been broken, by New Zealand's Sam Ruthe in 2025. As a senior he broke the 1500 metres European record several times and set a world record in the short track 1500 metres. He won the 1500 metres at the delayed 2020 Tokyo Olympics in an Olympic record of 3:28.32. He then won consecutive 5000 metres world titles in 2022 and 2023. In 2024 he set a world record in the 3000 metres, running 7:17.55 to break Daniel Komen's mark, which had stood for almost 28 years. At the Paris Olympics in 2024 he finished fourth in the 1500 metres before winning gold in the 5000 metres. He completed a rare Olympic double, having also won 1500 metres gold in Tokyo. In 2025 he became the first man to win both the 1500 metres and 3000 metres at a World Indoor Championships. He needed surgery on his Achilles tendon in early 2026, then returned to win the 5000 metres at that year's European Championships. He also races on the road. In September 2026 he was beaten to the world 5 km title in Copenhagen by Eritrea's Dawit Seare, finishing three seconds back in a Norwegian record of 12:59. She described herself to iRunFar as traditionally a stronger climber than descender, saying she remains cautious on technical downhills late in long races. In 2026 she also finished second at the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg Trail and third at the Chianti Ultra Trail. - [Agnes Ngetich: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/agnes-ngetich): Runners / Agnes Ngetich Photo: filip bossuyt / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Agnes Ngetich Born 2001 (age 24 or 25) Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Road, Track Agnes Ngetich is a Kenyan long-distance runner, born on 23 January 2001. On 20 September 2026 she ran 1:05:15 to win the half marathon at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen, a world record for a race run by women alone. The time beat by one second the mark Peres Jepchirchir had held since 2021 and took Kenya to the team title as well. Ngetich won by 50 seconds from her Kenyan team mate Veronica Loleo, with Florence Niyonkuru of Rwanda three seconds further back for bronze. Her fastest form on the road began in 2024. That January she ran 28:46 in a mixed-gender race in Valencia, becoming the first woman to break 29 minutes for 10 km and setting a world record for the distance in a mixed field, passing 5 km along the way in 14:13, itself a world record split. In October 2024 she won the Valencia Half Marathon in 1:03:04, missing Letesenbet Gidey's outright world record by 13 seconds but moving to second on the all-time list. She retained the Valencia title in October 2025 in 1:03:08. Ngetich has built a strong cross country record alongside her form on the road and track. At the 2023 World Cross Country Championships in Bathurst, Australia, she took individual bronze while Kenya won the team title, then helped Kenya to another team gold in 2024. In 2026 she won the senior women's race outright at the World Cross Country Championships in Tallahassee, beating Uganda's Joy Cheptoyek by 42 seconds, with Kenya taking team silver in the same event, making her the reigning world cross country champion. She has also raced at the top level on the track. Ngetich finished fourth over 10,000 metres and reached the final of the 5,000 metres at the 2025 World Athletics Championships, and won 5,000 metres races on the 2025 Diamond League circuit including the Memorial Van Damme meeting in Brussels. In July 2026 she won the 3,000 metres in a meeting record of 8:08.95 at the Herculis Diamond League meeting in Monaco. She is coached by Julien Di Maria and has said she now wants to target the track at the 2027 World Athletics Championships, calling a track title the one major medal still missing from her collection. - [Rob Krar: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rob-krar): Runners / Rob Krar Photo: Rocky Vachon / iRunFar 🇨🇦 Rob Krar Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 661 (9 November 2026) Rob Krar is a Canadian ultrarunner from Hamilton, Ontario, who is based in Flagstaff, Arizona. He won the Western States 100 in 2014 and 2015. In 2014 he won Western States, Leadville and Run Rabbit Run within 11 weeks. He won Leadville again in 2018. As a teenager he raced triathlon and twice represented Canada at the world championships. At Butler University he ran cross country, 800 m and 1,500 m while studying pharmacy. He graduated in 2002 and worked night shifts as a pharmacist in Phoenix before moving to Flagstaff in 2006. Heel surgery later kept him away from running for two years. His return began with an unexpected win at the Moab Red Hot 33K. He moved up quickly. Victory at the 2013 Leona Divide 50 Mile earned him a Western States place. He then set a fastest known time for the double crossing of the Grand Canyon. In his first 100-miler, at Western States in 2013, he was second in 15:22:05. Later in 2013 he won the UROC 100K and The North Face Endurance Challenge 50 Mile in California. In 2014 he won Western States in 14:53:22, Leadville in 16:09:32 and Run Rabbit Run in 17:40:05. He defended his Western States title in 2015 in 14:48:59. He was twice voted men's Ultra Runner of the Year. Krar won Leadville again in 2018 in 15:51:57. In 2017 he represented Canada at the Ski Mountaineering World Championships in the Dolomites. Runner's World placed him on its list of running's 50 most influential people. He coaches and runs ultrarunning camps in Flagstaff. - [Tomoe Abe: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/tomoe-abe): Runners / Tomoe Abe TA 🇯🇵 Film My Run 🇯🇵 Tomoe Abe Born 1971 Country 🇯🇵 Japan Runs Road, Track (legend) Tomoe Abe is a retired Japanese marathon and ultramarathon runner from Kitsuki in Ōita Prefecture. Born on 13 August 1971, she took marathon bronze at the 1993 World Championships. In June 2000 she ran 6:33:11 for 100 km at Lake Saroma in Hokkaido. That set a women's world record for the distance. She joined the Asahi Kasei athletics club in 1990, straight from high school in Ōita. That year she placed 11th over 10,000 m at the World Junior Championships in Plovdiv. Her marathon debut came at Osaka in January 1993. She finished second in 2:26:27, one second behind Junko Asari. Close to the finish she followed a television vehicle and missed the turn into the stadium, and the lost ground cost her the win. Seven months later she took bronze at the World Championships in Stuttgart in 2:31:01, with Asari winning gold. It was the first time two Japanese women had won medals in the same event at a global championship. Abe went back to Osaka in January 1994 and won in 2:26:09, a Japanese record at the time. She pulled clear of Nobuko Fujimura and Asari inside the final 100 metres. At Lake Saroma in 2000 she was sixth overall at 50 km, running among the men. She held roughly four minutes per kilometre through the second half and kept passing men who were slowing. She finished second overall and cut 27 minutes 37 seconds from the previous women's best. Takahiro Sunada had set the men's record on the same course in 1998, so both 100 km world records now belonged to Japanese runners. Her other wins include the Hokkaido Marathon in 2:31:21 in 1996 and the Senshu International Marathon in 2:29:09 in 2000. She left Asahi Kasei after placing sixth at the Nagoya marathon in March 2002. - [Francesco Puppi: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/francesco-puppi): Runners / Francesco Puppi Photo: Gianina Lindsey / Wikimedia Commons 🇮🇹 Francesco Puppi Born 1992 (age 33 or 34) Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 950 (9 November 2026) Francesco Puppi is an Italian trail and ultrarunner for Hoka, born 26 January 1992, with a general UTMB Index of 952. He was named world champion at the 2017 World Long Distance Mountain Running Championships, awarded the gold medal after the Eritrean runner Petro Mamu was disqualified for doping. He also won the Italian Vertical Kilometer title in 2015. His 2025 season was his strongest yet. He won the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC in 10:06:02, the Canyons Endurance Runs 100K in 08:04:36 and the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 50K in 04:02:31. He added wins at the Chianti Marathon Trail and the Transgrancanaria Marathon. In 2026 he finished second at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in 13:51:08 and seventh at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc OCC. He has also raced Sierre-Zinal every year since at least 2020. Earlier wins include the Vibram Ultra Trail Lago d'Orta 75 km and the Lake Sonoma 50 Miler, both in 2024. He also won the Dacia UTMB Mont Blanc OCC and the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 50K in 2023. - [Anna Tarasova: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/anna-tarasova): Runners / Anna Tarasova Photo: UTMB profile Anna Tarasova Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 802 (9 November 2026) Anna Tarasova runs for the Norda Trail Team and carries a UTMB Index of 803. Her results run from 2019 to 2026, mostly across Spain, Andorra and the Canary Islands. She started modestly. In 2019 she finished sixth woman at CMG Trail and eighth woman over the half marathon distance at Cames de Ferro al Puigsacalm. By 2022 she had turned that into outright wins, taking the Transgavarres CMG and the 82km Costa Brava Stage Run. 2025 was her best season. She won ten women's races, from Argentina's El Cruce and Bariloche Patagonia Bella Vista to Japan's Mt Fuji 100 and Spain's Lavaredo Ultra Trail 80K, Mozart 100 Ultra and Tenerife Bluetrail. Her best result against a bigger international field came at the 101km UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC, where she finished third woman in 11:44:18. She was second woman over the 82km Transgrancanaria Advanced. Her 2026 season opened with a win at the 70km GTPE-Picos de Europa Ultra in 09:57:34. She was fifth woman at the Mozart 100 Marathon. - [Paula Radcliffe: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/paula-radcliffe): Runners / Paula Radcliffe Photo: Neil / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Paula Radcliffe Born 1973 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Road, Track (legend) Paula Radcliffe is a British former distance runner, born in December 1973 near Northwich in Cheshire. Her 2:15:25 at the 2003 London Marathon stood as the women's world record for 16 years, until Brigid Kosgei broke it in 2019. She started running at seven, joining her father on his jogs. At 12 she moved to Bedford & County, where Alex Stanton coached her for the rest of her career. In 1992 she won the world junior cross country title in Boston. Her first marathon was a win in London in 2002, in 2:18:55. Six months later she ran 2:17:18 in Chicago for a world record. She won London three times and New York three times. Her one global marathon title came in Helsinki in 2005, in a championship record of 2:20:57. It was Britain's only gold of those championships. She ran at four Olympic Games, from 1996 to 2008, without a medal. She was made an MBE in 2002 and was voted BBC Sports Personality of the Year. Her last competitive race was the 2015 London Marathon. - [Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/aurelien-dunand-pallaz): Runners / Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz Photo: @rising.story / iRunFar 🇫🇷 Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 921 (9 November 2026) Aurélien Dunand-Pallaz is a French ultra runner, 33, based in Annecy and raised in the Bauges mountains of Savoy. In September 2026 he took over two hours off the fastest known time for Corsica's GR20 trail, reaching Conca in 27 hours and 29 minutes after setting off from Calenzana the previous morning. The old mark of 29:46 had belonged to fellow Frenchman François D'Haene, who had gone under 30 hours for the first time only two months earlier. Dunand-Pallaz first walked parts of the GR20 as a child on family trips to the island and started planning the attempt back in 2020. He made five scouting runs over six years to learn the trickiest northern stretches, with a final look a month before he went for the record. He ran to feel rather than a pace chart, checking his splits only twice, and had built close to a two-hour cushion by 145 kilometres. A ten-person crew of friends supported him along the way, working within a rule that allows just two pacers with him at any time. Afterwards he said the run surprised even him, since his private target had been half an hour slower. The GR20 run followed a strong 2023, in which he took the Hardrock 100 title in Colorado and won Réunion's Diagonale des Fous. UTMB's own records show a second place at UTMB itself and a win at Transgrancanaria in 2021, plus victory in July 2026's Restonica, a 110km race also held in Corsica. He called the GR20 crossing one of the best performances of his career. - [John Kelly: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/john-kelly): Runners / John Kelly Photo: Keith Dunn / iRunFar 🇺🇸 John Kelly Born 1984 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) John Kelly is an American ultrarunner, born on 19 November 1984, known for the Barkley Marathons and the Pennine Way. In 2017 he became the 15th person ever to finish the Barkley. In May 2021 he ran the Pennine Way in 58:04, a fastest known time still standing in 2025. Kelly grew up in Morgan County, Tennessee, and ran for Oak Ridge High School. He then stopped racing until the 2013 Marine Corps Marathon. After qualifying for Boston he took up ultras and triathlon to stay motivated. At his third Barkley attempt, in 2017, he completed all five loops in 59:30:53. That left him about half an hour inside the limit. He had reached three loops in 2015 and four a year later. Later in 2017 he won the RRCA national ultra title at the Lookout Mountain 50 Miler. In 2018 he set a 23:48:00 course record at Virginia's Wild Oak Trail Run. He won the Franklins 200 Mile in Texas in February 2019 in 60:53:12. Kelly then moved to Britain. He won the Spine Race in January 2020 in 87:53. That July he ran the Pennine Way south to north in 64:46, beating Mike Hartley's 1989 time of 65:20. Damian Hall lowered the record to 61:35 only eight days later. In August 2020 Kelly completed the first Grand Round, linking the Paddy Buckley, Bob Graham and Ramsay rounds by bike, in 130:43. Running north to south in May 2021, he took the Pennine Way record back by more than three hours. A year later he ran all 214 Wainwrights in 5 days, 12 hours and 14 minutes, beating Sabrina Verjee's record by 11 hours 35 minutes. Back in the United States he was tenth man at the 2022 Hardrock 100 and ran the California International Marathon in 2:26:50. He finished the Barkley again in 2023 in 58:42:23. In 2024 he became only the second three-time finisher, in 59:15:38. Away from running he holds a PhD from Carnegie Mellon University and works in data analytics. - [Haile Gebrselassie: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/haile-gebrselassie): Runners / Haile Gebrselassie Photo: Foreign and Commonwealth Office / Wikimedia Commons 🇪🇹 Haile Gebrselassie Born 1973 Country 🇪🇹 Ethiopia Runs Track, Road (legend) Haile Gebrselassie is an Ethiopian former long-distance runner, born on 18 April 1973 in Asella. Known as The Emperor, he is considered one of the greatest distance runners in history, setting 27 world records across events from 1500m to the marathon. Gebrselassie won the 10,000m at four straight World Championships, in 1993, 1995, 1997 and 1999. He also won Olympic 10,000m gold at the 1996 Atlanta Games and again at Sydney in 2000, becoming only the third man to retain the title after Emil Zatopek and Lasse Viren. His win over Paul Tergat in Sydney came by just 0.09 seconds, a closer margin than that year's Olympic 100m final. Through the 1990s Gebrselassie repeatedly broke the 5,000m and 10,000m world records, including a 10,000m time of 26:22.75 in Hengelo in 1998 and a 5,000m time of 12:39.36 in Helsinki the same year. In 1999 he played himself in the film Endurance, based on his pursuit of Olympic gold. Gebrselassie moved into road racing in the 2000s. He won his first half marathon in 2001, in 1:04:34, and took the IAAF World Half Marathon title the same year, the year he also helped establish the Great Ethiopian Run, now one of Africa's biggest mass-participation races. He won the Berlin Marathon four years running, from 2006 to 2009, and set a marathon world record of 2:03:59 there in 2008, improving his own mark by 27 seconds. His results faded after 2010, with drop-outs at the Berlin, Fukuoka and New York marathons and a fourth-place finish at the 2012 Tokyo Marathon. Gebrselassie retired from competitive running in May 2015, having placed 16th at the Great Manchester Run. His 25-year career had brought two Olympic gold medals, eight World Championship titles and 27 world records. He went on to serve as president of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation and built a business empire in Ethiopia, including a Hyundai car dealership, hotels and coffee farms trading under the Haile Estate name. - [Mark Darbyshire: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mark-darbyshire): Runners / Mark Darbyshire Photo: Mark Kite 🇬🇧 Mark Darbyshire Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 880 (9 November 2026) Mark Darbyshire is a British ultrarunner from Birmingham who works as an anaesthesiologist associate. He came to the sport relatively late. His first half marathon was at 35, in around 1:45. The Manchester and Berlin marathons then showed him that the road distance was hard on his body. Trail running in the Brecon Beacons suited him better. He ran his first ultra there in 2017, finishing fifth in the Beacons Ultra in 6:58:02. He was second in 2018 and 2019 before winning it in 2021 in 6:09:15. He later took the shorter Beacons Trail Marathon twice, in 3:27:48 in 2022 and 3:28:12 in 2023. Darbyshire is one of Britain's most successful 100-mile racers. He won the Centurion North Downs Way 100 in 2019 in 15:18:41. At the Arc of Attrition he won the 100-mile race in 2022 in a course record of 19:12:48. He took the Arc50 in 2023 in 7:39:31, then returned to the full distance in 2024 and lowered his own record to 18:51:54. At Ultra-Trail Snowdonia he won the 102km UTS 100 in 2021 in 14:25:47 and the 164km UTS 100M in 2024 in 23:41:13, a route with 9,949m of climb. He added the Centurion South Downs Way 100 in 2025 in 13:42:54. Abroad he has finished 19th at UTMB in 2022 in 23:03:42, 12th at the Transgrancanaria Classic in 2025 and 10th at the 169km Lake Biwa 100 the same year. His 2026 season began with a second win at the Centurion Hundred Hills 50km, in 3:50:02. He then won Ultra Wales, an 80km race with 3,394m of climb, in 8:39:49, and finished 26th at the 168km Istria 100 by UTMB in 25:25:48. His latest result came in the Lake District. He won the men's 180km race at the Altra 13 Valleys Ultra, which started in Keswick on Friday 25 September, in 22:09:03. That was more than two hours inside the previous year's course record on a route that crosses the fells with around 7,000m of climbing. He carries a UTMB Index of 880. - [Sebastian Coe: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sebastian-coe): Runners / Sebastian Coe Photo: World Economic Forum, derivative work Connormah / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Sebastian Coe Born 1956 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track (legend) Sebastian Coe was a British middle-distance runner who set nine outdoor and three indoor world records over 800 metres, 1000 metres, 1500 metres and the mile. In 1979 he set three world records in 41 days, at 800 metres, the mile and 1500 metres, becoming the first man to hold all three at once. His rivalries with fellow Britons Steve Ovett and Steve Cram defined middle-distance running through the 1980s. At the 1980 Moscow Olympics, Coe and Ovett each won the other's specialist event, with Ovett taking 800 metres gold while Coe won the 1500 metres. Coe returned four years later at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics to win the 1500 metres again, in an Olympic record of 3:32.53, and took silver in the 800 metres behind Joaquim Cruz. He remains the only man to have won consecutive Olympic 1500 metre titles. Coe set an 800 metre world record of 1:41.73 in Florence in 1981 that stood for 16 years and remains the British record. He also won 800 metre gold at the 1986 European Championships in Stuttgart. He retired from competitive athletics in 1990 after his final race, a sixth-place finish at the Commonwealth Games in Auckland. After retiring, Coe moved into politics and sports administration. He served as a Conservative MP, is now Baron Coe in the House of Lords, led the London 2012 Olympic bid and has led World Athletics since 2015. - [Frédéric Tranchand: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/frederic-tranchand): Runners / Frédéric Tranchand Photo: Torben Utzon / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇷 Frédéric Tranchand Born 1988 (age 37 or 38) Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 958 (9 November 2026) Frédéric Tranchand is a French runner born on 25 May 1988. He built his early career in orienteering before moving into trail and skyrunning. In 2010 he won silver in the relay for France at the European Orienteering Championships in Primorsko, racing alongside Philippe Adamski and Thierry Gueorgiou. Later that year he took bronze in the sprint at the World Orienteering Championships in Trondheim, a result seen as a major surprise at the time. After four years without a medal at the World Championships, Tranchand returned to the podium in the relay. He added a second individual medal at the World Championships in Estonia in 2017, taking silver in the sprint behind multiple world champion Daniel Hubmann. He competes in orienteering for the club OK Hällen in Stigtomta, Sweden, and on the trail for the team Merrell. On the trail, he took the Short Trail title at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in 2025, clocking 4:42:10. In 2026 he took the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc OCC in 5:10:08 and won the 52K trail race at the European Athletics Off-Road Running Championships in 3:55:14. He also won the Skyrace des Matheysins three times, in 2020, 2021 and 2026, and the Golden Trail Championship Volcanoes Trail in 2020. - [Max King: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/max-king): Runners / Max King Photo: Bryon Powell / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Max King Born 1980 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road (legend) Max King is an American runner who has won world titles in mountain running and at 100 km on the road. Born on 24 February 1980, he graduated from Cornell University in 2002. He won the World Mountain Running Championships in Tirana, Albania, in 2011. Three years later he became IAU 100 km world champion in Doha. His mountain title came in 52:06, 35 seconds clear of Turkey's Ahmet Arslan, with Italy's Martin Dematteis third. Doha in November 2014 was his first attempt at 100 km on the road. He sat in the chase pack while the early leaders ran inside world-record pace. He broke away at around 45 km and took the lead between 60 and 65 km. King won in 6:27:43, ahead of Sweden's Jonas Buud in 6:32:04 and Spain's Jose Antonio Requejo. His time took about two and a half minutes off Tom Johnson's North American record of 6:30:11 from 1995. The United States also won the men's team title. He has won national titles at distances from the half marathon to ultras, along with several national runner of the year awards. In 2016 he took bronze at the NACAC Cross Country Championships. He has set 20 fastest known times, including a 2020 record on the 44-mile Grand Loop in Olympic National Park.
