- [Athing Mu-Nikolayev: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/athing-mu-nikolayev): Runners / Athing Mu-Nikolayev Photo: Erik van Leeuwen, attribution: Erik van Leeuwen (bron: Wikipedia). / Wikimedia Commons Athing Mu-Nikolayev Runs Athing Mu-Nikolayev is an American middle-distance runner, born on 8 June 2002 in Trenton, New Jersey. The 800 metres is her event, though she has also run quick times at 400m, 600m and 1500m. She began competing at the age of six. As a teenager she raced for Trenton Track Club rather than her high school team, and she later ran collegiately for Texas A&M. Her first national mark came early. On 24 February 2019, aged 16, she ran 1:23.57 for 600m indoors at the US championships. That took two hundredths off Alysia Montaño's American record and came close to the world record of 1:23.44. In 2021 she ran an indoor 800m of 1:58.40, a world under-20 record. In April she clocked 1:57.73 outdoors in Waco, Texas, a collegiate record. At the NCAA Championships in Eugene that June she won the 400m in a collegiate record of 49.57. Later the same day she anchored the Texas A&M 4x400m team to another collegiate record, 3:22.34. She won the US Olympic trials in 1:56.07. In the Tokyo 800m final she led from the gun and won in 1:55.21, an American record, with Keely Hodgkinson second and Raevyn Rogers third. She was 19. No American woman had won the Olympic 800m since Madeline Manning in 1968. She added a second gold in the 4x400m relay. At the Prefontaine Classic she cut her national record to 1:55.04, running the final lap on her own. She won 35 of her 36 races that year and was named World Athletics Female Rising Star. At the 2022 World Championships in Eugene she held off Hodgkinson by 0.08 seconds to win in 1:56.30. She was the first American woman to take the world 800m crown. Nobody had completed the Olympic and world double in an individual event at an earlier age. In 2023 she started working with coach Bobby Kersee. She was second over 1500m at the US championships. In August she took 800m bronze at the World Championships in Budapest behind Mary Moraa and Hodgkinson, having raced the distance only once before that season. In September she won the Diamond League final at the Prefontaine Classic in 1:54.97, another American record, beating both. She then largely stepped away from racing and has since spoken about the mental strain that came with her success. Her return, at the 2024 US Olympic trials in Eugene after nine months out, ended with a fall in the final. She finished ninth and last, and missed the Paris Games, where Hodgkinson took the title. A month later she was fifth in 2:00.29 at the Holloway Pro Classic in Gainesville, Florida. She last raced in August 2025, at the national championships in Eugene. A season's best of 1:59.79 left her fourth in her semi-final, and she did not make the final. Kersee confirmed in December 2025 that the pair had parted ways, and she has moved to Dallas. She married the former Russian middle-distance runner Yegor Nikolayev in March 2025. She appeared in a Nike campaign in April but has not raced this season. On 15 October 2026 the couple announced they are expecting their first child. - [Yiannis Kouros: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/yiannis-kouros): Runners / Yiannis Kouros Photo: Damjan Končar / IAU 🇬🇷 Yiannis Kouros Born 1956 Country 🇬🇷 Greece Runs Road, Track (legend) Yiannis Kouros is a Greek ultramarathon runner born on 13 February 1956 in Tripoli, Greece. He ran his first marathon in 1977, aged 21, in 2 hours 43 minutes and 15 seconds. His times improved steadily and he won the Athens Marathon in 1981. By 1983 he had run 25 marathons, before turning to ultra-distance racing. Kouros ran his first ultra-distance race, the 251km Spartathlon from Athens to Sparta, on 30 September 1983. Organisers expected the winner to take about 27 hours, but he won in 21 hours, 53 minutes and 42 seconds among 45 starters. He returned in 1984 and cut his time to 20 hours 25 minutes, a course record that stood for almost 40 years until Fotios Zisimopoulos beat it in 2023. In 1985 Kouros won the Sydney to Melbourne Ultramarathon, covering the 1,011km course in 5 days, 5 hours and 7 minutes to break the record held by Cliff Young. He won the race four more times, his fastest coming in 1989 in 5 days and 2 hours. Over his career Kouros set world records at distances from 100 miles to 1,000 miles. These included 303.5km for 24 hours, 473.5km for 48 hours and 1,036.8km over six days. Kouros emigrated to Australia in 1990 after a dispute with his employer in Greece, and became an Australian citizen in 1994. In 2019 the Australian Ultra Runners Association added him to its Hall of Fame. He retired from ultrarunning competition in 2014, at the age of 58. Away from racing, Kouros has written poetry, composed music and played Pheidippides in the 1991 film The Story of the Marathon: A Hero's Journey. - [Honoka Akiyama: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/honoka-akiyama): Runners / Honoka Akiyama Photo: World Trail Majors 🇯🇵 Honoka Akiyama Country 🇯🇵 Japan Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 793 (9 November 2026) Honoka Akiyama is a Japanese trail runner who races for Hoka and holds a UTMB index of 793. Her results stretch back to 2017 and cover dozens of trail races across Japan and abroad. Her most consistent result has come at Japan's IZU Trail Journey, which she has won three times, in 2020, 2022 and 2025. She was runner-up there in both 2021 and 2024. Akiyama has represented Japan at the Trail World Championships and its successor events several times. She finished 40th at the 2019 Trail World Championships in Portugal. She was 14th over the long course at the 2022 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Chiang Mai, and 9th at the 2023 edition in Innsbruck-Stubai. In 2025 she placed 12th in the 82km long trail race at that year's championships. In 2024 Akiyama took second at the Desafio Urbión, the ultra race at that year's ISF Skyrunning World Championships. Her form continued into 2026, when she finished third at the Tarawera Ultra-Trail T102 in 09:00:24, then 11th at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in 16:57:41. She was 7th over 107 km at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC in 12:37:02 that same year. Akiyama built her reputation with a string of wins on the Japanese trail circuit from 2018 onward. That year she won the Spa Trail Shima to Kusatsu, the Skyline Trail Sugadaira 50K Sky Marathon and the OSJ Amani Jungle Trail 50K. She also finished third at the Ultra-Trail Mt. Fuji STY that year. In 2019 she added wins at the Osj Shinshiro Trail 32km and the Senba Coastal Cliff Trail Running Race. - [Mo Farah: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mo-farah): Runners / Mo Farah Photo: Katie Chan / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Mo Farah Born 1983 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track, Road (legend) Sir Mo Farah is a British former long-distance runner, born Hussein Abdi Kahin in Somalia on 23 March 1983. Traffickers took him from Djibouti to London at the age of nine, using a different child's name, Mohamed Farah, and forcing him into domestic labour. He kept the name, became a British citizen in 2000, and did not reveal he had been trafficked until 2022. Farah has won more global championship gold medals than any other male track distance runner: four Olympic titles and six World titles. He won the 5,000m and 10,000m double at both the 2012 London and 2016 Rio Olympics, becoming only the second athlete after Finland's Lasse Viren to retain both titles. He completed the same double at the 2013 and 2015 World Championships, a feat known as the quadruple-double. Between 2011 and 2017 Farah won ten successive global track finals, a run that ended when he finished second in the 2017 World Championship 5,000m, his final track race. At the 2012 Olympics he won 10,000m gold in 27 minutes 30.42 seconds, Britain's first Olympic title in the event, before adding the 5,000m in 13 minutes 41.66 seconds. He successfully defended both titles at the 2013 World Championships in Moscow. Farah set a European record for the 10,000m, with 26 minutes 46.57 seconds in Eugene in 2011, and for the 1500m, with 3 minutes 28.81 seconds in Monaco in 2013. In September 2020 he set the world record for the one-hour run, covering 21,330 metres in Brussels and breaking the mark Haile Gebrselassie had held since 2007. After his final track race in 2017 he moved to road racing, winning the 2018 Chicago Marathon in 2 hours 5 minutes and 11 seconds, a European record. Farah failed to qualify for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics in 2021, missing the qualifying time by 19 seconds. He retired from competition in September 2023, after running his final race at the Great North Run. He was appointed CBE in 2013, and the 2017 New Year Honours list made him a knight for his services to athletics. He won the BBC Sports Personality of the Year award in 2017, was named European Athlete of the Year three times, and received an honorary degree from the University of Oxford in 2025. - [Pete Kostelnick: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/pete-kostelnick): Runners / Pete Kostelnick Photo: Iowa State University Alumni Association 🇺🇸 Pete Kostelnick Born 1987 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road, Trail & Ultra (legend) Pete Kostelnick is an American ultrarunner best known for the fastest run across the United States. Born on 12 September 1987, he ran from San Francisco City Hall to New York City Hall in 2016, taking 42 days, 6 hours and 30 minutes. He has also won the Badwater 135 twice, setting a course record in 2016. Kostelnick grew up in Boone, Iowa, and earned a degree in international business and finance at Iowa State University in 2009. He ran track and cross country at high school but did not compete at college. He raced 5Ks, half marathons and marathons before finding his level in ultras on the road. In 2013 he became the first person to run the full 423-mile RAGBRAI route, Iowa's famous bike ride. He finished Badwater in 2014, won it in 2015 and won again in 2016. His 21:56:32 that year set a new men's course record. The race covers 135 miles, starting below sea level in Death Valley and finishing high on Mount Whitney. He has run 163.5 miles in 24 hours, which ranked him fifth among North Americans. His crossing of America began on 12 September 2016. Averaging around 72 miles a day, he beat the 1980 record of Frank Giannino Jr. by four days. He ran through snowstorms in Utah and 35 mph winds on the plains. A serious road accident also wrecked his support vehicle. To prove the run, he carried a satellite tracker and two GPS watches while his team gathered witness signatures. He returned to racing in 2017, running a 24-hour race and Badwater that summer. - [Marshall Ulrich: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/marshall-ulrich): Runners / Marshall Ulrich Photo: Colorado Running Hall of Fame 🇺🇸 Marshall Ulrich Born 1951 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road (legend) Marshall Ulrich is an American ultrarunner, mountaineer and adventure racer, born on 4 July 1951. He is best known for Badwater, the race across Death Valley in high summer. He won the original 146-mile race to the summit of Mount Whitney four times. His 1991 time of 33 hours 54 minutes remains the record for that course. Ulrich has gone back to Death Valley again and again. In 1996 he became the first finisher of the Death Valley Cup, which pairs Badwater with the Furnace Creek 508 bike race. In July 1999 he made the first crossing to Whitney's summit with no crew and no resupply. He pushed a cart loaded with 225 lb of gear and water and reached the top in 77 hours 46 minutes. In 2001 he completed the first Badwater Quad, four straight crossings, in ten days. In autumn 2008, aged 57, he ran across America from San Francisco to New York. The 3,063.2-mile journey took 52.5 days. It brought Masters and Grand Masters records and ranks as the third-fastest run across the country. The run was filmed for the 2010 documentary Running America. He told the story in his 2011 memoir, Running on Empty. His range goes well beyond Death Valley. He has finished more than 120 ultramarathons averaging over 100 miles each. He climbed the Seven Summits, Everest included, each at the first attempt. In 1989 he became the first runner to finish all six 100-mile trail races in a single year, with top-ten places in five. He has also raced in every edition of the Eco-Challenge adventure race. In 2012 he and Dave Heckman made the first trek around the whole of Death Valley National Park, about 425 miles in 16.5 days. He has raised more than $850,000 for charity and joined the Colorado Running Hall of Fame in 2013. A second book, Both Feet on the Ground, followed his memoir. - [Hobbs Kessler: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hobbs-kessler): Runners / Hobbs Kessler Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Hobbs Kessler Born 2003 (age 22 or 23) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Track Hobbs Kessler, born 15 March 2003, is an American middle-distance runner who competes for Adidas. He has held the world record for the short track 2000 metres since January 2026, and turned professional straight out of high school. Kessler comes from a running family. His father Michael raced collegiately at Eastern Michigan University, and his mother Serena ran the marathon at the 2012 US Olympic Trials. He was also a national-level rock climber as a youth, representing the United States at the 2019 IFSC Climbing Youth World Championships in Italy. Kessler ran for Skyline High School in Ann Arbor, since his own school, Community High, had no competitive sports team. His father coached the school's team but stepped back from coaching him directly, arranging for University of Michigan coach Ron Warhurst to plan most of his training instead. In February 2021 Kessler broke the US high school indoor mile record with 3:57.66. That May he ran 3:34.36 for 1500 metres at the Portland Track Festival, faster than the NCAA record at the time and a new North American under-20 mark. He was named the Gatorade National Athlete of the Year in track and field for 2021. Kessler turned professional the day before the 2021 US Olympic Trials, signing with Adidas and giving up his place at Northern Arizona University. He trains under Warhurst in Ann Arbor with the Very Nice Track Club, alongside professional runners including Bryce Hoppel, Nick Willis and Mason Ferlic. In October 2023 he broke the road mile world record, clocking 3:56.13 at the World Road Running Championships in Riga. At the 2024 World Indoor Championships Kessler won bronze in the 1500 metres. Emmanuel Wanyonyi broke his road mile record that April, running 3:54.56 in Germany while Kessler finished second in 3:56.18. He qualified for the Paris Olympics in two events at the US trials, taking third in the 1500 metres in a personal best 3:31.53. He was also second in the 800 metres, in 1:43.64. In Paris he finished fifth in the 1500 metre final, in 3:29.45. Training partners Yared Nuguse and Cole Hocker took third and first, the first time in 112 years that two Americans had shared the men's 1500m podium. Kessler was runner-up to Yared Nuguse in the 2025 Wanamaker Mile, running 3:46.90 as Nuguse set a world indoor record of 3:46.63. On 24 January 2026 he outkicked Grant Fisher to break Kenenisa Bekele's short track 2000 metres world record, clocking 4:48.79. That September he finished third in the 1500 metres at the inaugural World Ultimate Championship in Budapest, behind Josh Kerr and Cameron Myers. He won the PizTri Vertikal race in August 2024, was 2nd at the Montee du Nid d'Aigle and the Grossglockner Mountain Run, and 4th at the Trofeo Nasego and the Val Bregaglia Trail. Kiprotich was 8th in the men's Up and Down category at the World Mountain Running Championships in 2023. In 2025 he raced the Vauban Mountain Trail in France, finishing 2nd in the vertical race and 7th in the main event. - [Courtney Olsen: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/courtney-olsen): Runners / Courtney Olsen Photo: photographer unknown 🇺🇸 Courtney Olsen Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road UTMB Index 778 (28 September 2026) Courtney Olsen is an American road ultrarunner. In September 2026, at 39, she won her first world title, taking the IAU 100k World Championships in Ames, Spain, in 7:10:31. Japan's Miho Nakata finished second, 1 minute and 26 seconds back, with Spain's Gemma Arenas third. Olsen ran a patient race. She sat sixth at halfway, on a course of a 4.8km opening loop followed by nineteen 5km laps through the town, in temperatures that climbed from 16C to 32C. She moved into second by lap 14 before taking the lead for good on lap 17. She also collected the World Masters Athletics 100k title contested within the same race. She holds the American record over 100km, 6:59:55, set winning the 2025 Tunnel Hill 100 Mile event's 100km race in Illinois. She is a former world record holder over 50 miles. Before her win in Spain she had been tenth at the 2024 IAU 100k World Championships and seventh at the 2026 Comrades Marathon in South Africa. - [Letesenbet Gidey: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/letesenbet-gidey): Runners / Letesenbet Gidey Photo: Erik van Leeuwen / Wikimedia Commons 🇪🇹 Letesenbet Gidey Born 1998 (age 27 or 28) Country 🇪🇹 Ethiopia Runs Track, Road Letesenbet Gidey was born on 20 March 1998 in Ethiopia, where she races long distances on the track and roads. She is the only athlete, male or female, to have held the 5000m, 10,000m and half marathon world records at the same time. At 17, in 2015, she won the World Cross Country Championships junior race, then defended the title in 2017. She took bronze in the senior race at the same championships in 2019. Gidey won 10,000m silver at the 2019 World Championships in Doha, in a personal best of 30:21.23. That November she set a 15km world record of 44:20 at the Zevenheuvelenloop in the Netherlands, the first woman under 45 minutes for the distance. In October 2020 she broke Tirunesh Dibaba's 5000m world record with 14:06.62, a mark later broken by Faith Kipyegon in 2023. In June 2021 she broke Sifan Hassan's two-day-old 10,000m world record, running 29:01.03, a time since broken by Beatrice Chebet. She took bronze in the 10,000m at the Tokyo Olympics that August. On her half marathon debut in Valencia that October she ran 1:02:52, becoming the first woman under 64 minutes and then under 63. It improved the world record by 70 seconds, the biggest jump in the event since 1978. In July 2022 she won her first global title, taking 10,000m gold at the World Championships in Eugene in 30:09.94. That December she finished second in her marathon debut at the Valencia Marathon, in 2:16:49, one of the fastest marathon debuts in history. She won 10,000m silver at the 2023 World Championships, and was second at the New York City Marathon that November. Her half marathon world record of 1:02:52 still stood as of September 2026. - [Steve Cram: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/steve-cram): Runners / Steve Cram Photo: Adambro / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Steve Cram Born 1960 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track (legend) Steve Cram was a British middle-distance runner known as "The Jarrow Arrow", after his home town. He won 1500 metres gold at the 1983 World Championships in Helsinki and silver at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics behind fellow Briton Sebastian Coe. In the summer of 1985, Cram set three world records in 19 days, over 1500 metres, the mile and 2000 metres. His 1500 metres time of 3:29.67 in Nice made him the first man to run the distance inside 3 minutes 30 seconds. His mile record of 3:46.32, run in Oslo, stood as the European record until 2023. At the 1986 Commonwealth Games in Edinburgh he won both the 800 metres and the 1500 metres. He added 1500 metres gold at the European Championships in Stuttgart that year, beating Coe, in what proved to be his last major title. Injuries limited him through his later career, including a calf injury that hampered his 1988 Seoul Olympics campaign, where he finished fourth in the 1500 metres. He retired from athletics in 1994 and still holds the UK record over 2000 metres. Cram went on to work as a television athletics commentator and co-founded the children's charity COCO in 2000. - [Andreu Blanes-Reig: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/andreu-blanes-reig): Runners / Andreu Blanes-Reig Photo: Golden Trail World Series / Sierre-Zinal / Jordi Saragossa 🇪🇸 Andreu Blanes-Reig Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 919 (9 November 2026) Andreu Blanes-Reig is a Spanish mountain runner and orienteer with a UTMB index of 920, one of the highest in this batch. He was awarded victory at Sierre-Zinal in 2022 after crossing the line second in 2:29:19, behind Kenya's Mark Kangogo. Kangogo was disqualified two months later after the Athletics Integrity Unit brought doping proceedings against him. He accepted the sanction and waived his right of appeal, and Sierre-Zinal declared Blanes-Reig the winner. His time ahead of Patrick Kipngeno and Kilian Jornet, who finished fourth, stood as the official result. He returned to Sierre-Zinal in 2025 and finished eighth, having placed third in the short trail race at that year's World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. He also won the Kodiak Ultra Marathons by UTMB 50K in 2025 and was runner-up at the Zegama-Aizkorri Marathon. He remains active in 2026, finishing 19th at Sierre-Zinal and 21st at the OCC race during UTMB Mont-Blanc week. - [Khairi Bejiga: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/khairi-bejiga): Runners / Khairi Bejiga Photo: Brasov Running Festival Khairi Bejiga Runs Khairi Bejiga is an Ethiopian long-distance runner, born on 27 April 2006. He races 5000m on the track and 10km on the road. In 2025 he set an Ethiopian under-20 best for 10km. His track record has improved steadily. He was 11th over 5000m at the Doha Diamond League on 16 May 2025. On 31 May he finished second at the Meeting Nikaia in Nice. He clocked 13:06.95 behind Eritrea's Saymon Amanuel and beat Niels Laros. He went quicker in June at the Paavo Nurmi Games in Turku with 13:06.53. In May 2026 he was sixth at the Xiamen Diamond League in 13:06.45. At Athletissima in Lausanne on 21 August 2026 he finished ninth in 13:03.27, his fastest so far. The roads have brought his biggest wins. His first 10km road race was the tRUNsylvania 10km in Brasov, Romania, in October 2025, and he won it in 26:54. That equalled the fastest debut at the distance, the 26:54 set by Sabastian Sawe in 2022. It also put him second on the all-time under-20 list, three seconds short of the course record. On 11 January 2026 he was second over 10km in Valencia in 26:52, behind Andreas Almgren. On Sunday 4 October 2026 he returned to Brasov and won again. Nobody else has won the event, a World Athletics Elite Label race now held six times, in successive years. He ran 27:01, one second ahead of his training partner Nibret Kinde, the reigning Ethiopian 10,000m champion. A group of 12 reached halfway in 13:32 before Bejiga ran the sixth and seventh kilometres in 2:42 and 2:40. Kinde held on until the final 200m. Ethiopian runners filled all six podium places across the men's and women's races. Bejiga collected the $5,000 first prize but was not entirely pleased. He had wanted the 26:51 course record and felt the early pace was slow because "nobody wanted to go faster". His next race is the Valencia Half Marathon on 25 October. He has run the distance once before, finishing in 1:02:04. - [Yaseen Abdalla: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/yaseen-abdalla): Runners / Yaseen Abdalla Photo: Soriak1144 / Wikimedia Commons Yaseen Abdalla Runs Yaseen Abdalla is a long-distance runner who races internationally for Sudan. He was born in Austin, Texas, on 13 August 2001 and still lives and trains in the United States. He holds Sudanese records over the indoor mile, 3000m, 5000m, half marathon and marathon. He came to the sport late, taking it up in his second year at Lyndon B. Johnson High School in Austin. By his final year he was third at the Texas state cross country meet. His college running took in three universities. He joined Texas as a walk-on in 2019 and ran the anchor leg for the Longhorns' distance medley relay team that won the 2022 NCAA indoor title in 9:25.20. Earlier that winter he took the Big 12 indoor 5000m in a school record of 13:33.26. At Tennessee he ran 7:42.23 for 3000m indoors in 2023, a school and Sudanese record. After moving to Arkansas in July 2024 he was fourth at the NCAA Cross Country Championships, covering 10km in 28:41.5. In Boston on 7 December 2024 he set Arkansas indoor records of 7:34.17 for 3000m and 13:22.29 for 5000m. He cut the 5000m mark to 13:09.99 there on 14 February 2025. His first global championship came at the 2022 World Championships in Eugene, where he was 38th over 5000m. Sudan picked him for the Paris Olympic marathon in 2024 although he had never recorded an official marathon. He finished 33rd in 2:11:41, a national record at the first attempt. At the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo he was 21st in the marathon in 2:13:32. Abdalla made his half marathon debut in Valencia on 25 October 2026 and finished eighth in 59:12. Guor Maker had held the national best for Sudan since 2013 with 1:04:21. Abdalla beat it by more than five minutes. The time was also five seconds inside Conner Mantz's American record of 59:17. It will not be ratified as one. Under USATF rules, only an athlete free to compete for the United States at every international event can hold a national record, and his Olympic and World Championship appearances for Sudan rule him out. Mantz keeps the record. Abdalla has nonetheless described himself on social media as the fastest American ever over the distance. - [Ethan Strand: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ethan-strand): Runners / Ethan Strand Photo: Quejaytee / Wikimedia Commons Ethan Strand Runs Ethan Strand is an American middle-distance runner from Alabama. He went to Vestavia Hills High School near Birmingham and was twice named the state's Gatorade Cross Country Player of the Year. He specialises in the 1500m, the mile and the 3000m. He made his name racing for the University of North Carolina. In November 2024 he took eighth place at the NCAA cross country finals, held that year in Madison, in 28:53.0. His teammate Parker Wolfe was one place ahead. His college indoor record is the standout. In Boston on 7 December 2024 he ran 7:30.15 for the short track 3000m. That took more than six seconds off Drew Bosley's collegiate record of 7:36.42. Wolfe was 0.08 behind after Strand passed him in the home straight. Back in Boston on 1 February 2025 he ran the mile in 3:48.32. That beat Cooper Teare's collegiate record of 3:50.39 and made him the seventh fastest indoor miler in history. He came past Robert Farken in the closing stages and covered the last 200m in 27.10 seconds. In March 2025 he won the NCAA indoor 3000m title in 7:52.03. The step up to the senior ranks came quickly. In June 2024 he reached the 1500m final at the US Olympic Trials, one of five collegians to do so. On 5 July 2025 he won the International Mile at the Prefontaine Classic in 3:48.86. He signed with Nike later that month. On 2 August 2025 he crossed the line second in the 1500m final at the US Championships in a personal best of 3:30.25. He was later promoted to first place and is now listed as the national champion. He was 16th over 1500m at the World Championships in Tokyo. At 24, Strand now holds a mile best of 3:46.97, also set at the Prefontaine Classic. In August 2026 he won the Diamond League 1500m in Silesia. On 12 December he lines up in Honolulu for the Kalakaua Merrie Mile, which is being staged for the tenth time. The certified course follows Kalakaua Avenue with Waikiki Beach alongside. He heads a men's field that includes Oliver Hoare and Nico Young. He has never run the race before, although Oahu was his training base before the 2025 World Championships. The chase format sends the women off first with a head start. The men's course record is 3:53.3, set by Edward Cheserek in 2019. Strand sees the race as a way to "get my season rolling". - [Michal Rada: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/michal-rada): Runners / Michal Rada MR Film My Run Michal Rada Runs Michal Rada is a Czech 400m hurdler, born on 25 May 2007. He runs for České Budějovice Sokol and is coached by Jiří Couf. His early results came across several events. At the 2022 Czech Student Championships in Prague he took gold in the long jump and silver in the 60m hurdles. He has since lowered his 60m hurdles best indoors in Prague, to 7.78 in January 2024 and then 7.74 a year later. The longer hurdles soon became his event. In June 2024 he ran 49.89 for the flat 400m at the Josef Odložil Memorial, a Czech junior record. A month later he won the European U18 400m hurdles title in Banská Bystrica, Slovakia, with a European under-18 best. In August he went to the World U20 Championships in Lima, Peru. He reached the final with 49.36, which was a world U20 lead, a personal best and a Czech U20 record. In the final he improved the national record to 49.30 and took silver. His 2025 season brought senior-sounding times at junior level. At the European U20 Championships in Tampere in July he won the 400m hurdles in 48.78, a championship record. He then ran the anchor leg as the Czech 4x400m relay team also took gold. He was shortlisted for the European Athletics Rising Star award in both 2024 and 2025. The title that had escaped him in Lima came in August 2026. At the World U20 Championships in Eugene he took 400m hurdles gold, stopping the clock at 48.59. That set a European under-20 record, removing the 48.74 Vladimir Budko had held since 1983. The European Athletics awards were handed out in Lausanne on 24 October, and Rada was voted men's Rising Star for 2026. Samuel James of Great Britain, who holds the European U18 high jump title, was also on the shortlist. Bulgarian triple jumper Viktoria Angelova received the women's award. Rada is 19. - [Krissy Moehl: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/krissy-moehl): Runners / Krissy Moehl Photo: Henry Iddon / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Krissy Moehl Born 1977 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Krissy Moehl is an American trail ultrarunner, coach and race director from Bow, Washington. Born in 1977, she won UTMB in both 2003 and 2009. In 2005 she was the youngest woman ever to finish the Grand Slam of Ultrarunning. She set the women's record at the Hardrock 100 in 2007. Moehl ran track in high school and raced 800 metres for the University of Washington. While working at a Seattle running shop alongside Scott Jurek, she was talked into the Chuckanut 50k in 2000. It was her first ultra, at 22. She won Chuckanut twice and became its co-race director in 2003, aged 24. She was still directing it more than 15 years later. Her first UTMB in 2003 was the race's first edition, cut to about 150 km by bad weather. She won in 29:28:24. A run of American wins followed, at Wasatch in 2004 and Vermont in 2005 among others. Her 2005 Grand Slam also brought fourth at Western States and second at Leadville. At Hardrock in 2007 she won in a women's record of 29:24:45. She returned to Chamonix in 2009, a few months after placing second at Western States. Lizzy Hawker was the favourite, and Moehl let her go early. At Champex-Lac, about 110 km in, her crew told her Hawker was close by. She took the lead, ran the last 50 km in just over seven hours and won in 24:56:01, a women's record. Later wins include the San Diego 100 in 2011, the Ultra-Trail Mt. Fuji in 2013 and the 160 km Mt. Gaoligong Ultra in China in 2018. She holds the women's fastest known time for the 170-mile Tahoe Rim Trail, 47 hours 27 minutes. In 2015 she published Running Your First Ultra, a guide to the distance. - [Ciara Mageean: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ciara-mageean): Runners / Ciara Mageean Photo: Sandro Halank, Wikimedia Commons / Wikimedia Commons Ciara Mageean Runs Ciara Mageean came from Portaferry, County Down, and made her name on the track as a middle-distance athlete. The 1500 metres was her event, though she also held national records from 800 metres to the mile. She first ran senior international races for Northern Ireland and later wore the Irish vest at two Olympic Games. Jerry Kiernan coached her through serious ankle injuries early on. She moved to Manchester in 2017 to train with the New Balance group, the same year she graduated in physiotherapy from University College Dublin. She died on 1 November 2026, aged 34. Her talent showed early. She took silver over 800m at the 2009 World Youth Championships, then 1500m silvers at the 2010 World Juniors and the 2011 European Juniors. At 18 she was tenth in the 1500m at the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi. Her first senior medal came at the 2016 European Championships, a bronze, and she reached the semi-finals in Rio that summer. In Glasgow on 3 March 2019 she won European indoor bronze. That October she finished tenth in the World Championships final in Doha in 4:00.15. In Bern on 24 July 2020 she became the first Irish woman to run under two minutes for 800m. The best years came in her thirties. In August 2022 she won silver at both the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham and the European Championships in Munich, each time behind Laura Muir. On 2 September that year she beat Muir to win the Memorial Van Damme in Brussels, her first Diamond League victory. Her 3:56.63 took her under four minutes for the first time and removed Sonia O'Sullivan's Irish record from 1995. In 2023 she ran 4:14.58 for the mile in Monaco, second only to Faith Kipyegon. She was fourth in the world final in Budapest and lowered her 1500m record to 3:55.87 in Brussels. Two days before Christmas she ran 15:13 at Victoria Park in Belfast, the fastest women's parkrun on record. On 9 June 2024 she won the European 1500m title in Rome in 4:04.66. It made her the first Irish athlete since O'Sullivan to win an individual European crown. An Achilles injury then forced her out of the Paris Olympics a day before her first heat. She will be remembered for that complete set of European medals and for four Irish records, among them 1:58.51 for 800m and 2:31.06 for 1000m. She was the national Athlete of the Year in 2022 and BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year in 2023. In July 2025 she announced that she had cancer. It was stage four bowel cancer, and it ended a career she had hoped to finish at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Even so, she put on a public run under her own name at the national championships. Her memoir, My Greatest Race, was a collaboration with Clíona Foley, a journalist. She married Thomas Moran at Belfast City Hall in October 2026, about three weeks before she died. She is survived by her husband and by her parents, Christopher and Catherine. Athletics Ireland called her "much-loved and inspirational". Northern Ireland's first minister, Michelle O'Neill, said Portaferry would feel her absence deeply, since the town had always thought of her as belonging to it. - [Ella Fryer: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ella-fryer): Runners / Ella Fryer EF 🇬🇧 UTMB Index 528 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Ella Fryer Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 528 (9 November 2026) Ella Fryer is a British runner whose recorded results so far come from long trail races. Her general UTMB Index stands at 528, drawn from two finishes at 50 and 100 kilometres. Her first listed result is from Race To The Stones in 2024. She covered the 100 km course, which carries 1,341 m of climb, in 11:58:25. That put her 20th woman. She returned to the results in 2026 at the Chiltern Ridge Classic 50K. The route is 50 km with 996 m of ascent. Fryer finished fourth woman in 5:14:52, the highest placing on her record to date. A runner named Ella Fryer is also one of four young women chosen by the coach Geoff Wightman for a new training group. The available records do not confirm whether this is the same athlete. Wightman, a former marathon runner, coached his son Jake to the world 1500m title in Eugene in 2022. He found the group through an appeal on Instagram that drew around 60 replies. He then drew up a shortlist, held interviews and made four offers. Fryer was picked alongside Pippa Roessler, Lucy Austin and Annie Testar. Three of the four are 22 and one is 24. None has yet reached the standard that would earn support from the National Lottery. Wightman picked them for what they might become, and because runners in their early twenties tend to take well to an unfamiliar training approach. Most of the group fit their running around jobs, and they meet to train on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Their first meeting was filmed for YouTube. - [Hawi Feysa: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hawi-feysa): Runners / Hawi Feysa Photo: Photoguy1212 / Wikimedia Commons Hawi Feysa Runs Hawi Feysa is an Ethiopian distance runner who has moved from the track and cross country to become one of the fastest marathoners in the world. Born on 1 February 1999, she comes from Ambo in the Oromia region and grew up on a farm there. She started running young on a local loop, with Tirunesh Dibaba among her idols. At 16 she moved to Addis Ababa to join a club. She still lives and trains in the capital, in a group coached by Gemedu Dedefo that also includes Tigst Assefa and Tigist Ketema. Her early results came off-road and on the track. Her first global medal was silver among the under-20 women at the 2017 world cross country championships, then staged by the IAAF. Two years later she won 5000m silver at the African Games in Rabat, Morocco, and finished eighth over the same distance at the 2019 World Championships. Her 5000m best is 14:33.66, set in 2022. Repeated injuries on the track pushed her towards the roads. The switch paid off in 2024. At the Frankfurt Marathon she won in 2:17:25, a course record by 1:45. It made her the 19th quickest woman ever over the distance. Only 11 faster marks were set anywhere that year. In 2025 she finished third at the Tokyo Marathon in 2:17:00, a personal best. Her biggest run so far came in Chicago on Sunday 11 October 2026, where she returned as defending champion. She spent most of the race locked with Kenya's Sharon Lokedi, the two-time Boston winner. The two went through 30km together in 1:34:16 and were still trading the lead at 25 miles. Feysa broke clear only in the final mile and won in 2:13:33. Lokedi crossed the line 34 seconds later in 2:14:07. Brigid Kosgei took the last podium place with 2:14:55. Feysa's time was faster than the 2:14:04 Kosgei ran on the same course in 2019, which stood as the world record at the time. Feysa said she was confident of winning from 35km. She had previously named a sub-2:15 marathon as her next target. Chicago took care of that with more than a minute to spare. - [Takahiro Sunada: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/takahiro-sunada): Runners / Takahiro Sunada Photo: Runtrip 🇯🇵 Takahiro Sunada Born 1973 Country 🇯🇵 Japan Runs Road (legend) Takahiro Sunada is a Japanese road runner who held the men's 100 km world record for 20 years. Born in Osaka on 19 January 1973, he ran 6:13:33 at Lake Saroma in June 1998. Nao Kazami lowered the mark to 6:09:14 on the same course in 2018. Sunada joined Osaka Gas straight from Taisei High School. In 1992 he ran 2:15:30 at the Hofu Yomiuri Marathon, a Japanese under-20 best. After moving to Sekisui Chemical in 1995, he took second at the World Cup Marathon in Athens in 2:13:16. He placed tenth at Fukuoka that December in 2:12:01. The Saroma win began a strong spell over 100 km. He was third at the IAU 100 km World Championships in France in May 1999, in 6:26:06. In April 2000 he won the IAU 100 km European Championships at Belvès in 6:17:17. That September he set his marathon best, finishing fourth in Berlin in 2:10:07. He also ran the Comrades Marathon in 2002, placing 20th. Since leaving top-level racing he has stayed involved in the sport. He was an ambassador for the Wings for Life World Run when it first came to Japan, in 2015 and 2016. He travelled as a coach with Japan's team to the 2015 IAU 100 km World Championships in Winschoten. A year later in Los Alcázares he led the squad, and the women won team gold while the men took silver. - [Dawit Seare: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/dawit-seare): Runners / Dawit Seare Photo: Gaelle Mobuchon / World Athletics 🇪🇷 Dawit Seare Born 2004 (age 21 or 22) Country 🇪🇷 Eritrea Runs Track, Road Dawit Seare Berhanyukun is an Eritrean long-distance runner born on 29 December 2004. He competed in the 5000 metres at the 2024 Summer Olympics, qualifying for the final and finishing nineteenth in 13:31.50. He is the reigning African 5000m champion after winning gold at the 2026 African Championships in Accra, Ghana. It was only Eritrea's second gold at that championships, coming 14 years after Nguse Amlosom took the country's first in 2014. Seare first made his mark in 2023, finishing fourth in the 5km road race at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Riga, Latvia, in a national record of 13:21:03. That same month he claimed his maiden road-race victory, over 10 km in Berlin. At the delayed 2023 African Games in Accra in March 2024, he was sixth over 10,000 metres and ninth over 5000 metres. In March 2025 he placed tenth in the 3000 metres at the World Athletics Indoor Championships in Nanjing. The following month he won the Boston 5K in Massachusetts in 13:33, ahead of Amon Kemboi and Patrick Dever. Seare won the world 5km road title on 19 September 2026, beating Jakob Ingebrigtsen, the Olympic 5000m champion, in the final sprint through the streets of Copenhagen. The race counted as that year's World Athletics Road Running Championships. Seare stopped the clock at 12:56, an Eritrean record, with Ingebrigtsen three seconds back in 12:59, a Norwegian record. His teammate Saymon Amanuel, 19, took bronze in 13:00. Seare took the lead with about a kilometre to go, and Ingebrigtsen closed from more than 10 metres back before the Eritrean edged clear again in the final strides. Ingebrigtsen had raced sparingly that year because of injury, Copenhagen was just his sixth outing of the season. He had claimed European gold in August, and eight days before Copenhagen he had taken the 5000m title at the Ultimate Athletics Championships in Budapest. Three years earlier, Seare had taken fourth place over 5km when Riga hosted the inaugural World Road Running Championships. He said he had spent two months preparing for Copenhagen and that the closing kilometre against Ingebrigtsen had been hard. He also said he intends to relocate to the United States to continue racing. - [Kelly Holmes: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kelly-holmes): Runners / Kelly Holmes Photo: Russell Garner / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Kelly Holmes Born 1970 Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Track (legend) Dame Kelly Holmes is a retired British middle-distance runner who won gold in both the 800 metres and 1500 metres at the 2004 Athens Olympics. She was only the second British woman to take Olympic 800 metres gold, after Ann Packer in 1964, and the seventh British woman to win any Olympic athletics title. Born in Pembury, Kent, in 1970, she joined Tonbridge Athletics Club at 12 and won the English Schools 1500 metres in 1983. She then served in the British Army, qualifying as a physical training instructor, and did not become a full-time athlete until 1997. Her senior record before Athens was long, though injuries kept interrupting it. She won the 1994 Commonwealth 1500 metres title and took European silver the same year. A silver and a bronze followed at the 1995 World Championships in Gothenburg. She ran her first Olympics, in Atlanta in 1996, with a stress fracture and left without a medal. Her first Olympic medal came four years later, bronze in the 800 metres in Sydney. She added 1500 metres silver at the 1998 Commonwealth Games, then won that title again in 2002 and took 800 metres bronze at the European Championships in Munich. In 2003 she was second in the 1500 metres at the World Indoor Championships and second over 800 metres at the World Championships. Athens was her last major championship. She still holds British records over 600 metres and 1000 metres, and kept the 800 metres record until 2021. Holmes was appointed a Dame in 2005 and announced her retirement that December. She founded the Dame Kelly Holmes Trust in 2008 to support young athletes and young people facing disadvantage across the UK. In 2009 she became president of Commonwealth Games England. From 2018 until 1 November 2024 she was honorary colonel of the Royal Armoured Corps Training Regiment. These days she works as a motivational speaker and has written five books, the most recent being Running Life. She has been a regular panellist on Loose Women since September 2022 and speaks publicly on mental health and menopause. She remains a familiar face at parkrun, and was among the well-known names in a field of more than 29,000 at the Cardiff Half Marathon on Sunday 4 October. - [Holly Page: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/holly-page): Runners / Holly Page Photo: Holly Page 🇬🇧 Holly Page Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 717 (9 November 2026) Holly Page is a British mountain and sky runner from Yorkshire who now races for Adidas Terrex. She grew up watching her father compete in fell races and began racing herself as a junior, running for England from around age 10. After studying languages at Durham University she spent years travelling the world by bicycle and hitchhiking, often racing spontaneously along the way. Page's breakthrough season came in 2018, when she won the Skyrunner World Series Classic and took third overall in the Golden Trail World Series after winning its grand final in South Africa. That year she was also selected for the Great Britain team at the IAU Trail World Championships in Spain, finishing 9th over 85 kilometres in her first ultra distance race. She added a third place finish at the Skyrunning World Championships' Ring of Steall skyrace the same season. In 2019 she raced widely, winning the 91 kilometre El Cruce Columbia in Argentina and finishing second at the 50 kilometre Oman by UTMB. A serious fall on Mont Blanc in 2017 had torn ligaments in her knee, and further foot and ankle injuries in 2021 needed reconstructive surgery. She has said she still hopes to be racing into her sixties and seventies. - [Jonathan Albon: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jonathan-albon): Runners / Jonathan Albon 🇬🇧 Jonathan Albon Born 1989 (age 36 or 37) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 932 (9 November 2026) Jonathan Albon was born in Britain on 19 April 1989, and races as a sky runner and trail runner. He grew up in Great Dunmow, Essex, and now lives in Bergen, Norway, racing for The North Face Trail team. Albon made his name in skyrunning and obstacle course racing before turning to longer trails. He won the Sky Extreme series twice, in 2016 and 2017, and took the overall Skyrunner World Series title once. In obstacle racing he won six world titles between 2014 and 2019, and the Spartan World Championships in 2014 and 2018. He won the Trail World Championships in 2019. In 2021 he took the UTMB OCC title, and won the Mont Blanc Marathon the following year. He was runner-up in the CCC at UTMB in 2022, then won it outright in 2023. Albon won the Transvulcania Ultramarathon on La Palma in 2024, and finished sixth at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run that same year. He won the 100km race at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia in 2025, and was second at Transgrancanaria Classic that year. His 2026 season opened with wins at Molde 7 Peaks, the 50K at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia and Transgrancanaria Classic, where he moved up from second to first. - [Brigid Kosgei: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/brigid-kosgei): Runners / Brigid Kosgei Photo: Paul Hudson from United Kingdom / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Brigid Kosgei Born 1994 (age 31 or 32) Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Road Brigid Kosgei is a Kenyan marathon runner, born on 20 February 1994. She once held the women's marathon world record for a mixed-sex race, running 2:14:04 at the 2019 Chicago Marathon. She took Olympic silver in the marathon at the delayed 2020 Tokyo Games. She has won the Chicago Marathon twice, the London Marathon twice and the Tokyo Marathon twice. Kosgei grew up in Elgeyo-Marakwet County in Kenya. Her sister Pamela runs the steeplechase. She took up running at 17. Her marathon career started strongly, with a top-two finish in eight of her first nine races. Her 2:24:45 for second at the 2016 Lisbon Marathon was a personal best at the time and quicker than the existing course record. In 2017 she ran 2:20:22 for second in Chicago, then won the Honolulu Marathon weeks later, taking more than five minutes off the course record. Her first major marathon win came at Chicago in 2018. She pulled away from two Kenyans and three Ethiopians somewhere between 30 and 35 kilometres and finished in 2:18:35. The following year she won the London Marathon in 2:18:20, the youngest woman to take that title. At the 2019 Great North Run she ran 1:04:28, a course record and 23 seconds inside the half marathon world record of the day. She capped 2019 by taking the marathon world record at Chicago. Her 2:14:04 beat the old mark by 81 seconds and left her more than six minutes clear of second place. She wore an adapted Nike shoe, later alleged to have been worth 60 to 90 seconds. Kosgei won a rescheduled London Marathon in 2020 in 2:18:58, having gone clear at 18 miles and finished more than three minutes ahead. She led Kenya's marathon squad into the delayed Tokyo Olympics and took silver in 2:27:36, 16 seconds behind compatriot Peres Jepchirchir. She won the postponed 2021 Tokyo Marathon in March 2022 in 2:16:20, then the third fastest time in history. She set a course record of 2:19:15 at the 2024 Abu Dhabi Marathon and won Tokyo again in 2026. In April 2026 World Athletics refused an application for her to switch nationality to Turkey. It said the move formed part of a coordinated drive to recruit athletes from overseas, which did not fit its transfer of allegiance rules. She returned to the Great North Run on 13 September 2026, at 32, and led from the start on the route from Newcastle over the Tyne Bridge to South Shields. She ran much of the race alone and won in 1:06:15, more than two minutes ahead of defending champion Sheila Chepkirui in 1:08:19. A month later, on 11 October, she was back in Chicago and finished third in 2:14:55. Hawi Feysa won in 2:13:33, quicker than Kosgei's 2019 world record time on the same course, with Sharon Lokedi second in 2:14:07. - [Guye Adola: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/guye-adola): Runners / Guye Adola Photo: Guillaume Baviere from Copenhagen, Denmark / Wikimedia Commons Guye Adola Runs Guye Adola is an Ethiopian road runner who made his name over the half marathon before stepping up to the full distance. He was born on 20 October 1990 in Adola, in the Oromiya Region of Ethiopia. He trained with the group run by Gianni Demadonna and first came to wider notice in 2014. That year was a busy one. His first race at a high level was the Marrakech Half Marathon in January, which he won in 61:26. Fourth place at the Ethiopian half marathon championships came next. On his international debut, at the 2014 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships, he was the best of the Ethiopians. He took individual bronze in a personal best of 59:21 and led his team to third. He was then third at the Giro Media Blenio in Switzerland and at the Luanda Half Marathon in Angola. He also won the Delhi Half Marathon in New Delhi in 59:06, a further best. Six years later he lined up at the 2020 World Athletics Half Marathon Championships in Gdynia, Poland. His marathon debut came in Berlin in 2017. He took on Eliud Kipchoge and finished second in 2:03:46. At the time no one had run faster on a first attempt at the distance. He returned to the German capital in 2021 and won the men's race. In 2026 he added two more big wins. He took the Rotterdam Marathon in 2:03:54. Then on Sunday 27 September he won the 52nd Berlin Marathon in 2:02:50, a personal best and his second title there. One other set of results gave his time as 2:02:51. The race had lost its defending champion, Sabastian Sawe, to a shin stress fracture in August, and Kenenisa Bekele withdrew three days before the start with a left Achilles injury. Gabriel Geay of Tanzania came in fastest on paper and led for much of the first half. The leaders reached halfway in 61:01, and seven men were still together at 30km, which Adola passed in 1:26:57. By then the pace had drifted outside record territory. Adola broke away soon afterwards. He ran through the Brandenburg Gate 29 seconds clear of Gemechu Dida Diriba, who cut more than three minutes from his best with 2:03:19. Geay held on for third in 2:03:59. Ethiopia won both races on the day, with Tigst Assefa taking the women's title in a course record of 2:11:04. The Berlin win is the latest result on Adola's record, and it leaves him as the most recent men's champion on one of the quickest courses in the sport. - [Kenenisa Bekele: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kenenisa-bekele): Runners / Kenenisa Bekele Photo: Ian Robertson / Wikimedia Commons Kenenisa Bekele Runs Kenenisa Bekele is an Ethiopian distance runner, born on 13 June 1982 in Bekoji, in the Arsi Zone of Oromia. The same highland town produced the Dibaba sisters and their cousin Derartu Tulu. He has raced across cross country, track and road at the highest level. From 2004 until 2020 he held the world records at both 5,000m and 10,000m. Plenty of people in the sport rate him the finest distance runner there has been. Cross country made his name first. He won the junior world title in 2001. Then, from 2002 to 2006, he took both the 4km short course and the 12km long course races at the World Cross Country Championships every year, something nobody else managed even once. A sixth long course title followed in Edinburgh in 2008. That left him with 11 senior individual golds, the best record in the championships' history. His run of 27 straight cross country wins ended in the heat of Mombasa in 2007, when he dropped out on the last lap. On the track he won Olympic 10,000m gold in Athens in 2004 in 27:05.10, with silver in the 5,000m. In Beijing in 2008 he defended the 10,000m in an Olympic record of 27:01.17. Six days later he led most of the 5,000m and closed with a 53.87 last lap to win in 12:57.82, almost eight seconds inside Saïd Aouita's Olympic record. He won world 10,000m titles in 2003, 2005, 2007 and 2009, and went unbeaten at the distance from 2003 until 2011. In Berlin in 2009 he became the first man to win both long track titles at one World Championships, running 26:46.31 and 13:17.09. His 10,000m world record of 26:17.53 came in Brussels on 26 August 2005. The marathon came later. He won on debut in Paris in April 2014 in a course record of 2:05:04. Berlin brought wins in 2016 in 2:03:03 and in 2019 in 2:01:41, two seconds outside Eliud Kipchoge's then world record of 2:01:39. At the 2024 London Marathon he ran 2:04:15, a masters world record for over-40s. His last completed marathon was the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he finished 39th in 2:12:24. Since then his racing has been sparse. He dropped out in Valencia later in 2024 and in New York in November 2025, and withdrew from London in 2025 before race day. In April 2024 he told Olympics.com that injuries had troubled him over a long spell. Berlin organisers named him as a late entry for the 2026 race, then confirmed on 24 September that he had withdrawn with a left Achilles injury picked up in one of his final sessions. The Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 will fall after his 46th birthday. - [Sheila Chepkirui: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sheila-chepkirui): Runners / Sheila Chepkirui Photo: Katie Chan / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Sheila Chepkirui Born 1990 (age 35 or 36) Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Track, Road Sheila Chepkirui is a Kenyan middle- and long-distance runner, born on 27 December 1990. She began on the track over 1500 metres and 5000 metres and has since moved to the roads. She has won the New York City Marathon twice, in 2024 and 2026. She also holds bronze from the 10,000 metres at the 2022 Commonwealth Games. As a junior she won 1500 metres gold at the 2005 World Youth Championships, beating Yuriko Kobayashi in a championship record of 4:12.29. She returned to defend that title in 2007 and came away with bronze. At the 2008 World Junior Championships she went out in the heats. She left the sport after that season. She joined the Kenya Defence Forces and was racing at their track meetings again around 2012. Her return to top-level competition came in late 2015. Third place at the Kenyan Cross Country Championships earned her a place at the 2016 African Cross Country Championships, where she took silver on her senior debut. Alice Aprot and Beatrice Mutai joined her on a podium filled entirely by Kenyans. That same season she took the national 5000 metres title, then the African title in a championship record of 15:05.45. She was Kenyan 5000 metres champion again in 2019. On the roads she set a 10 kilometres best of 29:46 in a mixed race in Valencia in 2020. In September 2022 she ran 30:07 at the Brasov Running Festival in Romania. That took more than two minutes off the Romanian all-comers record and left her six seconds outside the women-only world record. She won the New York City Marathon on her debut there in November 2024 in 2:24:35, ahead of Hellen Obiri. A year later she was third in 2:20:24 as Obiri won in a course record of 2:19:51. Her 2026 season has been her best yet. In March she won the Nagoya Women's Marathon for a second successive year in 2:21:54. Brigid Kosgei beat her on Tyneside six months later, with Chepkirui taking the runner-up spot at the Great North Run in 1:08:19. On 1 November, aged 35, she won in New York again in 2:24:36 on the 50th anniversary of the five-borough course. She and Obiri were left to fight it out on the approach to Central Park, and Chepkirui pulled clear only in the last 150 metres. The American Jess McClain came through for second in 2:24:42, with Obiri third in 2:24:43. Chepkirui said she had needed patience over a "really tricky" final mile. - [Peres Jepchirchir: age, results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/peres-jepchirchir): Runners / Peres Jepchirchir Photo: Gr5555 / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Peres Jepchirchir Born 1993 (age 32 or 33) Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Road Peres Jepchirchir is a Kenyan road runner, born on 27 September 1993. She grew up on a farm in Turbo, Kenya. She left school at 18, unable to pay the fees, and turned to running as a way out of poverty. She has raced mostly on the roads, from 10K up to the marathon. She made her name over the half marathon. She was world champion in 2016 and again in 2020, when she ran 1:05:16 in Gdynia, Poland, a women-only world record. She broke half marathon world records on four occasions. The first came in 2017 and the other three in 2020. Her women-only mark stood until 20 September 2026, when Agnes Ngetich ran 1:05:15 in Copenhagen. Her marathon record is the stronger one. She won Olympic gold at the delayed Tokyo Games in 2:27:20, ahead of Brigid Kosgei and Molly Seidel. Later that year she won New York in 2:22:39, the first runner to take Olympic marathon gold and a New York title in the same year. Boston followed in 2022, with a winning time of 2:21:02. Her 2:16:16 victory in London in 2024 set a women-only world record. Tigst Assefa has since brought that mark down to 2:15:41. She went back to Tokyo in September 2025 and won the world title. Three months on, she was runner-up in Valencia in 2:14:43, which places her ninth in history. She missed the 2026 London Marathon. Her first race of the year was the Sydney Marathon on 30 August. Her winning time was 2:18:31. Irene Chepet Cheptai was next home in 2:22:11, over three minutes behind. The Athletics Integrity Unit placed her under a provisional suspension, made public on 23 October 2026. An out-of-competition sample collected in Kenya in July, six weeks before Sydney, had returned an adverse analytical finding for EPO. The suspension is not a finding of guilt. She can ask for her B sample to be tested. After that, the AIU will decide whether to charge her or drop the matter. Until a decision is reached she is barred from competing. - [Tara Dower: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/tara-dower): Runners / Tara Dower Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Tara Dower Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 828 (9 November 2026) Tara Dower, born in 1993, is an American ultrarunner who has made her name on long-distance trails and in 100-mile racing. She grew up in North Carolina and played soccer, track and cross-country at school. She then played rugby at East Carolina University, graduating in 2016. Her UTMB Index stands at 828. In 2017 she set out to thru-hike the Appalachian Trail but did not finish. She completed it in 2019. In 2020, before she had raced any organised ultramarathon, she set her first speed record on North Carolina's 1,175-mile Mountains-to-Sea Trail, taking 29 days, 8 hours and 48 minutes. Further records followed on the Benton MacKaye Trail in 2022, in 4 days, 21 hours and 25 minutes, and on the Colorado Trail in 2023, in 8 days, 21 hours and 59 minutes. Her best-known run came in 2024. She set the overall fastest known time on the Appalachian Trail, heading southbound, in 40 days, 18 hours and 6 minutes. That was about 13 hours inside Karel Sabbe's 2018 mark of 41 days, 7 hours and 39 minutes. It made her the first woman since Jennifer Pharr Davis in 2015 to hold the outright record. Her crew chief, Megan Wilmarth, supported the run, and Dower used it to raise money for the charity Girls on the Run. That year she also won the Umstead 100 outright in 14:58:21. She began racing ultras regularly in 2021 and won the Blood Rock 100 Mile that year in 26:30:55. In 2022 she won the Devil Dog 100 outright in 20:08:31 and was second at both Cruel Jewel 100 and the Run Rabbit Run 100 Hare. She went one better at Run Rabbit Run in 2023, winning in 20:32:22, and also won the Hellbender One Hundred in 24:45:21. She was fourth woman at Hardrock in 2024 in 33:10:55. In 2025 she won the Lake Sonoma 50 in 7:36:21 and set a Long Trail speed record of 3 days, 18 hours and 29 minutes. She also ran 13:31:47 at the Javelina Jundred that year, beating Camille Herron's course record by more than 30 minutes. Her 2026 season opened with third at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 8:11:46, her fastest time there. She was third at the Gorge Waterfalls 50K in 4:17:06 and sixth woman at Western States in 16:13:07. At Hardrock she finished third woman in 33:02:04, on a course of 162km with 10,365m of climb. Her Javelina record survived the 2026 race on 31 October. Heather Jackson won the women's title in 13:48:29, 16 minutes 42 seconds outside Dower's time. - [Molly Seidel: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/molly-seidel): Runners / Molly Seidel Photo: Justin Britton / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Molly Seidel Born 1994 (age 31 or 32) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Road, Track, Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 802 (9 November 2026) Molly Seidel is an American distance runner, born on 12 July 1994 in Hartland, Wisconsin. She won bronze in the marathon at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, in only her third ever marathon. She became the first American woman to medal in an Olympic marathon since Deena Kastor in 2004. At the University of Notre Dame she was a four-time NCAA champion and six-time All-American. She turned professional with Saucony in 2017, then finished second at the 2020 US Olympic Trials Marathon in her marathon debut. She ran a personal best of 2:23:07 to finish eighth at the 2023 Chicago Marathon. Injuries have interrupted her career since. A hip impingement ended her 2022 Boston Marathon, and a broken patella ruled her out of the 2024 Olympic Trials. In February 2026 she stepped onto the trails for the first time, taking on the Black Canyon 100K in Arizona and placing fourth in 8:25:13. The run earned her a Golden Ticket entry into the Western States 100. She returned for the 2026 Western States, finishing 28th woman in 24:29:27. - [Hannes Namberger: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hannes-namberger): Runners / Hannes Namberger Photo: iRunFar / Meghan Hicks 🇩🇪 Hannes Namberger Country 🇩🇪 Germany Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 944 (9 November 2026) Hannes Namberger is a German trail and ultra runner from the Chiemgau region of Bavaria, close to the Austrian border. He carries a UTMB Index of 944 and races for Dynafit. He also works as a police officer. Namberger raced as an alpine skier into his early twenties, then moved into hiking and climbing. He took up trail running from there. His first race was the 52 km Karwendelmarsch in Austria in 2015. He has said his body was not ready for running at first, and it took time to adapt to the training load. He broke through on the long-course scene in 2022, winning the Lavaredo Ultra Trail and the Madeira Island Ultra Trail, and finishing sixth at UTMB. He has called his 2021 UTMB run, where he also finished sixth, the coolest day of his career. He says he never leads a race from the start and prefers to run his own pace. He has since finished UTMB eighth in 2023, fourth in 2024 and sixth again in 2026. He has won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail four times, most recently in 2026. He has also taken wins at the Eiger Ultra Trail, the Serra de Tramuntana in Mallorca and Ultra-trail Cape Town. - [Michael Serani: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/michael-serani): Runners / Michael Serani MS 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 594 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Michael Serani Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 594 (9 November 2026) Michael Serani is a Canadian trail and ultra runner. His recorded results come from hilly 50 km trail races and the backyard ultra format. He holds a general UTMB Index of 594. His best placing on record came at the Freaky Creeky 50 in 2025. The course covered 50 km with 2,120 m of climb, and he finished fourth man in 5:26:22. In the same year he ran the Slay the Dragon 50K, a 51 km race with 1,751 m of climb. He came home 15th man in 6:27:49. In 2026 he was one of Canada's 15 runners at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championships. The Canadian team raced on the B.C. Backyard Ultra course in Sicamous, British Columbia. Each of the 67 competing countries held its own race at the same time. A 6.706 km loop set off every hour, and anyone who could not finish it within the hour was out. Every completed yard added a point to the national total. Serani was still running as the championships moved into a third day on the Monday. He was one of seven Canadians left on the loop, along with Ryan Quinlan, Mark Nendick, Pier-Alexandre Beaulieu, Benoit Labreche, Michael Rouleau and Nick Burmey. Eight team-mates had stopped by then. The furthest of them was Sandra Auger, who reached 51 yards, or 342 km. Canada sat sixth in the world at that stage, having finished eighth in 2024 with 673 yards. - [Jamie Crowe: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jamie-crowe): Runners / Jamie Crowe Photo: Bobby Gavin / scottishathletics 🇬🇧 Jamie Crowe Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Jamie Crowe is a British runner who races on the road and in the mountains. He runs for Central Athletics Club, and his results range from a fast flat half marathon in Glasgow to a steep uphill mountain race. His most notable win came at the AJ Bell Great Scottish Run, the edition held the year before the 2027 event. Crowe won the men's half marathon in 1:03:27. The runner-up was Jamie Burns in 1:05:24, with Dougie Selman completing the podium in 1:06:52. Crowe's winning margin was almost two minutes. The course started on St Vincent Street, crossed the River Clyde and headed south through Pollok Country Park. It finished through the McLennan Arch onto Glasgow Green. It was the largest weekend in the event's history, with 35,000 runners taking part across two days. In 2024 Crowe ran the Montée du Nid d'Aigle, a 19 km race with 1,850 metres of climbing. He finished in 2:00:51 and was ninth man. That is a very different kind of effort from a road half marathon. Most of the race is climbing rather than running at speed. Crowe does not currently hold a UTMB Index. His record so far shows a runner with real speed on the road and a willingness to take on the mountains. - [Xavier Lemaître: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/xavier-lemaitre): Runners / Xavier Lemaître XL 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 798 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Xavier Lemaître Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 798 (9 November 2026) Xavier Lemaître is a Canadian trail runner whose results favour short, steep races. His UTMB profile gives him a general UTMB Index of 798. None of his listed races is longer than 26 km, and most pack close to 1,000 m of climb or more into that distance. His best-documented race is Le demi marathon des altitudes at the Ultra Trail Chic-chocs, a 23 km course with 1,220 m of climb. He was second man there in 2023 in 2:20:05. He returned in 2024 and won it in 2:26:55. The winning run was 6 minutes 50 seconds slower than his runner-up time a year earlier. In the same season he finished eighth man in the MSA Classic Up & Down at the Défi des Couleurs, covering 10 km and 960 m of climb in 56:00. In 2025 he took another win, this time in the QMT 25 at the Québec Mega Trail. That course runs 26 km with 950 m of climb, and he finished in 1:56:25. His most recent listed result is from 2026, back at the Défi des Couleurs for the MSA Uphill. It climbs 770 m in 5 km, roughly 154 m for every kilometre. He was 17th man in 31:59. A runner of the same name also features in Canadian university cross-country. A Xavier Lemaître won the RSEQ men's race in Quebec in 24:57 and led Sherbrooke, who go into the U Sports national championships ranked second. The title races are on 14 November, with McMaster as hosts on the Christie Lake grounds in Dundas, Ontario. The available records do not confirm whether the trail runner and the Sherbrooke student are the same person. In cross-country she runs for Laval at university level. On the trails she holds a general UTMB Index of 607. Her standout trail result came at the Ultra Trail Chic-chocs in 2026. She won the women's race over the Mont Xalibu 26k, a 26 km course with 1,290 m of climbing. Her winning time was 2:55:41. Her other headline win came in cross-country, at the RSEQ championships in Quebec, one of the four regional meetings in the U Sports calendar. Drouin won the women's race in 28:35. Laval teammate Léane Baril was 25 seconds back in 29:00, and Béatrice Fillion took third in 29:30 to give Laval every place on the podium. Laval won the team title on 24 points. McGill were a long way back in second on 85. That regional title came shortly before the U Sports national championships. McMaster are the hosts, with the race set for 14 November at Christie Lake Conservation Area, near Dundas in Ontario. A fortnight after that, Canada's national cross-country championships go to Quebec City. Laval will stage them over 28 and 29 November, with the Plains of Abraham as the venue. - [Mercy Adongo Oketch: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mercy-adongo-oketch): Runners / Mercy Adongo Oketch MO Film My Run Mercy Adongo Oketch Runs Mercy Adongo Oketch is a Kenyan 400m runner and the national record holder over one lap, both outdoors and indoors. She was born on 30 July 2002 and grew up in Kabobo village in Migori County. She spent a couple of years playing football as a striker before returning to the track. In 2019 she missed selection for the African U18 and U20 Championships after losing a photo finish to Nelly Chepchirchir at the trials. Later that year she won the 400m at the national championships in Mombasa. Her rise came quickly. She ran a 52.22 split for Kenya in the mixed 4x400m at the 2023 World Championships in Budapest. In 2024 she took 400m silver at the African Military Games in Abuja, then ran 51.80 in Nakuru to go under 52 seconds for the first time. A Kenyan women's 4x400m quartet with Oketch on board clocked a national record of 3:25.80 in May 2025, and that month she also won the Kip Keino Classic in Nairobi in a national 400m record. Accounts differ on the time, giving either 50.14 or 50.25. She won the national title in 50.32 that June and reached the semi-finals of the 400m at the 2025 World Championships. Indoors in 2026 she opened with a Kenyan record of 52.98 in Germany in January. She improved to 52.25 in Madrid on 6 February and then to 51.53 in Metz. At the World Indoor Championships in Toruń, Poland, she finished fifth in the 400m final. She was the first Kenyan woman to reach that final. Back outside, she won the Kip Keino Classic again in 50.17 and the 300m at the Simbine Classic in South Africa in 35.77. In May she ran on the Kenyan mixed 4x400m team that finished fourth at the World Athletics Relays in Botswana in an African record of 3:09.87. She retained her national title in 51.14 and reached the 400m semi-finals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Kenya's national anti-doping body, ADAK, has since barred Oketch from competing while her case is dealt with. Her sample contained two prohibited substances, trimetazidine and furosemide. A provisional suspension is not a final ruling, and she awaits a hearing with the agency. It is not yet clear whether her recent marks will stand. - [Luke Grenfell-Shaw: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/luke-grenfell-shaw): Runners / Luke Grenfell-Shaw Photo: UTMB profile 🇬🇧 Luke Grenfell-Shaw Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 910 (9 November 2026) Luke Grenfell-Shaw is a British ultra runner for Brooks Trail Runners, with a UTMB Index of 911 built on a run of strong 100 km-plus results since 2022. At UTMB's own CCC race around Mont Blanc he has been eighth in 2023 and fourth in 2026, finishing the 2026 edition in 10:47:23 over 107 km. He was also third at the Chiangmai Thailand by UTMB's Elephant 100 in 2024. In 2026 he won the Eiger Ultra Trail's E51 Panorama race in 04:45:07, and was eighth man at the European Athletics Off-Road Running Championships' 52K trail race. The year before he was second at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia's 50K and third at the Eiger Ultra Trail. Grenfell-Shaw has also won closer to home, taking the Rab Scafell Sky Race and the Salomon Serpent Trail 50K in 2023, and the EcoTrail Wicklow 80K in 2022. - [Karen Nash: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/karen-nash): Runners / Karen Nash KN 🇬🇧 UTMB Index 625 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Karen Nash Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 625 (9 November 2026) Karen Nash is a British ultra runner from Preston with a racing record that runs from Yorkshire challenge events to the longest mountain races in the Alps and Pyrenees. She ran cross-country at school and took up orienteering in her 30s. Her first fell ultra came in 2009. She also organises running events, and her UTMB index stands at 625. Her early ultra results came close to home. She was second woman at the Hardmoors 55 in 2010 in 11:09:00 and first woman at Rowbotham's Rotherham Round in 2013 in 8:21:49. That same year she won the Wye One Way 50 in 9:29:31. In 2014 she took the women's Hardmoors 110, covering 182km in 27:29:45, and finished the UTMB in 39:07:44 as 35th woman. Wins followed in 2016 at the St Cuthbert's Way 100K in 13:25:00 and the 10 Peaks Brecon Beacons Long Course in 15:57:48. The distances then grew. She was second woman at the 315km Hardmoors 200 in 2017 in 56:06:55. She won the South Wales 100 in 2017 and again in 2018, cutting her time from 32:26:10 to 27:04:11. Her 2018 win at the 296km Northern Traverse took 63:18:13. At the Tor des Géants she finished 20th woman in 121:21:51 in 2019, then 12th in 119:51:54 in 2021 over a 352km course with 24,000m of climb. The Grand Raid des Pyrénées has become a fixture. She was second woman there in 2021 in 38:57:11, fifth in 2022 and tenth in 2026 in 42:04:57. Aged 65, she won the women's 180km at the Altra 13 Valleys Ultra, held in the Lakes, in 35:58:26. The race began in Keswick on Friday 25 September and crosses the fells with around 7,000m of climbing. Runner's World reported that the win made her the oldest British woman to take an ultramarathon. That made four races of at least 100 miles inside four months, after reaching 120 miles at the Hardmoors 200 before stopping, the Lakeland 100 and the 185km Grand Raid des Pyrénées. She believed she was running second at Grasmere and only found out near Threlkeld that she was in front. Nash says she follows no fixed training routine. A typical week brings roughly four hours of indoor climbing, split between Monday and Friday sessions, a good deal of cycling and hill runs of around 20km when the mood takes her. After the 13 Valleys she planned some orienteering and a short ultra. The Original Mountain Marathon was also pencilled in, along with a 24-mile race in late October. Havering finished second in the women's first division on 61 points, behind Basildon on 22 and ahead of Colchester Harriers on 103. Her recorded results cover distances from 25K to 50K. Her longest listed race is the Sulphur Springs Trail Race 50k in 2022. The course covered 50 km with 1,225 metres of climb. She finished in 5:15:34 and was sixth woman. Her biggest win came at the first Hustle at Pinehurst, the revived version of the Run for the Toad. The race was held at the Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area near Cambridge, Ontario. It was put on by Straw Dog Racing, the same organisers behind Sulphur Springs. The course runs in 12.5K loops over rolling, cross-country style ground, and each lap has more than 250 metres of climb. Hol won the women's 25K, two laps of that circuit, in 2:09:17. Because it was the first edition, her time stands as the women's course record. She does not currently hold a UTMB Index. The Pinehurst win is her most recent recorded result, and the organisers have already said they are planning a 2027 edition. In 2026 she won the Broken Arrow Skyrace 46K in 04:48:48, a step up from third in the same race the year before, and finished 40th woman at the CCC, the 107 km race that runs alongside UTMB itself around Mont Blanc. She has been especially strong at 50K. Moreno won the HOKA Canyons Endurance Runs 50K in 2024 in 03:52:24 and the Kodiak Ultra Marathons 50K in 2023 in 04:19:08. She has also raced Zegama-Aizkorri and Sierre-Zinal, and won the Eiger Ultra Trail's shorter distance outright. Moreno's results stretch back to 2016, when she won the Marin Ultra Challenge 25K, and her career includes wins at the Power of Four 25K, the Franklin Mountains Trail Run, the XTERRA Kualoa Trail Run and an earlier Broken Arrow Skyrace, the 26K, in 2018.
