- [Jack Bromley: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jack-bromley): Runners / Jack Bromley JB 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Jack Bromley Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Jack Bromley is a British runner whose recorded results take in hilly trail races from 42 km to 84 km and, more recently, the road marathon. His UTMB race history lists five finishes between 2016 and 2020. He does not currently hold a UTMB Index. His best trail result came at the Ultimate Trails 55 Km in 2017. He covered the 58 km course, with 1980 m of climb, in 06:03:58 and finished second man. A year earlier he had placed 24th on the same course in 07:01:27, so he went 57 minutes and 29 seconds quicker on his return. Also in 2017 he ran the Colporteur race at the Trail des Crêtes du Chablais, 42 km with 2710 m of climb, and came home 60th man in 06:43:13. He has also raced twice in Centurion events. At the North Downs Way 50 in 2019 he finished 18th man in 08:06:25 over 84 km and 1560 m of climb. The following year he was fifth man at the South Downs Way 50, running the 79 km course with its 1760 m of ascent in 06:38:02. On the road, a Jack Bromley ran 2:19:54 at the Amsterdam Marathon on Sunday 18 October to win his age category. He was the fastest of four British age-group winners on the day. More than 25,000 people finished a race that starts and ends in the Olympic Stadium, run in cold rain and wind. The overall men's title went to the Ethiopian Lemi Berhanu, who stopped the clock at 2:03:32. The marathon result appears under the same name, though the race report does not tie it directly to his trail record. - [Ida Amelie Robsahm: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ida-amelie-robsahm): Runners / Ida Amelie Robsahm Photo: @utmbworldseries / Instagram 🇳🇴 Ida Amelie Robsahm Country 🇳🇴 Norway Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 800 (9 November 2026) Ida Amelie Robsahm was a Norwegian mountain and trail runner who raced for Asics Trail, with a UTMB Index of 800. According to the Norwegian magazine Kondis, she took up running seriously only around four years before her death, and rose quickly through the sport. In March 2026 she won the Chianti Marathon Trail in Italy in 03:39:10. At the Marathon du Mont-Blanc over 42 km she finished runner-up behind Tove Alexandersson of Sweden in 04:18:28, having placed 4th at Zegama-Aizkorri. In August 2026 she was 5th at OCC, the 60 km race at the UTMB World Series Finals in Chamonix, in 06:27:34. She placed 4th at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. Runner's World reports that result led to a semi-professional deal with Asics Trail. She raced on the road too. She made her marathon debut in Valencia in December 2025, running 02:29:57, after winning the 10K at the Grue Halvmaraton earlier that year in 33:15. Away from racing she taught chemistry, and reportedly also mathematics, at Foss Upper Secondary School in Oslo. Robsahm died on 19 September following a fall on the Romsdalseggen ridge in western Norway. She was climbing with a group close to the ridge's 1,329 m summit when she slipped and dropped some way down the mountainside. A helicopter crew airlifted her off the mountain, but she could not be revived, and investigators had not established what caused the slip. She was 30. Fellow trail runners including Kilian Jornet and Asics Trail colleague Ben Dhiman offered tributes, and Asics described her as a remarkable athlete and teammate. - [Harvey Lewis: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/harvey-lewis): Runners / Harvey Lewis Photo: Mike Trimpe / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Harvey Lewis Born 1976 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road (legend) Harvey Lewis is an American ultrarunner best known for the backyard format, in which he set a world record of 108 hours in 2023. Born on 13 April 1976 in Wheeling, West Virginia, he grew up largely in Berea, Ohio. A high school teacher by profession, he has made his home in Cincinnati. In July 2014 he won the 135-mile Badwater Ultramarathon in 23:52:55. In the same year he shared second place at the Arrowhead 135. He also won SC24 in Spartanburg, South Carolina, covering 154.59 miles. Team USA picked him for the IAU 24-hour world championships four times between 2012 and 2017. Lewis first won Big Dog's Backyard Ultra in 2021 with 354.16 miles. The race in Bell Buckle, Tennessee, serves as the world championship of the format. Each runner must finish a loop of about 4.17 miles, known as a yard, inside every hour. The last one still going wins. In 2023 six runners passed 100 hours. Lewis was the slowest of the final three, averaging 52:23 per lap. Bartosz Fudali declined to start yard 104, which left Lewis to duel with Ihor Verys. Verys turned back during yard 108. Lewis completed it alone for a record 108 yards and 450 miles. On trails he won the Sulphur Springs 100 in 2010 and the Burning River 100 in 2020. He was second at the Superior 100 in 2021 and finished Western States in 2024. Away from racing, a grant took him along the route of Gandhi's 241-mile Salt March in 2008. A year later he retraced the Selma to Montgomery march. - [Jon Noll: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jon-noll): Runners / Jon Noll JN 🇺🇸 Film My Run 🇺🇸 Jon Noll Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra Jon Noll is an American ultra runner whose record is built on 100-mile trail races and, more recently, backyard ultras. His listed results run from 2013 onwards. He has no current UTMB Index. His early results came well down the field. In 2013 he finished the Leadville Trail 100 in 26:48:40 for 167th man, over 159 km with 4,400 m of climb. That same year he ran the Ice Age Trail 50 Mile, 81 km with 1,600 m of ascent, in 11:47:37 for 222nd. In 2016 he was 29th man at the Kettle Moraine 100 in 23:47:42. Later that year he won the Tbunk Endurance Challenge 50 Mile in 6:46:01, an 80 km course with 2,590 m of climb. The wins kept coming at the longer distance. He took the Mines of Spain 100 Mile in 2018 in 17:45:20, covering 170 km and 4,360 m of climb. In 2019 he went back to Kettle Moraine and won it outright in 16:17:31. That was seven hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds faster than his 2016 run on the same 161 km course. Noll has since turned to the backyard format, where each 6.706 km yard begins on the hour. He was one of the last two Americans still running at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship, held on Laz Lake's home course in Tennessee. Sixty-seven nations set off together at 12:00 UTC on 17 October. Yard 105 was under way by 21:09 UTC on the 21st, and he and Mark Dowdle were both still on the loop. Team USA had 1,117 yards at that point, ahead of Australia on 1,069 and Japan on 1,038. Teammate Nicholas Steel had stopped at 94. No final world classification had been confirmed at that stage. The 50 highest-ranked national winners will qualify for Big's, which gets under way in Bell Buckle on 16 October 2027. - [Joey Hadorn: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joey-hadorn): Runners / Joey Hadorn Photo: Spiralwidget / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇭 Joey Hadorn Born 1997 (age 28 or 29) Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 925 (9 November 2026) Joey Hadorn is a Swiss orienteering competitor, born 11 April 1997 in Bern. He also races on the trail running circuit, mostly in short mountain events, and holds a general UTMB Index of 928. As a junior he swept the sprint, long distance and relay titles at the 2016 Junior World Championships in Engadin, and added a middle distance silver at the same event. A year later he took junior sprint bronze. In 2018 he became Swiss middle distance champion. In 2019 he won a middle distance round of the Orienteering World Cup in Laufen and was second in the knockout sprint there. He later took another runner-up place over the middle distance when the World Cup season closed in China. In 2023 he won World Championship middle distance silver on home soil in Switzerland, then relay gold with the Swiss team. Switzerland won the mixed sprint relay at the 2024 World Championships in Edinburgh, with Hadorn running leg three. Natalia Gemperle, Riccardo Rancan and Simona Aebersold completed the gold-winning quartet. He also reached the knockout sprint final and finished fourth, 0.2 seconds short of bronze. On the trail his best results include third at the Dolomyths Run Sellaronda Ultra Sky in 2021 in 1:52:23, and seventh at Sierre-Zinal in both 2019 and 2020. His fastest run on the 31km Sierre-Zinal course, with 2190 metres of climb, is 2:36:15 from 2019. He was 16th at the 2024 Golden Trail Finals in Ascona and Locarno in 1:59:58. The 2026 season has brought more Golden Trail World Series racing. He was sixth at the Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail in Austria in 2:15:50, then 73rd at Sierre-Zinal in 2:53:48, his sixth visit to the race. On 27 September he returned to the Jinshanling Great Wall Trail Race in Chengde, China, a 23.1km course with 1,667 metres of climbing over stone stairs on the old wall. He finished third in 2:15:42 behind the Kenyans Patrick Kipngeno and Philemon Kiriago. It was the same podium, in the same order, as in 2025, when he ran 2:14:01. - [Philemon Kiriago: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/philemon-kiriago): Runners / Philemon Kiriago Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Philemon Kiriago Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 982 (9 November 2026) Philemon Kiriago is a Kenyan mountain and trail runner with a UTMB Index of 982. Sierre-Zinal has been his standout race. It covers 31km with 2,190 metres of climbing. He won it in 2023, 2025 and 2026, was runner-up in 2024 and finished fifth in 2022. His fastest winning time there is 2:26:24, from 2026, when Patrick Kipngeno was second. His quickest run on the course came in defeat, though. He clocked 2:25:36 for second place in 2024. In 2025 Kiriago won the Classic 14K at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in 1:02:30. His 2026 season brought wins at the Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K in 1:42:59, the Trofeo Nasego in 1:30:08 and the Transvulcania Media Maratón on La Palma in 2:07:43. He was also second in the Transvulcania vertical kilometre in 47:33. At the Innsbruck Alpine Trailrun Festival he was fifth in the Trail Hunt and fourth in the vertical. He won the Golfo dell'Isola race in 2025 in 2:01:47, having finished second in the Golden Trail World Series final there in 2023. He has won the Trofeo Nasego three times, in 2023, 2025 and 2026, and was runner-up there in 2022 and 2024. He also won the Sky Gran Canaria AA21 race in 2023. Kiriago has been a regular podium finisher at shorter mountain races too. He has finished in the top three at the Broken Arrow Skyrace three years running, going third, second and then first. He was runner-up at Montée du Nid d'Aigle in 2022 and 2023, and fifth there in 2024. His most recent result came on 27 September 2026, when he raced on the Great Wall near Chengde, China, at the Jinshanling Great Wall Trail Race. The 23.1km course climbed 1,667 metres over stone stairs and mountain paths on and around the wall. Kiriago was second in 2:14:24, behind Kipngeno in 2:12:30, with Joey Hadorn of Switzerland third in 2:15:42. The top three repeated their order from 2025, when Kiriago was second in 2:13:48. That race brought the regular season of this year's Golden Trail World Series to a close. Only the Grand Finale remains. It takes place in Muju, South Korea, on 24 October, and the field will tackle 25.6km and 2,294 metres of ascent. - [Sara Alonso: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sara-alonso): Runners / Sara Alonso Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇪🇸 Sara Alonso Born 1999 (age 26 or 27) Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 807 (9 November 2026) Sara Alonso is a Spanish trail and mountain runner, born in 1999 and a former 3,000 metres steeplechase athlete. She studied physiotherapy and sport science at the University of Lleida, where a school trip into the mountains first introduced her to trail running. She signed with the Salomon Espana trail team in 2019 after contacting them on Instagram, and made her Golden Trail World Series debut in 2021. Her breakthrough came in 2022. She won the Transgrancanaria Marathon, then the Marathon du Mont-Blanc in 4:14:49, taking the provisional Golden Trail World Series lead. She was crowned Spanish trail running champion that June, and finished the season third overall in the series. She signed with Asics at the end of the year. A stress fracture kept her out of racing for all of 2023. She returned in 2025, opening the Golden Trail season with a win at Japan's Kobe Trail. In May she won her home race, the Zegama-Aizkorri mountain marathon, leading from start to finish. She took silver in the short trail race at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, held that year in Canfranc, and the Spanish team also won silver. Third place at the season-closing Ledro Sky Trentino race sealed her the runner-up spot in the 2025 Golden Trail World Series overall standings. She opened 2026 in the Skyrunner World Series, winning Acantilados del Norte in La Palma and the Calamorro Skyrace in Benalmadena, taking the lead in the women's standings. She returned to defend her Zegama-Aizkorri title in May, finishing third. - [Dominik Rolli: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/dominik-rolli): Runners / Dominik Rolli Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇭 Dominik Rolli Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 928 (9 November 2026) Dominik Rolli is a Swiss mountain and trail runner with a UTMB Index of 929. He has competed at the top level of the sport since at least 2019, racing regularly on the Skyrunning and Golden Trail World Series circuits. His best recent result came at the 2026 European Athletics Off-Road Running Championships, where he finished 2nd in the men's Up & Down race over 13 km in 01:01:03. In 2025 he placed 4th in the Classic 14K at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, clocking 01:03:56. Rolli has raced Sierre-Zinal, one of the sport's oldest mountain races, five times since 2019. His quickest run there came in 2025, when he finished 7th in 02:34:07 over the 31 km course. He was 3rd at the Jungfrau-Marathon in 2024, in 03:07:37, and 3rd in the Europe Up & Down Elite category at Reventon Trail El Paso in 2022. He also races on the Golden Trail World Series, finishing 7th at the Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail in 2025. - [Lucia Stafford: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lucia-stafford): Runners / Lucia Stafford Photo: CooperRiverRunner / Wikimedia Commons Lucia Stafford Runs Lucia Stafford is a Canadian middle-distance runner whose main event is the 1500 metres. Born in London, Ontario, on 17 August 1998, she grew up in Toronto. She has run for Canada at two Olympic Games and now trains in Manchester as part of the M11 Track Club, a group that includes the 2024 Olympic 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson. Her first international title came in 2017, when she won the 1500m at the Pan American U20 Championships. She went on to study civil engineering at the University of Toronto and raced for the Varsity Blues. At the 2019 Summer Universiade she was fifth in both the 1500m and the 4x400m relay. At the Tokyo Olympics, held in 2021, she lined up in the 1500m alongside her older sister, Gabriela DeBues-Stafford. Stafford reached the semi-final and ran a personal best of 4:02.12, but placed 13th overall, 0.43 seconds behind Spain's Marta Pérez, and did not advance to the final. The following seasons brought a run of global championship appearances. She was eighth in the 1500m at the 2022 World Indoor Championships in Belgrade and 11th in the final at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games that summer. On 28 January 2023 she set a North American indoor record for 1000m, clocking 2:33.75 at the John Thomas Terrier Classic in Boston. That put her ninth on the world indoor all-time list. She lowered her 1500m best to 4:02.03 at the USATF LA Grand Prix on 27 May 2023 and raced the same event at the Paris Olympics in August 2024. The 2026 season has been her quickest yet. In May she ran 4:00.83 for 1500m in Rabat. On 1 August she was fourth in the mile at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland. She then made her road mile debut at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen, finishing eighth in 4:29.51. A week later she took six seconds off that mark. Back in Toronto during her break, she took the women's title at the inaugural Bloor Street Mile in 4:23, 19 seconds clear of Sadie-Jane Hickson. The route was flat and kept to Bloor Street between Yonge Street and Brunswick Avenue, passing the Royal Ontario Museum on the way. Stafford noted on Instagram that the finish was "literally three metres" from her parents' house. - [Anne Flower: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/anne-flower): Runners / Anne Flower Photo: Anne Flower 🇺🇸 Anne Flower Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 847 (9 November 2026) Anne Flower is an American ultrarunner who works as a doctor and began running to cope with the pressures of medicine. In 2020 she reached the Olympic Trials over the marathon, then turned her focus to longer races. She is from Cincinnati and studied at Ohio University and Regis University. She races for HOKA and holds a UTMB index of 847. Flower's breakthrough at ultra distances came in 2024, when she won the Javelina Jundred 100K in 08:23:13. The following year she ran the Leadville Trail 100 for the first time and won in 17:58:19. That performance broke a course record Ann Trason had held since 1994, one that had stood for 31 years. She closed 2025 with victory at the Tunnel Hill 50 Mile in Vienna, Illinois, in 05:18:57. The win also gave her the women's world record for 50 miles. In 2026 she was second woman at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 07:57:59. Earlier in her career Flower ran the Pikes Peak Marathon twice, finishing 10th woman in 2021 in 05:39:02 and 4th in 2023 in 05:06:26. She also won the Burning River Endurance Run 50 Mile in 2021 in 08:05:42 and the Dead Horse Ultra 50 Mile in 2019 in 07:43:40. - [Nichole Abma: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nichole-abma): Runners / Nichole Abma NA 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 689 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Nichole Abma Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 689 (9 November 2026) Nichole Abma is a Canadian ultra runner who races long mountain courses, from 50 kilometres up to 100 miles. Her general UTMB Index stands at 655. Her recorded results begin in 2021, when she finished fifth woman at the Black Spur Ultra 108k in 15:53:16. That course covered 109 km with 4,461 metres of climb. Her biggest result is a win in the women's 100 miles at Kodiak Ultra Marathons by UTMB. Within the UTMB World Series, Kodiak holds Major status for the Americas. The race starts at the Rim Nordic Ski Area and finishes in the Village at Big Bear Lake, California. Abma crossed the line in 20:43:40 and was 11th overall. Her fellow Canadian Madeline Wighardt was second in 22:05:50, more than 80 minutes behind. The win earned her an automatic place at the 2027 Finals, which went to the first ten finishers of each sex. Before Kodiak she had already made the podium over 100 miles. In 2022 she was third woman at the Whistler Alpine Meadows 100 Mile in 34:03:10, on a 161 km course with 7,775 metres of climb. That year she was also 11th woman at the Sinister 7 Ultra 50-Miler in 13:36:03. In 2025 she went further still. She finished fourth woman at Ultra-trail Cape Town over 163 km and 6,995 metres of climb, in 29:56:43. She has also raced shorter and faster. In 2024 she was 11th woman at the Black Canyon Ultras 60K in 5:42:46, and seventh woman at The Rut Mountain Runs 50k in 6:52:37. Her most recent listed result came in 2026, at the Desert RATS Trail Running Festival by UTMB 100K. She finished fourth woman there in 10:51:29, on a course with 2,050 metres of climb. - [Andy Symonds: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/andy-symonds): Runners / Andy Symonds Photo: UTMB profile 🇬🇧 Andy Symonds Born 1981 (age 44 or 45) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 863 (9 November 2026) Andy Symonds is a British engineer and mountain and trail runner, born 28 April 1981. He is the son of fell running record holder Hugh Symonds and grew up in Sedbergh, where he discovered the hills with his brother Joe. He has raced trail and mountain events across Britain, France and further afield since 2006. Symonds has won a string of major European trail races, including the Lavaredo Ultra Trail in 2016 and the Trail du Ventoux, Sainte-Victoire and Templiers races in the early 2010s. He has twice finished in the top 20 at the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc, placing 16th in 2017 and 5th in 2019. His racing has taken him from Scotland and England to New Zealand and France. He remains highly active on the UTMB circuit, winning the Grand Raid du Guillestrois-Queyras and the Grand Raid Ventoux Ultra Géant de Provence in 2026. He also won the Trail de la Sainte Baume and finished 19th at the full UTMB Mont-Blanc race that year. His UTMB Index of 864 ranks him among Britain's leading ultra distance racers. - [Michael Wardian: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/michael-wardian): Runners / Michael Wardian Photo: John Manard / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Michael Wardian Born 1974 (age 51 or 52) Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 717 (9 November 2026) Michael Wardian is an American marathon and ultramarathon runner, born in Morgantown, West Virginia, on 12 April 1974. He has won US titles at 50 km, 50 miles and 100 km. In 2011 the International Association of Ultrarunners named him its first Athlete of the Year. He is known for racing far more often than most elite runners. Wardian only began running competitively after Michigan State University, where he played lacrosse. He won the National Marathon in Washington DC six times between 2006 and 2012. In 2007 he won the JFK 50 Mile and ran 13 marathons. He raced the Olympic Marathon Trials in 2004, 2008 and 2012. A 2:17:49 at Grandma's Marathon in 2011 earned his place at the last of those. He finished the 2010 Marathon des Sables third, in 23:01:03, the fastest time an American had run there. He won bronze at the 2009 IAU 50 km World Championships in Gibraltar and silver at the 100 km worlds in 2011. USATF named him its ultrarunner of the year in 2008 and 2009. He also chases unusual records. From 2007 to 2009 he held the world best for a marathon pushing a jogging stroller, set with 2:42:21 at Frederick. In January 2017 he ran seven marathons on seven continents in seven days, averaging 2:45. In 2019 he set the fastest known time for the 631-mile Israel National Trail. In 2020, during the pandemic, he won the Quarantine Backyard Ultra after almost 263 miles in 63 hours. On the trails, UTMB lists wins at the Tussey Mountainback in 2011 and 2014 and at EcoTrail AlUla in 2020. He was 42nd at UTMB in 2016 and finished the Hardrock 100 in 2017, 2018 and 2025. He works as an international shipbroker and lives in Arlington, Virginia. - [Rachel Entrekin: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rachel-entrekin): Runners / Rachel Entrekin Photo: iRunFar 🇺🇸 Rachel Entrekin Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 822 (9 November 2026) Rachel Entrekin is an American ultramarathon runner and physical therapist, born on 17 June 1991 in Birmingham, Alabama. Nobody else has won the Cocodona 250 three times, and it ranks among North America's toughest ultramarathons. In 2026 she became the first woman to win it outright, setting a new course record. She began running in college, where she studied exercise science, and later completed a doctorate in physical therapy in 2016. She completed her first half marathon in 2010, then stepped up to the marathon distance in 2011. She moved into ultramarathons in 2013, starting out over 50 km. After relocating to Washington State in 2016, she began setting Fastest Known Times on long trails, including Mount Rainier's Wonderland Trail and Mount Hood's Timberline Trail. She holds 15 such records spread across the Sierra Nevada range, the Cascades, California's Transverse Ranges, and on Catalina Island. She won the Cocodona 250 outright in 2026, in 56 hours, 9 minutes and 48 seconds, having already taken the women's race in 2024 and 2025. Along the way she slept for only 19 minutes and reportedly stopped to pet dogs on the course. The win drew unusually wide mainstream coverage, including from the Guardian and the BBC, and earned her the nickname 'Queen of Cocodona'. She also won the Coldwater Rumble 100 Miles in January 2026 and finished third at the Chianti Ultra Trail by UTMB later that year. In August 2026 she finished second on her debut at the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc, behind Blandine L'Hirondel. She signed with Norda in December 2025 and is also sponsored by Precision Fuel and Hydration. - [Thomas Roach: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/thomas-roach): Runners / Thomas Roach Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Thomas Roach Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 890 (9 November 2026) Thomas Roach is a British mountain and trail runner with a general UTMB index of 897, built from a long run of results across the Alps since 2018. He was second over the short course at the 2023 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Innsbruck-Stubai. He also won the 2023 Three Peaks Race and, in the Masters category, took the 2024 World Masters Mountain Running Championships' Long 34K and the 2025 European Masters Off-Road Running Championships' trail race. He has dominated the Tour de Tirol series, winning its Pölventrail, Kaisermarathon and 75 km editions across 2022, 2023 and 2024. He also won the PIUT50 and the Innsbruck Alpine Trailrun Festival's K42 Trailmarathon in 2024. His other wins include the Innsbruck festival's K65 Panorama Ultra Trail in 2022 and its K25 race in 2018, 2020 and 2021. He has raced Sierre-Zinal five times since 2022, finishing as high as 15th. - [Eli Hemming: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/eli-hemming): Runners / Eli Hemming Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Eli Hemming Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 929 (9 November 2026) Eli Hemming is an American trail and mountain runner who races for Adidas Terrex. He has built his reputation over shorter, steep courses rather than long ultras. In 2025 and 2026 he won back-to-back editions of the Broken Arrow Skyrace 46K in California. His 2025 time was 3:50:48, ahead of 3:58:01 in his title defence a year later. Hemming won the OCC race at UTMB Mont-Blanc in 2024, in 5:11:48. He returned to the Mont-Blanc trails in 2025 to finish seventh in the tougher CCC, in 10:34:36. He was also runner-up at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc's 42 km race in 2023. He has won repeatedly on the US ultra circuit too. Hemming took the Big Alta 50K in both 2024 and 2025, and the Desert RATS 21K in both of those years as well. He also won the Canyons Endurance Runs 50K and the Black Canyon Ultras 60K in 2024, and the Rothrock by UTMB 50K in 2026. Hemming represented the United States at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in 2025, finishing 18th in the short trail race over 45 km. He has also stepped up to the longer Black Canyon Ultras 100K, finishing fourth there in 2025 in 7:32:41. He was 21st in the same race in 2026. He grew up in Annecy, in the French Alps. He ran track and cross country at school, though not at a high level. He won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc outright in 2024, completing the 176.4 km course in 19 hours, 54 minutes and 23 seconds. He entered as an unsponsored athlete, and the win was seen as a major upset. It ranked as the third-quickest winning time the race had seen up to then. His day job is as a product engineer for the shoe brand Hoka. He has also won Western States in 2026, and the Kodiak 100 Mile and the Gorge Waterfalls 100K in 2023. He finished third twice at the Chianti Ultra Trail by UTMB, in 2025 and 2026. - [Nienke Brinkman: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nienke-brinkman): Runners / Nienke Brinkman Photo: UTMB profile 🇳🇱 Nienke Brinkman Born 1993 (age 32 or 33) Country 🇳🇱 Netherlands Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 789 (9 November 2026) Nienke Brinkman is a Dutch runner who competes on both the road and on trails, with a UTMB Index of 789. Born in 1993, she took up running as a hobby while completing a PhD in geophysics in Zurich, having previously played field hockey to a decent level in the Netherlands. She won the Zermatt Marathon in 2021, in a course record of 3:19:43, more than 40 minutes quicker than her time there the year before. That same year she finished 2nd at Sierre-Zinal and won both the Chiemgau Trail Run and La Skyrhune, taking 2nd overall in the Golden Trail World Series. In 2022, after joining the NN Running Team, Brinkman ran a personal best of 2:22:51 for 2nd place at the Rotterdam Marathon, breaking the Dutch record. She also won Zegama-Aizkorri, the Pikes Peak Ascent and the five-day Madeira Ocean and Trail stage race that year, enough to top the overall Golden Trail World Series standings, and finished 3rd in the marathon at the European Athletics Championships in Munich. She has continued to race at the highest level on trails, finishing 6th at Sierre-Zinal in 2023 and 5th in both Sierre-Zinal and the Broken Arrow Skyrace in 2026. - [Nashon Kiplimo: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/nashon-kiplimo): Runners / Nashon Kiplimo Photo: UTMB profile 🇰🇪 Nashon Kiplimo Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 938 (9 November 2026) Nashon Kiplimo is a Kenyan trail runner who has only been racing on trails for the last two years. His results so far include wins at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc 23km in 2025 and the Mistral Marathon Trail at the Grand Raid Ventoux in 2026. His breakthrough came at the 2026 OCC, part of the UTMB World Series Final in Chamonix and his longest race to date at 60km. He was not among the early frontrunners. By the Col de Balme checkpoint at 34km, he had moved past Petter Engdahl, Maximilien Drion and Andreu Blanes into a surprise second place. The checkpoint sits at the race's high point, 2,321 metres up. Kiplimo was eight minutes behind leader Frederic Tranchand at the time. He held second through the Vallorcine checkpoint at 41km and pushed hard on the final downhill into Chamonix, closing the gap on Tranchand without ever catching him. Kiplimo finished in 5 hours 14 minutes and 37 seconds, four and a half minutes behind the winner. In 2026 she finished second woman at the TDS, one of UTMB's flagship Mont Blanc races, in 22:30:29 over 154 km and 9,500 metres of climbing. That result came off the back of a long run of victories. She won the Ultra Trail des Montagnes du Jura's La Franco Suisse in 2025 over 105 km in 12:00:53, and the Trail du Cirque du Fer à Cheval's 80 km race the same year. In 2024 she won four races outright, including the Transju'Trail's 40K and the Raidlight Trail Festival's Trail Tour, and was second at the Ut4M 80 Challenge in 2023. Her wins go back to 2019, when she took the Trail des Passerelles du Monteynard's Petit Train 28K and the Chartreuse Trail Festival's Semi Trail, both outright. - [Sylvain Cachard: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sylvain-cachard): Runners / Sylvain Cachard Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇷 Sylvain Cachard Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 935 (9 November 2026) Sylvain Cachard is a French mountain and trail runner who races for HOKA Europe. His UTMB Index of 936 is built on a career stretching back to his junior debut at Sierre-Zinal in 2017. His biggest recent win came at the 2025 La Asics SainteLyon, a 79km night race, which he won in 5:36:33. The same year he won the Marathon des Causses at the Festival des Templiers in 2:35:42, having also won that festival's shorter VO2 Trail race in 2024. He has been a regular at Sierre-Zinal, the Swiss mountain-running classic, finishing 4th in 2023 and 7th in 2024 across more than a dozen appearances since his junior debut. At UTMB's Mont-Blanc OCC he placed 17th in 2024 and 4th in 2026. His other wins include the Skyrace des Matheysins and the Trail Nivolet-Revard in 2022, and several French mountain-running titles over shorter distances, including the Devoluy course elite and the Serre Che Trail's Tour des Chapelles, both in 2020. - [Ekaterina Mityaeva: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ekaterina-mityaeva): Runners / Ekaterina Mityaeva Photo: Alexis Martín from España / Wikimedia Commons 🇷🇺 Ekaterina Mityaeva Born 1989 (age 36 or 37) Country 🇷🇺 Russia Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 769 (9 November 2026) Ekaterina Mityaeva, born Ekaterina Filippova on 15 February 1989 in Pokhvistnevo, Russia, is a trail and skyrunning specialist who now races for adidas Terrex. She finished fourth at the 171km Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc in 2019, in 25:53:26, at the time the best result by a Russian woman in the race's history. Mityaeva started running at school aged 10 and moved into orienteering at 14. She later took up radio direction finding and won gold, silver and bronze medals at the 2008 World Championships in Seoul. She studied physical culture and sport at the Kuban State University, graduating in 2013. She ran the Moscow International Marathon in 2:43:49 in 2012 before switching to trail racing the following year. Her first trail event was the Konzhak Marathon in the Ural Mountains, where she finished second. Since 2014 she has trained alongside Dmitry Mityaev, and the pair run an online trail running school under adidas Terrex sponsorship. Mityaeva holds Master of Sports of Russia rankings in five endurance disciplines, including athletics, skyrunning and orienteering. She has reached the podium at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc nine times since 2016, winning the 90km race outright in 2024 in 12:40:04. She also won the Salomon Cappadocia Ultra-Trail and the Uludag Premium Ultra Trail in Turkey in 2023. She remains competitive into her late 30s. In 2025 she was runner-up at the Chiangmai Elephant 100 in Thailand and at Transvulcania on La Palma, and in 2026 she finished third at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc's 90km race in 12:15:12. - [Veronika Leng: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/veronika-leng): Runners / Veronika Leng Photo: Sportograf 🇸🇰 Veronika Leng Country 🇸🇰 Slovakia Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 787 (9 November 2026) Veronika Leng is a Slovak trail runner with a UTMB Index of 787, built almost entirely on races across Hong Kong and the rest of Asia. She has been winning regularly since 2018 and remains near the top of the sport in 2026. In 2026 she shared victory at the Anta Hong Kong 100, covering 93 km and 5,073 m of climb in 10:43:35, after closing a near 14-minute gap on her Vietnamese rival Hau Ha over the second half of the course. In 2025 she won the Nike ACG Ultra-Trail Chongli 168's 100 km race in China in 12:19:47, finished fifth woman at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC in 12:00:27, and was second at the Vietnam Ultra Marathon's 75 km race and the Anta Hong Kong 100's full 102 km race. Her results stretch back through a long run of Hong Kong and Asian ultras. She won the TransLantau by UTMB 50K in 2024, the TNF Malaysia Mountain Trail Festival's 84 km race and the Vietnam Jungle Marathon's 70 km race in 2019, and the Oxfam Trailwalker's virtual 100 km event in 2021. She was second woman at the Vibram Hong Kong 100 in 2020, in 11:47:40. - [Robert Brouillette: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/robert-brouillette): Runners / Robert Brouillette Photo: UTMB profile 🇨🇦 Robert Brouillette Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 773 (9 November 2026) Robert Brouillette is a Canadian trail and ultra runner with a UTMB Index of 773. His recorded results run from a half marathon in 2016 to a 162 km finish at the Leadville Trail 100 Run. In between, he has built a habit of winning at Sulphur Springs. His earliest listed result is second place at The North Face Endurance Challenge Ontario Half Marathon in 2016, in 1:31:52 over 21 km with 770 metres of climb. At Sulphur Springs he won the 20K in 2022 in 1:16:28. A year later he moved up to the 50K and finished fourth in 3:52:19. He returned in 2024 and won it in 3:33:41. In 2025 he stepped up again and took the 100K in 8:07:22, covering 2,450 metres of climb. He has also raced across the border. At the JFK 50 Mile he was 12th man in 5:58:41 in 2024 and 13th in 5:59:10 in 2025, only 29 seconds slower. The 2025 Leadville Trail 100 Run was a bigger test, 162 km with 4,230 metres of ascent. He finished 39th man in 23:57:45, with two minutes and 15 seconds to spare inside 24 hours. In Quebec he was 99th man in the QMT 50 in 2025 in 7:52:24, and 29th in the 77 km QMT 80 in 2026 in 10:39:16. His 2026 season has also included 11th man in the Grit & Grind 20K at Camp Fortune in 1:48:48 and 17th in the Grindstone 100K in 13:02:47, a race with 3,350 metres of climb. He then won the 50K at the first Hustle at Pinehurst, the revived Run for the Toad at the Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area near Cambridge, Ontario. The race is put on by Straw Dog Racing, which also organises Sulphur Springs. The course is four laps of 12.5K, each with more than 250 metres of climb on rolling, cross-country style ground. He finished in 3:34:36, a course record as it was the first edition. Kyle McCandless of Burlington was second in 4:17:16, 42 minutes and 40 seconds behind. - [Anna Frost: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/anna-frost): Runners / Anna Frost Photo: iRunFar 🇳🇿 Anna Frost Born 1981 Country 🇳🇿 New Zealand Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) UTMB Index 560 (9 November 2026) Anna Frost is a New Zealand trail and mountain runner from Dunedin, born on 1 November 1981. She won the Hardrock 100 in 2015 and 2016. In 2010 she took the overall Skyrunner World Series title. She twice won Transvulcania, setting a course record in 2012. Frost turned professional in 2004 and later joined Team Salomon. Her 2010 series wins included the Three Peaks Race and the Table Mountain Challenge. She won The North Face Endurance Challenge 50 Mile in California in 2010 and 2011. In 2011 she also won the Six Foot Track Marathon. In 2012 she won Transvulcania on La Palma in 8:11:31, a course record. That year she also won the Speedgoat 50K and the Maxi-Race in Annecy, and finished second at Cavalls del Vent. In 2013 she won the Trail du Colorado in Réunion. She returned to Transvulcania in 2014 and won again in 8:10:41. Her first 100-miler was the 2014 Bear 100 in Utah, which she won in 20:59:24. The race qualified her for Hardrock, and she won there in 2015 in 28:22:47. She retained the title in 2016 in 29:02:09 and was fourth in 2017. In 2015 she and Missy Gosney also completed the Nolan's 14 line in Colorado. Merrell and Icebreaker are among her sponsors. A middle-grade book about her, Fearless Frosty by Chloe Chick, opened the SisuGirls series in 2015. - [Rob Molke: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rob-molke): Runners / Rob Molke RM 🇺🇸 UTMB Index 824 Film My Run 🇺🇸 Rob Molke Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 824 (9 November 2026) Rob Molke is an American trail and ultra runner. He races everything from 25km to 100 miles, and his General UTMB Index stands at 824. His record shows steady progress since 2023, when he was still finishing well down the field at the bigger mountain events. His biggest result came at the Javelina 100 Mile on 31 October 2026. He won the men's race in 12:11:30. Will Murray's course record, run in 2025, stands at 12:10:12, so Molke missed it by 78 seconds. The race covers five loops in McDowell Mountain Regional Park, near Fountain Hills in Arizona, with 1,919m of climb. Heavy rain the night before left the trails muddy. Molke had failed to finish there the year before. At mile 83.7 he was third, almost five minutes behind the leader, Noah Dusseau. He was still 58 seconds down at Jackass Junction, mile 90.2, but passed Dusseau soon afterwards and won by 1min 27sec. He first ran the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in 2025, having got in with a single lottery ticket. He finished 16th in 18:12:33 over 162km and 5,790m of climb. In 2026 he was second at The Big Alta 100K in 8:38:12, a course with 3,885m of climb. He was also second in the Superior Fall Trail Race marathon in 3:48:25 and second in the Afton Trail Run 25km in 1:40:46. That Afton time was 16min 51sec faster than when he finished eighth there in 2023. Other results include fourth at the Desert RATS 50K in 2025 in 4:01:45, 13th at the Grindstone 100K in 2024 in 12:01:57, and fourth at the Wild Duluth 50K in 2023 in 4:51:53. Seven races hand out Golden Tickets to the 2027 Western States 100, and Javelina came second on that calendar. The leading two men and leading two women each earn an entry. His win means Molke will be back on the Western States start line in 2027, this time without needing the lottery. - [Jennifer Lichter: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jennifer-lichter): Runners / Jennifer Lichter Photo: Meghan Hicks / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Jennifer Lichter Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 849 (9 November 2026) Jennifer Lichter is an American ultrarunner based in Missoula, Montana. She took a job as a hiking guide in Glacier National Park in 2020, and it was there that she found trail running, saying the terrain grabbed her and left her wanting to go further than hiking allowed. She began racing in the autumn of 2021, at the Rut in Big Sky, Montana. Lichter trains alongside a close-knit group of women runners near Missoula. Before stepping up to 100 miles she finished fourth at the 2023 Trail World Championships, won the JFK 50 Mile, and in February 2026 set a course record at the Black Canyon 100k, then her longest race. Her 100-mile debut came at the 2026 Western States 100, and she won it outright. She ran a patient race, holding back when Riley Brady took an early lead at Dusty Corners, then pushed through the canyon section to Devil's Thumb, where her climbing strength put her in front. She power hiked the steep climbs of the closing miles on her coach's plan, and only realised how close she was to the course record on the climb out of Robie, near the finish. Lichter crossed the line in 15 hours 28 minutes and 5 seconds, 14 minutes and 9 seconds clear of Brady in second. It beat Courtney Dauwalter's 2023 course record by 88 seconds and was her second course record of the year, after Black Canyon. Commentator Dylan Bowman called it one of the best performances in the 53-year history of Western States. - [Ann Trason: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ann-trason): Runners / Ann Trason Photo: photographer unknown 🇺🇸 Ann Trason Born 1960 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) Ann Trason is an American ultrarunner from Auburn, California, born in 1960. She set 20 world records between 40 and 100 miles. When she entered the American Ultrarunning Hall of Fame in 2020, many rated her the most successful woman the sport has had. Her first ultra was the American River 50 Miler in 1985, at 24. She won it and set a course record. In 1991 she ran 5:40:18 for 50 miles, a world record that lasted until 2015. Western States made her name, though not straight away. She failed to finish her first two attempts and only won in 1989. She went on to win it 14 times, the last in 2003. Her 17:37:51 from 1994 stood as the women's course record for 18 years. In 1996 and 1997 she won the Comrades Marathon in South Africa and then Western States 12 days later. Her 18:06:24 at Leadville in 1994 was the women's record there until 2025. She stepped away for a decade and returned to the sport in 2013, crewing for others and racing now and then. She continued that form into 2026, winning the TERREX Lake Sonoma 100K, the Centurion Hundred Hills 50K and the North Cornwall Ultra Marathon. She represented Great Britain at the 2023 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, finishing 18th woman in the long trail race. She signed a professional contract with adidas running in early 2026. - [Cody Poskin: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/cody-poskin): Runners / Cody Poskin Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Cody Poskin Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 851 (9 November 2026) Cody Poskin is an American trail and ultra runner whose results run from 50 km to beyond 400 km. He holds a general UTMB Index of 805. His record covers mountain 100-milers, desert 100 km races and the Cocodona 250. His best-known result came at Kodiak Ultra Marathons by UTMB, where he won the 100-mile race in 16:46:21. The race left the Rim Nordic Ski Area at 1 p.m. on a Friday. Poskin arrived at Big Bear Lake, California, at 5:46 on the Saturday morning. Runner-up Alex Proctor came home in 17:23:05, a gap of 36:44. Max Jolliffe completed an all-American podium in 18:15:45. Cocodona has been the other fixture. In 2025 he finished seventh man in 71:11:53 over 413 km and 12,395 m of climb. He returned in 2026 and took second place in 58:13:44 on a 408 km course with 11,824 m of ascent. That was almost 13 hours faster than the year before. His earlier record includes a win at the 2023 Midstate Massive Ultra Trail, 159 km with 3,580 m of climb, in 19:47:08. In 2024 he was 12th man at the Leadville Trail 100 Run in 19:28:46 and 30th at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 9:09:58. He went back to Black Canyon in 2026 and improved to 13th in 8:23:38. The 2026 season also brought a win at the Avalon Benefit 50K in 3:36:20 and 12th man at the Broken Arrow Skyrace 46K in 4:38:04. Within the UTMB World Series, Kodiak holds Major status for the Americas. Its top ten finishers of each sex earned automatic places at the 2027 Finals, and Poskin's win put him among them. - [Kirsty Skye Dickson: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kirsty-skye-dickson): Runners / Kirsty Skye Dickson 🇬🇧 Kirsty Skye Dickson Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 768 (9 November 2026) Kirsty Skye Dickson is a Scottish mountain runner who represents Great Britain and Northern Ireland, with a UTMB index of 764. Outside sport she is training as an orthodontist, dividing her working week between Fife and Dundee. She races for Carnethy under the guidance of mountain running coach Angela Mudge and does much of her training around Edinburgh's Arthur's Seat. Originally from Aberdeenshire, near Banchory, she grew up for a time in Calgary before returning to Scotland. In 2025 she finished third at the WMRA World Cup final held in Slovenia, having taken the British Mountain Running Trials uphill title that same August. Three years earlier she had earned her GB and NI vest for the first time, helping the squad to gold at the European Off-Road Running Championships. In 2026 she was third at both the Marathon du Mont-Blanc's 23km race and the Transvulcania half marathon, and finished 14th at Sierre-Zinal. She won the Castle Peak 100K in 2021 in 13:46:27, then took the Valhöll Argentina Advance 80K in 2023. That year she also won the Speedgoat Mountain Races 50K and the Broken Arrow Skyrace 46K, and finished third over 100 km at the CCC at UTMB Mont-Blanc, in 12:38:05. In 2024 she won both the Kodiak Ultra Marathons 50K and the Desert RATS Trail Running Festival 50K, and placed third at the Javelina Jundred over 31 km. She was second at the Broken Arrow Skyrace 46K in 2025 and fourth at the Tarawera Ultra-Trail's 103 km race. She opened 2026 with a second place at MIUT Legend, Madeira's 110 km race, in 15:50:00, and a sixth place at Val d'Aran's Peades d'Aigua. - [Hal Koerner: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/hal-koerner): Runners / Hal Koerner Photo: Kbertilson / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Hal Koerner Born 1976 Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) UTMB Index 571 (9 November 2026) Hal Koerner is an American ultrarunner who won the Western States 100 in 2007 and 2009 and the Hardrock 100 in 2012. He was born in Morgantown, West Virginia, on 23 January 1976. He owns Rogue Valley Runners, a running shop in Ashland, Oregon, and has completed more than 150 ultramarathons. UTMB's records show him 17th at Western States in 2001, eighth in 2003 and third in 2004. He won it in 16:12:16 in 2007 and again in 16:24:55 in 2009. He also won the Angeles Crest 100 in 2006 and 2008 and the Canadian Death Race in 2010. He is one of the runners followed in JB Benna's documentary Unbreakable: The Western States 100. Koerner was third at Hardrock in 2005 and came back to win it in 24:50:00 in 2012. That February he won the Rocky Raccoon 100 in 13:24:52. He took the Javelina Jundred in 2011 and 2013, running 13:47:43 the first time. He has held the fastest known times on the Colorado Trail and the John Muir Trail. While training for UTMB in 2014 he tore the meniscus in his right knee and needed surgery. He was racing again in 2015, when he finished second in the Umstead 50. His book, Hal Koerner's Field Guide to Ultrarunning, came out with VeloPress in 2014. He directs the Pine to Palm 100 Mile and the Siskiyou Out Back Trail Run Festival, both in southern Oregon. - [Katie Schide: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/katie-schide): Runners / Katie Schide Photo: Bastou83 / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Katie Schide Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 860 (9 November 2026) Katie Schide is an American trail and mountain runner, born on 24 January 1992 in Gardiner, Maine. As a child she was a keen hiker and played field hockey, and she later took jobs at huts in the White Mountains. She read geology at Middlebury College, then took up trail racing while studying for a master's at the University of Utah. She went on to complete a PhD in geology at ETH Zurich in 2022, studying landslides and erosion caused by earthquakes. She moved to the French Alps in 2019 and has lived since in the small village of Saint-Dalmas-le-Selvage, and also races skimo alongside ultramarathons. Schide has won some of the biggest 100-mile races in the sport, including UTMB, the Diagonale des Fous on Reunion Island, the Western States 100 and the Hardrock 100. In 2024 she broke the UTMB women's course record. Her time, 22 hours 9 minutes and 31 seconds, was 21 minutes quicker than the mark Courtney Dauwalter had set. In 2025 she broke the Hardrock 100 counter-clockwise women's record too. Her time of 25 hours 50 minutes and 23 seconds was again 21 minutes quicker than Dauwalter's previous mark, making her the first woman to finish Hardrock in under 26 hours. She was busy elsewhere that year too, winning the long trail at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships and the Madeira Island Ultra-Trail, and finishing second at Sierre-Zinal. - [Rui Ueda: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rui-ueda): Runners / Rui Ueda Photo: UTMB profile 🇯🇵 Rui Ueda Country 🇯🇵 Japan Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 907 (9 November 2026) Rui Ueda is a Japanese trail and skyrunner with a general UTMB index of 909, among the highest in the men's field. He has been racing since at least 2013, when he ran the Hasetsune Cup in Japan. He kept winning into 2026, taking the Xtrail Kenting 50K in Taiwan and the Central Alps Skyline Japan race outright. In 2024 he won the Chiangmai Thailand HMONG 50 in northern Thailand, then came back to finish second there a year later. He also won the TSAIGU 50 in Taiwan in 2024 and the Hasetsune 30K in Japan in 2025. On the wider UTMB circuit Ueda placed second in the UTMB Mont Blanc ETC in 2022 and second in the UTMB CCC in 2016. He won the Ultra-Trail Kosciuszko in Australia in 2023, and has taken the Hasetsune Cup itself, Japan's best known trail race, twice, in 2014 and 2017. - [Antonio Martinez Perez: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/antonio-martinez-perez): Runners / Antonio Martinez Perez Photo: UTMB profile 🇪🇸 Antonio Martinez Perez Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 915 (9 November 2026) Antonio Martinez Perez is a Spanish trail and skyrunner with a UTMB index of 916, among the highest in this batch. He has raced consistently across Spain and Europe since at least 2019, with dozens of top-three finishes on his record. He was runner-up at the OCC race at UTMB Mont-Blanc twice, in 2022 and 2023, and won the Cortina Skyrace at the Lavaredo Ultra Trail in 2022. He also won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail's Cortina Trail race outright in 2021. In 2024 he won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail's 50K race and the Marathon des Causses at the Festival Des Templiers, and finished third at that year's OCC. He also placed 13th in the short trail race at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. He remains a frequent winner into 2026, taking the Kaçkar 50K in Turkey, the Montée du Nid d'Aigle near Mont Blanc, and the Centurion South Downs Way 50km in England. - [Ian Sharman: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ian-sharman): Runners / Ian Sharman Photo: iRunFar 🇬🇧 Ian Sharman Born 1980 (age 45 or 46) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 692 (9 November 2026) Ian Sharman is a British-American ultrarunner, coach and podcaster based in Bend, Oregon. Born on 30 August 1980, he won the Leadville Trail 100 four times between 2013 and 2017. In 2013 he ran the fastest Grand Slam of Ultrarunning on record. He also writes for UltraRunning Magazine. Sharman's early ultras came in Europe. He raced the Swissalpine K78 in 2008 and 2009 and the Marathon du Mont-Blanc in 2009. In 2010 he was fourth at the EcoTrail de Paris 80 km. He won the Rocky Raccoon 100 in 2011 in 12:44:33, and again in 2015 and 2016. The 2013 Grand Slam took in four 100-mile races over one summer. He was fourth at Western States and fourth at Vermont, then won Leadville in 16:30:03. Second place at Wasatch completed the set in a combined 69:49:38. He went on to win Leadville again in 2015, 2016 and 2017. Western States has been a fixture of his calendar. He finished in the top ten every year from 2010 to 2018, with fourth places in 2013 and 2018. His fastest run there was 15:47:50 in 2014. He once held nine Guinness world records for the fastest marathons run in costume. He still races in Oregon and won the Smith Rock Ascent 50K in 2022. - [Christian Allen: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/christian-allen): Runners / Christian Allen Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Christian Allen Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 933 (9 November 2026) Christian Allen is an American mountain and trail runner known online as Slim the Runner. He carries a UTMB Index of 933. He grew up in Utah with the Wasatch Mountains close by. He studied at Weber State University, near the trails he later raced on. He built his trail base over summers spent training for cross country. Allen races on the road as well as in the mountains. He has run a 2:10 marathon and says the two disciplines reinforce each other. Road speed helps him on flatter trail sections. Trail strength and endurance carry over into his road form. He told iRunFar he won three US national titles in 2024 across the mountain and trail disciplines. He won the 2025 Broken Arrow Ascent, which doubled as a qualifier for the US team at the World Mountain Running Championships. He trains in Utah alongside professional runners including Clayton Young, Conner Mantz and Kenneth Rooks. He caps most of his racing at around 50 kilometres, saying his leg speed holds up to roughly that distance but not much further. He races the Golden Trail World Series most seasons and aims for its October final. His results include a win at the Trail des Celtes in Alsace in 2026 and the Speedgoat 50K in 2023. He was sixth at Sierre-Zinal in 2026, an improvement on 21st there the year before. - [Mark Nendick: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mark-nendick): Runners / Mark Nendick MN 🇨🇦 UTMB Index 463 Film My Run 🇨🇦 Mark Nendick Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 463 (9 November 2026) Mark Nendick is a Canadian trail and ultra runner whose results lean towards long, hilly courses. He holds a general UTMB Index of 463. His record is built on mountain races of 50 km and upwards, and more recently on the hourly loops of backyard ultra. He first appears on the Canadian Death Race 118K in 2023. That course covers 118 km with 4,543 m of climb, and he finished in 22:27:09 as 83rd man. A year later he stepped up to the Fatdog 120 Mile, a 199 km route with 8,670 m of ascent. He took 44:09:52 to finish and was 44th man. His 2025 season showed clear progress. He went back to the Canadian Death Race and ran 20:36:56, finishing 62nd man and cutting 1:50:13 from his 2023 time. He also ran the 50 km Run for Water Trail Race, which has 2,570 m of climb, and placed 11th man in 9:10:11. In 2026 he was picked for Canada's team of 15 at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championships. Canada's runners raced on the B.C. Backyard Ultra course in Sicamous, British Columbia, where a 6.706 km loop starts every hour. Racing began on a Saturday. When it moved into a third day on the Monday, Nendick was one of seven Canadians still going, with eight of his teammates already out. Canada was sixth in the world at that point. - [Tom Evans: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/tom-evans): Runners / Tom Evans Photo: iRunFar/Eszter Horanyi 🇬🇧 Tom Evans Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 952 (9 November 2026) Tom Evans is a British ultra-trail runner with a general UTMB Index of 952, racing for the ASICS Trail Team. He won UTMB itself in 2025, finishing in 19:18:58. He also won the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in 2023, in 14:40:22. Two years earlier he had already reached the UTMB podium, taking third in 2022. His breakthrough came at the Marathon des Sables in 2017, where he finished third in his first major ultra. The following year he won UTMB's CCC race in 10:44:32. In 2025 he also won the Tenerife Bluetrail's 110K and the Arc of Attrition's 50-mile race. He has been racing since at least 2017. - [Ionel Cristian Manole: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ionel-cristian-manole): Runners / Ionel Cristian Manole Photo: UTMB profile 🇪🇸 Ionel Cristian Manole Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 903 (9 November 2026) Ionel Cristian Manole is a mountain and ultra runner racing for Spain, with a UTMB Index of 904 built over a long career of results since 2018. His biggest win came at the Val d'Aran by UTMB's VDA race in 2021, a 163 km course with almost 10,700 metres of climbing, which he won outright in 23:56:26. He has since become a leading figure on the Chinese ultra circuit, winning the Nike ACG Ultra-Trail Chongli 168 in 2025 in 20:45:34 before finishing second there in 2026, and won the Ultra-Trail Ninghai UTNH105 in 2025 in 10:37:31 after finishing fifth the year before. On the Canary Islands circuit he has been a regular podium finisher at Transgrancanaria, third in 2024 and fourth in 2025 over its Classic distance, and has raced Transvulcania multiple times, taking fourth in both 2023 and 2024. His deepest test came at the Tor des Géants in the Aosta Valley, where he finished sixth in 2019 in 85:35:45 over 358 km and more than 25,000 metres of climbing, having placed 122nd there the year before. In 2023 he was 19th at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' Trail Long in Innsbruck-Stubai. - [Despoina Simantrakou: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/despoina-simantrakou): Runners / Despoina Simantrakou DS 🇬🇷 UTMB Index 614 Film My Run 🇬🇷 Despoina Simantrakou Country 🇬🇷 Greece Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 614 (9 November 2026) Despoina Simantrakou is a Greek ultra runner who races for Kasimis Training. Her results on the UTMB database run from 2016 to 2026. They range from 20km mountain races to 100-mile courses. Her general UTMB Index stands at 614. In September 2026 she added a different kind of result, winning the Spartathlon from Athens to Sparta. Her first listed race was the 20km at the Metsovo Ursa Trail in 2016. She finished 58th woman in 3:03:08. Two years later she ran the same distance in 2:14:39 for fourth. In 2018 she also won the Intersport Ellinikon Cross Country Race, 51km with 2,260m of climb, in 6:55:27. The following year brought victory at the Ultra Pelion Trail 80K. She covered the 81km and 4,040m of ascent in 12:50:34. That season she was also third at the Zagori TeRA 80km and third at EcoTrail Florence 80K. In 2020 she returned to Metsovo for the 103km Ultra Ursa Trail and was second woman in 15:19:15. The longer races followed. In 2021 she was second woman at the Virgin Forest Trail, 161km with 7,320m of climb, in 28:54:41. She took third at the TDS, listed at 55km with 3,700m of ascent, in 7:42:17. She was also third at the 102km Olympus Mythical Trail in 19:48:45. In 2022 she finished third woman at the Nice 100M, a 167km course with 9,070m of climb, in 38:51:53. In 2023 she reached the start of the UTMB Mont Blanc race itself. She completed the 171km and 9,963m of ascent in 31:57:08 for 26th woman. That year she was also second at the Trail du Saint-Jacques Grand Trail 100K, a 75km race, in 9:15:56, and won the 31km Rogkas race at the Olympus Mythical Trail in 4:55:39. Metsovo remains a fixture. She won the 41km Ursa Trail there in 2025 in 5:11:11, on a course with 2,890m of climb. In 2026 she was 21 seconds quicker, in 5:10:50, but finished second. Seven years earlier she had been eighth on a 42km version of the route in 5:56:47. Her 2026 season has also included a win at the Kissavos Marathon Race, 40km with 2,610m of climb, in 5:39:34. At the Chianti Ultra Trail by UTMB she was 17th woman over 119km and 5,121m of ascent in 15:06:32. Her biggest result came at the 44th Spartathlon, which left the foot of the Acropolis at 07:00 on Saturday 26 September 2026. The field of 397 runners from 51 countries started in rain, and showers came back through the day. Simantrakou reached the statue of King Leonidas in Sparta, 244.7km from the start, after 24:45:43. No Greek woman had taken the title before her. Her winning time was said to be a record for the women's race. The Czech runner Radka Churaňová spent long stretches in front and had to settle for second place. Lemonia Panagiotou, another Greek, was third in 26:58:04. - [Theres Leboeuf: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/theres-leboeuf): Runners / Theres Leboeuf Photo: UTMB profile 🇨🇭 Theres Leboeuf Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 781 (9 November 2026) Theres Leboeuf is a Swiss mountain runner for Compressport/Lowa, with a UTMB Index of 781. She has raced Sierre-Zinal every year from 2016 to 2026, finishing as high as 11th in 2017, and has won the Tour des Alpages three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026. She has also won the Jungfrau-Marathon, in 2023, after finishing 2nd and 3rd there in earlier years. Leboeuf's best result at a global championship came at the 2023 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Innsbruck-Stubai, where she finished 3rd in the short trail race. She was 3rd at Zegama-Aizkorri the same year and 2nd at the Eiger Ultra Trail by UTMB E51 Panorama Trail in 2025. In 2026 she finished 10th at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC, a 107km race with 6,200m of climbing. - [Kilian Jornet: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kilian-jornet): Runners / Kilian Jornet Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇪🇸 Kilian Jornet Born 1987 (age 38 or 39) Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 947 (9 November 2026) Kilian Jornet is a Spanish trail runner and ski mountaineer, born in Sabadell in Catalonia in 1987. He has won the Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc, Western States, Hardrock and the Grand Raid on Réunion. His general UTMB Index is 947. He grew up in a mountain hut in the Pyrenees, where his father was the keeper and a mountain guide. By five he had climbed Aneto, the highest peak in the range. His first UTMB win came in 2008, in 20:56:59. He won again in 2009 and 2011, and a fourth time in 2022 in 19:49:30. Hardrock has been almost as kind, with wins in 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2022. He also won Western States in 2011. The shorter classics suit him too. Sierre-Zinal and Zegama keep coming back to him, and in 2024 he won both again. Away from racing he chases speed records. In 2013 he went up and down the Matterhorn from Breuil-Cervinia in 2 hours 52 minutes, and Mont Blanc from Chamonix in 4 hours 57 minutes. He has lived in Norway since 2016. - [Riley Brady: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/riley-brady): Runners / Riley Brady Photo: iRunFar/Meghan Hicks 🇺🇸 Riley Brady Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 826 (9 November 2026) Riley Brady is an American ultra-runner with more than a decade of results on US trails, from 50km races up to the 100-mile distance. Her UTMB Index is 826. Her best finish at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run came in 2026, when she placed 2nd woman in 15:42:14, an improvement on 14th in 2023. She has won several of the biggest ultra-distance races in the US, including the Javelina Jundred 100 Miles in 2024 in 14:19:01, after finishing 2nd there in 2022 and 3rd in 2023. She won the Run Rabbit Run 100 Hare and the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 2025, the Gorge Waterfalls 100K in 2023, and the Vermont 100 Endurance Race's 100K distance in 2022. She opened 2026 with a win at the Canyons Endurance Runs by UTMB's 100K, before her runner-up finish at Western States and 13th place at the full UTMB in Chamonix, a 174km race with 9,700m of climbing. - [Thomas Cardin: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/thomas-cardin): Runners / Thomas Cardin Photo: Eszter Horanyi / iRunFar 🇫🇷 Thomas Cardin Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 933 (9 November 2026) Thomas Cardin is a French trail and ultrarunner with a UTMB index of 934. His results run from 2017 to 2026, mostly on the French trail circuit. They also include a fourth place in 2026 at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in the United States. Cardin has won the SaintéLyon three times, in 2021, 2023 and 2024, and was runner-up in 2022. His fastest win came in 2023, when he ran 05:41:56 over 78 km. In 2024 Cardin also won the Festival Des Templiers' Grand Trail Des Templiers in 06:38:14 and the trail race at the European Off-Road Championships in 04:58:21. Cardin's 2026 season brought four results at distances up to 162 km. He won the Marathon des 3 Vallées in 04:35:03 and the Ultra-Trail des Coursières over 104 km in 09:03:10. He also won the Chianti Ultra Trail by UTMB's Ultra Trail Chianti Castles over 119 km in 09:58:38. He also finished fourth at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in the United States, in 14:07:58. Cardin's early results included wins at the Hivernale des Templiers' Astragale Trail in 2017, the Trail des Forts de Besançon in 2019, and the X-Trail Courchevel 22km in 2020. He also finished fourth at the UTMB OCC in 2021, over 56 km. - [Manuel Merillas: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/manuel-merillas): Runners / Manuel Merillas Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇪🇸 Manuel Merillas Country 🇪🇸 Spain Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 936 (9 November 2026) Manuel Merillas is a Spanish trail and mountain runner from La Cueta in Leon, close to the Picos de Europa. He was born in 1991 and grew up working cattle with his family on the same terrain he now trains on. He carries a UTMB Index of 937. He joined the Spanish army at 18, a life that kept him near the mountains. He moved from football and track into mountain running in his late teens. He has said it took him 14 years to feel like a proper professional in the sport. In 2016 he needed surgery for Achilles tendinitis and spent nearly two years away from racing. He returned gradually, then broke through at the 2021 European Skyrunning Championships, winning the 65 km race by a course record of 83 minutes. He has also won the Travesera Integral Picos de Europa several times, including in 2015, 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2023. Zegama-Aizkorri, one of the sport's toughest mountain marathons, took him longer to crack. He finally won it in 2023, after seven previous attempts stretching back to 2013. He still lives and trains in La Cueta, where he grew up. - [Anna Gibson: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/anna-gibson): Runners / Anna Gibson Photo: Christian David / Wikimedia Commons 🇺🇸 Anna Gibson Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 791 (9 November 2026) Anna Gibson is an American mountain and trail runner from Jackson Hole. As a schoolgirl she picked up 17 Wyoming state titles between track, cross country and Nordic skiing, and still holds the state records for cross country and the 1,600 metres. She later ran distance events for the University of Washington, reaching an Olympic Trials semi final over 1500 metres in 2024. Since turning to the mountains she has become a regular podium finisher on the American and European short-course circuit. She took the win at Gorge Waterfalls 30K in 2025, was third at the Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K that same year having twice finished on the podium there before, and placed third over the steep, thin air of Pikes Peak Ascent in 2023. At the higher end of the sport she has finished sixth twice at Sierre-Zinal, in 2024 and 2026, and eighth in 2025, and took third in the uphill race at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. Her UTMB Index stands at 792. Gibson has doubled up in ski mountaineering, a sport she had only picked up six months earlier when she and Cameron Smith won the mixed relay at the season opener of the 2025-26 ISMF Ski Mountaineering World Cup, the first American pairing to reach a World Cup podium in the discipline. That result carried an Olympic quota place, and she went on to compete for the United States at the 2026 Winter Games. - [Ben Rothery: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ben-rothery): Runners / Ben Rothery Photo: George Foster / Living North 🇬🇧 Ben Rothery Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 881 (9 November 2026) Ben Rothery is an English fell runner based in Ilkley, Yorkshire, who races for Rab and Team VJ. He grew up in the Saddleworth area on the edge of the Peak District and took up fell running after a running club at his sixth form introduced him to the sport. Rothery was crowned England's Fell Running Champion in 2024, having placed third and then second in the two years before that. The English Championship is run over six races split across short, medium and long distances, and Rothery counts his downhill running among his biggest strengths. He has since taken on longer distances too. He won the Three Peaks Race in 2025 in 3:00:00 and the RunThrough Trails Lake District 48K in 2026 in 3:56:31. He also placed 27th at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' Short Trail 45K in 2025. In 2026 Rothery won the 51km Run Through Lakes race, taking the Trail Running Association's British Middle Distance title. The result earned him European Off-Road Championships selection to race in Slovenia, where he finished 21st in the 52km trail event. - [Barry Keem: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/barry-keem): Runners / Barry Keem Photo: Hammer Nutrition 🇦🇺 Barry Keem Country 🇦🇺 Australia Runs Trail & Ultra Barry Keem is an Australian trail and mountain runner from Wollongong in New South Wales. His results run from short, steep mountain races to the hour-by-hour grind of backyard ultras. He was 46 when he raced for Australia at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship, which began on Saturday 17 October. His standout result came at the 2008 Six Foot Track Marathon. Keem was first man over the 45km course, which carries 1,530m of climb, in 3:23:13. Three years earlier he had raced the WMRA world championship event in Wellington. That course was 14km with 930m of ascent, and he finished 45th man in 1:00:26. In 2015 he lined up for the Mount Solitary Ultra, a 47km route with 2,467m of climb. Keem came home sixth man in 5:20:23. The team worlds were staged on his home patch. The Australian race ran at Kembla Grange in the Illawarra, with a 6.706km loop starting every hour from 11pm on the Saturday night. Keem had aimed for 100 loops but stopped after 70 hours. When he went to bed, eight or nine of his teammates were still out on the course. By the time he woke, only two remained. Dan Camac was the last Australian standing with 87 loops, and the team closed on 1,069. - [Scout Adkin: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/scout-adkin): Runners / Scout Adkin Photo: Meghan Hicks / iRunFar 🇬🇧 Scout Adkin Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 800 (9 November 2026) Scout Adkin is a British long-distance and mountain runner from Peebles in Scotland, born on 16 August 1993. She was a competitive swimmer before turning to running. Her brother Jacob Adkin is a fellow mountain runner and was the 2019 European Mountain Running champion. Scout ran her first hill race in 2008 aged fifteen and was UK junior champion in 2011. Adkin studied physiotherapy at Robert Gordon University in Aberdeen, then settled in the Lake District to combine running with physio work. She made her senior Great Britain debut in 2022, at the first European Off-Road Running Championships, held in Spain. She won team gold there and finished fourth individually in the uphill race, the first British runner to do so. She also took individual bronze in the event's up-and-down race. In 2023 Adkin finished third at the World Long Distance Mountain Running Championships. She then won silver in the team uphill race and bronze in the team up-and-down race at that year's World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. She also won the Montemuro Vertical Run in Portugal and the Sky Gran Canaria Vertical race. Adkin won the Mountain Running World Cup in both 2024 and 2025. In 2024 she also took European silver in the uphill race at Annecy, where her brother won silver in the men's event. She retained her World Cup title in 2025 despite missing the season's final races through injury, having already won at Bukovina's Zmeu X-Fest and Poland's Tatra Fest. - [Jiaju Zhao: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jiaju-zhao): Runners / Jiaju Zhao Photo: Kailas Fuga / iRunFar 🇨🇳 Jiaju Zhao Country 🇨🇳 China Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 898 (9 November 2026) Jiaju Zhao is a Chinese trail runner, 31, who races for the Kailas Fuga team. In September 2026 he won the Tor des Géants, a single-stage race of roughly 336 kilometres around Italy's Aosta Valley, in 65 hours 55 minutes and 22 seconds. He became the first runner from China to win the event, finishing 13 minutes quicker than the previous course record set by Victor Richard in 2025. The 2026 edition climbed about 24,000 metres, and with a 150-hour cutoff, competitors must decide for themselves when to stop and sleep. Zhao led from early on and stayed clear for most of the distance. Switzerland's Jonathan Schindler took second place, while Germany's Katharina Hartmuth set a new women's record and finished third overall, 75 minutes behind Zhao. Zhao found the race brutal. Afterwards he spoke of nosebleeds, deep tiredness and pain through the soles of his feet, and said he had resorted to slapping his own face to stay awake. He described it as "a living hell" and ruled out ever racing further than 168 kilometres again. The Aosta Valley win crowned a heavy 2026 season. He had already taken the 170.7 kilometre Chongli race in July and finished runner-up at Japan's Mt. Fuji 100 earlier that year. His long career of wins stretches back through China's biggest ultras, among them the 205km Chongli 168 in 2023, the Jiangnan 100 Mile in 2020, and a runner-up finish over 400km at the Ultra Gobi in 2018. At world and continental championship level she was eighth woman in the Short Trail 45K at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships, and 12th at the 2026 European Athletics Off-Road Running Championships' 52K race. She has also raced Sierre-Zinal and Zegama-Aizkorri. Rharsalla has further wins at the Ultra Sierra Nevada, the Carrera Alto Sil and the 3 Días Trail Ibiza, and was second at the X Trail Las Palomas, part of the Spanish trail running championships, in 2023. - [Gemma Hillier Moses: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/gemma-hillier-moses): Runners / Gemma Hillier Moses Photo: UTMB profile 🇬🇧 Gemma Hillier Moses Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 778 (9 November 2026) Gemma Hillier Moses is a British trail runner who competes for Team Hoka. Her general UTMB index stands at 779, built from a fast rise through European ultras since 2023. She won the Chianti Ultra Trail over 73 km in 2025, then returned in 2026 to place fourth over the longer, 119 km Chianti Castles course. She also took the Arc Of Attrition's 50-mile race in 2026, finishing in 8:12:56, after coming second in its 25-mile event the year before. Hillier Moses has raced the CCC at UTMB Mont-Blanc twice, finishing 22nd in 2025 and 12th in 2026 over a lengthened 107 km course. She was 26th in the shorter OCC there in 2024. Her other wins include the Trail du Saint-Jacques Monistrail 50K in 2026 and two British ultras in 2024, the Ladybower 53K and Tittesworth Water 50K. She was third in the Verbier X-Plore at Trail Verbier St Bernard in both 2023 and 2024. - [Sunmaya Budha: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sunmaya-budha): Runners / Sunmaya Budha Photo: World Trail Majors 🇳🇵 Sunmaya Budha Country 🇳🇵 Nepal Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 813 (9 November 2026) Sunmaya Budha is a trail runner from West Jumla, in Nepal's remote western mountains. She first showed promise at school, finishing second in a 1600m race in seventh grade, and her principal picked her out for further competitions. She went on to join a running club based in the town of Jumla Bazaar, training there under coach Hari Bahadur Rokaya. Budha signed with the Kailas FUGA team in 2024. By then she was ranked eighth in the world over 100km and was Nepal's top-ranked female trail runner. She has called her second place at the UTMB CCC in 2022 a turning point in her career. In 2025 she finished second at the Trail World Championships Long Trail, then won the Ultra-Trail Cape Town 100k two months later in 12:25:55. Antonina Iushina led the early running over Signal Hill, but Budha took over on the first major climb and pulled away, leading by four and a half minutes at the Platteklip Gorge summit. Her advantage grew to more than 12 minutes by 56km and to almost an hour by 79km. She returned to Europe in 2026 and won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 120km, holding off a strong field to finish in 13 hours 33 minutes and 18 seconds.
