- [Lucy Bartholomew: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lucy-bartholomew): Runners / Lucy Bartholomew Photo: Futureshape / Wikimedia Commons 🇦🇺 Lucy Bartholomew Born 1996 (age 29 or 30) Country 🇦🇺 Australia Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 799 (9 November 2026) Lucy Bartholomew is an Australian ultrarunner born on 20 May 1996 in Melbourne. Her father, Ash Bartholomew, is also an ultrarunner and introduced her to trail running early. At 15 she ran her first 100 kilometre ultramarathon alongside him, finishing in about twelve and a half hours. She races for Salomon. She broke through as a teenager, winning races over mountain and trail terrain. In 2017 she won both Ultra-Trail Australia 100K and Ultra-Trail Cape Town 100K, and was runner-up at the 80K Marathon du Mont-Blanc. A year later she took third at Western States, the prestigious 100-mile race held each year in California. In 2023 she completed the full UTMB in Chamonix in 27:39:23, finishing 10th. That year she also completed her first Ironman triathlon, at Ironman Western Australia, placing fourth in her category, which earned her a place at the Ironman World Championship. She went on to complete both UTMB and the Ironman World Championship in the same year, finishing Kona in 10:43:41. That made her only the second woman to do both in one season. Her personal bests include 10:01:06 for 100 kilometres on trail, set at the 2025 Tarawera Ultramarathon, and 17:13:27 for 100 miles, set at Tarawera in 2023. She has also run a 2:47:06 marathon, in Brisbane in 2026. She continues to race at the top level, finishing 7th at the UTMB in both 2025 and 2026. - [Richard Mcdowell: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/richard-mcdowell): Runners / Richard Mcdowell RM 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Richard Mcdowell Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Richard Mcdowell is a British ultra runner. His recorded results come from long races at distances from 70 km to 161 km. He has four results on record, from 2021 and 2022, and he was first man in every one. His first listed win came at the Centurion South Downs Way 50 in 2021. He covered the 78 km course, with 1,770 m of climb, in 6:02:19. The same year he also ran the Centurion Thames Path 100. That race runs 161 km with 3,210 m of climb, and he finished first man in 13:43:42. In 2022 he won Country to Capital, a 70 km race with 820 m of climb, in 4:57:27. He also took the Centurion South Downs Way 100, recorded at 151 km with 3,160 m of climb. His winning time was 14:49:35. That was more than an hour slower than his Thames Path run despite the shorter listed distance. No results after 2022 appear on his record, and he has no current UTMB Index. His four wins remain the full extent of what is publicly listed. She has competed since 2015. She won the 23km Marathon du Mont-Blanc in both 2015 and 2016, and added wins that year at Zegama-Aizkorri, the Arctic Triple Lofoten Ultra-Trail and the BUFF Epic Trail Aigüestortes. 2019 was a breakout year, with wins at the K42 Canarias K42 and vertical races, the Transvulcania half marathon, Innsbruck's K25 and the Trail Cap de Creus. She also finished second at the Pikes Peak Marathon, the Aspen Backcountry Marathon and the Tromsø Skyrace's Tromsdalstind race that year. She was runner-up at Madeira's MIUT 85 in 2021, and again at the Transvulcania Ultramarathon in 2022. In 2023 she won the UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC over 100km, the Kullamannen Seventh Seal and the Tromsø skyrace Hamperokken. She finished fifth at the Western States 100-Mile Endurance Run in 2024. In 2025 she won the Stranda Fjord Trail Race, and was runner-up at the Lavaredo Ultra Trail's 80km race and the 58km race at Ultra-Trail Snowdonia. Her 2026 season has brought a win at the 107km UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC, another at Molde 7 Peaks, and second place over 119km at the Chianti Ultra Trail. - [Jasmin Paris: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jasmin-paris): Runners / Jasmin Paris Photo: Paul Dobson / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Jasmin Paris Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra (legend) UTMB Index 611 (9 November 2026) Jasmin Paris is a British fell and ultrarunner, and a senior lecturer in veterinary studies at the University of Edinburgh. She was appointed MBE in 2024 for services to fell and long-distance running. She dominated British fell running through the 2010s. She won the Three Peaks Race, the Isle of Jura Fell Race and the Ennerdale Horseshoe among others, and took the Scottish Hill Running Championship in 2014 and 2015. She added the British Fell Running Championship title in 2015 and 2018. In 2015 she also set a women's record at the Fellsman and was the first female finisher, second overall, in the five-day Dragon's Back Race across Wales. In 2016 Paris broke three of Britain's biggest mountain running records within six months. She ran the Bob Graham Round in 15:24 that April, more than two and a half hours faster than the previous women's record. The mark stood until Beth Pascall lowered it in 2020. In June she ran the Ramsay Round in 16:13, an outright record for anyone regardless of sex, which held until 2019. In October she added the women's record for the Paddy Buckley Round, in 18:33. In January 2019 she became the first woman to win the Spine Race outright. She completed the 268-mile route along the Pennine Way in 83 hours 12 minutes and 23 seconds, beating the previous men's course record by around 12 hours. Paris set a women's record for the most Munros climbed inside 24 hours, running a 29-summit circuit of the Cairngorms in July 2021. She went on to win the Ultra Tour Monte Rosa in Switzerland later that year. Paris then took on the Barkley Marathons, and in March 2024 she became its first female finisher. She completed the notoriously brutal course in 59 hours 58 minutes and 21 seconds, just 99 seconds inside the cut-off. - [Elle Twentyman: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/elle-twentyman): Runners / Elle Twentyman Photo: Harrier Run Free 🇬🇧 Elle Twentyman Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 731 (9 November 2026) Elle Twentyman is a British mountain runner who switched from triathlon and road racing to the trails in 2023. After being knocked down and trampled at the start of the Valencia 10km, she suffered a series of injuries that kept her out of racing for most of that year. During her recovery she moved back to her mother's home and began running the trails nearby, and never really looked back. Her first senior fell race came at the Edale Skyline in 2025, where she won outright and set a new course record. Weeks later she qualified for the European Mountain Running Championships in Annecy in her first ever mountain race, competing in the Uphill Only event. She won a silver medal there as part of the Great Britain team. Twentyman has since raced across the WMRA and UTMB circuits, finishing 1st at the Skyline Scotland Ben Nevis Skyline in 2025. In 2026 she placed 5th at the Vauban Mountain Trail Grand Parcours and 16th at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc ETC. She is sponsored by New Balance and coaches other runners alongside her own racing. - [Joyline Chepngeno: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/joyline-chepngeno): Runners / Joyline Chepngeno Photo: Christian David / Wikimedia Commons 🇰🇪 Joyline Chepngeno Country 🇰🇪 Kenya Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 806 (9 November 2026) Joyline Chepngeno is a Kenyan trail runner who races for the Milimani Runners club. She ran track as a young athlete, then stepped away from the sport. She later lost about 30 kilograms and decided to return to running. Her first trail race was the 2024 Sierre-Zinal. She led from the start and extended her advantage throughout, winning by more than eight minutes in 2:54:06. It was a breakthrough iRunFar described as a shock. She followed it with victory at that year's Golden Trail World Series final in Ascona-Locarno. In 2025 she won the Marathon du Mont-Blanc and finished third at the Restonica Trail 50K. She also won that year's Sierre-Zinal and the OCC at the UTMB World Series Final, though both results were later struck from her record. The Athletics Integrity Unit ruled that a sample taken after the 2025 Sierre-Zinal contained triamcinolone acetonide, a banned corticosteroid. It banned her for two years from 8 September 2025 and disqualified her results from 9 August 2025 onward, including that Sierre-Zinal win and the OCC win. Chepngeno said she had received a knee injection in July 2025 without knowing it contained a banned substance. - [Marie Nivet: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/marie-nivet): Runners / Marie Nivet Photo: Nike ACG 🇫🇷 Marie Nivet Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 773 (9 November 2026) Marie Nivet is a French skyrunner with a UTMB Index of 773, who has built her results on short, steep races around the French Riviera and on the international mountain running circuit. In 2026 she won the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc ETC in 1:34:20, finished 18th woman at Sierre-Zinal and ninth at the European Athletics Off-Road Running Championships' up and down race over 13 km. In 2025 she was second woman at the Ultra-trail Cape Town Explorer 23, 11th at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' classic 14K, and seventh at both the Golfo dell'Isola and the Jinshanling Great Wall Trail Race in China. She won three races in 2024, the Mimo Trail, the Trail du Soleil Levens 15K and the Nice Côte d'Azur by UTMB's 20K around Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat, and took her first UTMB win in 2023 at the Ardennes-Mégatrail's Crêtes De Semoy race. - [Kate Avery: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/kate-avery): Runners / Kate Avery Photo: Rory / Wikimedia Commons 🇬🇧 Kate Avery Born 1991 (age 34 or 35) Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 735 (9 November 2026) Kate Avery is a British runner from Bishop Auckland who built her early career on the track and in cross country. Running for Iona College in the United States, she led the 2014 NCAA Division I Cross Country Championship from start to finish, the first time a British woman had taken that individual title. She also won the Honda Sports Award that year as the outstanding female collegiate cross country runner in America. At senior level Avery took silver at the European Cross Country Championships in both 2014 and 2015, helping the Great Britain women's team to gold on both occasions. She made her England debut at the 2014 Commonwealth Games, finishing fourth in the 10,000 metres in a personal best of 32:33.35. She went on to represent Great Britain at the World Cross Country Championships in 2019, finishing 30th in Aarhus. After more than a decade on the track and in cross country, Avery moved into mountain and trail running. Just a couple of seasons after her first Great Britain mountain running vest, she won the Ultra-Trail Australia UTA50 in 2024, a 50 kilometre UTMB World Series race with over 2,200 metres of climbing. The win came little more than a year after she had first tried racing at ultra distance, underlining the range she had shown throughout her career. Avery has gone on to win the Buffalo Stampede's Bright 20km SkyRun in 2023 and 2024 and its 42km SkyMarathon in 2026. She also won the Grampians Peaks Trail GPT50 in 2023 and the Ultra-Trail Kosciuszko Kosci50 in 2024. Her UTMB Index of 727 reflects a fast and successful switch from the track to the trails. - [Martin Anthamatten: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/martin-anthamatten): Runners / Martin Anthamatten Photo: Johann Conus / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇭 Martin Anthamatten Born 1984 (age 41 or 42) Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 901 (9 November 2026) Martin Anthamatten was born on 12 September 1984 in Zermatt, Switzerland. He first made his name as a ski mountaineer, joining the Swiss national ski mountaineering team in 2007 after playing ice hockey in the second-tier National League B. As a ski mountaineer he won the Patrouille des Glaciers relay in 2010 alongside Yannick Ecoeur and Florent Troillet, took European Championship relay gold in 2012, and set the course record at the Zermatt-Rothorn mountain race in 2007. Anthamatten later moved into mountain and skyrunning, where he now races for adidas Terrex and holds a UTMB index of 901. He won the Ultra Skymarathon Madeira in 2021 and the Trail des Cabanes in 2022, and has been a regular finisher at Sierre-Zinal since 2011. He is still competing in his forties. In 2024 he won the Matterhorn Ultraks Extreme outright, and in 2026 he won the Swiss Alps 100 Vertical and the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg Trail, a 82km race with 6300m of climbing, in 09:32:39. - [Rowan Boswood: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/rowan-boswood): Runners / Rowan Boswood Photo: Graham Hewitson / Monument Photos 🇬🇧 Rowan Boswood Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 872 (9 November 2026) Rowan Boswood is a British ultrarunner and a member of Carnethy Hill Running Club. He previously raced bicycles for eight years, competing nationally in the UK and spending seasons racing in Spain's Basque Country. After stepping away from competitive sport for over a decade, he entered his first ultramarathon through the Lairig Ghru race in the Cairngorms. Boswood has since won every ultramarathon he has entered, with the Lairig Ghru his sole exception. He has won the West Highland Way Race, a 154 kilometre route from Milngavie to Fort William, and the shorter Highland Fling Race three years running. In 2026 he lowered his own Highland Fling time to 6 hours 46 minutes, the second fastest in the race's history. He trains and races without a coach, drawing on lessons from his cycling career about pacing and effort. Ahead of his fastest Highland Fling run he focused his training on raw speed, aiming to hold form over the closing miles of an ultra. His results across Scottish ultra racing place him among the country's most consistent winners at the distance. - [Mark Dowdle: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/mark-dowdle): Runners / Mark Dowdle Photo: courtesy of Mark Dowdle / Mpls.St.Paul Magazine 🇺🇸 Mark Dowdle Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra Mark Dowdle is an American trail and ultra runner. His recorded results cover 50K and 50-mile trail races in the United States, and he has also run for his country in backyard ultra, the format where runners repeat a 6.706 km loop every hour until only one is left. He has no current UTMB Index. His trail results have been steady rather than spectacular. In 2020 he ran the AZT Oracle Rumble 50K, 53 km with 1,360 m of climb, in 7:16:55 for 30th man. Later that year he finished the Elephant Mountain Trail Runs 50 Mile, 80 km with 1,950 m of climb, in 12:26:20 and fifth place among the men. In 2023 he ran the Wild Duluth 50K, 50 km with 1,264 m of climb, in 4:58:40 for seventh man. His longest effort came at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship. Sixty-seven nations set off together at 12:00 UTC on 17 October, each team of 15 scoring one point for every yard completed. Dowdle ran for the United States on Laz Lake's home course in Tennessee. At 21:09 UTC on 21 October the bell rang for yard 105 and he was still in the race alongside Jon Noll. That meant at least 104 completed yards, or nearly 700 km. Teammate Nicholas Steel had already stopped at 94. At that point the Americans had 1,117 yards and a clear lead. Australia had finished on 1,069 and Japan on 1,038. Belgium, the 2024 champions, were on 1,020 with two runners still out. No final world classification had been confirmed when the figures were reported. Hewitson / Sports for All Pics 🇬🇧 Nicola Reece Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Nicola Reece is a British runner from Wilmslow who races on road and trail in the W40 category. Her results run from a 50km ultra at Ladybower Reservoir to a marathon around Kielder Water. She holds a general UTMB Index of 556. Her biggest win came at the Kielder Marathon in Northumberland on Sunday 4 October. She won the women's race in 3:08:38. The organisers' own timing had her a few seconds quicker, at 3:08:35. Joseph Vis of Kent won the men's race in 2:52:53. Kielder is not a course for fast times. The 26.2-mile route circles Kielder Water, billed as northern Europe's largest man-made lake. It runs on lakeside paths and forest tracks through Kielder Forest, the largest woodland in England. Winning times there are only ever compared with earlier editions of the same race. The weather was mostly sunny, with the odd shower and some strong gusts. It was the 16th running of the event. In 2024 she ran the 50K ultra at the RunThrough Trails Ladybower Reservoir event. The route covered 50km with 1,069m of climb. She finished in 5:35:20 as the 10th woman. - [Caitlin Fielder: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/caitlin-fielder): Runners / Caitlin Fielder Photo: photographer unknown 🇳🇿 Caitlin Fielder Country 🇳🇿 New Zealand Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 811 (9 November 2026) Caitlin Fielder is a trail runner from New Zealand. She came to the sport relatively late, after three years of boxing and a spell playing football at university, taking up running only in 2015. Her first goal was the Old Ghost Ultra, an 85km race in New Zealand. Fielder moved to Spain in 2016, and her training became far more structured once someone there offered to write her a weekly plan. She had a major hip operation in February 2020 that kept her out of running for seven months. She regards 2021, the year after her recovery, as her first serious season of both training and racing. She has been near the front of women's trail racing for most of the years since. She won the Tarawera 50km in both 2020 and 2021, and took the Grand Trail des Templiers in both 2024 and 2025. At the 2026 UTMB CCC she finished fifth, and she was fourth at Western States 100 that year, after finishing eighth there in 2025. Adeline Martin led the women's race at the 2024 Grand Trail des Templiers from the start and still held the lead through 65km. Fielder worked her way into second alongside Norway's Sylvia Nordskar by around 56km. She made her break on the steep drop into Massebiau, at the 70km mark, and went clear of Nordskar to lead for good. Fielder won in 7 hours 42 minutes and 24 seconds, 2.5 minutes clear of Nordskar. - [Katie Asmuth: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/katie-asmuth): Runners / Katie Asmuth Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Katie Asmuth Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 758 (9 November 2026) Katie Asmuth is an American ultra runner with a UTMB Index of 758. She has raced mostly across the western United States since 2018, from 50km trail races up to 100 miles. Her first results of note came that year, with second place at the Angeles Crest 100 Mile in 22:49:12 and second at the Marin Ultra Challenge 50 Miles in 8:42:50. She has been a regular at the Western States 100. She was fifth woman in 2021 in 18:23:24 and ninth in 2022 in 19:30:26. Her best run there came in 2023, when she finished fourth in 17:21:06. In 2019 she won the women's race at the Bear 100 in 23:23:31, over 163km with 6,680m of climb. That same year she won the Zion 100km in 9:57:09 and the Kodiak 50 Miler in 9:40:30. Further wins followed at the Bandera 100km in 2021 in 9:25:00, and at the Black Canyon Ultras 60K in 5:05:57 and the Bishop High Sierra Ultras 55k in 4:48:53, both in 2022. She also took third at the Ultra-Trail Harricana 125K in Canada in 2021. In 2025 she won the Javelina Jundred 100km in 8:32:18 and was 11th woman at the Canyons 100K. Her 2026 season has taken her further afield. She was fifth woman at the Tarawera Ultra-Trail T102 in New Zealand in 9:37:47. She then ran UTMB, 174km with 9,700m of climb around Mont Blanc, and finished 28th woman in 26:49:59. On 31 October she stepped up to the Javelina 100 Mile in McDowell Mountain Regional Park, Arizona. Heavy overnight rain had left mud and small washouts across the five-loop course. Asmuth finished third in 14:06:34, behind Heather Jackson in 13:48:29 and Britain's Carla Molinaro in 13:49:24. Javelina offered Golden Tickets for the 2027 Western States 100 to the top two women only, so third place left her just outside an automatic return. - [Charlotte Redhead: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/charlotte-redhead): Runners / Charlotte Redhead CR 🇬🇧 UTMB Index 600 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Charlotte Redhead Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 600 (9 November 2026) Charlotte Redhead is a British runner who races on road and trail in the north of England. She runs for Heaton and competes in the W40 category. Her General UTMB Index stands at 600. Her most notable win came in the half marathon at the 16th Kielder Marathon on Sunday 4 October. She was the first woman to finish the 13.1-mile race in 88:37, with the organisers' own clock giving her 1:28:34. The event is based at Kielder Water in Northumberland, described as northern Europe's largest man-made lake. The full marathon route runs through Kielder Forest, England's largest woodland. Her clubmate Jacob Garthwaite won the men's half marathon in 74:24, giving Heaton both titles. Steve Cram, the race figurehead, rated the conditions "really good" despite occasional showers and strong gusts. In 2026 she took second place among the women at The Northumbrian Ultra 28K Trail. That course covered 28 km with 400 m of climb, and she completed it in 02:17:11. - [Carla Molinaro: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/carla-molinaro): Runners / Carla Molinaro Photo: Carla Molinaro 🇬🇧 Carla Molinaro Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 720 (9 November 2026) Carla Molinaro is a British ultrarunner and running coach. She spent ten years racing triathlon before switching to running after entering the Glasgow Half Marathon in 2014. She is the reigning 50km World Champion and one of the Comrades Marathon's most consistent overseas competitors. At the 2026 Comrades Marathon she finished 10th among the women in 6:14:04, her fifth Comrades gold medal. She has also finished third in the Comrades Down Run, fourth in its Up Run and third at South Africa's Two Oceans Ultra Marathon. In 2020 she ran the length of the UK over multiple days, a run that led to a sponsorship contract with HOKA. Her trail record is shorter but includes several wins. She took the Magaliesberg Challenge 35km in South Africa in 4:37:29 in 2019 and the 69km Country to Capital in 5:32:33 in 2020. In 2021 she won the Ultra X 125 Scotland in 13:09:13, over 3,513m of climb, and the Spring Trail Series 50km in 4:40:02. The mountains have been harder going. She was 46th woman at the CCC in 2021 in 18:40:01 and 29th at The Canyons 100km in 2022. In 2026 she placed 10th at the Black Canyon Ultras 100K in 9:21:18. Her best 100-mile result came at the Javelina 100 Mile on 31 October 2026. The race covers five loops in McDowell Mountain Regional Park near Fountain Hills, Arizona, with 1,919m of climb, and overnight rain had left the trails muddy. Molinaro took the lead after Des Linden slowed beyond mile 60.3. She was still 3min 21sec ahead of Heather Jackson at mile 95.3, but Jackson passed her late in the dark and the rain. Molinaro finished second in 13:49:24, 55 seconds down. That second place earned her a Golden Ticket to the 2027 Western States 100. Javelina was the second of seven qualifying races, with places for the top two women. - [Reid Burrows: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/reid-burrows): Runners / Reid Burrows Photo: UTMB profile 🇨🇦 Reid Burrows Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 715 (9 November 2026) Reid Burrows is a Canadian trail and ultra runner who came to the sport from triathlon and now races as a professional. Most of his results have come in North America, over distances from 50K to 100 miles. He does not currently hold a UTMB Index. His earliest recorded ultra is the 2019 Sinister 7 Ultra Solo. He covered the 161 km course, with 5,730 m of climbing, in 23:10:56 and placed sixth among the men. He was 15th man at the JFK 50 Mile in 2021 in 6:35:01. A year later he went back and took more than 23 minutes off that time, running 6:11:45 for 14th. In 2022 he also won the Sulphur Springs Trail Race 50K in 3:37:46. He was eighth man at the Crown King Scramble 50K in 5:12:09 and 20th at the Canyons 100K in 10:51:53. At Run Rabbit Run 100 Hare, 163 km with 6,210 m of ascent, he finished eighth man in 20:46:19. His best 100-mile result came at Leadville in 2023. He ran the 162 km course, which climbs 4,230 m, in 20:12:34 to finish eighth man. That season he was also 17th at the Canyons 100K in 11:34:19 and 45th at the Black Canyon 100K in 10:35:26. In 2024 he returned to Black Canyon and ran 9:31:38 for 37th. He was third at Sulphur Springs in 4:08:24 and third at the Sawatch Ascent 50K, 53 km with 2,135 m of climb, in 5:48:45. Leadville went less well the second time. He finished 60th man in 24:20:02. In early October Burrows was runner-up over the Wériga distance at Chihuahua by UTMB, held in Mexico's Copper Canyon. The course ran 94 km from Cerocahui through the canyon, with 4,700 m of climbing, and 67 runners finished. He came home in 13:15:04, about 37 minutes behind the Mexican winner José Luis Nieto Salgado, who ran 12:37:38. Horacio Rangel Ramirez was roughly ten minutes further back in third. It was Burrows's first podium at a UTMB World Series event. The result also guarantees him a start at the CCC in 2027. That is the 100K event at the World Series Finals, and an automatic place there had been his main target. He said the canyon mattered to him just as much. Getting to "run with the Tarahumara" had pulled him south, he said. - [Ben Flanagan: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ben-flanagan): Runners / Ben Flanagan Photo: jenaragon94 / Wikimedia Commons Ben Flanagan Runs Ben Flanagan is a Canadian distance runner from Kitchener, Ontario, born on 11 January 1995. He has raced everything from indoor 3000m to the marathon. He is best known on the roads, where he holds the Canadian records for 5km and 10km and has won the Falmouth Road Race three times. His international career began early. At 16 he placed 16th in the 1500m at the 2011 World Youth Championships in Lille. Two years later he was the first Canadian home in the junior race at the World Cross Country Championships in Bydgoszcz, finishing 34th. He then went to the University of Michigan, coached by the three-time Olympian Kevin Sullivan. His defining college moment came at the 2018 NCAA Division I Outdoor Championships. He caught Alabama's Vincent Kiprop in the closing metres to win the 10,000m in 28:34.53. His delighted post-race interview, in which he asked where his mother was, spread widely online. He won Falmouth the same year. He took the seven-mile race in 32:21, then won it again in 2021 and in 2022, the last in 32:25. He also took the Manchester Road Race in November 2021. On the roads he ran 28:11 at the B.A.A. 10K in 2022 for a Canadian 10km record. At the Valencia Half Marathon that October he was 18th in 1:01:00, a national record that edged Cam Levins by four seconds. In April 2023 he ran 13:26 at the B.A.A. 5K for another Canadian record, second behind his training partner Morgan Beadlescomb. The track brought steady progress too. He was Canadian 10,000m champion in 2019 and Canadian 5000m champion in 2023. That summer he made his first World Athletics Championships, running 13:38.69 for 11th in his 5000m heat. In October 2023 he was 12th in 13:34 in the first 5km road race at the World Road Running Championships in Riga. In January 2024 he needed a final lap of 28.22 seconds in Boston to reach the Olympic 5000m standard. He ran it in 27.85 and finished in 13:04.62. Two months later he clocked 27:20.93 for 10,000m in San Juan Capistrano, third on the Canadian all-time list behind Moh Ahmed and Levins. Home is Ann Arbor again, where Ron Warhurst oversees his training as part of the Very Nice Track Club group, with On as his sponsor. His attention has turned to the marathon. At the Chicago Marathon on Sunday 11 October he finished 28th in 2:12:36, the second Canadian man. It was only his second race over the distance and 3:03 quicker than his 2:15:39 debut. - [Sifan Hassan: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/sifan-hassan): Runners / Sifan Hassan Photo: Chad Veal / Wikimedia Commons Sifan Hassan Runs Sifan Hassan is a Dutch middle- and long-distance runner whose range stretches from the 1500m to the marathon. She was born in Adama, Ethiopia, in January 1993 and grew up in the countryside of Kersa, in the Arsi Zone of Oromia. She arrived in the Netherlands as a refugee in 2008, aged 15, and took up running while studying to become a nurse. Dutch citizenship followed in November 2013. A month later she won the European under-23 cross country title, covering the 6km course in 19:40. The track results came quickly. In 2014 she took European gold over 1500m and silver over 5000m. A year later she won 1500m bronze at the World Championships in Beijing and the senior European cross country title. She won the world indoor 1500m in 2016. Her standout season was 2019. On 12 July in Monaco she ran the mile in 4:12.33, removing Svetlana Masterkova's world record after almost 23 years. At the World Championships she then won the 10,000m in 30:17.62, only her second race at the distance, and the 1500m in 3:51.95, a championship and European record. No other athlete, male or female, has won both events at a single World Championships or Olympics. She also won both the 1500m and 5000m Diamond League titles that year. Records kept coming. On 4 September 2020 at the Memorial van Damme in Brussels she covered 18,930 metres in the one-hour run, a world record she still holds. In Hengelo on 6 June 2021 she ran 29:06.82 for 10,000m, a world record that lasted two days before Letesenbet Gidey ran 29:01.03 on the same track. At the Tokyo Olympics she won the 5000m in 14:36.79 and the 10,000m in 29:55.32, and added bronze in the 1500m. In one of her 1500m races there she went down at the start of the final lap and still won. She remains the only athlete to medal in the 1500m, 5000m and 10,000m at one Games. In Paris in 2024 she took bronze in the 5000m and 10,000m before winning the marathon. No other woman has won Olympic gold at 5000m, 10,000m and the marathon. Her marathon career began with victory in London on 23 April 2023, in 2:18:33 on her debut at the distance. She ran three marathons in 2025, finishing third in London in 2:19:00, winning Sydney in 2:18:22 and placing sixth in New York in 2:24:43. She also holds six European records, from the 1500m to the marathon. That New York race in November 2025 is still her most recent of any kind. An Achilles injury kept her out of London in April 2026. On 14 October, three weeks before the New York City Marathon, she withdrew. She explained that a spell of illness had disrupted her training and she was not in the form she had hoped for. The race went ahead on 1 November without her, and Sheila Chepkirui won it in 2:24:36. Because illness rather than injury stopped her, a later race was not ruled out at the time. With New York gone, though, the 34-year-old is unlikely to race again in 2026. - [Ryan Sullivan: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/ryan-sullivan): Runners / Ryan Sullivan Photo: Eszter Horanyi / iRunFar 🇺🇸 Ryan Sullivan Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 873 (9 November 2026) Ryan Sullivan is an American ultrarunner from Colorado. In September 2026 he won the Run Rabbit Run 100 Mile in Steamboat Springs in 17:03:38, a new course record set in heavy rain and hail. He led from Mount Werner at mile 5, built a nine-minute gap by mile 30 and ran the last 75 miles largely alone, skipping the final aid station to protect his margin. His winning time took nearly 20 minutes off the previous mark of 17:23, set by Dave Stevens in 2023. He crossed the line 55 minutes and 36 seconds ahead of Jeff Mogavero, with defending champion Jesse Rich third. Fellow American Hannah Allgood also broke the course record in the women's race, and both winners collected $20,000 from a purse the organisers say is among the largest in trail running. The win came a year after Sullivan finished fourth at the same race in wet conditions, and followed an earlier 2026 victory at Colorado's High Lonesome 100 Mile. He has also won the San Juan Solstice 50 Mile three times, most recently in 2025, and Québec's QMT 80 in 2024. In 2024 he was fourth at the Leadville Trail 100. Race organisers announced before this year's event that the 2027 and 2028 Run Rabbit Run winners will each earn $100,000, funded by sponsor Insight Global, whose chief executive is himself an ultrarunner. He started out on the unmarked fell courses of the Peak District before switching to international mountain and skyrunning races. He now holds a UTMB Index of 893, among the highest of any British runner on the discipline. Grant races the U23 age group on the Merrell Skyrunner World Series, and often beats senior runners outright. He finished runner-up overall in the U23 Trofeo Esteban Olivero standings and won the U23 race at Poland's Tatra SkyMarathon in 2025, clocking 1:02:21 over 15km. He has also picked up senior results. Grant won the K42 Canarias Anaga Marathon in the Canary Islands in 2025, completing the 30km course in 2:50:17, and took third at both the Sobresobio Redes Trail and the Lozère Trail Skyrace that year. In 2023 he finished second in the Dacia UTMB Mont Blanc YCC. In 2026 he moved up to fourth at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc ETC and was third again at the Lozère Trail Skyrace. He also raced the Skyrace des Matheysins and the Calamorro SkyRace in Spain that year. - [Jazmine Lowther: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jazmine-lowther): Runners / Jazmine Lowther Photo: Ming Poon / iRunFar 🇨🇦 Jazmine Lowther Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 777 (9 November 2026) Jazmine Lowther is a Canadian ultrarunner sponsored by Arc'teryx, with a UTMB general index of 777. She finished 5th woman at the UTMB Mont-Blanc in 2026, in 23:21:55, over the full 174 km distance. She won the Ultra-Trail Cape Town 100 in 2024, in 12:04:25, and the Speedgoat Mountain Races 50K that same year, in 06:15:05. In 2022 she won the Canyons Endurance Runs 100K in 10:01:54. Lowther finished 4th woman at the 2025 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships long trail race, over 81 km, in 10:45:18. She was 2nd woman at the Transgrancanaria Classic in 2023, in 16:26:41, and 4th woman at the UTMB Mont Blanc CCC in 2022. Earlier in her career she was 8th woman at the Run Rabbit Run 100 in 2021 and 2nd woman at the Sinister 7 Ultra 50-Miler that same year. She was also 2nd at the Rut Mountain Runs 50K in 2024. - [Martyna Mlynarczyk: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/martyna-mlynarczyk): Runners / Martyna Mlynarczyk Photo: UTMB profile 🇵🇱 Martyna Mlynarczyk Country 🇵🇱 Poland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 803 (9 November 2026) Martyna Mlynarczyk is a Polish trail and ultra-runner who races for HOKA. Her UTMB Index of 803 sits on an almost unbroken run of wins since 2023. Her biggest win came at the 2025 HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc CCC, the 101km race in Chamonix, which she won in 11:41:55 after finishing 2nd there the year before. She also won the European Games' 100km race in Poland in 2023, in 10:28:50. She has dominated the Pieniny Ultra-Trail in her home country, winning the Wielka Prehyba route in 2024, the Chyża Durbaszka in 2025 and the Lubań Vertical in 2026. Other outright wins include the Tenerife Bluetrail's 73km route in 2024, the Istria 100's 42km race in 2025 and the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg's Walserwaeg Trail, also in 2025. She opened 2026 with a win at the Trail Alsace by UTMB's Trail des Celtes, adding to a run of victories stretching back to the Tatrzański Festiwal Biegowy's Tatra Trail in 2023. She has raced everything from 25K to 100K over a career stretching back to 2018. She has won several US races outright, including the Way Too Cool 50K and the Canyons Endurance Runs 25K, both in 2022, the Mammoth Trail Fest 50K in 2023, and the La Sportiva Table Rock 30K in 2019. Sullivan has also raced at the top international level, finishing 9th woman at the 2023 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships short trail race in Innsbruck-Stubai. At 100K she was second woman at the HOKA Canyons Endurance Runs in 2024, in 10:01:26, and third woman at the Black Canyon Ultras in 2025, in 08:48:50. She was also fourth woman at the Speedgoat Mountain Races 50K in 2024. She placed sixth at the Marató per Muntanya Marina Alta Tres Tossals in 2017 and fourth there in 2018. In 2021 she won the Trail de Primavera Confrides Maraton Serrella, and was third at the Barbudo Trail over 32km. She was second at the Salomon Ultra Pirineu Marató 42k and third at the Transgrancanaria Marathon that year, and finished ninth in the OCC at UTMB. In 2025 she won the SKY race at Val d'Aran in Baqueira Beret, and was fifth over 81km at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships. She placed sixth in the OCC at UTMB, and fourth at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc, Zegama-Aizkorri and Golfo dell'Isola. She won the individual title at the 2013 World Mountain Running Championships and now races for Brooks Trail Runners, holding a general UTMB index of 762. She has taken seven medals for Italy at the World Mountain Running Championships, including that individual gold. She has added a clutch of team medals at the European Mountain Running Championships too, among them an individual silver. She has also won the Italian mountain running title twice, in 2014 and 2017, and the Italian long-distance mountain running title three times between 2015 and 2018. On the UTMB circuit, Gaggi has won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail's 20 km race three years running, from 2022 to 2024, and is a regular at Sierre-Zinal, where she has finished as high as fifth. In 2026 she was sixth over the 50 km course at Nice Cote d'Azur and won the Primiero Dolomiti Marathon outright. - [Guangfu Meng: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/guangfu-meng): Runners / Guangfu Meng Photo: UTMB profile 🇨🇳 Guangfu Meng Country 🇨🇳 China Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 936 (9 November 2026) Guangfu Meng is a Chinese trail and ultrarunner sponsored by Hoka. He carries a UTMB Index of 937, among the highest of any Chinese runner. He has raced several times a year across China's ultra scene since 2019. His biggest results have come at the Hong Kong 100. He won the race in January 2024, in 10:16:56. He defended the title in January 2025, finishing in 9:43:10, about eight minutes clear of runner-up Guidu Qin. He has also won several of China's toughest 100Ks. He took the Ultra-Trail Ninghai 105 in 2024, in 10:05:00. In 2023 he won the Doi Inthanon Elephant 100 in Thailand and the TransLantau 100 in Hong Kong, both first-place finishes on rugged mountain terrain. He has stepped up twice to UTMB's flagship CCC race in the French Alps, finishing 6th in 2025 and 12th in 2026. His 2026 season also brought wins at the Ultra-Trail Mogan EMG and the Huangyan Jiufeng Trail Master Challenge. - [Susanna Saapunki: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/susanna-saapunki): Runners / Susanna Saapunki Photo: Christian David / Wikimedia Commons 🇫🇮 Susanna Saapunki Country 🇫🇮 Finland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 778 (9 November 2026) Susanna Saapunki is a Finnish mountain runner with a UTMB index of 778. She won the Jungfrau-Marathon in Switzerland in 2024, covering 42km and 1,953m of climbing in 03:29:17. She finished sixth in the women's elite up and down race at the 2024 European Off-Road Championships, and seventh at Sierre-Zinal in 2025 in 03:02:29, having finished 13th there two years earlier. She also placed third at the Montée du nid d'aigle in 2023. Saapunki won the NUTS Pyhä Tunturikymppi race in Finland in 2020 and has competed regularly at the Trofeo Nasego in Italy since 2021, improving to third place there in 2024. - [Maude Mathys: age, results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/maude-mathys): Runners / Maude Mathys Photo: Ludovic Péron / Wikimedia Commons 🇨🇭 Maude Mathys Born 1987 (age 38 or 39) Country 🇨🇭 Switzerland Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 814 (9 November 2026) Maude Mathys, born Maude Kung on 14 January 1987 in Ollon, Switzerland, is a Swiss ski mountaineer and trail runner who also races ultramarathons. She competes for Asics and for the SAC-CAS Swiss ski mountaineering team, and has a general UTMB Index of 814. She has dominated Sierre-Zinal over more than a decade, winning the race outright in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022, after finishing on the podium there as early as 2012 and 2013. In 2026 she also won the Trail Verbier St Bernard Marathon in 04:42:02. Mathys finished second at the 2018 World Mountain Running Championships in Andorra, behind Kenya's Lucy Wambui Murigi and ahead of Kenya's Viola Jelegat in third. She won the 2017 European Mountain Running Championships, and took third in the team event at the 2012 European Championships alongside Emilie Gex-Fabry. In 2015 she was reprimanded for an anti-doping rule violation, after testing positive for clomiphene, a substance banned under the World Anti-Doping Agency code. She was not suspended. Her recent form includes wins at the Chiangmai HMONG 50-Day and Inthanon 50 races in Thailand in 2025. She also won both the half marathon and the vertical kilometre at Transvulcania on La Palma that year, and the Golden Trail Championship's GTC Azores race over 112 km in 2020, in 10:47:41. - [Leonard Mitrica: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/leonard-mitrica): Runners / Leonard Mitrica Photo: UTMB profile 🇷🇴 Leonard Mitrica Country 🇷🇴 Romania Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 904 (9 November 2026) Leonard Mitrica is a Romanian trail and ultra runner for Joma Trail/Datacor, with a UTMB Index of 906. He won the Seoul100K's 50km race in South Korea in 2026, covering 49km with 2,896m of climbing in 6:12:28, and finished 2nd at the Transgrancanaria Advanced over 81km the same year. He was 10th at the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc OCC in 2026 and 12th in the trail race at the European Athletics Off-Road Running Championships. He raced Zegama-Aizkorri five times between 2022 and 2026 and Sierre-Zinal in both 2023 and 2024. Mitrica represented Romania at the 2023 World Mountain and Trail Running Championships in Innsbruck-Stubai, finishing 18th in the short trail race. She won the 63km Crimea X Run RUN2 in 2021, finishing in 7:33:43, and also won the ArkhyzXRunAlpindustriaTrail Fedoseeva 25 that year, with a second and third place at the Hoka Wild Trail races. - [Lauren Puretz: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/lauren-puretz): Runners / Lauren Puretz Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Lauren Puretz Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 771 (9 November 2026) Lauren Puretz is an American ultrarunner with a UTMB Index of 772, built on a deep results history stretching back to 2017 and centred on Colorado's Pikes Peak races before she moved up to 100 milers. Her strongest year to date came in 2025, when she finished 8th woman at UTMB itself, the 174 km race around Mont Blanc with almost 10,000 metres of climbing, in 24:54:57. She has been a regular top finisher at the Javelina Jundred 100 Miles in Arizona, taking third in 2024 in 15:00:50 after fourth the year before and eighth in 2022. At the Black Canyon Ultras 100K she was third in both 2024 and 2025. She was 13th woman at the Western States 100 in 2024 and 14th in 2026. Puretz took third place among the women at the 2026 Run Rabbit Run 100, a mountain hundred-miler based in Colorado, crossing the line in 20:32:27 behind race winner Hannah Allgood. That same year she was fifth over the tougher 119 km distance at the Chianti Ultra Trail in Italy. Further back, Puretz won the Sawatch Ascent 50K in 2023 and the Cheyenne Mountain Trail Race 25K in 2019, and finished fifth at the 2024 World Masters Mountain Running Championships' 34 km long course. - [Morven Goodrum: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/morven-goodrum): Runners / Morven Goodrum Photo: European Athletics 🇬🇧 Morven Goodrum Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra, Road UTMB Index 793 (9 November 2026) Morven Goodrum is a British mountain runner who only moved onto the trails in the last two or three years. She started with track and cross country at school, then moved up in distance to road racing. She ran a marathon and a half marathon before her coach, Sophie, whose own background is in trail running, suggested she try the trails. Her breakthrough came at the 2026 European Off-Road Running Championships uphill race, held in Kamnik, Slovenia, which she won. It was the first time most of the trail running world had heard her name. A late invitation from the organisers brought her to the 2026 Sierre-Zinal, her first time racing it and her first look at the course. She led at the halfway point and reached the Ponchette checkpoint first, in 57:36, but lost ground on the final seven kilometre descent. She finished third, in 2:57:15, behind winner Madalina Florea of Romania and runner-up Caroline Kimutai of Kenya. She said she knew she would be stronger on the climbs, so pushed hard from the start and tried to hang on. She has said the downhills are still something to work on. - [Melissa Paauwe: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/melissa-paauwe): Runners / Melissa Paauwe Photo: courtesy of Melissa Paauwe / Calgary Booster Club 🇨🇦 Melissa Paauwe Country 🇨🇦 Canada Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 624 (9 November 2026) Melissa Paauwe is a Canadian runner who races on both trail and road. Her UTMB results cover short mountain events of 21 to 50 km. She does not currently hold a UTMB Index. Her earliest UTMB result came in 2019 at the Marin Ultra Challenge. She was second woman in the 25 km race, which has 1,070 m of climb, finishing in 2:05:12. In 2024 she was second woman again, this time at the Sinister 7 Ultra 50K. That course packs 2,255 m of climb into its 50 km, and she covered it in 5:41:29. Her first win on the UTMB record followed in 2026. She took the women's title at the Black Spur Ultra Half Marathon, a 21 km race with 911 m of ascent, in 1:59:20. On the road she has shown real pace as well. At the 52nd Berlin Marathon on Sunday 27 September she was the first Canadian woman home in 2:44:58. That placed her 68th woman overall and second in the W40-44 category. The next Canadian, Caitlin Schindel, finished in 2:51:02, just over six minutes behind. More than 50,000 runners finished in Berlin that day, on a course long known for fast times. The fastest woman was Tigst Assefa, whose 2:11:04 set a new best for the Berlin course. Paauwe's run there, alongside her Black Spur win, marks her as a runner capable on both surfaces. - [Katharina Hartmuth: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/katharina-hartmuth): Runners / Katharina Hartmuth Photo: iRunFar 🇩🇪 Katharina Hartmuth Country 🇩🇪 Germany Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 776 (9 November 2026) Katharina Hartmuth is a German ultra runner who competes for HOKA. She carries a UTMB Index of 777. She specialises in the longest mountain races, including multi-day events that push runners past 300 kilometres. In September 2026 she defended her Tor des Geants title in Italy's Aosta Valley, finishing in 67 hours 10 minutes. She placed third overall, behind winner Jiaju Zhao of China. She became the first woman to break 70 hours over the roughly 336 km course, and the first to reach the outright podium. Reports said she slept for only about 15 minutes during the entire race. Her win came two years after she first went under 80 hours at the same race, in 2024. Earlier the same year she also ran the quickest time by a woman on England's Bob Graham Round. She also won the Madeira Island Ultra-Trail that year, and was third at UTMB, having finished second there in 2023. Hartmuth has twice finished third at the Hardrock 100, in 2024 and 2025, one of the toughest 100-mile races in the sport. She has won the Eiger Ultra Trail twice and the Swiss Alps 100 twice, and took the Innsbruck Alpine Trailrun Festival's K110 race in 2020. - [Caroline Guest: results and profile](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/caroline-guest): Runners / Caroline Guest CG 🇬🇧 Film My Run 🇬🇧 Caroline Guest Country 🇬🇧 United Kingdom Runs Trail & Ultra Caroline Guest is a British runner whose results take in trail ultras and road marathons. Her recorded trail races run from a 23km half marathon in Yorkshire to a 100km challenge between London and Brighton. She does not hold a current UTMB Index. Her longest race on record came in 2016 at the London 2 Brighton Challenge. She completed the full 100km, which carries 1,930m of climb, in 23:37:19 and was the 179th woman to finish. Six years later she ran the 50km Run To The Sea to Brighton, with 700m of ascent, in 5:24:16 for 21st woman. In 2023 she finished the North Downs Ridge 50k, a 53km route with 960m of climb, in 6:13:18. That put her 17th among the women. Her highest placing came closer to home for Yorkshire runners. At the 2023 Yorkshire Reservoir Dogs Trail Half Marathon she was fourth woman over 23km and 435m of climb, finishing in 2:48:35. A British runner of the same name won an age-category title at the Amsterdam Marathon on Sunday 18 October in 2:56:48. She was one of four Britons to win their age groups that day. Jack Bromley was the quickest of the four in 2:19:54. More than 25,000 people finished a race run in rain, wind and low temperatures, starting and finishing in the city's Olympic Stadium and passing the Vondelpark on the way. Her results stretch back to 2013 on the US West Coast trail circuit. She was 2nd woman at the Angeles Crest 100 Mile Endurance Run in 2022 in 27:01:12, and has repeatedly reached the podium at 100-milers, finishing 3rd at the Orcas Island 100 Mile in 2017 and 9th at the Cascade Crest 100 in 2016. She was 2nd woman at the Gorge Waterfalls 100K and 7th at the Broken Arrow Skyrace 23K that year. She has also won the Cuyamaca 100K in 2023, the San Jacinto 50K and Noble Canyon 50K in 2022, and a run of 50K wins between 2015 and 2017 including the Oriflamme 50K twice and the San Diego 50 Trail Marathon. His general UTMB index of 901 comes from nearly a decade of results in the French Alps. He has built a strong record at the TDS at UTMB Mont-Blanc, finishing sixth in 2021, third in 2024 and second in 2025, in 18:28:04. In 2026 he was runner-up at both the Restonica Trail's UTC100M in Corsica and MIUT Legend on Madeira. He won the Trail des Aiguilles Rouges in 2023, having placed second there four times between 2018 and 2022. He also won the Restonica Trail in 2022 and the Serre Che Trail's Grand Tour des Cerces in 2019. His other wins include the Ultra Tour du Môle and the Trails De La Vallée Du Brevon's Trail Des Crêtes Du Brevon, both in 2018. He was sixth at the Festival Des Templiers' Grand Trail Des Templiers in 2022. - [Fabiola Conti: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/fabiola-conti): Runners / Fabiola Conti Photo: photographer unknown 🇮🇹 Fabiola Conti Country 🇮🇹 Italy Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 793 (9 November 2026) Fabiola Conti is an Italian trail and skyrunning specialist who races for Mud&Snow. Her UTMB Index of 793 spans results from short vertical kilometre races up to a 122km mountain ultra. Her biggest win came at the 2025 Monte Rosa WalserWaeg by UTMB, where she won the 122km Les Sentiers des Valdôtains route in 18:02:01 with 8,200m of climbing. She followed it with 3rd woman at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' long trail race the same year, an 81km course with more than 5,000m of climbing. Conti has taken outright wins across a wide range of shorter races, including the K60 Vibram Maremontana and the EOLO Campo dei Fiori Trail in 2023, the Trail del Marchesato in both 2022 and 2023, and the Sanremo Trail's 32km route in 2022. She also won the La Thuile Trail's 70km ultra in 2024 and its shorter 25km route back in 2021. She opened 2026 with wins at the Monte Rosa WalserWaeg's 43km Walserwaeg Trail and at the Trail Monte San Giorgio Sky Race, alongside third-place finishes at FlettaTrail and the Skyrace des Matheysins. - [Jeff Mogavero: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/jeff-mogavero): Runners / Jeff Mogavero Photo: Andy Cochrane / jeffmogavero.com 🇺🇸 Jeff Mogavero Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 925 (9 November 2026) Jeff Mogavero is an American ultrarunner with a UTMB Index of 925, built over more than a decade of racing since his first wins in 2014 and 2015. He has become one of the most consistent finishers at Western States, placing seventh in 2026 in 14:38:36 and fourth in 2025 in 14:30:11. In 2025 he won the Ultra-trail Cape Town 100 outright in 11:04:53, and the year before he was second at the Javelina Jundred 100 Miles in 12:54:31. He has twice finished second at the Broken Arrow Skyrace's 46K, in 2023 and 2024, and was third at Puerto Vallarta by UTMB's 170 km race in 2022, the same year he was 16th at UTMB itself. He is also a regular at the mountain hundred-miler Run Rabbit Run, held each autumn in Colorado. Mogavero took third there in 2019 and again in 2021, then moved up to second in 2026, stopping the clock at 17:59:14. Further back, Mogavero won the Beaverhead Endurance Runs 100K and the River of No Return Endurance Runs 55K in 2021, and took the Marin Ultra Challenge 50K and the McDonald Forest 50K in 2017 and 2018. His UTMB results run continuously from 2014 to 2026. - [Henriette Albon: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/henriette-albon): Runners / Henriette Albon Photo: Petter Engdahl / iRunFar 🇳🇴 Henriette Albon Country 🇳🇴 Norway Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 775 (9 November 2026) Henriette Albon is a Norwegian ultrarunner with a UTMB general index of 773. She won back-to-back editions of the Transgrancanaria Classic in 2025 and 2026, in 15:02:50 and 15:16:33. She has also won the Ultra-Trail Snowdonia UTS 50K in 2024, the Boffi Fifty at the Festival des Templiers in 2023, and the Grand Trail du Saint Jacques 100K in 2025, in 08:37:48, as well as the Romsdalseggenlopet Fjord to Summit race in 2026. Her results in Europe's toughest skyraces include 3rd woman at Trofeo Kima in 2024, 6th woman at the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 80K in 2023, and 6th woman at the UTMB Mont Blanc CCC in 2022. She was 6th woman at UTMB's OCC race in 2021 and 4th woman at Ultra Pirineu 100K that same year. Away from racing, Albon has set a winter speed record on the Bob Graham Round and holds the fastest known time for crossing Norway on the 120km Norge Pa Tvers route. She has raced in Norway's fjord skyraces since 2016 and competed at the Trail World Championships in 2019, finishing 41st woman. - [Virgile Moriset: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/virgile-moriset): Runners / Virgile Moriset Photo: UTMB profile 🇫🇷 Virgile Moriset Country 🇫🇷 France Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 928 (9 November 2026) Virgile Moriset is a 25-year-old trail runner from Lyon. He spent more than a decade racing bikes before switching to running, and trains largely on feel, with a self-taught, sensation-led approach rather than a fixed programme. His rise has been rapid. At the SainteLyon, a long-running French trail race, he finished 18th in 2022, seventh in 2023, fourth in 2024 and second in 2025. In 2025 he also won the 100km race at Nice Cote d'Azur by UTMB and was runner-up at the Marathon du Mont-Blanc 90km. Moriset went into the 2026 UTMB, his first attempt at the race, having not finished three races earlier in the season. He was down in 20th place at Lac Combal, 68km in, but began working through the field. By Arnouvaz, 99km in, he had moved up to 14th, and he was inside the top 10 by Grand Col Ferret at 104km. Coming out of Vallorcine he was still nearly five minutes behind Spain's Joaquin Lopez, but kept moving well and passed him by La Flegere. Moriset crossed the line in Chamonix fourth, in 19 hours 0 minutes and 23 seconds, with Lopez fifth six minutes later. He said afterwards he had been very emotional at the finish, and had not expected such a result on his UTMB debut. - [Dmitry Mityaev: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/dmitry-mityaev): Runners / Dmitry Mityaev Photo: UTMB profile 🇦🇳 Dmitry Mityaev Country 🇦🇳 Curaçao Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 906 (9 November 2026) Dmitry Mityaev is a trail runner who races for adidas Terrex, with a UTMB index of 907. He has finished on the podium of the Marathon du Mont-Blanc's 90km race five times since 2021, winning outright in 2024 in 10:44:14. He was runner-up at UTMB's TDS race in 2019 in 18:16:16 and 3rd in 2018, and has won the Ultra-trail Cape Town's 100km race three times, in 2018, 2022 and 2023. In 2023 he won the Salomon Cappadocia Ultra-Trail's CUT race and the adidas Terrex Infinite Trails 60K, and in 2024 he won the Salomon Ultra Pirineu's 100km race. - [Taylor Stack: results and UTMB Index](https://filmmyrun.com/runners/taylor-stack): Runners / Taylor Stack Photo: UTMB profile 🇺🇸 Taylor Stack Country 🇺🇸 United States Runs Trail & Ultra UTMB Index 926 (9 November 2026) Taylor Stack is an American trail runner with a UTMB Index of 926, among the highest of any man in this group, built on short, steep skyrunning courses in the United States and Europe. In 2026 he won the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc ETC in 1:19:23 and the Desert RATS Trail Running Festival's 50K in 3:39:41, and was third man at Zegama-Aizkorri in 3:52:17. He also finished fifth at The Broken Arrow Skyrace's 23K and 38th at Sierre-Zinal. In 2025 he was 12th man at Sierre-Zinal in 2:38:37, third at the Pitz Alpine Glacier Trail on the Golden Trail World Series, and second at the Desert RATS Trail Running Festival's 21K. He was also 12th at the World Mountain and Trail Running Championships' classic 14K. His UTMB results begin in 2024 at The Broken Arrow Skyrace and the Mammoth Trail Fest, though he had already won the Run Through Time Marathon's half marathon in both 2015 and 2016.
